title: Arshdeep Singh to Sai Sudharsan, 1 run

commentPreTextItems.html: Game time. Gill and Sudharsan, so prolific for GT last season, walk out to the middle in New Chandigarh. PBKS are wearing red and blue this season. Arshdeep Singh has the new ball. Sudharsan to face. Toss, 7.00 pm Shubman Gill calls heads. It's tails. PBKS are bowling first, no surprise there so early in the season. Cooper Connolly, Marcus Stonis, Marco Jansen and Bartlett are PBKS' overseas players. Shreyas Iyer brushes off last season's exploits and says it's a fresh start. Let's end the suspense for, Jim. Glenn Phillips is in! GT line up with Buttler, Phillips, Rashid and Rabada, so no Jason Holder. Ashok Sharma, who is supposed to be express pace, also makes his IPL debut for GT. PBKS (bowling first): Prabhsimran Singh, Cooper Connolly, Shreyas Iyer, Nehal Wadhera, Shashank Singh, Marcus Stoinis, Marco Jansen, Xavier Bartlett, Vyshak Vijaykumar, Arshdeep Singh, Yuzvendra Chahal. Priyansh Arya will come in as Impact Player when PBKS chase. GT (batting first): Shubman Gill, Sai Sudharsan, Jos Buttler, Washington Sundar, Glenn Phillips, Shahrukh Khan, Rahul Tewatia, Rashid Khan, Kagiso Rabada, Ashok Sharma, Mohammed Siraj. Prasidh Krishna will come in as Impact Player when GT bowl second. The pitch is expected to be great for batting, though they usually say that. Sachin: "Where's Sai Kishore??? He was a stud last season." He's not even on the GT impact subs list. Perhaps there's a fitness issue. Or perhaps Jayant Yadav, Manav Suthar, Jason Holder and Kumar Kushagra are all better fielders than Sai? Sai: "Poor selection by GT, surely Holder is a must in this team. You'd go for Kushagra over SRK as well I think." Avyan Bhoj: "Seems PBKS has upper hand while bowling, as a GT fan though I can't lose hope :)" DaWolf: "Not a fan of these impact subs. Most of the time it just adds an extra batsman, this devaluing the art of picking and balancing the team in the first place. Just play XI. Thoughts?" It's divided opinion, the Impact Player, with a few captains criticising it and a few coaches liking it. It's here to stay for now. 6.50 pm PBKS and GT played each other only once last season (because of the IPL's grouping system) and scored nearly 500 runs in Ahmedabad. They played each other in New Chandigarh in IPL 2024, and that was a much lower-scoring contest. Shaurya: "There is one more crazy probability which can happen that Jos gets dropped to make way for GP!!..I hope GT doesn't make that mistake.." Surely not ... the Boss has got to start at least. Thamizhachi : "Unpopular Opinion: Shreyas Iyer can / should replace SKY as Indian T20I captain right away. He is a far more accomplished batter and also a better captaincy option that SKY who has been given the longest of ropes." Phew, a little harsh on a captain who's just won a T20 World Cup? Here's Jim again with more Phillips love. "Phillips-naysayers need to understand that if he's in the team, immediately add 10 runs to your score because he'll save that much more than any other player would in the field. Then for every 25 runs he scores, add another 10 because he turns that many singles into twos. Then remember every two games or so he'll take a catch that no other player on earth could catch. Plus he can bowl and keep wicket if needed (but too good in the field for that). Leaving him out of your IPL XI is madness!" Let's hope only really difficult catches come his way, because he doesn't do as well with the sitters. Sanket: "Punjab had a incredible run of form last season largely due to the their uncapped Indian player performing brilliantly. In IPL, the toughest thing for the new comer is to replicate the same form in next year because in the first year teams don't know your game that much so there is very limited knowledge to prepare against you but after a season they will hard at you, with lot of preparations. So will be interesting to see how someone like Priyansh Arya goes this time." They call it second-season syndrome. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi did not suffer from it last night. Nishh: "There's no way someone thinks Iyer is a better T20 batter than SKY. Even looking at just numbers doesn't justify it, SKY has been a bit out of form but even then I have never seen him waste balls or be afraid to hit his first ball for a boundary" 6.40 pm Sanket: "What would be GTs overseas combination no doubt about Buttler (despite an awful form in English Colors), Rashid and Rabada. The headache will be choosing out of Phillips vs Holder. In my opinion they should go with Holder, firstly their death over bowling seems a bit weak as Rabada hasnt been at his best , Siraj and Prasidh can do a job but are not designated either for the job, Holder who has that experience can be handy to bowl couple of overs and also he has been in incredible form with bat." We'll find out soon enough. I'd like to see them line up with Buttler, Phillips, Holder and Rashid ... but the other talking point is Washington Sundar, who played only six games last IPL season, and two in 2024. The Indian team management have so much time for Sundar, but he hasn't got much love from his IPL teams. Jp: "PBKS should not play cooper if he is just going to bat and cant bowl.. he is a better bowler than a batsman ...Owen should be the ideal choice for just batting prospective ..plus he can give 2 overs of bowling as well." Charan: "Looking forward to see Shreyas in this season. With an amazing season, he can really start breathing down the neck of the current Indian T20I captain who's been in awful form. And if he takes them to the title, arguably becoming one of the best captains going around, the competition will only get more intense. " Sanket: "When you look at GT's batting line up you can easily recognise that they are very heavily reliant on top 3 and you think that if you get them out, even 2 out of them cheaply you can hold this batting line up but this trio has been racking up some incredible runs very consistently. But replicating that form wont be easy this season especially considering Buttler's form. So the middle order Washy, Shahrukh, Tewatia would have larger role to play here." Nilashish: "Eager to see Kumar Kushagra play. Hope he gets a chance soon.. What a SMAT season he had!!" 6.15 pm Tonight's match sees the return of Shubman Gill and Shreyas Iyer to the T20 spotlight. They both had 600+ seasons in IPL 2025 at a strike rate of more than 150, but such is the vastness of India's T20 riches that both batters have been left out of the national team. Gill was part of the plan for the T20 World Cup until he got overtaken by faster scorers, while Shreyas has not played a single T20 since his incredible run of form in IPL 2025. Staggering. Neither would be thinking about that as they begin to lead their teams in IPL 2026, but ... The PBKS combination seems fairly settled - Cooper Connolly is likely to make his debut for them tonight, and slot in at No. 3. The rest of the XI lines up largely line it did last season. The question for GT is their overseas combination. They haven't played Glenn Phillips much so far, they've bought Jason Holder who's been in supreme T20 form in 2025, and they have Buttler, Rashid and Rabada. You'd imagine that Buttler and Rashid definitely start, but who are their other two overseas players? They sometimes played only three last season. Jim: "Tonight better be the night Glenn Phillips returns to a starting XI and stays there. I'll probably throw my TV out the window if that doesn't happen." Are you planning to staying up for the game, Jim? Mustafa Moudi: "Fun Fact: Since 2021, all of the IPL Finals features either of these 2 skippers. From 2021 to 2023, Gill played all the 3 Finals winning just once while 2024." Jim: "I'll stay up if GP is in the team. Otherwise I'll defenestrate the TV, head to bed, and write GT off for the season." Umair: "Baffles me how Shreyas Iyer is not in the T20I setup for India. He has to be the first name on the squad list and this might be harsh but I think he gets in over Tilak. Also given his captaincy record he should be the obvious choice to takeover from Surya as well." Shrihari S : "Surely I agree with Shubman Gill that he doesn't have any point to prove. But spots in the Indian T20I team are very tough to book / seal. Once dropped, it is tough to get back , given the bench quality. " 6.00 pm Good evening, folks, and welcome to ESPNcricinfo's live coverage of the fourth game of the IPL 2026 season - Punjab Kings hosting Gujarat Titans in New Chandigarh. We've had three rather one-sided games so far, so here's hoping for a more closely-fought contest tonight. I'm George Binoy, your commentator for the game. It's been a while since I've been in this hot seat, so be gentle please. Both PBKS and GT made the playoffs last season - PBKS finished runners-up - and both teams didn't do anything too dramatic in terms of changing squad composition between then and now. They have largely the same look. In terms of overseas players, PBKS have Cooper Connolly instead of Josh Inglis, while GT have Jason Holder and Tom Banton after trading Sherfane Rutherford to Mumbai Indians. Ricky Ponting reckons PBKS are stronger this season than they were last year. The pitch in Mullanpur is expected to be a high-scoring surface tonight. The boundaries are not tiny, but not especially large either - the straight hit down the ground is about 71 metres. We've had 200-plus first innings totals in two of the three games so far, and both were chased down. It's a bit cloudy at the moment but there's no forecast for rain.

title: Washington Sundar to Connolly, FOUR

commentPreTextItems.html: alex: "14 to 3 sixes tells a story. Even with all those extras in Ashdeep's epic last over... GT only managed a pathetic 31 in the final overs phase due to lack of batting depth... Holder a must for Rabada... especially when Ashok has come back well and Siraj has only bowled 2 overs..."

commentTextItems.html: Cooper Connolly is a star on IPL debut, seeing PBKS home in a tricky chase, when his team-mates were losing their heads all around him! He scores the winning runs by hanging back in his crease and cutting a flat and quick ball from Sundar to the cover boundary, those fast hands of his have the final say in this topsy-turvy contest.

commentPostTextItems.html: Four wins in four games for the home team, four wins in four games for the chasing team, four wins in four games for the team that's won the toss. That's been the pattern so far in IPL 2026. Unlike the previous three chases, though, which were extremely one-sided, PBKS had a few nervous moments in tonight's chase. Shubman Gill: "I think we bowled pretty well, we didn't get going in the last five or six overs (with the bat), it wasn't a 200 wicket, but if we had 175 it would have been different, but we kept losing wickets and we couldn't get going in the last five overs ... once the ball got older it was difficult to hit down the ground, there was no pace on the wicket ... when we were bowling, with the rain coming down it did not stop as much in the second innings, we did well with the bowling. "I could have got Prasidh on earlier, but we were in the game until the end, there will always be ifs and buts ... Ashok bowled pretty well up front and in the back, as he plays more and gets more experience he will be of value for us. He works very hard on his game, he's a good fielder for us, I met him at a camp a couple of months ago and was very impressed." Shrikant : "Perplexing bowling strategy. Prasiddh introduced after twelve overs and Siraj bowling only 2 overs. A lot to ponder over batting strategy and bowling strategy " KM: " 1 on what Alex said. GT team is fine for par 160-180 type surfaces where their top 3 maximizes the odds of getting median scores that fall in that range. But for flatter surfaces, being *that* top-heavy also hinders the top order's ability to slog in the powerplay. " Time for the presentation ... Shreyas Iyer: All I can say about the hand is that it's nice, same as it was before, I don't want to jinx anything ... Some of the shots he (Cooper Connolly) played was surreal to watch, especially the one off Rashid ... I was focused on my hand inside, icing it, suddenly we lost two wickets back to back, these things happen in the IPL, you have to stay composed, Cooper was there, he was composed and calm ... After the third over we realised the wicket is slow, Arshdeep came and said it was holding a bit, we tried to make the ball old as soon as possible. Vyshak is carrying forward the form he performed in the last season, he is a big match player ... I was surprised to see a short leg for me, I told Shubman I had never seen that before, it's good to see captains attacking. Cooper Connolly is the player of the match: "I was looking forward to the experience of playing with some world class players, but to put that performance in tonight, very happy. I spent some time with friends and family at home before this just to reset. I'm just more of a tempo player, feel the flow of my hands, don't hit too many big sixes ... working with Ricky is great. Not a lot was said, we were quite relaxed, in a great position out there, nice to get the win with Xavier, looking forward to the rest of the tournament. That was the first time I played Rashid Khan, was nice to get the win." That brings us to the end of our live coverage of the game. Thank you for staying with us, and writing in. Until tomorrow, good night.

title: Mukesh Kumar to Marsh, 1 run

commentPreTextItems.html: 7.25pm Hello hello. Thanks, Ekanth, and there's a bit of grumbling among the feedbackers with DC opting to bench Nabi. Let's see how that decision pans out as they bowl first, with just five specialist bowlers in their line-up too. Rishabh Pant and Mitchell Marsh head out to the middle. The DC players break out of a huddle too. Let's play! A few curiosity-inducing calls, selection-wise and batting orders too. Will Pooran actually bat at 5? Find out with Abhijato. Here's the ever so calm Sohum: "No Aquib Nabi today? Outrageous, infuriating. My disappointment is immeasurable and my day is ruined." Dhinesh: "Mayank said that he is fit and raring to go. Now LSG have benched him. What is happening?" Think that'll be an early question in the press conference if not the presentations LSG have picked Mukul Choudhary over Akshat Raghuwanshi and Himmat Singh. No Mayank Yadav. Mukul is a big-hitting keeper-batter from Rajasthan. You can read more about him here LSG impact options - Digvesh Rathi, Avesh Khan, Himmat Singh, Shahbaz Ahmed, Akshat Raghuvanshi LSG 1 Aiden Markram, 2 Mitchell Marsh, 3 Rishabh Pant (Capt, wk), 4 Ayush Badoni, 5 Nicholas Pooran, 6 Abdul Samad, 7 Mukul Choudhary, 8 Mohsin Khan, 9 Mohammed Shami, 10 Anrich Nortje, 11 Prince Yadav Mukesh Kumar has been picked over Auqib Nabi. Beside that, no surprises from DC. Ashutosh Sharma likely to come in as impact player DC impact options - Ashutosh Sharma, Auqib Nabi, Sameer Rizvi, Dushmantha Chameera, Karun Nair DC 1 KL Rahul (wk), 2 Pathum Nissanka, 3 Nitish Rana, 4 Vipraj Nigam, 5 Axar Patel (Capt), 6 David Miller, 7 Tristan Stubbs, 8 Lungi Ngidi, 9 Kuldeep Yadav, 10 T Natarajan, 11 Mukesh Kumar DC are the first away team to win a toss this season Rishabh Pant, LSG captain Not much will change on this wicket, so toss won't matter. It's a completely new energy, new logo, colour and mindset. We're feeling good and rearing to go. Injuries was a concern last year, won't dwell on that too much. Bowlers are fit, everyone's willing to go in and make an impact. Markram, Marsh and Pooran and Nortje are our overseas picks Axar Patel, DC captain Fresh wicket, red soil, we want to see if the wicket offers assistance to the pacers. Data says chasing teams win, but it's also a new tournament and I think we should start by bowling first. Last year, we started well but lost it in the middle. We want to start well again. Overseas picks - Three batters - Miller, Nissanka, Stubbs and the bowler Ngidi 7pm Heads is the call from Axar at the toss, he wins, DC bowling first Pitch The square boundaries have a bias - 56 and 64 metres. Kevin Pietersen says it's a beautiful wicket. You want to chase, tough to set a total. Red soil, these pitches have been relaid and the scoring rates have increased from around 7.5 to 9. Six out of the eight games here last year were won by the chasing team. Mustafa Moudi: "Last season was very disappointing for Rishabh Pant scoring just 135 Runs in the first 12 matches and scoring almost that much in the last 2 game with double strike rate. Hope this time he starts performing right from the beginning and we get to watch more Somersault Celebration this time !!" jagpreet: "strange call from DC wrt Nissanka. thought in absence of Starc they will go for both Ngidi and chameera to strengthen their pace attack at this Ekana's surface. the pace bowling looks below par in comparison to LSG" 6:50pm LSG's batting is well set even though Pooran at 4 might be a spot down. Their Indian middle order - Badoni, Samad and Raghuwanshi - need to fire. THeir bowling is set with Nortje, Mayank as all-out pacers, Shami as the seam exponent, Rathi and Shahbaz. They might not have a sixth bowler. Keep calm, swing the ball, and carry on: The Auqib Nabi mantra 6:40pm David Miller, Lungi Ngidi and Pathum Nissanka and Nitish Rana have been handed their DC caps. That solves one selection debate - Ngidi will play over Dushmantha Chameera. The rest of the bowling line-up is unlikely to throw up surprises. Kuldeep, Natarajan, Axar and Auqib Nabi. Check out the above feature for more on Nabi. There's a good mix, a left-arm pacer and two spinners, two right-arm quicks. Nilashish: "Hasaranga's uncertainty throws a major clog in LSG's juggernaut. No other team has managed to assemble such an injury prone pace attack." Match preview by Himanshu Agrawal All eyes on fit-again Mayank as LSG kickstart season against DC 6:30pm The final two teams to play their first games are taking on each other and both of them have different strengths. Delhi Capitals' middle order is strong with Axar, Miller and Ashutosh and LSG's top order is star-studded with Marsh, Markram, Pant and Pooran. Their bowling line-ups have been hit by unavailability, Starc in DC's case and Hasaranga for LSG, but the ones that remain are solid. More on that later. For now, welcome to our coverage, hope you have a great time.

commentPostTextItems.html: Lungi Ngidi: (Pooran wicket) Trying to use the bigger side, we know the type of ball-striker he is. No pace to work with, trying to do him in the air. Used the dip too. Last one was the best wicket, executing the wide slower yorker is hardest for me. At the World Cup, I mentioned Bravo told me I need a deceptive slower ball. It took years of practice. I'm close to 100% but not there, trying to emulate Bravo. Abhra: "Will Ngidi be on a hat-trick next game?" Yeah shaz: "who does Starc replace when he comes back? good headache for Delhi " 9:09pm A fizzle for LSG and.... fizzing performance from DC. It started with a lucky run out of the new LSG opener, Pant, but they kept Marsh quiet for the most part. Four of the top-five fell for single-digit scores. Axar, Ngidi, Natarajan and Kuldeep all got to the party. LSG were even forced to bring out Shahbaz as Impact Player ahead of Rathi. That didn't work out with bat. Let's see how it goes with ball. Abhijato will be on for it.

title: Abdul Samad to Sameer Rizvi, SIX

commentPreTextItems.html: Samad to bowl the final over

commentTextItems.html: Final ball as it turns out. Long-hop just outside off is hauled over deep midwicket with a pull. Rizvi smiles and punches Stubbs' arms as they hug

commentPostTextItems.html: Each team has now played a game and there are some early impressions to be made. Tonight was about bowling units, same might apply tomorrow for SRH vs KKR. Join us then, thanks for coming on today. Goodnight. Sameer Rizvi, POTM During practice sessions and matches, I was told I'll bat at 4 and was given a lot of support by the coaches. Playing at home, you know the conditions and that helped as my state league takes place here. I wanted to be positive in the powerplay but two wickets fell and the situation changed, Stubbs said respect the conditions. Once we were set, we knew we could play our natural game. It's not that I started hitting after getting to fifty. I wanted to take on bad balls, if I got it I'd hit it to the boundary. Axar Patel, DC captain Game finished early, got close in the middle. The new ball was doing a bit, our chat was about a big partnership and we finished well. Happy with bowling. We knew it swung and seamed at the start. We told that to all new bowlers and they did well. There's a big boundary and I felt since the pitch was assisting pacers, I'd bowl them over me. Plan was to bring in Rizvi early. Ashutosh Sharma was also an option if the innings started well. Last year, Ashu proved himself first game and this time Rizvi. He's been excellent at practice, glad he pulled it off tonight. Tristan Stubbs I wasn't fully padded up, had to go straight in. Was simple what we needed, bat time and build a partnership. Rizvi was brilliant. You're always looking to score but the situation tells you what to do. It was doing a bit, swung for long and seamed. We kept saying keep batting normally and look to score. Rizvi takes on spin naturally, makes my job easier. We knew it was one big over and it's run a ball. (Chat at the start of Shahbaz's over) Let's see if it's spinning and the first three balls went for 12, wasn't the plan to take him on but it worked out. I like No 6, you bat at different situations and try to take the team over the line. Rishabh Pant, LSG captain Best way to recover from my dismissal is to ignore it as you can't control it. The way we batted, we couldn't get a partnership for long. The plan was for Pooran to take on the middle overs from No. 5. We had to get someone who could add a few runs as the impact player because we didn't have enough, on a good pitch. e had a role defined for Badoni, when we lose early wickets, that's the time he can make a mark. We wanted to explore left-right at the top as to stop them from bowling from the left-arm spinner. There was enough help with the new ball. But you can't put pressure on the opposition with 140. 20 extras hurt, at the same time, you try too much on a wicket like this and are trying to restrict them under 140. 50-50 call, but definitely we'll see me in the top order. Jim: "Too many games decided by the toss. The toss-losing side needs to be given an advantage of some sort. " Sidd: "Who's this player extras? Did his job today. " 11:02pm A definitive partnership clears the game for DC but it was anything but an easy chase given they were 26 for 4. The ball offered seam, extra bounce or swing for a long time and LSG's pacers exploited it nicely. Prince Yadav, in particular, who got Axar with a brilliant inswinger and Nissanka who looked to slog. LSG had to bring the fifth bowler at some point, and once they brought in Shahbaz - who they subbed in instead of Digvesh Rathi due to LSG's batting not clicking - and that was when Rizvi broke free.

commentPreTextItems.html: 7:28pm The players make their way out. Rahane to open the batting alongside Allen, so no surprises there. Arshdeep has the new ball. Can he get the ball to shape into Allen early? Let's find out, although Rahane is on strike for now! Gokul Pradeep V: "Keeping Varun out is understandable, but how can you keep Narine out. KKR will miss him for sure !!" -- Neither has been dropped, for what it is worth. Varun injured himself in the last game, whereas Narine pulled up unwell for tonight's contest. Nitin Shetty: "Who's KKR's 5th bowler? Green, Powell " -- Muzarabani should come in when KKR bowl. Them having just three overseas players in their starting eleven gives them that option. Adarsh: "Rahane saying the pitch looks on the drier side (as a justification to bat first) and not including their two frontline spinners, is not a good sign for KKR fans." -- It does send out mixed signals. Guess we will have to wait and see if he and KKR got their pitch-reading right. 7:20pm Shreyas Iyer, because he led KKR to a title in 2024 and was still not retained, only to be bought for a heavy sum at the 2025 mega auction by PBKS, is currently front and centre of this rivalry. And the Iyer touch, as Sreshth Shah writes, may have something to do with both franchises' fortunes. Deepak Gupta : "Guys please stop talking about Arsenal. Still hurt from Southampton loss. Let me enjoy Cricket till tomorrow when we will play Champions League." -- Well, apparently the whole world likes talking about Arsenal and what they do (or don't do) but anyway, back to the cricket. Tonight will be the first time since this game in 2019 that KKR will be without both Narine and Varun. Karanbir Singh: "Saw the mention of Arsenal in the comments thread. Kings XI Punjab fan here since the inception of IPL. Arsenal fan since 2005 when I started following Football. Even though the past few years is as close to the top as I have seen these teams, I have seen too much to assume a happy ending. Hoping for the best but expecting the worst." -- As they say, the final step is often the hardest. Pitch Report: 64m and 65m square boundaries, with a 74m hit straight down the ground. Kevin Pietersen says he is not very wise when it comes to pitches. There is some live grass through the majority of the surface but there are also some bare patches, although most are on the front foot, he reckons. This has been a high-scoring venue in recent years but spinners will have to bowl very well to have a big impact tonight. Daren Ganga concludes by saying that bat will dominate ball. 7:10pm Well, lots to unpack from the toss. Narine and Varun both being absent is obviously a massive blow for KKR, and by the looks of it, they are happy to have just a solitary spinner in Anukul. Might have to keep an eye on the over-rate when they bowl. PBKS sticking to their tried and tested formula, with Arya likely to come in when they bat. Kolkata Knight Riders batting-first XI: Finn Allen, Ajinkya Rahane, Cameron Green, Angkrish Raghuvanshi, Rovman Powell, RInku Singh, Ramandeep Singh, Anukul Roy, Navdeep Saini, Vaibhav Arora, Kartik Tyagi KKR bench: Manish Pandey, Tejasvi Singh, Rahul Tripathi, Saurabh Dubey, Blessing Muzarabani Punjab Kings bowling-first XI: Prabhsimran Singh (wk), Cooper Connolly, Shreyas Iyer (capt), Nehal Wadhera, Shashank Singh, Marcus Stoinis, Marco Jansen, Xavier Bartlett, Vijaykumar Vyshak, Arshdeep Singh, Yuzvendra Chahal PBKS bench: Suryansh Shedge, Vishnu Vinod, Pravin Dubey, Priyansh Arya, Harpreet Brar 7pm It is time for the toss. And Danny Morrison belts out a welcome message for everyone. Rahane and Shreyas out there in the middle. Shreyas calls tails, but heads it is. KKR will bat first. Wow, that is a surprise. Rahane says the pitch looks on the drier side and that he wants to put up runs on the board. Preparation-wise, it has been fantastic, and he stresses the importance of winning the big moments. They are confident as a unit. Says they will think about Narine as an opener, with a smile, of course. Narine and Varun are both out - Varun due to an injury; Narine because he is unwell. Powell and Saini come in. Big news again. Shreyas says he would have bowled anyway, so he is happy with the decision Rahane has taken. Says his chemistry with Ponting blossomed from when they were at DC together. Says he is an inspiration and working beside him is a phenomenal feeling. Same team, says Shreyas. MC: "Capitalisation of Arsenal tells me cricket match not be the only sport Jugilee is following :p" -- Well, PBKS will hope for a better fortnight than the one Arsenal have just had... Shaurya Ghodkha: "I believe KKR is reuniting the Finn-Seifert duo at the top..!! Are we in for a run scoring thriller!!" -- That might be the unlikelier route, given Rahane has done fairly decently in the powerplay, as he has been quick to point out. Plus, if Rahane is in the side, it does make sense to have him up top when the field restrictions are on. 6:48pm Navdeep Saini has received his KKR cap. That could open the door for KKR playing another overseas batter. They could also have included Saini in place of one of the other Indian pacers (Arora or Tyagi). Either way, we should know KKR's combination in a few minutes from now at the toss. 6:45pm It has been a season of contrast already for the Kings and the Knight Riders, and that is not just restricted to results. All that and much more in Himanshu Agrawal's preview. VS: "Hope Cam green fires today. He is the vital cog in KKR line up.. " -- He has been bowling in the warm-ups but no news yet on if he will bowl in the game. ICYMI, this is all that has happened in the Cam Green will-he-wont-he bowl saga. Jugilee : "Punjab seem to be the team to beat. Their Arsenal is amazing and have the power to deliver at home and away , setting and chasing. " 6:40pm Sreshth Shah is our eyes and ears at the venue today and this is what he has to say: Navdeep Saini is marking his run-up, so are Vaibhav Arora and Kartik Tyagi. Haven't seen Blessing Muzarabani mark his just yet. Does that mean KKR will drop Muzarabani and make way for a Rachin Ravindra or Rovman Powell. 6:35pm First things first. There is a bit of rain forecast today and the bowlers' run-ups at both ends are under a cover each, although they are in the process of being peeled off. But more crucially, it is dry at the moment, with both sets of players going through their warm-up routines. Let's hope it stays that way and we get an uninterrupted game tonight. 6:30pm The last time the Kolkata Knight Riders lost their opening two games of an IPL campaign, the world looked…different. The Mumbai Indians had not won an IPL title yet. The Chennai Super Kings had only won two. MS Dhoni was India's all-format captain. Sachin Tendulkar was still playing international cricket. And Lionel Messi had not made a senior World Cup final. But the last time KKR went 0-2 at the start of the season, they also won the whole thing. It was 14 seasons and many moons ago, but it did happen, meaning that there is precedent. Although following through on that is another matter altogether. The Punjab Kings have never won the IPL, and that is quite well-documented. But history is not a wall. It is a door waiting to be broken down. And on the back of a runners-up finish in 2025, and two consecutive wins to begin this campaign, there is belief, not just among the PBKS camp, that this could indeed be their year. And so, here we are. At the Eden Gardens. For Match 12. KKR in historically uninhabited territory but in front of their fans, hoping their season can catch fire and be the rage, like it was all those years ago; the Punjab Kings, bullish about their chances, and sizing up another scalp to surge to the top of the table once again. This promises to be fun, so hop on to ESPNcricinfo's live coverage!

commentPreTextItems.html: 11:07pm And that will be all from us for tonight. A damp squib, quite literally, with the weather (and rain) winning. We will be back at it tomorrow from Guwahati, although fair warning - there could be some rain in the offing there as well. Anyway, until then, from all of us here at ESPNcricinfo, it is goodbye. Take care, folks! 10:58pm The two captains are having a chat with the two on-field umpires and the fourth umpire. And the captains shake hands now. The game has been called off. Ah, what a shame. This was shaping up to be a nice contest, and a match where both teams would have wanted those two points. But in the end, both get a point apiece and KKR, by virtue of that, are off the mark this season. PBKS, meanwhile, reclaim their place at the top of the table. 10:56pm The super sopper is out now. Proper race against time this. 11:14pm local time is when they need to start. 10:48pm The ground staff are doing their best to get this ground ready. Seems like the rain has passed fully. Now it is up to how quickly the ground can be dried. Water droplets are visible on the field, for what it is worth. Ponting now makes his way out and immediately brushes his palm, checking for how wet the grass is. 10:36pm Covers being peeled off now. We might actually have a game here. 10:29pm Okay now, hang on, folks. The rain seems to have eased up considerably and has almost stopped. Could we be in for a game from here? 11:14pm local time is the cut-off for the game to resume and be a five-overs-per-side match. The ground staff are out in full force too now, beginning their mop-up operation. Mehtab: "Hats-off to ground staff. they are the real heroes" 10:13pm Sreshth pings, saying that people in the vicinity of the ground have received a thunderstorm alert on their phones. The prospects of a resumption indeed bleak now. Raj: "RCB bowling is not looking great. they have not been tested yet in two games. I will go with MI, pBKS, DC and RR for top 4. " Shaurya: "Shashwat should we do something productive like predicting the top 4 in the meantime? Everybody should also give reasons too!!" Well, why not? If you are asking me, I might go with MI, RCB, DC and PBKS, because they seem to have the four best bowling attacks. Their batting is not shabby either. Mahi: "Update? it will be unfair for PBKS . After starting the match that good.Cut off time is 11:14 so rain must stop at 10:44" -- Might need rain to stop a little before that. This mop-up operation will take time. Sunil.G: "Looks like GT and CSK will be the only 2 teams without points after the washout tonight." shardul: ""Rain stops Play." "Rain stops. Play" One placement of a dot is all we need at this moment " -- Getting bored without the cricket, are we? Mohammad : "what is the scenario now on ground and how much chances of play ??" -- Steady rain, at the moment. The whole ground has been covered since the onset of rain but it might still take upwards of 30-40 minutes to get it ready for play. If we are to have a game tonight, the rain needs to stop soon. 9:52pm The rain has definitely gotten lighter than, say, an hour ago. But is is still steady and persistent rain. Gokul Pradeep V: "When do we start losing overs ?" -- We are already well into that territory. Soham: "In the NFL, lots of teams are moving from open stadiums to domes... while in Tests weather is part of the game, I don't get why T20s can't be played under a closed roof. Rain delays and cancellations shouldn't be a thing in the IPL" -- Think that might be a lot more difficult to execute in a sport like cricket because of the height of the roof etc. 9:38pm For those asking, it is still raining. Steady rain too, and you can see some puddles forming on the covers. Wind may have eased up a little, though. 9:18pm The rain seems to have gotten lighter but only on a relative scale. Still steady. 9:06pm Here is Sresth with an update from the press box: "The press box is shaking like an earthquake because of how strong the winds are." The game must resume at 11:14pm local time for five-overs-a-side. Game Must end by 11:40pm local time. Mohammed Ali: "According to the forecast, the rain will stop at 10 PM, so we'll have to wait until then for the game to start" -- May have to wait a bit more because this mop-up operating might take a bit of time... 8:57pm Still bucketing down at the Eden Gardens. Plenty of wind blowing too. Not sure if that is a good or a bad sign. Might be the former because wind tends to blow the rain over. Don't take it as gospel, though. We start losing overs from 9:10pm local time. 8:45pm Raining pretty steadily, and the covers are rooted to the playing field. Most of the uncovered stands wear a deserted look, which is another sign of how heavy the rain is. Sreshth chimes in with a not-so-promising update, saying that the rain is getting heavier. Strap in folks, we could be here a long time... Shan: "Shashwat, What time will be when we start loosing overs? " -- Still waiting for an official time. But with the rain that is falling (and has fallen), it is very likely we will have to settle for a shortened game. 8:36pm The rain seems to be at its heaviest yet. Not sure if that inspection at 8:45pm local time will be happening. S P: "How's the drainage at Eden and how fast can we get back to play if the rain stops...Shashwat?" -- Drainage should be good. Not sure of the exact time frame but since the whole ground has been covered (again), the mop-up operation might not take a lot of time. We have gotten word that there will be an inspection at 8:45pm local time. For now, the covers still firmly in place, with the rain still falling. Swaroop : "During last year's IPL this very same fixture at Eden Gardens was washed out due to rain but after PBKS had finished their innings and KKR had barely begun theirs. Hopefully lightining doesn't strike twice literally and figurative speaking!" Saurabh: "Any update? From people around, if it's going to be a washout, so that we can plan ahead!!" -- Only if anyone could predict the weather... 8:10pm Some good news, folks. The covers are being removed, one by one. Seems like the rain has stopped too. Well, scratch that. A few spots of rain still visible. But the covers are in the process of being peeled off. Looks like we were too early to the party. Covers coming back on. Ashwin: "Without a doubt Sameer Rizvi.Two POTM awards in the first two matches and both when the team was struggling in the powerplay" 8:03pm Shahrukh Khan is at the ground and when his face comes up on the giant screen, there is, unsurprisingly, a huge cheer. Covers still on, though, so no change on that front. In the meantime, do chip in with who you think has been the standout player of the season so far. Sowmya : "At park street (nearly 4 km away from Eden Gardens) it is pouring heavily and yours truly won't risk getting to the ground. Let us prepare mentally for a wash out !" -- Well, that is not the update we wanted to here. Fingers crossed the rain abates enough for play to resume. 7:48pm Uh-oh, the rain has gotten heavier and the covers are coming on. Ground staff scurrying to get the covers in place. The whole ground can be covered here, but because they have now gone off, they might not be able to come back on until the rain fully stops now. Full ground covered now, for what it is worth. As we wait for the rain to relent, the time might be ripe to indulge into this piece of Bartlett, and how he might end up becoming an X-Factor for PBKS, both with the ball and as a late-order basher.

title: Mukesh Kumar to Sai Sudharsan, FOUR

commentPreTextItems.html: 7:27pm Thanks Himanshu, hi all. Umpires walk out on a pleasant evening. 20 degrees celsius is what I heard. Axar has a pep talk, then Gill and Sudharsan walk out. Mukesh Kumar to bowl, slip in place. TanVerma: "I'm rooting for GT tonight as always but I have a feeling that this is going to be a nail-biter!" Sanyam Kamat: "Given form in last couple of matches, why not keep Nitish Rana as sub instead of Rizvi?" fair point 7.25pm Five minutes before the action, it's time for Ekanth to take over. Let him know whom you're supporting tonight. AJ: "DC has a long tail even with impact player!! GT should make big score to take advantage of this weakness" Paras: "Yeah - no rain to interrupt this game. In fact, the players are lucky they'll enjoy rather cool conditions for this time of the year in Delhi!" Gujarat Titans: 1 Shubman Gill (capt), 2 B Sai Sudharsan, 3 Jos Buttler (wk), 4 Washington Sundar, 5 Glenn Phillips, 6 Shahrukh Khan, 7 Rahul Tewatia, 8 Rashid Khan, 9 Kagiso Rabada, 10 Mohammed Siraj, 11 Ashok Sharma. Impact Subs: Prasidh, Holder, Suthar, Jayant and Rawat. Delhi Capitals: 1 KL Rahul (wk), 2 Pathum Nissanka, 3 Nitish Rana, 4 David Miller, 5 Tristan Stubbs, 6 Axar Patel (capt), 7 Vipraj Nigam, 8 Kuldeep Yadav, 9 Lungi Ngidi, 10 T Natarajan, 11 Mukesh Kumar. Impact Subs: Rizvi, Ashutosh, Nabi, Chameera and Nair. 7pm Time for the toss. DC opt to bowl. Axar Patel believes they have chased well, so he wants to continue with that. He thinks there could be moisture on the pitch, given rain has been around. DC are unchanged. Gill, meanwhile, says his neck is "much better". He would have batted first anyway. Gill hopes for a "good powerplay" with Sai Sudharsan. He wants just one person from the middle order to stick around till the end. Gill replaces Kumar Kushagra in GT's only change. Nilashish: "Sameer Rizvi's resurgence has halted the entry of a talent like Ashutosh Sharma in this line-up. Would love to see him in the team, with Rana sitting out." Pitch report: The first thing Daren Ganga points out is that the boundaries are uneven. Kevin Pietersen, meanwhile, sees some "patches" on the pitch. He feels "it's dry", and thinks it could be a "decent batting wicket". Karun: "I think Delhi should keep the same combination. Why change a team that works? But Nitish is on thin ice. Maybe Holder coming in for KG for GT?" --- Fitting Holder in has become a problem for GT, even as they paid him plenty. 6.55pm We're only five minutes away from the toss. What changes do you feel the two sides would make? Gill's return is certain, by the way. Himanshu Dhingr: "Sitting here in south-west Delhi, about 30-40 minutes drive away from the stadium, not a chance of rain." --- Thanks for helping us take a giant step in our coverage before play by proving that weather update from 10 kms away! Meanwhile, after that weather update, here's some cricket news. GT captain Shubman Gill is set to return after missing their previous game. But GT need their middle order to fire. That and more in our preview to help you get up to speed. 6.35pm After successive nights of rain interruption, cricket looks set to go ahead safely this evening. We're in Delhi today, where, although the weather had threatened to play spoilsport in the build-up to Delhi Capitals hosting Gujarat Titans, it looks all clear at the moment. The sun is quietly setting, and the clouds have thankfully cleared. This is Himanshu saying hello ahead of the contest, with Ekanth set to join me soon.

I would say so [that 210 is enough]." 9.18pm Just 58 runs off the last six overs for GT, despite having eight wickets in hand at that stage. commentTextItems.html: Have GT have won by one run?! This is an amazing finish. The umpire has given Kuldeep run-out, but hang on... this could be wide for height. Plenty is happening even as GT look confident. The players are lurking on the field, waiting for the final decision. Ohh, the ball passes below Miller's head, although he's "on his toes", as per the third umpire. More wait. More nerves. More drama. If it's not a wide, GT will win by one run. Indeed. The ball passes well below the head height. So it's not a wide. So it's confirmed: GT win by one run. This was the delivery: Prasidh bowled a slower one, and short in length. Miller looked to pull but missed. The ball shaped away just before landing into Buttler's gloves. Miller and Kuldeep ran, but the latter fell short despite diving as Buttler hit the stumps at his end

commentPostTextItems.html: A thriller in Delhi. Just imagine rain washing this game out - as was the threat. Instead, it was alive until the last ball even as supporters of both DC and GT were breathless. The first points for GT in the end, as they break DC's run of successive wins. Read Shashank Kishore's report to relive the action. But until next time, this is Himanshu signing off on behalf of Ekanth, Sudeep and Raghav. Goodnight and take care! Rashid Khan is the Player of the Match: "Quite happy [with] how things were coming. The win made it special. I had a break... tried to hit the right areas consistently. After long, I got such a wicket [like Rizvi's]. Yesterday, I had that in mind [going across to Axar]. If he hits me for a boundary, that's fine... we have been part of close games. It was just about making sure we focus on each and every delivery. Happy to be on the winning side in the end." Shubman Gill: "All three games we have played have gone in the last over. [When Miller didn't take the single, I thought] we have a chance to win! We decided if we bowl a good slower one, it will be difficult to hit for a boundary. Those five or six runs in fielding makes a difference. Every effort counts. 210 we always thought on this wicket we were 10-15 runs above par. We thought if we bowl well, we should be able to win. Now I just need to sleep and see how I wake up tomorrow!" Time for the presentations Jos Buttler: "Amazing. Good to get the win. Very lucky. We desperately needed the win. Been searching for the runs a little bit. Played for long enough to know it [the runs] will come back. It's a long tournament, but you need to start well. We desperately needed some points on the board. Rashid is outstanding. It's the kind of wicket that suits him... crucial wickets at crucial times." Shubha: "The cricketing universe saw the flip side of not taking an easy single" Axar Patel: "Both teams played very good cricket. These types of close games you can't point out anything. We could have been smarter in the chase. We lost wickets at crucial times. If not for that, we could have finished the chase off. Rahul kept the momentum on even after the powerplay, and despite wickets. He didn't let the run rate go down." Abhishek: "How many heartbreaks can one take??" --- As long as one can still take it?! 11.38pm Who would've thunk?! Miller was thrashing and pumping boundaries for fun, only for it to fall barely centimetres short. He turned a single down off the penultimate ball of the over, and left himself with two to get in one delivery. Eventually, he walked back with his head down; it was with that head down that he was sending the ball beyond the stands, but who knew he would walk back disappointed? One run, one centimetre. That's all what separated the sides.

commentPreTextItems.html: 7:28pm The umpires make their way out. Faf du Plessis rings the bell. Allen and Rahane to open. They have gone big on their batting and will want their opening partnership to fire. Shami to take the new ball and he has been sensational so far this season. What does tonight have in store? Slip in place for Rahane, let's play! Abbas: "first century of the IPL today.." -- Interesting... dev: "Why pick an out of form Green who cant contribute with ball instead of a Tim Siefert who is in very good form from the recent WC. " -- KKR have invested a lot in him, quite literally. And now that he is able to bowl, he does give KKR the option of having more middle-order muscle in Powell. But if his returns do not improve, alongside KKR's fortunes, they might have to have that tough conversation. 7:08pm Right. KKR have given us another talking point at the toss. No Muzarabani is a huge call, given how much their bowling has struggled. They have instead doubled-down on their batting, and that will be put to the test now that they will be setting a score and defending it. LSG's side is along expected lines. Badoni will likely come in when LSG bat, with Arora likely to be KKR's Impact Player. Lucknow Super Giants bowling-first XI: Mitchell Marsh, Aiden Markram, Rishabh Pant (capt & wk), Nicholas Pooran, Abdul Samad, Mukul Choudhary, M Siddharth, Avesh Khan, Mohammed Shami, Digvesh Rathi, Prince Yadav LSG bench: Ayush Badoni, Matthew Breetzke, Shahbaz Ahmad, Mayank Yadav, Himmat Singh Kolkata Knight Riders batting-first XI: Finn Allen, Ajinkya Rahane (capt), Cameron Green, Angkrish Raghuvanshi, Rovman Powell, Rinku Singh, Ramandeep Singh, Sunil Narine, Anukul Roy, Navdeep Saini, Kartik Tyagi KKR bench: Manish Pandey, Vaibhav Arora, Tejasvi Singh, Rahul Tripathi, Tim Seifert 7pm It is time for the toss. Rahane and Pant out in the middle, and both are all smiles. Rahane will give the coin a spin. Pant calls tails, and tails it is. LSG will bowl first. Pant says they want to put the opposition in and that they trust their bowlers enough to do a job up front. Wins definitely add to the atmosphere, remarks Pant. Same team, says Pant. He adds that their batting unit is a little top-heavy but that they also trust them to get through, saying that is what they are here for. Rahane says he would have bowled first too. Just one change - Narine comes in for Blessing. Varun still recovering, he adds. Green will bowl when he gets allowed to bowl, and that might give them a better combination, he says. As a batting unit, they want to just watch the ball, rather than focusing on other stuff and putting themselves under pressure. 6:55pm KKR may have had a tough call to make, with regards to their overseas players, had Green been unable to bowl. But early signs are that he will be rolling his arm over, meaning that if Narine returns, Powell will have to make way. LSG's side is much more settled, with the only toss-up perhaps between Mohsin Khan and Avesh Khan. Toss in 5. 6:50pm KKR's bowling wore a depleted look even before the tournament began. They were then hit with the absences of Sunil Narine and Varun Chakravarthy against the Punjab Kings. Varun's participation remains doubtful, but Narine is slated to return. Oh, and their big-money signing aka Cameron Green, is also reportedly ready to bowl. Pitch Report: The same pitch as the other day (KKR-PBKS) is going to be used. Lot of dry patches from one end, and Faf du Plessis thinks the spinners might operate primarily from there. When there is a bit of rain around, fielding first could be the way to go, despite the pitch looking slightly dry. New ball might swing, reckons Deep Dasgupta, although he still expects it to be a high-scoring game. Chuvi : "LSG seem a well oiled unit ! They have their bases covered after the early lapses ! Where Rishabh Pant bats remains to be seen !" -- He batted at three the other day and on a high-drama afternoon, it gave LSG the happy ending they wanted. 6:40pm Both teams (and their fans) might have an eye on the weather, but KKR will also be wanting to get their campaign going - something they have failed to do so far. All that and much more in Ashish Pant's match preview. Sowmya : "LSG hold the edge but a resurgence from KKR can't be ruled out.. looks to be a cracking contest, at least on paper " 6:32pm Here is the update all of you have been waiting to hear. This is what Sreshth (who is at the ground), has to say: cloudy conditions. Last rained around noon and although there's some chances of rain today, there's more optimism for a full game. 6:30pm Let's do this again then, shall we? On Monday, there was a lot to talk about at the Eden Gardens. But only because everyone had so much time on their hands with all the rain that fell. The Kolkata Knight Riders' decision to bat first, despite the pitch being under covers and the seemingly imminent downpour, dominated much of that discourse, but the night ended with KKR finally getting on the board. The Lucknow Super Giants got off the mark in their previous game too, although the circumstances could not have been more different. Under the blazing Hyderabad sun, they ran rampant with the new ball before their skipper, batting at three, played an innings of note. And now that they have opened their kitty, they will want to cash in further, especially in a city their owners call home in another sport, and at a time when KKR still rummage for answers. And so, here we are. Back at the Eden Gardens. Where those in attendance might have already begun murmuring and muttering the prayers of their choice, longing for a full game, with KKR and LSG indulging in a similarly hopeful hum themselves, itching to hit the right notes and click into rhythm as the points table takes shape. Plenty to look forward (perhaps including but not restricted to rain-watch), so tag along to ESPNcricinfo's live coverage!

commentPostTextItems.html: 9:15pm A strange innings. KKR began sluggishly before Rahane and Raghuvanshi found their range towards the end of the powerplay. Then there was a slow-down through the middle and Green, in particular, looked woefully out of sorts. He found some rhythm towards the end, and with Powell teeing off, KKR were able to get past 180. LSG will be decently happy with their effort. At one point, they would have felt a bigger chase was on the cards. Then, they were in with a chance of keeping KKR down to under 170. Avesh and Prince were expensive but Shami was tidy, as were the spinners. This does not seem like a very daunting chase, especially with LSG's firepower, but they will need to bat well to get these. Join us in a bit for the chase! Powell: (On the pitch) It is not a classic KKR wicket. Not a 220-250 wicket. 180-190 is a good score once we control the powerplay. (Chat with Green) Just a case of holding your shape a little bit longer - that is what we talked about. (On attacking left-arm spin) It is something I work on. Not try to go and push around the spinners and try to be a bit more aggressive against spin. Deepak Gupta: "Just a curiosity - Can you replace an overseas player with an overseas player as Impact Sub?" -- If you had four overseas players in your starting eleven, you cannot.

commentPostTextItems.html: 11:46pm And...breathe. A bona-fide IPL classic, headlined by a youngster the IPL is designed to throw up into the imagination. LSG go back-to-back with their wins; KKR remain without one, and this tournament is now shaping up rather nicely. We hope you enjoyed our coverage. More post-match stuff will come your way, so stay tuned to ESPNcricinfo. Until next time, from all of us here, it is goodbye! Mukul Choudhary, Player of the Match: (On his journey) Even before my dad got married, it was his dream that his son would play cricket. Financial condition was not very good at the start. Began playing at 12-13 years. There were not a lot of academies (in Jhunjhunu) and then I moved to Jaipur. I saw how much T20 cricket is growing, so I moved to Gurgaon and stayed there for 3-4 months. (On when he or his father knew he would make it) My dad tells me there was an U-19 match against UP. It was a low-scoring match but I scored runs and that is when he knew I would make it big. Second match (under lights). Pressure is always there. But God has given us this opportunity, and I try to do what I can do. I see it as an opportunity, rather than taking pressure. My plan was to play till the end, and I believe in myself that much that I knew if I batted till the end, I could make the team win. (On his favourite six) The first six. I had not hit a six before today, so that was special. (On what he was feeling when 7 were needed off 2) I knew one ball would be in my area and I knew I needed to hit just one six. (On his preparation and confidence about power-hitting) I have always been hitting, since I have been young. If it is in my area, I smash it. Rishabh Pant, LSG captain: (On Mukul) I do not have words to describe but what a fantastic effort. One thing I made sure is that personally, that trust and when you believe in someone, a player can do wonders. The character, with each and every match like this, it shows something is building. We don't want to talk much about it but something is cooking inside. (On Badoni) He is now a senior pro in our team. That is the role we have given him. In a situation like him, when we talk about Badoni, these are the kind (of contributions) you want to see from Badoni. (On Shami) He is not getting any young. But the experience he brings to the side is invaluable. Having someone like him is amazing. Whole bowling unit is doing an amazing job. Ajinkya Rahane, KKR captain: Tough one to take. Really proud of the boys, the way we played. Mukul's knock was defining. The way he played his shots…in games like this, you do not want to pinpoint too many things. Execution here and there can happen, but credit to Mukul and that partnership. Those (slower balls into the pitch) deliveries did work. They (LSG) had nothing to lose. It was about swinging (every ball). There were brilliant shots. The way he (Mukul) batted was amazing. Thought our bowlers did their job. When you lose a game, you think about how you could have done better. 180-185 was a very good total on this wicket. In the end, I thought, let's give credit to the (LSG) batters and the way they batted. (On bringing the field up for the first ball of the 20th) We wanted to keep him on strike, but we had to keep five inside. It is tough for the bowlers (bowling the last over with five up). Here is Sampath with a stat: Only batter before Mukul Choudhary to score 50+ runs in death overs (52 off 21) in a successful IPL chase was Kieron Pollard against SRH in 2013. Pollard scored 57 off 17 balls (from being 9 off 10 to 64 off 27) at the death when MI needed 62 off 24. 11:22pm Incredible. Just incredible. It is one of the most overused words. In sport. In the IPL. In almost all walks of life. But you can search through and through, and you might not find a better word to describe all that transpired at the Eden Gardens. KKR had it. They had it right in the centre of their palms. But then, came the Mukul Choudhary storm. With wrists of steel, with fire in his belly and ultimately, with ice in his veins. And this will now be an evening that he will remember and rejoice forever. KKR, of course, will be at the other end of that emotional spectrum. They utilized the conditions well and made LSG toil for every run. But just when it mattered, they were trumped by someone who handled the big moments better. A few more runs may have been handy but tonight is not about what KKR did not do right. Rather, it is about what Mukul did right, and what he kept doing right, even when put into a cauldron of pressure. Santosh : "Lesson: "Never Turn off the TV when Avesh Khan is batting" "

commentPreTextItems.html: 3:29pm Head and Abhishek are out. Arshdeep has the ball. Sun is still out. One slip in. Qursheed: "Have bowlers figured out how to bowl to Abhishek? There is no fear of him, they feel like they can get him out even if he hit them couple of boundaries!" Pacers seem to be bowling into his body more now. Offspinners troubled him during the World Cup but PBKS don't have one. Thanks Abhijato, hello all. In the last five T20 games at New Chandigarh, there were two 210-plus first-innings scores, two in the 150-160 range and one 101. Say hello to Ekanth! He's here to lead you through the action for the first ten overs of the SRH innings. 3.15pm Wondering who Praful Hinge, a potential debutant today, is? Here's our resident expert on the matter, Shashwat Kumar: Hinge, who made his FC debut for Vidarbha in 2024, was a regular fixture earlier in the season, picking up 16 wickets across six matches (11 innings). His T20 breakthrough, though, came at the inaugural edition of the Vidarbha Pro T20 League last year, when he was a vital contributor to Neco Master Blasters' title charge. Hinge can be a nippy pacer and could be a handful with his lanky frame. He has openly talked about Cummins being his idol and wanting to share the dressing room with him. Time spent with Umesh Yadav has also inspired him, and it will not be a surprise if he tries cranking it up later in the day. 3.10pm Well well. Biggest news from the toss seems to be, err, that Kishan's lost the coin flip again. Plenty of consternation in the feedback section! zain: "4 straight losses in toss for Ishaan Kishan and SRH" Krishna Sumanth: "why is it that the team I support always loses the toss?" Soumith Potturi: "Ishan has lost 4/4 tosses" More pertinently, perhaps, Luke: "Surprising that SRH has opted for just 3 overseas players." Indeed! Rock: "What Ishan Kishan said about team combination and the team list you shared do not match! Praful Hinge missing in playing XI!" - He's in the Impact Players list. We might see him slot in for their bowling defense. 3pm The captains head out to the middle. We are ready for the toss. Shreyas Iyer flips the coin. Heads is the call, but it lands tails. Shreyas - and PBKS - decide to bowl first. "It's a day game. Want to get a knack of how the wicket plays. Other than that, we've been thriving on [assessing conditions]. You can't control nature - we have to go with the flow," Shreyas says. "Just back each other, all the youngsters in the team. Better to live in their own nature and express themselves... Priyansh comes in for Nehal [Wadhera]." "We would have loved to bowl first. Wicket's looked pretty hard to me," Ishan Kishan says. "Pat is a tremendous bowler. But still, we've got a young bowler in the team. We'll execute the plans, which is the important thing. Salim comes in place of Livingstone, and Praful Hinge - on his debut game - in place of Unadkat." He's also in charge of the Live Report, in case you want to dig into more detailed nuggets that come our way from this match today. "The 1st game and even the statistics don't suggest that there will be plenty of runs on offer here," Huzefa chimes in. "My guess is 170 plays 170." Ah well, to think of days when 170 on the board used to be plenty! Meanwhile, Aseem has a more holistic view on proceedings: "Here is my *benched 12* from the IPL so far. Team lost Venkatesh Iyer yesterday.1 Mitchell Owen 2 Quinton de Kock 3 Jacob Bethell 4 Karun Nair 5 Musheer Khan 6 Manish Pandey 7 Ashutosh Sharma 8 Will Jacks/ Azmatullah Omarzai 9 Sai Kishore 10 Auqib Nabi 11 Suyash Sharma 12 Mayank Yadav" - World-beating team, I suspect. Ajit Lloyd: "2:00 am at Seattle, and ready for a run feast. A very nervy SRH supporter, but very promising two spinners in Harsh and Shivang. Any sign of Pat? " - No Pat around, I'm afraid, Ajit. But like you say, plenty of home-grown talent to plug the gaps. 2.30pm You can't help but marvel at the prospect of what lays ahead of us today: Travis Head and Abhishek Sharma vs Prabhsimran Singh and Priyansh Arya. commentPostTextItems.html: 5.20pm Just 50 runs from those last five overs. In fact, after scoring 100-plus in the powerplay, SRH have kind of fallen away in the back two-thirds of this innings. The PBKS bowlers were thrashed all around the park, when Travis Head and Abhishek Sharma were making merry. After that, though, Shashank took both of them out in what was almost a miracle dibbly-dobbly spell. His two-for changed the complexion of the innings. SRH mixed fuller deliveries with slower ones to stifle the finishers, especially an off-colour Klaasen. Still, it looks like a slow-ish pitch, and SRH might have enough on the board... Come back in ten minutes to join Ekanth, and see how the PBKS chase plays out! Here's Shashank: "Whenever I bowl in the nets, I plan for these situations... Then only I will get to bowl. I have planned my lines and lengths long before the IPL. Abhishek is a world-class batsman, and getting him thrice makes me happy. I love these situations, because I can use my limitations with bowling... I can do some good for the team. [On the total] To be honest, the wicket is slightly on the slower side. We've had good practice sessions here, so we knew it would be like that. If we bat to our strengths, this will be chaseable." DaWolf: "Innings of two halves. 105/0 from the powerplay, 114/6 from the remaining 14 overs. "

commentPostTextItems.html: 7.30pm And finally, we're done with what has been a high-scoring, topsy-turvy contest! Shreyas Iyer led from the front today, and PBKS are looking like early favourites this season. It's too early to tell, but their openers and diverse bowling attack might spearhead a formidable campaign. It's too soon to tell, of course, just as it is with the struggling SRH, who need to get a better sense of how to approach their bowling plans. For now, there's plenty of food for thought for both teams - and another contest for us to zoom towards. Go and follow along CSK vs DC. From Sudeep, Ranjith, Ekanth and I at ESPNcricinfo, bye-bye for now! And now the post-match presentation. Shreyas Iyer - PBKS captain, and Player of the Match! He speaks now: "Firstly, we've got a phenomenal start. When you're chasing 220, you need that start. Pleasing to the eye, proper cricketing shots. Steadied the rhythm at the start. Not easy, but maintaining that momentum - I needed to give myself time. Once I gauged the pace of the pitch... [After SRH's start] All of us came together, and Shashank approached me, give me an over. Ricky came and asked me, what's your thought? I said I'll go with Shashank - I need someone to take the pace off. He lived up to his expectations, he lived up to what he said, kudos to him... At the end of the day, we all know we've got the skills. We need a strong mindset when we go for such chases. Openers have been flowing throughout, they don't need to curb their instincts. Others, who set their platforms from ball one, it's easy for us to rotate strike and go according to run rate. Overall, we've been magnificent with our work ethic. All players worked their... bodies off [he had a different word in mind initially, he laughs!]. Work: they're delivering on the field. I keep reiterating every now and then, you have to be in the present. Ricky [Ponting] also takes a lot of importance in this aspect. Even last year, we came so close to winning the trophy. This year, we want to lift it. It will take a lot of effort to envision that." Brad Haddin, assistant coaching for PBKS, has the mic now: "I'm glad I'm not a bowler in the first six overs... The one thing we did really well after those first six was we stayed calm, got the game back. The middle overs... That's where it was won. Ricky spoke to the players: they know their plans, and just stay calm. Things might be bubbling up, but you know your plans. If you get a chance, you pounce on it, like they did here. It's interesting to talk to batters about rotating strike - they say we don't need to that anymore, we just put it in the second tier. They need to keep their courage and be brave in the first six covers, we're very clear about our bowlers getting wickets... We've seen that in the game against Kolkata, against Finn and Green. The mindset is to get wickets, not be defensive." Ishan Kishan, the losing captain, wears a disappointed look: "We could have ended with a total of 250, the way we started... At the same time, they batted well in the beginning. At the same time, we were not so good with the execution - in T20 cricket, the most important thing is the execution of your good balls. 190 is a par score here, we could have had 240 here. But 220 was a great total. We had six or seven bowlers. It showed in their batting that it was easier scoring runs for them. I think in today's age, you don't have to plan much - you just do ahead of the game. You know which batter hits where. When you don't execute balls, you have nothing - you just end up giving 10-20 runs. [On their 200-plus totals not being safe] No, to be honest, we don't think so much. It's simple cricket. Your bowlers have a total, you try to defend. If you don't bowl in the right areas, you don't stop runs in the middle." 7.15pm Shreyas Iyer has put up his hand, and how. Just like SRH struggled after their boshing openers got out, PBKS too lose their half-centurions in quick succession. But Iyer ensured that a slowdown in the chase never happened. He's taken them over the line in a high-scoring contest, and his team have laid down the marker for how to chase 200-plus totals in this IPL. SRH's bowling was quite poor, in all fairness, offering up slot balls even as they tried to land the yorkers. Great chase, and plenty of lessons for both teams, you'd imagine!

commentPreTextItems.html: 7:27pm Plenty of noise as the players take the field. Gaikwad and Samson to open. Neither has hit their straps so far. Nabi, who was superb throughout the domestic season, will take the new ball on IPL debut. Samson on strike. Slip in place. This could be a blockbuster opening exchange. Let's play! Shyam : "Why are they not playing spencer johnson? Just a desperate CSK fan asking." -- Because he is yet to join the squad. He is expected to join up in a week or so. Gokul Pradeep V: "When an experienced player like Matt Henry gets hit all over the park, not sure what Gurjapneet can bring to the table. It goes on to show the fearless batting approach by the new age batters. Let's see if CSK can turn their fortune around with these forces changes !!" -- As Shashank showed earlier in the day, he will at least bring a tinge of the unknown. Joe: "Noor has been poor for a while now and Akeal has been in better recent form and can bat, too. Why not give him a go?" -- Noor's form is a concern and Akeal may still play. But CSK look at Noor as a point-of-difference bowler through the middle, even if he is a little inconsistent. Not sure three matches will have changed that. Vasumathy : "Good old saying : people will forget all the good you did , they will latch on to that 1 mistake you did forever. Likewise , David Miller was smacking 4s " -- That is how sport works. It is eventually (unfairly or not) judged on how much, how often and what can teams/players win. For example, no one will praise Arsenal for their 2025-26 season and their form prior to April if they fail to win the league. As tough as it sounds, that is exactly how it rolls, and from a finisher's POV in white-ball cricket, that only gets amplified further. Mohd Irshad : "This is looking much better CSK, atleast on paper. Bring in akeal as well." Abhimanyu Selot: "Beyond happy to see Nabi get the debut. Hope him and Harsh Dubey who bowled very well for SRH earlier today get the debut for India in tests against Afghanistan " 7:15pm So, the big news is that Brevis is back for CSK. They have still gone in with three overseas players in their eleven, meaning one of Henry or Hosein could feature later. If there is another collapse, Short and Kartik might be the fail-safe options. DC, since they are bowling first, will likely bring in Ashutosh later in the evening. But with Nitish Rana out, everyone, including Rizvi and Axar, might have to move up a spot. Chennai Super Kings batting-first XI: Sanju Samson (wk), Ruturaj Gaikwad (capt), Ayush Mhatre, Sarfaraz Khan, Dewald Brevis, Shivam Dube, Jamie Overton, Noor Ahmad, Anshul Kamboj, Khaleel Ahmed, Gurjapneet Singh CSK bench: Matthew Short, Akeal Hosein, Kartik Sharma, Prashant Veer, Matt Henry Delhi Capitals bowling-first XI: KL Rahul (wk), Pathum Nissanka, Sameer Rizvi, Axar Patel (capt), Tristan Stubbs, David Miller, Auqib Nabi, Lungi Ngidi, Kuldeep Yadav, T Natarajan, Mukesh Kumar DC bench: Vipraj Nigam, Ashutosh Sharma, Karun Nair, Dushmantha Chameera, Nitish Rana 7pm It is time for the toss. Axar and Gaikwad out there in the middle. Gaikwad has the coin. Axar to call. Axar calls tails, and tails it is. DC will bowl first. Axar says the wicket looks good and they are backing themselves to chase a score. Dressing room atmosphere is very chill and he says they are talking about controlling things they can control. Hopefully they can do well tonight, he adds. Two changes, says Axar. Nabi plays, along with Ashutosh, says Axar Nitish and Vipraj go out. Ashutosh is in the Impact Player list and not in the starting eleven. Gaikwad says he would have bowled first too on this red-soil pitch. But he adds that the strip is on the drier side, so they were a little 50-50 on the decision. Batting has been doing well, he mentions, and says there have been few moments that they should have been catching on. Good to have Brevis back, says Gaikwad. Gurjapneet is in the side too, replacing Henry. MS is watching from the hotel but he hopes he will play really soon. Sunitha : "Significant dew in other grounds around chepauk all week. So it won't be a tough decision for the skipper winning the toss ! " 6:45pm Dewald Brevis has not featured for CSK this season but signs are that he will be fit enough to play tonight. The million-dollar question, though, is can he breathe new life into the five-time champions? Shubha: "The biggest worry for CSK fans thus far has been the fact that their shoulders dropped very quickly " -- Well, they have been in some pretty dire situations already, so can't really blame them. But yes, their fans will want to see more of a fight tonight, at the very least. 6:35pm CSK are pretty much looking for a reset, and they will want their star openers to click into gear to make that a tangible possibility. Alagappan Muthu sets the scene in his match preview. 6:30pm After 39.4 overs on Wednesday, the Delhi Capitals were in control, and on the verge of extending their perfect start. David Miller was doing his thing, winning his side a game they may have felt had slipped away. But then, something happened. Or rather, did not happen. A refusal to take a single off the penultimate ball meant Miller's great finishing act ultimately wasn't. The Chennai Super Kings, in contrast, have not even come close to winning this season. Not once. The Rajasthan Royals blitzed past them in Guwahati. The Punjab Kings coasted to a 200-plus chase, and the Royal Challengers Bengaluru put up a mountain of runs, the weight of which was too much to bear for CSK. But sport often has a way. Funny, quirky, strange - call it whatever you want - and it gives teams, players, and fans hope. That a different day will yield a different outcome, and lend to a vastly different mood. And it is with that hope that CSK return to Chepauk. Once a fortress but in the recent past, increasingly and incredibly fallible. There may still be light at the end of the tunnel for CSK because, well, there is a sense that things may not get any worse. But it could yet be another incoming train, especially as the Capitals, hurt and wounded themselves, yearn for a riposte to get back on track, and to quell fears of derailment. Plenty to tuck into, so sit back, relax and enjoy ESPNcricinfo's live coverage!

commentPostTextItems.html: 9:13pm A classy innings by CSK's high-profile off-season purchase. And good for CSK that Samson did because Gaikwad laboured through the powerplay, only to perish for 15 off 18. Samson, though, kept at it and Mhatre, until the death overs, proved to be an able ally, mustering his second fifty of the season in the process. Dube, who walked in after Mhatre had been retired out, did his bit at the end too. DC will not be overjoyed with this bowling display, but they will feel they have kept CSK down to a chaseable score. With the platform the hosts had, they could have easily gone past 220. That they did not was down to DC's defensive execution at the death. DC have firepower too and having seen PBKS chase down a 200-plus score already this season at Chepauk, they might just be fancying their chances. Join us in a bit for the chase! Samson: Feels great. Thanks to you (Ravi Shastri), you seem to be my lucky person to meet - please come for every game, sir (smiles). To be honest, whatever form you are in, the matches you have won for your country, a couple of failures put doubts in your mind. Wanted to stick to the basics, was thinking about whether I should go harder. Stuck to (what I do), and thankfully it came off. (On the pitch) To start off, it was holding. When Axar bowled in the powerplay, it held. But it got a great wicket to bat on (as the innings progressed). Had a great partnership with Ayush - amazing to bat with him. We wanted to put up as much of a big score on the board. We had a long batting order, so was about picking your bowlers and contributing. A challenging score. If we have a good powerplay, it will be very good.
