commentTextItems.html: taken at short third, and that is a fitting end to this contest! CSK are on the board at the fourth time of asking and they have won at Chepauk for the first time in seven attempts! Pushed across the batter outside off. Ngidi wafts at it and the ball flies off the outside edge. Gobbled up neatly by Gurjapneet, and cue the celebrations now. More relief than anything, given the history of this franchise, and this has comfortably been their best performance this season!

commentPostTextItems.html: 11:51pm That will be all from us for tonight. We will be back with more IPL action tomorrow, with another double-header on the cards. Until then, from all of us here at ESPNcricinfo, it is goodbye! Sanju Samson, Player of the Match: Really means a lot. The trust they (CSK franchise) showed in me, it was a very responsible feeling that I need to put in a show and say we are still in the tournament. Not easy to start off at a different franchise but it never felt like it. It was like coming to a second home. We just had a meeting of 50 seconds today (despite three losses) - that connects with the kind of person I am (smiles). I failed a lot. Failing a lot tells you how to come back. Mentally, you think if you need to go hard or change the game-plan. You need to bring your body and mind to basics. Basics are to get in a mentally different zone. We need to come back to timing the ball, and watching it come out nicely from the bowler's hand. Very happy things have come (out) nicely today. Very important to have a great partnership. It never looked like he (Mhatre) was coming out of U-19 - he was so calculative. Shows the character he has. (On his hundred celebration) That was for Fleming. I know how hard it can get, leading a franchise for five years. Just wanted to dedicate this (innings) to Fleming. Ruturaj Gaikwad, CSK captain: Feels good to finally get the win. Great performance. Always felt that coming here, we had been batting well. To post 200-210, when wicket is on slower side, we were showing good signs. One of those knocks where Sanju took to the opposition, played a magnificent knock. Ayush also. But today was about the bowling. Taking wickets, bowling aggressive lengths. We do not have that X-Factor in the bowling, but we have been discussing on how to be more effective and more proactive. In the last few games, we were almost there. Some big overs cost us. Bowling wise, we were on the mark (tonight). We were set back in the powerplay but we came back after it. Chennai fans are always behind us - have been receiving so many messages, good wishes. Wherever we go, they are backing us. That is what this side of the country is - wonderful people and loving the franchise. Axar Patel, DC captain: We started well but after the powerplay, we lost quick wickets and that broke the momentum. The fielding was the difference in the match. Wickets falling in clusters made it tough to regain momentum. Batters did a decent job but overall, our fielding was a let-down. (On the score) Want to credit the bowlers, to keep them to that score, despite them having set batters on a good wicket. A couple of dropped catches, had we taken them, it might have been different. Pitch did not change. It was a little more difficult for them (with the dew in the second innings) but they bowled pretty well. Jamie Overton: Very happy. Good to finally get a win in front of our home crowd. Couple of games have not quite gone my way. Feeling good since December in the Big Bash. Have been bowling good gas and have been trying to keep it going. (On his plan today) Just trying to hit the top of the stumps. Bit tacky (pitch), and some felt like it slipped through, some jumped up. Tried to reduce their cross-batted shots. (On his injury) It is fine. Just a bit of cramp. 11:31pm A commanding win in the end, fashioned by a stellar spell by Overton, who picked up his best IPL figures, and also notched up the best figures so far this season. His ability to hit hard lengths at pace caused DC loads of problems, and that ploy was replicated by Gurjapneet on debut too. CSK also caught well and that, plus the other bowlers doing their bit, meant that they never ceded control of the game after the powerplay. DC will be disappointed with their batting effort. There were no demons in the pitch and DC got off to a brisk start themselves, only to lose momentum through the middle. There were starts throughout but apart from Stubbs, none of the batters batted long enough to mount a sustained challenge.

commentPreTextItems.html: 7:27pm The players make their way out. Sooryavanshi has his orange cap on but he is sitting in the dugout for now. A fairly healthy crowd in already, and they are indulging in a lot of flag-waving. They will want Travishek to tee off too. Archer to take the new ball. Expect fireworks early, one way or the other. Abhishek on strike. Slip in place, let's play! Praveen: "Liam is not in the lineup, so will they get him as a bowler? That's impossible!" -- In case there is a batting collapse, SRH's hand may be forced. Prashant: "Which position Lhuan-dre Pretorius is likely to bat at?" -- Most likely in the middle order. Either four or five, based on the game situation and potential match-ups. Don't think RR should mess with their current top three the way they are going. Suman: "Ishan mentioned 2 changes. Assuming Liam wouldn't be needed after the 1st innings(fingers crossed). Can we expect to see Mavi or Sakib? Would be excited to see either of them." -- After last game, Kishan's toss comments can be taken with a pinch of salt. But after that gaffe, expect SRH to substitute Sakib in, at least based on what Kishan said. He can crank it up too, and that sort of pace could prove to be a point of difference. Rachit Agrawal: "So SRH is saying that Salil and Aniket are both better than Livingstone?" -- Looks like it. Salil Arora, for what it is worth, has been marked as the keeper for tonight too. Afroze: "Don't know why teams are leaving their important players like Vaibhav, as impact subs, doesnt it leave them restricted in case there arises a need to use someone else like RCB had to the other day? Any theories?" -- Understand the rationale if your team is fielding first because there are not many situations (if any) where a team will need to make a bowling change mid-way. When batting, always makes sense to have your best bowlers in the starting eleven, just in case a batting collapse prompts a change in tack. 7:08pm SRH have shuffled their bowling pack yet again. Out go the experienced pair of Harshal and Unadkat. Hinge is in the starting eleven and will make his debut. He is a right-arm pacer from Vidarbha, who can bowl hard lengths and relishes the task of bowling the hard overs too. Sakib is the other player Kishan mentioned would be playing tonight, but he is currently a part of the Impact Players list. RR have made a couple of changes too. Deshpande for Brijesh is along expected lines. Hetmyer resting (in Parag's words) is the bigger tweak. Pretorius, though, is a highly talented left-handed batter, who has also played for South Africa. Rajasthan Royals bowling-first XI: Yashasvi Jaiswal, Dhruv Jurel (wk), Riyan Parag (capt), Lhuan-dre Pretorius, Donovan Ferreira, Ravindra Jadeja, Jofra Archer, Nandre Burger, Sandeep Sharma, Ravi Bishnoi, Tushar Deshpande RR bench: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Shimron Hetmyer, Ravi Singh, Shubham Dubey, Brijesh Sharma Sunrisers Hyderabad batting-first XI: Abhishek Sharma, Travis Head, Ishan Kishan (capt & wk), Heinrich Klaasen, Salil Arora, Aniket Verma, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Harsh Dubey, Shivang Kumar, Eshan Malinga, Praful Hinge SRH bench: R Smaran, Sakib Hussain, Liam Livingstone, Shivam Mavi, Harshal Patel 7pm It is time for the toss. Kishan and Parag out there in the middle. Kishan has the coin and he gives it a spin. Parag calls tails, and he calls correctly. RR will field first. Parag says it is a fresh wicket and that they want to make the most of whatever help there could be. Couple of changes, he says, with Hetmyer resting. Pretorius comes in for him. Deshpande is back too, replacing Brijesh. Kishan says there are two changes, with Hinge and one other player coming in. Harshal and Unadkat miss out. Says he has been leading teams since his U-19 days, and adds that they always want to do more for the team. It makes a difference when you are the captain and it did help me, he says. VaibhavR: "Not that the current batting order is too shabby but I would like to see Smaran in the SRH batting lineup. He has been plundering some runs in the domestic tournaments across the last two seasons! " -- Wouldn't mind seeing him at all. Nothing more fascinating than seeing how a proven domestic performer does on the IPL stage. Although don't think SRH will be making so many wholesale changes. Sanket: "Both the teams are heavily reliant on the top order, so the new ball becomes really really crucial. RR has a far better bowling unit compared to SRH, Both Archer and Burger has been sensational with the new ball. Wickets upfront mean that you can contain the opposition teams but SRH probably has the worst bowling line up in this competition. Can they play Ansari here, also need to add Liam in that batting line up so that you can score 10-20 above par and help the bowling to have that cushion. " Shahed: "When is SRH captain marvel, Pat Cummins, expected back?" -- Prior to the tournament, he said that if all his rehab went according to plan, he would play the back half. Might still be a week, at least, before he is in contention, going by that timeline. Sai Krishna: "A debutant to take Vaibhav's wicket today. Mark these words. " -- Well, SRH were supposed to hand out a debut to Vidarbha pacer Praful Hinge in their previous game, until they made a U-turn and went to Unadkat instead. So, if that debut is indeed handed out, we can probably come back to this comment in a few hours from now! 6:55pm In IPL 2025, Ravi Bishnoi was bowling far too full, lost his wicket-taking ability, his place in the India T20I team, and his IPL franchise. Now, he is fixing his problems, and is second on the leading wicket-takers list. Read more about his upturn in form here. Pitch Report: Pitch number 3 in play today. 77m hit down the ground, 63m and 67m square boundaries. Faf du Plessis says it looks like an absolute belter. Nice and hard, and he says the powerplay, with the openers on both sides, could be huge. There could be dew in the evening and the captain winning the toss might look to bowl first. Phil: "If you could select an ideal opening pair from among these four openers, which two would you choose? I think I'd take Sooryavanshi and Head" -- Putting me right on the spot. On current form in this season of the IPL, might have to side with Abhishek and Sooryavanshi. In terms of pedigree, might have to go with the current SRH pair. VS: "Expecting a six galore from the openers. That kid Sooryavanshi has some power." Chuvi: "In many ways, SRH's batting woes have been swept under the carpet by Abhishek Sharma " -- SRH have not been having batting woes as such. In three of the four games they have played, they have gone past 200. The problem is that they are not batting at a tempo normally associated with them. A threadbare bowling attack is only making that issue starker. Sowmya : "SRH have to fix their batting beyond Travishek! " 6:35pm The battle of the two opening pairs is the obvious attraction and there may not be much to separate the two teams on that count. But the Royals, by virtue of their stronger bowling attack, might just have the edge. All that and much more in Abhijato's preview. 6:30pm Sport moves rapidly. It evolves. Yesterday's gospel could be reduced to an outdated theory today. Today's trend and vogue may feel archaic tomorrow. And those who are unable to keep pace, risk falling behind. In the IPL, all of it seems to happen that much quicker. In over drive, and at a million miles per hour. Scores of 200 no longer feel safe. 70-plus in the powerplay feels the bare minimum. A swashbuckling opening partnership a pre-requisite, and a desire to throw caution to the wind, a norm. But do you know what is better than watching one such belligerent and firecracker opening pair? Two opening pairs cut from the same cloth. Of course. And so, from the OG trendsetters Travishek to JaiSoorya, worthy ascenders to that throne, from an Indian and an Australian still considered the gold standard, to a 24-year-old itching to win back his place in the national side and imagination, and a 15-year-old capable of whipping up storms that have blown two five-time winners and the defending champions out of the water already - this is Sunrisers Hyderabad versus the Rajasthan Royals. From a venue that has often seen scores that make people wonder what is indeed possible in the format. SRH in dire need of a win, and of some of the verve that made rivals previously tremble. Against a side that has only known winning so far this campaign, and is fearful of no one. A cracker awaits, so hop on to ESPNcricinfo's live coverage!

RR have five front-line bowlers apart from him, and they are treating him as their sixth bowling option. But in conditions conducive to spin, expect him to play a bigger part. That is the beauty of having a well-rounded team, like RR have. Anyway, a bit to ponder for them at this time-out. Klaasen and Nitish threatening a late-overs charge, with SRH eyeing a total in excess of 200. Exe: "Klassen seems a bit rusty..does it have to do with age?" -- Don't think it is age. But he has retired from international cricket and not sure playing a multitude of leagues compares to international cricket on a regular basis. title: Deshpande to Arora, SIX

commentTextItems.html: Arora goes big, and SRH finish with 216! Deshpande misses the yorker just outside off. Juicy full toss and Arora wallops it over deep mid wicket!

commentPostTextItems.html: 9:19pm Another 200-plus score for SRH. Abhishek, though, did not do much this time. In fact, he was dismissed off the first ball. But Kishan found his groove after an initial teething period and his 91, which contained several stunning strokes, set SRH up nicely. Klaasen, Nitish and Arora, right at the end, played their parts too and SRH now have something to play with. RR will be slightly disappointed with giving away 62 off the final five. Their overseas quicks were excellent, as was Parag in his solitary over. But Deshpande and Sandeep were expensive, with both going for more than 50. That means RR have another hefty chase in front of them but they will have JaiSoorya to call upon. Join us in a bit for the second half. Avinash: "The real question is not whether RR can chase this, it is how comfortably can they chase this." -- Might we be getting too ahead of ourselves here, Avinash? Klaasen: (On his innings and what he would rate it) About a seven (out of 10). Lot better intensity. At the back end there, we lost Ishan and lost a bit of momentum. Before that, happy with my intensity (and how I was batting). It was a nice wicket. Bit difficult (to hit the wide yorkers). The moment they went wider, it was harder. Anything straighter, felt you could catch up on boundaries. (On the six that just cleared long off) Very happy that I have quality bats. Brought out the heavy ones. But he (the bowler) completely did me there (with the slower ball).

name: Sunrisers Hyderabad

commentTextItems.html: sliced to extra cover, and that will be that for the RR juggernaut! The streak has been broken, and two unheralded, uncapped debutants have brought the Royals crashing down to earth! Full toss on middle and leg. Deshpande has a swing at it and does not get any of it. Kishan is stationed at extra cover to complete the formality, and that is confirmation of a statement win for SRH in front of their fans!

commentPostTextItems.html: 11:42pm That will be all from us for tonight. We will be back tomorrow with more IPL action. Until then, it is goodbye from all of us here tat ESPNcricinfo. Goodnight, stay safe and take care, folks! Praful Hinge, Player of the Match: I had written this somewhere that I will take 4-5 wickets on my debut. I thought of dominating the powerplay. I believe in it (manifestation). At the age of 13, I started cricket. Did not know what leather ball cricket was. Asked my father to join a club. But he said I was too young. Then he just took me there, and I kept playing after it. Want to dedicate this award to my family. (On his favourite wicket) The Sooryavanshi wicket. I had told people that I would bowl a bouncer to him and get him out. I just wanted to get him out. Varun bhai (our bowling coach) helped me plan it, so thank you. (On his body) Right now, it is okay. I want to say thank you to MRF (Pace Foundation). Naveen sir was there and I want to thank him now that I am on this stage. Ishan Kishan, SRH captain: Very happy with this win. Just felt happy because what we were looking for from the bowlers (freedom in execution), we did that. Credit goes to the bowlers. (On the debutants) You also have to look how hungry and motivated they feel. They were working throughout the season with bowling coach Varun Aaron. They were talking to experienced players. Had to give them a chance at their home ground. It was the right move today. The way Abhishek plays, he can sometimes get out. Our job is to take it deep and allow him to play freely. He got out, he will be motivated in the next game. (On not keeping) As a captain, there was some miscommunication going on. Better to be there, ask what they (bowlers) are going to bowl, and set the fields. And it worked (tonight). (On if him not keeping this IPL is the way to go) Hopefully. Riyan Parag, RR captain: (On the top order collapse) Not a lot of time to feel emotions. Credit to the way they bowled. Few miscalculations from us. (On the pitch) It was pretty good. Felt bowling second might have been better. It was sticky with the new ball. After the shine went, it slowed down. But again, that is hindsight and we could have batted better. (On Hinge and Sakib) I have not seen them a lot domestically. Played Sakib (when playing for Assam versus Bihar) once. They bowled beautifully. The pressure they had, with the home crowd chanting their name, the way they bowled - it was beautiful. (What they could have done differently in the first innings and the decision to not bowl Jadeja) Started well, probably could have done a few things here and there. Split second decision, Kishan was batting well, so trusted Bishnoi (over Jadeja). They were 30 over par. Being five wickets down for nine, and still getting to 160, says a lot about the depth. It is just a blip. We move ahead to Kolkata and something better. Sakib Hussain: Every player wishes for a debut like this. It feels very nice. (On when he knew he would debut and his prep) The bowling coach, a day ago, told me I was playing and I was prepared. (On his work with Varun Aaron) He has been working with me in last 3-4 matches. All the improvements that have happened, it is due to him. (On how he was feeling during the first few overs) We were feeling very good - for all of this to happen in a debut match. 11:18pm A clinical display by the hosts, led and turbocharged by the two debutants, Hinge and Sakib. Hinge broke the back of this run-chase inside his first over, removing each of Sooryavanshi, Jurel and Pretorius. He returned for more, and got the better of Parag too. Sakib, while the carnage was unfolding at the other end, enticed Jaiswal into a false stroke in the second over, and garnished his spell with three more wickets at the death. A night to forget for the Royals. They stuck to their philosophy of going hard, but crashed and burned in the process. They will likely put this down as an off-day, although the challenge for them now will be to recover and bounce back, especially with their spotless record now punctured.

commentPreTextItems.html: 7:27pm The umpires make their way out to the middle, followed soon by the players. Big cheers as the two CSK openers stride out. Gaikwad and Samson opening, so no surprises there, despite the possible temptation of throwing Mhatre up the order. Samson to take strike. Arora has the new ball. Slip in place. Let's play! VS: "Come on Rutu, miss your batting. Today may be the day." -- The lack of runs do not stick out as much as the lack of intent so far. Gaikwad and CSK will hope that changes tonight. Shadow-Shell: "KKR usually reserve Narine for death in CSK matches for MSD. Atleast that won't be the case today, let's see how they'll use him now" karthik siram: "I wish Sanju opens with Ayush. CSK need to score atleast 80 runs in the powerplay." -- There is plenty of reason for Mhatre to open with Samson, with Gaikwad at three, but based on what CSK have done historically, they might not tweak things. Arun: "Don't understand CSK's team selection--shouldn't Matt Henry or Akeal Hosein be in the playing XI ahead of some of their current bowlers?" -- They are probably not fully sure of what this pitch is going to do. If there is spin on offer, Akeal comes in. if there is more seam movement/assistance, Henry might get the nod. "The big question - When MS does come in, who does he slot in for? It seems like CSK have reached their "perfect" balance with bat and ball (as much as they can), and there's no specific player putting out below-par performances." -- Well, CSK will probably cross that bridge when they get there, Kiran. Rajesh A: "With spin duo Sunil N and Varun C, KKR definitely can restrict CSK under 170 and chase it down in 17 overs" -- Both of them are proper match-winners, but this Chepauk spin has not been turning as much as it once did, meaning we could get a more high-scoring game. 7:08pm The big news from the toss is that Varun is back for KKR. Gaikwad has now lost four out of five tosses too and is nudging into Ishan Kishan territory on that count. Same side for CSK, which is not a big surprise. Based on how the pitch plays, they will either bring in Henry or Hosein. Both give them powerplay options, although Akeal adds a little more variety with his left-arm spin. KKR will likely bring in Allen. But if they have a change of heart, Seifert is a more than viable option too. Chennai Super Kings batting-first XI: Sanju Samson (wk), Ruturaj Gaikwad (capt), Ayush Mhatre, Dewald Brevis, Shivam Dube, Sarfaraz Khan, Jamie Overton, Anshul Kamboj, Noor Ahmad, Khaleel Ahmed, Gurjapneet Singh CSK bench: Matthew Short, Akeal Hosein, Kartik Sharma, Prashant Veer, Matt Henry Kolkata Knight Riders bowling-first XI: Ajinkya Rahane (capt), Angkrish Raghuvanshi (wk), Cameron Green, Rinku Singh, Rovman Powell, Ramandeep Singh, Sunil Narine, Anukul Roy, Varun Chakravarthy, Kartik Tyagi, Vaibhav Arora KKR bench: Manish Pandey, Finn Allen, Tejasvi Singh, Navdeep Saini, Tim Seifert 7pm It is time for the toss. Gaikwad and Rahane out in the middle. Lots of CSK, CSK chants already going around. Gaikwad to give the coin a twirl. Rahane calls tails, and tails never fails. KKR will bowl first. The last game was really good but the result did not go our way, says Rahane. Important to have that belief and stay positive. Adds they are looking forward to this game, hoping to restrict CSK to a score and then chase it down. Just one change for us, he says - Varun comes in for Saini. Gaikwad says he would have bowled first too. Putting up a big total on the board will be challenging. Bowling was really good in the last game and that gave them a lot of confidence. Really excited for today and adds they are confident. Says they are slowly getting the balance right, and that it is about delivering each game. Same team, mentions Gaikwad. Pitch Report: There is a bias in the square boundaries - 63m to the leg side, 70m to the other. 79m hit straight down the ground. All this while bowling from the North End. Lot of bounce and pace at Chepauk this season and that trend could continue tonight. Spinners have found it tough this season, and there may not be a whole lot of spin on offer again. Pacers might have to use their variations frequently. Here is a snippet from Deivarayan Muthu, who is our eyes and ears at Chepauk tonight: Varun Chakravarthy is darting it into one of the practice pitches along with Sunil Narine. On the eve of the match, Varun had his left hand taped, but had a stint at the MA Chidambaram B nets, bowling to Rovman Powell. Seems like he might not be far away from returning to action. For CSK, Gurjapneet Singh has marked his run-up and looks set to retain his place in the team. Matt Henry has also marked his run-up and it might come down to a late toss-up between him and Akeal Hosein Shaurya : "What's the update on MS, Shashwat?!!" -- He has hit the Chepauk nets but this game might come too soon. 6:45pm There has been a powerplay overdrive and a surge of 200-plus totals in the first 20 games of the season. Read more about it in S Rajesh's piece here. Gans: "Will M Short Play for Noor?" -- CSK finally seemed to arrive at a winning formula on Saturday. Don't think they will change much (if anything) for tonight. 6:38pm CSK and KKR have contested two IPL finals and a CLT20 final, but this season, both have struggled, making this a battle of stragglers. Sidharth Monga sets the scene in his match preview. Sowmya : "Battle of the wooden spoon is trending everywhere. " -- The current bottom three have 13 titles between them. The rest? 4. 6:30pm 20 playoff appearances. 14 finals. Eight titles. And yet, the Chennai Super Kings and the Kolkata Knight Riders find themselves marooned to the bottom trenches. Maybe that is another advertisement of how the IPL cares little for reputation and past laurels. Or maybe, a sign that the best is yet to come. CSK could make a case for it. After getting outplayed in their first three games, they handed out a pasting of their own on Saturday. Led by an Indian wicket-keeper batter, who is also a World Cup winner, and an overseas all-rounder - the type of players CSK have never had a dearth of. KKR have not had such success. Yet. But the last time they played CSK in Chennai, they routed them. And as KKR search for a spark to ignite their season, a few fond and happy memories might just be the gasoline they are after. Hello and welcome to ESPNcricinfo's coverage. We are back at Chepauk. The fortress that was breached multiple times last year and once this season, but where the first few bricks of a rebuild have now been laid. Two great franchises. Two incredibly successful sides. Two teams aware of the lofty heights they have hit previously, but also of the imminent danger of lagging behind. Tonight could either be a step back after a step forward, or the beginning of a redemption arc that has, in the past, so often turned fruitful. Plenty to tuck into, so jump on!

commentPostTextItems.html: 9:18pm Only 23 off the final three overs, and that will give KKR plenty of momentum heading into their chase. Things were not as smooth always, though. CSK, through Samson and Mhatre, came at KKR and ransacked 72 in the powerplay. But once the spinners were introduced, CSK were not as free-flowing. That spilled over at the death too, with Dube and Overton struggling to make a mark. Samson and Brevis kept CSK afloat with 40s, but they will now need their bowlers to back them up to defend this score. KKR, courtesy a sumptuous bowling display by Narine and the pacers at the back end, will feel they are ahead in this game as things stand. Join us in a bit for the second half. Kanth: "Is CSK short by 18-20 runs? With power play milking 72 runs, this is below par score" -- They will be disappointed having only gotten to 192, especially after the start they had. But if they bowl well, like KKR did, there might be enough in this surface to make this a competitive total. Dwayne Bravo, KKR mentor: (On the score) At the back end, we did a fantastic job. They have a powerful batting line-up. Credit to the bowlers, the spinners and Sunil. They did not get any momentum. At the half-way stage, momentum on our side. Good plans from the bowling group. They work very hard in the nets. Make sure we do our plans in practice first. All the guys have been fantastic throughout the camp. Very consistent message between Tim and myself - try not to get too flustered or make it too complicated based on the results. Going to be positive. If we get a good start, it is a total we can chase.

name: Chennai Super Kings

commentTextItems.html: this could be the final ball of the game, but we wait for confirmation because KKR have reviewed. Nothing doing on that count, and CSK make it back-to-back wins at Chepauk, and this is beginning to feel like a fortress all over again! Very full ball outside off. Powell swishes and misses and then, rather cheekily, tries to see if he can get a wide too. Ball well inside the tramlines, though, and that will be that for tonight. CSK with another clinical bowling display and after losing three on the trot, they have now won two on the spin!

commentPostTextItems.html: 11:53pm That will be all from us for tonight. We hope you enjoyed our coverage, and would love your company tomorrow as well, with the Lucknow Super Giants taking on the Royal Challengers Bengaluru. Until then, from all of us here at ESPNcricinfo, it is goodbye! Noor Ahmad, Player of the Match: Really happy to contribute to my team. Was humid, so was trying to keep my fingers dry - that helped me a lot to hit the right areas. Really happy with the pitch. Ball was not coming onto the bat. (On this performance) It gives a lot of confidence. Will keep putting a lot of effort to keep contributing to my team. Changing pace is great everywhere, on every wicket. Tonight, above 90(kph) was good. Ruturaj Gaikwad, CSK captain: Feeling good. Defended a good score. Felt it was a par score, given wicket changed drastically after the first 7-8 overs. It started spinning and gripping. We were looking for 200-210 initially but then thought anything above 180 would be a good score. (On the bowling) It was good. Slowly, it is coming together. Everyone knows what their role is. What lengths to bowl. Adjusting and adapting really well. We wanted to use Veer if we were short in batting but thought we had it covered. (On Akeal) More of a powerplay bowler but Sunil was batting. He bowled really well. (On CSK's catching) We dropped everything, just took one or two. Felt it was a bit humid. Lot of sweat coming into the hands. Not an excuse. We want to improve. As long as there is energy, intent and attitude behind every ball, we will be good. (On his form) Good to be on the winning side after a long time. Felt it was getting into my head even when batting. Feeling really good, just wanting to make sure to do what the team needs. Mentally, feeling positive. A big knock is just round the corner. Definitely I will do it when it is needed. Ajinkya Rahane, KKR captain: I thought with the ball, we did very good. 190 on this wicket was very good. To pull it back for 190 (after the powerplay CSK had) was very good. 36-37 in the powerplay (from us) was very important (in the result). We needed one batter to bat through till the end (for us to have a good chance). Combination wise, the one we had, last game and this, was really good. It is tough, not winning matches. About having to keep our heads up, chins up. If the results are not going your way, you have to think about combinations, but it is about being positive and keeping your heads up. (On Tyagi) He is bowling really good. All credit to him. The pace he is bowling at is amazing. Game by game, he is improving his skills. Not easy for batters to hit big sixes. From both sides, spinners bowled really well. We have to keep our head up, be positive and have self-belief. Akeal Hosein: (on the pitch and his plans) Finally good to see a good cricket wicket with something in it for everyone, and not just a belter. We just exploited whatever was on offer. There was something there, so about using natural variations. Most important thing was staying on the stumps and making them hit to balls that were slower or were skidding through. (On bowling with Noor) Very happy for Noor. last couple of games, he was struggling but happy for him to get some success and confidence behind him. (On the score) Cricket games, when you see teams score between 170-190, you know you will get a hell of a game. It was a day where you had to work for what you wanted, and not just turn up with eyes closed and magical things would happen. 11:31pm Another complete bowling display by CSK, and that will give them great belief, given how their campaign had begun. Khaleel and Kamboj kept things tight in the powerplay, before Akeal and Noor spun a yarn around the KKR batters. Overton was not as effective as the other day but Kamboj's death-overs execution was on point. Plenty to dissect for KKR. They shook up their batting order by promoting Narine but it was a familiar tale of lacking intent. None of their batters got going and even though Powell and Ramandeep got a few boundaries away, those ended up being consolatory runs, rather than acting as a catalyst for a turnaround.

commentPreTextItems.html: 7.25 pm Not too long now until Mitch Marsh and Aiden Markram walk out to open the innings for LSG. They haven't scored 200 yet this season. Can they do it tonight, at a really 200-friendly venue? The Chinnaswamy Stadium is packed full, a sea of red and black. Romario Shepherd is giving RCB the talk in their huddle, while Kohli chats with Pant and Shami on the sidelines. Game time. Will Krunal open the bowling to two right-handers, or perhaps one of the early overs? Marsh to face, Bhuvneshwar Kumar has the new ball. 7pm, toss Rishabh Pant calls heads, it's tails. Rajat Patidar says RCB are bowling first. "Pretty obvious," he says. Josh Hazlewood is back for RCB, and out goes Jacob Duffy. No changes for LSG, says Rishabh Pant. RCB bowling-first XI: 1 Phil Salt, 2 Devdutt Padikkal, 3 Rajat Patidar (capt), 4 Jitesh Sharma (wk), 5 Tim David, 6 Romario Shepherd, 7 Krunal Pandya, 8 Bhuvneshwar Kumar, 9 Suyash Sharma, 10 Rasikh Dar, 11 Josh Hazlewood. Virat Kohli is not in the bowling-first XI, and will likely come in as Impact Player for the chase. He had hurt his ankle during RCB's previous game against MI and did not field during the second innings. LSG batting-first XI 1 Mitchell Marsh, 2 Aiden Markram, 3 Rishabh Pant (capt & wk), 4 Nicholas Pooran, 5 Ayush Badoni, 6 Abdul Samad, 7 Mukul Choudhary, 8 Mohammed Shami, 9 Avesh Khan, 10 Digvesh Rathi, 11 Prince Yadav. LSG's impact player options are: Mayank Yadav, George Linde, M Siddharth, Himmat Singh and Matthew Breetzke. Mischief: "Is Kohli playing or not? I'm a bit confused, could he come as impact?" Yes, he most likely will, but until he does you can't be 100% sure. Kiran: "Assuming LSG get a (somewhat) decent batting performance in, there's still a chance we see Mayank!" Yes, if they don't need batting cover, then either Mayank, Linde or Siddharth could come in as Impact Player. Sujatha : "No better ground for Nicholas Pooran to get into some serious hitting form. True pitch , short boundaries and a chance to make an impact!" Speaking of, one square boundary is a tiny 61 metres, the other is 68m. The straight boundary is only around 74m. Sanjay: "What happened to Mohsin Khan??? Is he injured?" Played one game this season and got injured. He's not far from being fit again though. Aashish Calla: "Preposterous that Linde isn't in the XI and chances that he won't come in - He should have been in, in place of Avesh, to bat at 8, add the left arm spin and then Mayank would surely have been the sub! " Kedar: "Oh come on! Patidar is no fun. Fans wanted a fifth consecutive 200 . Looking at the stats comparisons, that looks much less likely now." Kedar has his priorities straight! Shaurya: "Well no offense to LSG, but this should have been a game to test the Duffy-Hazelwood combo for the more deadlier batting attacks in this long tournament..they could have easily done that while leaving Romario out for this one!?" 6.58 pm Toss in a couple of minutes. Shaurya: "Oh well, I just saw that Shaswattt isn't here...Welcome George...who are you backing today!?" He's taking a well-earned break, and who am I backing? I picked option three in the poll below. Alex F: "Last week this time, nobody would have expected only 3 teams to have more points than CSK!" Indeed, things can change quickly in the IPL. 6.40 pm More from Shashank Kishore at the Chinnaswamy: "Hazlewood is going through his warm-up drills. Began with some stretching with the elastic band followed by squats and lunges. He has now moved on to short sprints. "Meanwhile, Mayank Yadav is marking his run-up. But whether that means he starts, only time will tell. Because I can also see Prince Yadav and Avesh Khan marking theirs. Surely there's no space for all three in the LSG XI with Shami around too." Deepak: "Hope LSG batters get some form in the most easy batting friendly conditions of the country !!" Karthik Siram : "I really hope Mukul gains valuable experience from playing in different conditions. He is a keeper, and that stunning helicopter shot surely brought back memories of one of the greatest finishers India has ever produced." Shaurya: "Well it looks like we have got the DUFFY-HAZELGOD combo today, well Romario hasn't done anything wrong, it seems obvious to strengthen the bowling attack!!" Sanket: "To make this contest LSG batting unit needs to come to the party. The big guns like Marsh, Pooran haven't contributed with the bat, the Rishabh has been again inconsistent and also there isn't much depth available. So these experienced guys need to create more impact with the bat and these are the best conditions to bat.. it won't be bad to lose a toss here For under confident team batting first becomes a bit easy task than chasing a huge target." 6.25 pm When I said the weather was fair in Bengaluru, I meant no rain. Shashank Kishore has made his way into the Chinnaswamy press box and has a slightly different take: "It's a ridiculously hot evening in Bangalore. The temperature touched 36C earlier in the day, and there are many more water booths installed around the venue for the fans. The teams got in just a while ago. But there isn't much activity at the ground yet with players just slowly beginning to head down for some light warm-ups. "Abhinandan Singh and Jacob Duffy arrived a lot earlier than the rest of the RCB squad and did some bowling on the side pitch." Josh Hazlewood hasn't been sighted yet at the venue. He played against Rajasthan Royals in Guwahati on Friday but didn't travel to Mumbai for the game against MI on Sunday. He wasn't at training last evening either. Okay scratch all that! A huge roar has gone up around the Chinnaswamy, and it's not for Kohli but for Hazlewood, who's just emerged on to the field. The roar for Kohli, is obviously louder - "deafening" says Shashank. Mukund: "Is Kohli fit and playing today?" He looked at ease during training last night after not fielding against MI due to an ankle issue, so he should play. "Kohli has gotten straight down to business," says Shashank. "Taking throw downs from Dinesh Karthik." CSB: "RCB all the way. Knowing their strengths - I think batting first might be the way to go in this one. LSG need to bowl world-class to threaten RCB. I expect a comfortable win for RCB." VS: "Are we going to see an upset today? LSG triumphing today will make the table interesting." 6.00 pm Good evening folks, and welcome to ESPNcricinfo's coverage of the game between RCB and LSG at the Chinnaswamy Stadium. The weather is fair in Bengaluru so strap in for a full, and very likely high-scoring, contest. RCB are third in the points table with three wins in four games. Victory tonight will take them to No. 1, ahead of Rajasthan Royals on net run rate. LSG are seventh, but a win tonight will take them level with RCB on six points. 23 games into IPL 2026, there's very little separating the teams on the points table. There's a fair bit separating these two teams on the field though. RCB have been a batting behemoth this season, while LSG have been among the worst batting teams. That's a gulf they need to bridge if they are to challenge Patidar and company tonight. The pitch, as usual for the Chinnaswamy Stadium, is expected to be great for batting. Win toss and chase. It may not be a 240-250 surface, but 220 should be doable. Small mercies for the bowlers? RCB got 250 batting first against CSK in their previous game here. Cricfan: "Hoping that this will be the first comment to get published today. RCB has 4 scores of over 200, barely breaking a sweat except for the match against RR. But, they also conceded 4 scores of 200 . Hence, I think they have to strengthen their bowling by letting go of their additional batting depth in the form of excluding Romario Shepherd. Hope they play both Duffy and Hazelwood. And also pick left arm raw pace for variety in form of Mangesh Yadav (for Rasikh)." There you go, cricfan! Mustafa Moudi: "I want Digvesh Rathi to dismiss Virat Kohli tonight just to see whether he can write his dismissal down in this NOTEBOOK or not." Will Mayank Yadav play against RCB? It was here two years ago that he shot into the spotlight by hitting speeds of 156kph, and ratting players like Glenn Maxwell and Cameron Green. Tom Moody, LSG's director of cricket, says Mayank is finally good to go. Shashank Kishore kept a close eye on Nicholas Pooran at the nets last evening and the LSG batter seemed in great touch. But can he find that form in the middle? He's been so woefully out of form this season and the tournament is poorer for it.

commentTextItems.html: that's the game! Shepherd seals victory for RCB by going back and cutting a short ball to the backward point boundary. RCB are on top of the points table, having crushed LSG by five wickets and 29 balls to spare to seal their fourth win in five matches this season

commentPostTextItems.html: Too easy. RCB won the toss, chose to bowl first, and produced a masterclass on a two-paced pitch to dismiss LSG for 146. All of their bowlers were on point, led by Hazlewood and Rasikh. And then Kohli gave them a quick start to the chase to extinguish any hope LSG may have had of defending a below-par target. KumarS: "What an amazing NRR bump! from 1.148 to 1.503!! This will go a long way for RCB to help secure the number 1 spot if NRR comes to play" Nicholas Pooran: Tough season for us, we were below par, 175 would have been competitive, we have been struggling with the bat ... It's T20 cricket, tough game, tough to stay consistent, guys have been working hard, it's a matter of time, have to stay patient and take the opportunity when it comes. I'm feeling really good, stroking the ball nicely but it hasn't gone my way. I've been in this situation before and confident I can do it. Virat Kohli takes the Orange Cap: Much better than the last game, still not 100%, knee was sore last game, even health wise I was under the weather for the last four five days, happy with my intensity ... wanted to take the game head on. Should have finished that game off as well. Not enough grass on the pitch, slower than normal, last few days have been very hot ... it was different ... the idea was to take the game away from the opposition in the powerplay. Happy with my approach today. I'll have the presentation for you shortly. Rajat Patidar: Fantastic bowling, the way the fast bowlers hit the deck was nice. Krunal is a very courageous bowler, Suyash also ...For a captain, having a specialist like Bhuvi makes my job a lot easier. From the start, RCB has worked a lot on fielding ... today's was an easier catch for Salt. Long way to go, we're taking it one game at a time. The Player of the Match is Josh Hazlewood for taking 1 for 20 in four overs: Felt much better today, in good shape. Got to look at who you are playing against, conditions play a part, slow wicket today, just had to whack that length ... I'd like to have a few funky deliveries ... always working on them slower balls ... keep moving forward. Summing up the conditions as early as we can is a huge plus for us. The plan is hopefully to keep playing, the schedule is pretty good here on, so I should be okay to keep playing. So RCB are on top of the points table, level with Rajasthan Royals on eight points but ahead on NRR, which got a massive boost with the margin of victory tonight. Thank you for all your emails over the course of this game, we'll be back tomorrow for MI vs PBKS at the Wankhede Stadium. Until then, good night!

commentPreTextItems.html: 7.28pm Righto, time for some cricket. Out stride the two on-field umpires, followed by the Punjab Kings fielders. The two MI openers, the two left-handers - Ryan Ricklelton and Quinton de Kock walk out as well. Remember, there's no Rohit Sharma playing this evening. Arshdeep Singh has the new ball and he will bowl over the wicket to Ricklelton with a slip in place. Deep square leg and deep point are the two fielders out. 7.25pm Who is Mayank Rawat, MI's newest debutant? Rawat is a Delhi-based all-rounder whose journey to the IPL reflects years of persistence through the domestic cricket system. Rawat began his cricketing journey in Delhi under coach Rajesh Nagar, who has mentored him since 2011. A product of structured grassroots development, he trained consistently through school and academy cricket, receiving strong support from his coaching setup during his formative years. His resurgence came through strong performances in domestic competitions, particularly the Delhi Premier League, where his contributions brought him back into the spotlight and attracted the attention of IPL scouts. AJ: "MI should score around 210 here I feel..." I feel 210 won't be enough. Darshil: "Prediction: 250 on the cards for MI with QDK as highest run scorer(87 runs)" Mehak: "Sky - 84, Tilak - 63. MI 221/4." 7.20pm Evening, folks. This could and should be a high-scoring encounter. Let's hear some first-innings predictions in the comments? Ashish will be in to take you in for the first ten overs. Vignesh: "I don't understand the logic of not selecting will jacks in playing 11 despite Santner not there ! " Jacks is not available. He was on his way to India yesterday. Praveen: "So MI is playing with only 3 overseas players today?" Yep, it keeps the option of bringing in the overseas options: Bosch (in either innings since he's an allrounder) and Ghazanfar (legspinner from Afghanistan) MI impact options - AM Ghazanfar, Corbin Bosch, Raj Bawa, Robin Minz, Ashwani Kumar Mumbai Indians XI 1 Quinton de Kock (wk), 2 Ryan Rickelton, 3 Tilak Varma, 4 Suryakumar Yadav, 5 Hardik Pandya (capt), 6 Sherfane Rutherford, 7 Naman Dhir, 8 Mayank Rawat, 9 Shardul Thakur, 10 Deepak Chahar, 11 Jasprit Bumrah PBKS impact options - Nehal Wadhera, Vishnu Vinod, Harpreet Brar, Suyansh Shedge, Yash Thakur Punjab Kings XI 1 Priyansh Arya, 2 Prabhsimran Singh (wk), 3 Cooper Connolly, 4 Shreyas Iyer (capt), 5 Shashank Singh, 6 Marcus Stoinis, 7 Marco Jansen, 8 Xavier Bartlett, 9 Vijaykumar Vyshak, 10 Arshdeep Singh, 11 Yuzvendra Chahal Hardik Pandya, MI captain We were looking to bowl first as well, but good toss to lose. Time to play good cricket and get a W. We've played good cricket but have lost big moments. Last game, we went for four 20-plus overs which isn't acceptable. We've spoken, planned about it. Rohit misses out, he'll take a couple of games to see where he is. Santner is unwell. Quinton comes back, Mayank Rawat will debut Shreyas Iyer, PBKS captain So far so good, we've got a brilliant start. That's all a captain can ask for. Our combination has been splendid. I ask the team to be proactive throughout. It's easy to become complacent, you have stay in the zone. Pitch looks dry, but players have said it gets better with dew. Same team 7pm Toss time. Ravi Shastri in with the captains. Hardik will spin the coin, Tails is the call. It's Tails. PBKS will bowl Pitch report from Michael Clare - Bowling from the Southern End, the square boundaries are 61 and 67 metres, fine boundaries are small (56 and 58 metres) and straight ones are long - around 75 metres. Expect the wicket to be magnificent. Love the grass coverage, keeps the pace in the wicket, good for batting and bowling. Might get extra pace with the new ball. Ball kisses off the pitch nicely when you're batting. Both teams will want to chase, expect a high-scoring game. Shaurya: "Feel PBKS will bat first and also bat out MI in the powerplay and the middle overs itself...is it too much to ask for!!?" "Okay can see Rohit now", Sruthi informs with about six minutes to go for the toss, "Just speaking to Mahela with a racquet in his hand" VS: "Batters are playing safe with Bumrah that is the reason for lack of wickets. He is very economical though." He's gone at an economy of 8.2 so far, which isn't bad MI desperate to find a way out of their bowling mess 6:50pm Here's an update from Sruthi: Hello from the Wankhede! Will Rohit play today is the big question, but if he doesn't, how are MI going to balance the side? Just a while ago, Robin Minz was spotted doing wicketkeeping drills and Ryan Rickelton was seen practicing high catches… and left-arm quick Ashwani Kumar marked his run-up. No signs of Rohit - 10 mins before toss Karan: "Danish Malewar's batting style highly resembles Rohit Sharma's. I guess it's worth a punt " 6:40pm There shouldn't be any other doubts over player availability, and when placed next to each other MI and PBKS might seem equal, MI might even look better with Hardik, Bumrah, SKY, Tilak and Boult in. What they don't have is a cohesive unit firing like the one PBKS has. The batting flows nicely from the openers - Prabhsimran and Priyansh - to the middle order - with Shreyas and Shashank. Arshdeep's form hasn't been great. But they have found Vyshak and Chahal is back to his best. Sowmya : "A key takeaway from the RCB v MI encounter. Losing the toss may be a distinct disadvantage but it can be offset by going berserk while batting 1st. Anything above 220 is a very tall ask. " Samar: "Rohit Sharma's absence could be a big blow for MI. With Team desperately looking for win, now they'll need to find an opener who can boss the Powerplay." Param: "What is bigger problem for MI? Rohit missing or Bumrah not taking wickets?" Right now, it might be the former 6:30pm Let's get the big news out of the way, no signs of Rohit Sharma yet, reports Sruthi Ravindranath, our correspondent from the ground. There were doubts over his participation since he walked off last game due to a hamstring issue. Will he not make it? Who will replace him? Will Danish Malewar get a chance? What about Quinton de Kock? What do you think?

commentPostTextItems.html: Vibhanshu: "Almost one-third of this season is over and winners of 13 titles out of a total of 19 are sitting at the bottom of the table. " One of them will be on tomorrow as KKR take on GT. Do join us for that, and check out the quotes below. They're all excellent. Thanks for joining. Goodnight. Arshdeep Singh, POTM Feels good, it goes back to having a chat with Ricky. Told him the ball didn't feel right when it left the hand. Had a good session yesterday and the control returned, ball was seaming and swinging. The chat was nothing technical, I was expecting too many things from myself. He told me you're coming off a high from the WC win and you can't maintain that all the time. (Rickelton ball) The wobble ball is what I've worked on, still not there yet but I'm working on that as a variation. Wasn't the way I was expecting to get him out but you accept whatever comes in T20s. Wide yorkers I've been bowling a lot, wides too, but the plan is simple if the batters are set and there's a longer boundary. Sometimes, when the yorker is coming off nicely or the batter is new, you attack the stumps. When they're set you go wide. (On PBKS' increased following) Lot of credit goes to my social media. Lot of them know me from reels and memes. Shreyas Iyer, PBKS captain Confident and optimistic going forward. We've been playing phenomenally. We know each game is important, it's a collective effort, glad to have a comprehensive win. Prabhsimran has raised his bar, considering the last season, where he swung wild, got runs and gave excellent starts. Now he's got maturity and finishing off games. He's maturing with each game. My catch was the key to pulling things back (laughs), but we have the tendency to do that. Did that even against SRH. We have to be present and enjoy the moment. We haven't decided on how to set totals, lucky to have won tosses so far. We have a lot of positive players ready to go out there and express themselves. You need to keep getting better each game, focus on yourselves and that's the recipe we've been following. I've seen crowd coming in numbers, the fan following is going high. Great to see fans showering their love. Angad: "Dravid gets credit for Sooryavanshi, but no one actually talks about Yuvraj for grooming likes of Abhishek and Prabhsimran and getting a beast out of them" Deep: "POTM Ashsdeep or PrabhSimran?" we'll find out now as the presentations get underway Tejas: "Shreyas's total impact of 46 sounds a little but of an undercount, does it not? I get there were many other impactful performances, but still..." Soham: "Hardik is asking the right questions. But it's not a good look to be saying stuff like this when his performance with the bat today was arguably the catalyst for MI falling out of the game, and his bowling also hasn't been great. A great leader can ask those questions in the locker room but to the outside at least should be taking some responsibility and blame on himself as the leader." Think it was okay. They've looked toothless for a while, so the frustration must've been simmering. Prabhsimran Singh I didn't get many balls in the powerplay but I thought I'd bat long and kept belief in myself. I've worked with Yuvi in the off-season, he told me I have a lot of time and I should bat long. While chasing 200, we have to cash in during the powerplay. But the wicket can be slow as it was today, so you have to bat deep. Shreyas gives a lot of clarity, batting with him is easy. Strong stuff from Hardik tonight. You can tell MI are feeling the pinch. Ownership, as he says, has to be taken Hardik Pandya, MI captain To be honest, I don't have much to say. We need to go back and see where we're lacking - if it's individuals, groups or planning and work it out. Credit to PBKS, ball started reversing. Dew came in the second innings but they beat us. They bowled and fielded better. We need to see if we need to make difficult calls or see if we continue and turn things around. Ownership has to be taken. 11:01pm PBKS stay unbeaten and MI don't have answers. At no part of the chase was there a real sense of jeopardy. It threatened to arrive after Connolly fell and PBKS were 45 for 2 but Shreyas then took over with Prabhsimran for company. Prabhsimran was dropped by Bumrah and boy did he capitalise. The dew grew and the pitch got better to bat. MI bowled slow a lot but there was no grip. Shreyas and Prabhsimran's wagon wheels are art pieces with lines going everywhere. Ghazanfar struck twice but no one else took a wicket and they all went over ten too.

commentPreTextItems.html: Travishek in the middle. Clock counts down. Short with ball in hand - hit 'em with spin first up. Let's play! 7.25pm Miller's hit back-to-back sixes, then a four through deep midwicket, to seal a nervy chase for DC. Redemption in the final over, you have to say, after what happened a few nights ago... Anyhoo, time to put our minds on this match now! The men in yellow are huddled around the boundary line, while the openers waltz in. 7.20pm Meanwhile, DC vs RCB going down to the wire. 20 needed off the last 10 for DC, with Stubbs and Miller at the crease. Go catch that finale before the first act of this one! Sabu Aloysius : "Short is the correct bet and as off spinners does the job against left handers in last world cup,especially when ishan and Abhishek in top 3. Who else vote for a first over from short." We will have to wait for the chase to see Sakib and Hinge bowl tonight, after both of them took four-fors on debut. You can read up about there impactful debut here. 7.15pm Lots of thoughts in the feedback section about one particular matter: Raj: "I don't understand CSK team management decisions. After a couple of games, I thought Akeal Hosein would feature in the side in all games because of the fact that he can bowl in powerplays and also dry up runs at one end, which actually helped Noor find his mojo and pick wickets. But they dropped him for Short?" SSS: "Very strange lineup by CSK - no Akeal, so do they expect the part timer Short to give 4 overs?" Kartik: "Disappointed not to see Akeal Hosein or Zak Foulkes today, I reckon either of those two would have done really well against SRH's top order. Preparing for another run fest of a powerplay as a CSK fan :')" Abhilash: "Akeal not playing must be related to the top 3 left handers in SRH. lot of pondering, but not a sensible one perhaps from CSK" Let's see how this particular line-up call goes for them! 7.05pm Mizgan: "Ishan Kishan and a coin toss, the hate relationship continues, haha." - True! Shayan : "MSD?? yes? no? maybe??" - Won't be playing today, in the end... MC: "Might have been a good toss to lose for SRH (not that it would have mattered). No better opportunity for the openers to find their form than trying to set a target against a powerplay bowling attack that wasn't that strong to begin with, even before Khaleel's injury." 7pm We get ready for the toss now. Captains head out to the middle. Gaikwad calls tail and calls correctly: CSK will bowl first. "Looks like a good surface, won't change much. Good to be up from the bottom. From second time, we started doing basic things right. Batting was good, bowling was good, fielding was 50-50... Key today is just to stay consistent," Gaikwad says. "Last game, Noor bowled really well. Couple of guys stepping up with the bowling really helps. Looks like a belter." "We would have batted first," Kishan says. "Nothing to worry at all. Plan of batting in first innings is from ball one, you have to go for it. We look to do the same thing again and again. We just have it game by game. Doesn't matter where we are on the table right now, it's a long tournament. It's about being in a good headspace. Ball will move in the bit, but batters have to be watchful of the ball. Same team: Madushanka comes in place of Harsh Dubey, to give us more swinging options." Sunrisers Hyderabad batting-first XI: Abhishek Sharma, Travis Head, Ishan Kishan (c), Heinrich Klaasen, Salil Arora (wk), Aniket Verma, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Shivang Kumar, Praful Hinge, Sakib Hussain, Eshan Malinga Chennai Super Kings bowling-first XI: Sanju Samson (wk), Ruturaj Gaikwad (c), Sarfaraz Khan, Shivam Dube, Dewald Brevis, Jamie Overton, Matthew Short, Anshul Kamboj, Noor Ahmad, Mukesh Choudhary, Gurjapneet Singh 6.40pm While we await the toss and the team sheets, you should dip into Shashank's preview. At the same time, Al Muthu has fired up the Live Report - you can follow it for deep insights throughout the game. Shashank has also dug up a fantastic story about Nitish Kumar Reddy bumping up his pace through the unlikeliest of places: doomscrolling reels. A chance encounter and a week of training later, NKR is seeing instant gains. Read all about it here. Arav Agrawal: "Is Cummins warming up and is there a chance he will play today? Heard some pundits saying he was ready for selection" - He is in line to feature from April 25, according to head coach Daniel Vettori. He will fly out to Hyderabad on Friday. But he isn't back with the team just yet. Mustafa Moudi: "The Fans of both the sides are waiting for the World Cup Winning Skippers - Dhoni and Cummins to return. But seems like none of them might return this match !!" Arav Agrawal: "Travishek is due some runs, especially Travis hope he goes well today" - He's been struggling in the powerplay. At least compared to peak Travis Head. Let's see if he can get going today. 6.30pm Let's be honest, we have all been on Dhoniwatch. Will he finally play for CSK today? Or wait another game? While he has travelled with the team, there is no saying if he will take the field today. At the same time, more pertinent questions hang in the air as they look to take on the tospy-turvy SRH side in Hyderabad. How will CSK make up for Khaleel Ahmed's absence, who has been ruled out of the tournament? Will SRH's middle order - and an inexperienced bowling attack - come to the fore once more? This and much more awaits us today evening. Shashank Kishore and I will be bringing you all the updates at ESPNcricinfo.

commentTextItems.html: That's that, it's all over. SRH have pulled off a tight win that looked unlikely when CSK went hammer and tongs in the powerplay. Hinge closes it out with a superb yorker that is dug out to the leg side. <b> SRH surge to a third win now. <'/b>

commentPostTextItems.html: Thanks for joining us. Hope you enjoyed our company. Look forward to a double-header Sunday. "Lovely when you have a bunch of young bowlers coming up with their plans," says Ishan Kishan. "Looking at them [Praful, Sakib, Shivang], look at them getting better day by day at training, you have to trust them. I felt we were 30-40 short, need to be a lot better in our shot selection. Not looking at points table, need to keep our head down, we'll take it one match at a time and see how it goes." Eshan Malinga is Player of the Match for his 3/29. Ruturaj Gaikwad: "Looking at how their powerplay went, I was looking at 220-230. To pull it back by 30, I would have taken it any day under 200. It was just about 80 runs needed in 10 overs in the chase. From there it was just about building a couple of partnerships. We scored just four runs in the next two overs after the 10-over mark. Chasing 12-13 at the death is going to be difficult. It's been three successive games that the bowling unit has been doing really well. Even the powerplay today I thought Abhishek played brilliantly. I think everyone did a good job with the ball. Anshul is working really on his bowling, especially the death bowling. Very rarely you get bowlers who have clarity and tell the captain that I know what to do, this is what I am going to do." Nitish Reddy: Everyone did a good job, it's a team effort. I was thinking of bowling according to the situation and to use the fields. The pitch was good, fast bowlers did well. Good to bat on, we executed well. We got message from outside to bowl on top of off, not try too much. Shivang has been bowling really well, hope he continues. 11.32pm It's been a night of lessons for Praful Hinge and Sakib Hussain, but they'll be delighted at the manner in which they've bounced back to close the game out as SRH jump to No. 4 on the points table. CSK were on track to chase this down, but the wickets of Sarfaraz and Brewis in quick succession turned things around. After that, neither Dube nor Overton managed to get any momentum.

commentPreTextItems.html:
3.28pm It's a steamy cauldron out there but the fans are filling up the stands! The purple and yellow flags are fluttering, the purple caps have all been put to use and out walk the smashing RR openers. Looks like Jaiswal will take strike today and Arora will take the new ball, he also has a slip in place. Match 28, Sunday afternoon for double-header day, let's go! Varun C says in a TV interview that this is one of the best KKR squads he has been a part of but somehow the results aren't coming. He feels KKR need to improve in the powerplay, both while batting and bowling. Mustafa Moudi: "Excited for Vaibhav vs Vaibhav Contest !!" Woah, woah! What about Sooryavanshi vs Narine? I'm curious if Narine will bowl in the powerplay today. In this powerplay this IPL, he has bowled four overs for one wicket at an economy rate of 7.25. 3pm It's time for the toss...Riyan Parag makes the right call of tails and RR are batting first. He says it looks like a pretty dry wicket and is hoping for some turn. Hetmyer comes back! So out goes Lhuan-dre Pretorius. They also leave out Tushar Deshpande for Brijesh Sharma. KKR going with the same team. Rajasthan Royals: 1 Yashasvi Jaiswal, 2 Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, 3 Dhruv Jurel (wk), 4 Riyan Parag (capt), 5 Shimron Hetmyer, 6 Donovan Ferreira, 7 Ravindra Jadeja, 8 Jofra Archer, 9 Ravi Bishnoi, 10 Nandre Burger, 11 Brijesh Sharma
Impact options: Sandeep Sharma, Shubham Dubey, Lhuan-dre Pretorius, Ravi Singh, Yash Punja So someone like Sandeep Sharma could come in as an impact player. KKR: 1 Ajinkya Rahane (capt), 2 Tim Seifert (wk), 3 Cameron Green, 4 Rovman Powell, 5 Rinku Singh, 6 Anukul Roy, 7 Ramandeep Singh, 8 Sunil Narine, 9 Kartik Tyagi, 10 Varun Chakravarthy, 11 Vaibhav Arora
Impact options: Manish Pandey, Finn Allen, Angkrish Raghuvanshi, Tejasvi Singh, Navdeep Saini For KKR, Raghuvanshi will likely come in as an impact player which means Seifert keeps wickets first. 2.55pm Ian Bishop says in the pitch report that the square boundaries are extremely skewed: 58m and 70m! Wow, that's massive and will surely make the bowlers plan accordingly against the big hitters. Otherwise it's expected to be a belter, Katey Martin says. Will the team winning the toss opt to bat since it's a day game and given the scorching heat? Of course, it depends on the pitch and here's a snippet on that from the preview: The last two afternoon games on this particular surface, pitch no. 4, were won by the team batting first. But KKR and RR might not be swayed just by that, because in the first of those, KKR almost chased down 239 against Lucknow Super Giants, and in the second, Italy gave England a massive scare chasing 203 at the 2026 T20 World Cup. 2.50pm The players and coaches are all "warming up" in extremely hot conditions out there. Rahane has had a look at the pitch, Parag is having a chat with his head coach Sangakkara, Rinku is taking some throwdowns. And while we wait for the toss, you can watch... "@Vishal...Just one correction...it's a triple header today..with the women in bluess rocking today tooo!!!!!" Lessgooo! Thanks Shaurya. For everyone else, the second SA vs Ind women's T20I starts art 5.30pm IST today. 2.40pm The news from the KKR camp is that Matheesha Pathirana has joined the squad but it's unlikely he will play today. What about Royals - will they bring Shimron Hetmyer back? You can unpack all that and more in Hemant's preview here. Aarush : "Is rain expected today?" It's really bright and sunny, about 36-37 degrees Celsius and "feels like 40 degrees". And we can never take our eyes off Cam Green can we: VS: "Hope to see a fluent Cam green today. He is slowly coming into form." 2.30pm It's hot in Kolkata and we get ready for two teams which are certainly feeling the heat, although one team a lot more than the other. KKR, the hosts today, are reeling right at the bottom with a lot of questions to answer especially around their batting. The pressure is mounting on their captain Ajinkya Rahane, his batting position, and there have also hardly been runs from Rinku Singh. They run into Rajasthan Royals, flying high with their batting firepower, but who were demolished by SRH's debutants not too long ago. It's the Sunday double-header, I'm Vishal Dikshit and get ready to fasten your seat belts for the next nine hours of action!

title: Arora to Archer, 1 bye, OUT

commentTextItems.html: Arora misses the chance to run Archer out at his end... but Archer is eventually run out at the keeper's end. A comical end to the innings. The third umpire confirms that Archer is miles short of his crease. Arora bowled a bouncer, and got the ball to finish over middle stump as the ball climbed nicely. Archer went to scoop but missed, and pushed for a bye. Seifert threw it to Arora, who couldn't collect the throw cleanly. So in trying to capitalise on the miss, Archer and Brijesh went for the second but Archer fell way short

commentPostTextItems.html: Sunil Narine: "I think it's getting here [close to his best]... in every game, you try to do your best. The slower you bowled on this pitch, you were getting a bit more. Was a consideration [to bowl three overs in the powerplay]. Once Varun is back in form, it's good for us as a bowling unit. He's a wicket-taker. It's key to get him back. It always boils down to the powerplay; it's the best time to bat." 5.18pm Varun and Narine combine for figures of 5 for 40 in eight overs. Tyagi takes three wickets, but that came when the RR batters were looking to go big in the 19th over; one of his wickets was off a full toss, while the other was of a tailender. So other than the two spinners, the KKR bowlers combined for figures of 12-0-112-3. That included bowling ten wides. Similarly, RR had their heroes in Jaiswal (39) and Sooryavanshi (46), but went from 81 for 0 in the ninth over to 155 for 9 in 20. All this indicates it's a slow, spin-friendly pitch, where run-scoring won't be easy - not least for a new batter. But will KKR finally win? Join Vishal for the chase.

commentTextItems.html: top edge, six, Rinku's fifty, and KKR's first win this season!! Eden turns purple with a million KKR flags fluttering in the air. It was a short delivery from Brijesh, and Rinku went for the pull. But the ball ballooned off the top edge, and went over Jurel to land just beyond the boundary. The seventh-wicket pair of Rinku and Anukul takes KKR to their first win in seven attempts

commentPostTextItems.html: A last-over thriller at Eden is done. Both teams had their chances and moments, but, of course, only one could win. RR's bowler missed their lengths in the final overs, as Rinku ran riot. KKR show it's never too late to win, and move up from the bottom place in the points table. You can now follow PBKS vs LSG from New Chandigarh, as we wrap this one up. See you! Varun Chakravarthy is the Player of the Match: "Fells great. Before I talk about myself, I have to give credit to the entire coaching staff. There was too much outside noise. We deserve this win. I still have two fractures in my left hand. It's a little tough, but I'm still trying to manager. It was a little slow, but perfectly suitable for us. We don't know where we'll end up, but we're making a statement that we're not pushovers." Ajinkya Rahane: "Really happy to be here. Feels really good. There were a lot of emotions during the game. I'm really happy for Rinku, Anukul and Varun. The way Varun bowled... Anukul had a fantastic domestic competition. Most of the practice sessions, we have had conversations. It's about reading the situation well. Cricket is a simple game. This victory will give us confidence. The bowlers are coming nicely together. Batting wise, we can still improve. Kartik Tyagi has been really good. Since the practice games we played, he has been really clear about what he wants to do in the middle. He's still young, but the confidence he has is amazing. Really happy to see him gaining that confidence as a fast bowler. There's lots to learn. Batting wise, we've had a bad powerplay for the last three games. Sometimes I feel strike rate is over rated. A wicket like this... we saw what happened today. This was a great escape for us. As a batting unit, we need to learn very quickly. We'll get those five or six extra days now... The atmosphere we have is very amazing. The fans have been fantastic throughout. Last five games were really bad for us. This victory belongs to them. They have been amazing and very positive. You get those positive vibes." Time for the presentations Rinku Singh: "When runs don't come, you start thinking. It was not that I was hesitating in hitting my shots. The mindset was to take it till the end. You play those shots [when he was dropped off a no-look slog] when your mind isn't working. God helped me. It was a very good innings for my confidence. The win will give us a lot of confidence. We'll look to carry this momentum forward." Riyan Parag: "We assessed it was a 170 wicket. So we were dead under par. It was our game. No excuses there. We can't be dropping catches. We can't be bowling lines that favour the batsmen. There was a lot of spin on the wicket. The way Jaddu, Bishi and Punja bowled, I thought the way forward was spin [and hence he bowled an over]. Brijesh was almost there to bowl the 14th and the 16th [overs] as well. But they lost wickets and there were left-handers. So I bowled... Once Bishnoi's over was done, I felt spinners might go [for runs] here given the left-handers. I feel the game plan was there. It was a 170 wicket... we tried giving ourselves time, but it didn't come off. I felt Punja bowled really well. There were a few nerves in his first over." 7.17pm Rinku was dropped on 8 when Burger spilled a sitter. At that stage, KKR were 73 for 5 in 11 overs. They needed another 83 runs off 54 balls, with an out-of-form Rinku in the middle. But what a role luck plays in sport! Rinku ended up unbeaten on 53 off 34 deliveries, and added a match-turning 76 for the seventh wicket with Anukul, whose big hits may be forgotten amid Rinku's more impactful knock. KKR, though, are now on the board as a result of this win.

commentPreTextItems.html: 7.29pm Thanks Ekanth. And Vihaan, yes, fingers firmly crossed man! Anyway, here's Prabhsimran Singh - a man in stunning form - and Priyansh Arya - who is not doing too bad himself - against one of the new-ball masters in Mohammed Shami. Here we go Vihaan Patel : "please arsenal don't bottle the league. we need this for everyone to stop making fun of us. please beat city " Abhimanyu is better placed to comment on this. Here he comes minutes before the first ball fairoos: "LSG has 5 specialist bowlers " Yep, they'll have seven batters. That could go either way especially if it's a big chase Karan: "It's a nervy Sunday night where Arsenal fighting for premier league with odds stacked against them. " Angad: "The match would be pretty much decided in first 30 mins, where the in- form LSG pacers will face in-form PBKS top order. Hope ae get a high-scoring thriller today" Would balance things out after a low-scoring thriller LSG Impact options - Himmat Singh, Abdul Samad, Matthew Breetzke, Mayank Yadav, Digvesh Rathi LSG XI 1 Mitchell Marsh, 2 Ayush Badoni, 3 Rishabh Pant (Capt, wk),4 Aiden Markram, 5 Nicholas Pooran, 6 Mukul Choudhary, 7 Mohammed Shami, 8 Avesh Khan, 9 Prince Yadav, 10 M Siddharth, 11 Mohsin Khan PBKS Impact options - Vijaykumar Vyshak, Harpreet Brar, Suyansh Shedge, Yash Thakur, Vishnu Vinod PBKS XI: 1 Prabhsimran Singh (wk), 2 Priyansh Arya, 3 Cooper Connolly, 4 Shreyas Iyer (Capt), 5 Nehal Wadhera, 6 Shashank Singh, 7 Marcus Stoinis, 8 Marco Jansen, 9 Xavier Bartlett, 10 Arshdeep Singh, 11 Yuzvendra Chahal Shreyas: Don't mind losing the toss. Great challenge for us. This will give an idea of how to go in the first innings. You keep getting better every now and then, it's us vs us, not about the opponents. We'll triumph if we stay in the present. We've played many games, but still there is a moment we haven't fulfilled. Hope this is the game where we can get a comprehensive win. No changes Rishabh: Coming here, we want them to set a total. They've been one of the best tournaments. When you have transparency, you can have hard conversations. Generally, playing for 220 is better than playing for 200. Siddharth comes in, Rathi misses out. Elbow is much better 7pm Team batting first have won 3, and chasing have won 6 in IPL games since 2025 at this ground. Toss time. Shreyas spins the coin, heads called. It's heads, LSG bowl Sarvir: "Last year Arshdeep dismissed Marsh for ducks in both the matches and the former is back in form too." VS: "I'm looking forward to Mukul Chaudhary's batting" Pitch and conditions: It's been hot in the last two days. The pitch is brand new. From the North end, the square boundaries are 61 and 70 metres. Eoin Morgan says there have been seven 200-plus scores in 13 games here. Lowest score in them is 80, highest in the 220s. There is a nice covering grass with the odd crack. It should be consistent. There might be swing as it's humid. Dew not a concern, so toss won't matter too much. Likely to be a high-scoring game. 6:40pm Lucknow Super Giants are coming off a couple of convincing losses. Their middle order is in a rut. Rishabh Pant's promotion to No. 3 hasn't worked, and it's left Nicholas Pooran batting out of position. He wasn't in form as is, and the poor start has magnified his troubles. Will they change their approach or personnel? If not, for how long will they stick with what's currently in place? By the way, the afternoon game between KKR and RR is closing towards a tense finish. Follow the low-scoring thriller here. There's a live blog for highlights too Rachit: "A lot has been said about Iyer's captaincy, batting and even fielding but much of the less talked fact is his luck with the tosses. Last year as well he won more than tosses and in this year too won all of them except one." Samar: "I still feel Stoinis has been underused if he's not bowling. Someone like Omarzai can swing the new ball and bowl middle overs too and can even bat well." Stoinis also adds batting depth, at least theoretically, and is more experienced. Doubt they'll change things for now Akshat: "There were 2 back to back seasons where PBKS didn't register 2 consecutive wins. Now they have 5 wins in succession. We used to dream for days like this " Preview by Shashank Kishore LSG in need of batting lift against red-hot Punjab Kings 6:30pm There's only one team in IPL 2026 that's undefeated so far - last year's finalists Punjab Kings. They've won five of their six games and if it wasn't for rain, it would have been six out of six. Their batting was always set, the bowling is also strong. It was challenged in the last couple of games and they've found Shashank SIngh, who's coming in and getting set batters. They're the team that have all bases covered and will go in as favourites at home against Lucknow Super Giants today.
