commentTextItems.html: Stunnig bowling! Near yorker. 137ks low full toss on leg, flicked through midwicket. Pooran ran in and threw it on the bounce over leg stump. Pant whips off the bail... no, it was a direct hit replay shows. Five off the last over, effectively a maiden

commentPostTextItems.html: Govind: "What's the plus sign next to Prabhsimran's name in the scorecard" Wicketkeeper. Abhimanyu, our opening bowler, opening batter, premier allrounder, will be back for the chase. ashish: "Last 5 over run rate is lesser than overall rate. That shows punjab slowed just a little. Will it hurt them? Going by how Lsg batters have gone this season, i will give punjab the upper hand unless Pant says enough is enough and pulls himself and his team up and over." Hajam Zakir : "Peshawar Zalmi 255/7 beat Punjab Kings 254/7 by 1 run." Cooper Connolly Feels like a nice wicket, won't judge it till two wickets followed. Will back the bowlers, looking forward to get stuck in. I was playing the ball on merit early, 19 off 22 was panic stations, gave myself a chance to hit sixes late. Once you hit a couple of balls off the middle, you start feeling the flow. Priyansh doesn't say much to me, hits the ball far, world-class batter. 9:19pm Tough pitch to bat, Ball holding, flying through unpredictably, so much spin, how will another run ever be scored? You know, run fests in T20s are derided sometimes, and it's understandable, but gotta say, this was fun. It was a rough start for PBKS as Shami nicked off Prabhsimran early and Connolly took time to get set. Priyansh, though, got off to a flier and hit sixes at will. The carnage went next level in the back-ten overs. The first three, in fact, went for 69! Four of the last ten overs went under seven or less, yet PBKS made 154 in the phase. It was because Priyansh and Connolly didn't care for line or length and just mullered every ball out of sight. Word of praise for Prince Yadav who nailed his yorkers and finished with an economy of just 6.25.

commentPostTextItems.html: Yookay, weekend ends, fourth game. Fair to say a predictable result but the journey, in the first-innings particularly, was riveting. Join us tomorrow for a new week of adventures. Thanks for tagging along. From Abhimanyu, me, Thilak and Ranjith, take the care, bye! Priyansh Arya, POTM After the powerplay, I contributed today and that was special. I don't practice six-hitting, I try to time the ball as well as possible. Anand sir and Birla sir, our trainers send us schedules and I follow it. That helps me keep fit. I don't too much with in the middle as that keeps my mind free. I slashed one over point, that's my favourite shot. Shreyas Iyer, PBKS captain Exceptional partnership, some shots were jaw-dropping. Hitting fast bowlers off the back-foot straight. Composure in the middle overs was sensational. Was talking with Cooper and Arya, said let's compete in the side for the most no. of sixes. They're up for it. Prize is my bat, doesn't make sense but as long as we're all performing I'm happy. When you let players be, I think they just deliver. That's our mantra. I don't tell them how to go about their specific innings, they have their patterns set. Ricky motivates just before the game, I chip, boys come in and deliver. Majority of our bowlers are international bowlers with immense experience. We have plans against certain batters, it's all about execution. They just shouldn't get complacent. (Home ground a fortress?) Yes, I feel when we see the wicket, we feel immense pleasure to be part of the team. Last year, we had to brainstorm about how we'll come this season and how the wicket supports our batters and bowlers, so far so good. Presentation time. If you're licking your lips that's fair, Shreyas will come in first. Viraj: "Why has lsg not fixed their batting order. Too much chopping and changing. Never gonna work in IPL " Pravin Jadhav : "The review which was not taken that cost LSG this match and 2 Points!" Vyshak Vijaykumar There's a lot of planning from the coaches and video analysts. Without them backing me, it'd be tough. Last two games didn't go well. Prince bowled well, took cues from him. Backed yorkers and slower ones. The way our batters played, it was something to watch out for. Every ball looked like it'll go for six. Video analysts said length ball doesn't do well here, so went shorter. The approach is the same, whatever is the situation and how many ever overs I bowl I want to do well. The last two games when we didn't do well, Shashank came in, so it's not a given that everyone gets four overs. We would like to continue this form and go on to win the finals. Rishabh Pant, LSG captain Left hand is getting better, got a new tattoo today. Something to look forward to. It's difficult to point out one area, bowler's have done well. There have been areas of concern, some positivity with the batting. (Badoni opening) The idea was to go out and play freely. It was pre-decided, not a decision taken today. Tried to take the pressure off the top order. We believe in the team, but credit to PBKS for playing good, hard cricket. Great visuals of Shreyas laughing with and hugging Shashank during the handshakes. Ponting's jovial too. Poor Shashank hides his face for a moment but lets a smile out. 11:21pm The win margin could've been 20-25 more had the catching been clean but otherwise that was a clinical performance from PBKS. Particularly with the ball. Didn't let Badoni, promoted to open, and Marsh early on despite the boundaries looking convincing. The pressure of the asking rate was always going to be high, it was 15.3 after ten overs and 22.6 after 15. Pant swung a lot, got a few but couldn't surge on that deep incline. Pooran's bad run continued, Markram did okay from No. 5 but couldn't LSG get close. Vyshak was the pick of the bowlers, bowled into the pitch and yorked it nicely. Chahal ripped it and revved it. Bartlett missed his lengths at times but bowled across phases. Arshdeep and Jansen didn't swing it much but showed decent control.

commentPreTextItems.html: QdK takes strike first up. Siraj with the new ball. Let's play! 7.20pm You can hope over to Monga's Live Report to get in-depth analysis as the game proceeds. Most likely, we will see Malewar and QdK up top. It's been musical chairs for MI at the top of the order. What can Malewar do with the chance? He knows he's likely to drop back to the bench if and when Rohit is match-fit again... Here's our trusty knower-at-large Shashwat Kumar with a primer on Malewar: A lot of people might know Malewar from his red-ball exploits for Vidarbha and Central Zone in the most recent domestic season. He currently averages a little under 50 in FC cricket and has already made his mark with several noteworthy performances. But he has shown a different side - an evolution to adapt to the frenetic nature of the shortest format - to his game too. He, like Praful Hinge, who made headlines on debut, can be considered another star of the inaugural edition of the Vidarbha Pro T20 League. Meanwhile, Mohammed Siraj has been the quiet leader of this GT line-up. And there's Kagiso Rabada too... They've played a vital hand in GT's three wins in the game so far. Will they take the new ball today as well? Mathi: "Abhijato, waited for a day to talk about Arsenal bottling...." - Wait on. I'm not talking about it. Next! 7.10pm Hello then. Two spinners - Ghazanfar and Santner - in the MI side. Let's see how that plays out for them. Rohit : "No Rohit..seriously?" - No kidding, cross my heart! He's still out with his injury. Probably be assessed on the sidelines before the next game, and so on and so forth until the issue's resolved. Sumedh : "So who is MI's impact player here? Ashwani I'm guessing?" - Most likely. But you can never tell. Depends on how the pitch plays. Daniel : "Where is Will Jacks?" - Not in the eleven, that's for sure... Hafiz Muhammad : "Strange tactics by MI , they option to go with two overseas spinners despite there is chance of dew in later part they should go with bosch in first xi and used AM Ghanzanfar as Sub after seeing the condition." - They've made the call now. Let's see how it goes. Melissa: "Where's Ricky Rickleton for MI?" - He's made way for QdK. He did make a century last match. Right then, the toss is done and we have the team news. Two debutants to look forward to. Say hello to Abhijato now, and let him know what you think of MI's team selection. Gujarat Titans XI: Shubman Gill (capt), B Sai Sudharsan, Jos Buttler (wk), Glenn Phillips, Washington Sundar, Shahrukh Khan, Rashid Khan, Mohammed Siraj, Kagiso Rabada, Prasidh Krishna, Ashok Sharma GT Impact Player options: Rahul Tewatia, Jason Holder, Anuj Rawaat, Kulwant Khejroliya, Manav Suthar Mumbai Indians XI: Danish Malewar, Quinton de Kock (wk), Naman Dhir, Suryakumar Yadav, Hardik Pandya (capt), Tilak Varma, Sherfane Rutherford, Mitchell Santner, Krish Bhagat, Jasprit Bumrah, AM Ghazanfar MI Impact Player options: Raj Bawa, Ashwani Kumar, Corbin Bosch, Mayank Rawat, Raghu Sharma 7pm And it's now toss time. Gill gives it a toss, Pandya calls heads. Tails it is. Gujarat Titans will bowl first. Gill says wicket looks decent, but there was dew in the last game and so they'd prefer to chase. GT are unchanged. Pandya says MI would have bowled as well. "Last game was tough for us as a group. We had to regroup and speak about what Mumbai Indians stand for and how we want to play," he says. "We need to play overall better cricket. I can't pinpoint one factor. We win together, we lose together. We have to get better as a group. Couple of debuts. Danish makes his debut, and Krish as well who was part of our support bowlers and really impressed us. Got into the team three days back and he's playing today, such is life." No Rohit Sharma. Vicky: "@Nilashish - In short you have mentioned that almost their entire Playing XI is the problem :)" 6.50pm Looks like MI are ringing in a few changes. Batter Danish Malewar and medium pacer Krish Bhagat, who was signed as Atharva Ankolekar's replacement, have got caps before the Mumbai Indians huddle. This is then set to be T20 debuts for both of them, let alone IPL debuts. Malewar was the second-highest run-scorer in the Vidarbha Pro T20, and had the highest strike rate among the top-ten scorers. Meanwhile, Dale Steyn reckons it's a very "fascinating" pitch. He says it looks like a "Western Australia, Perth wicket". There are cracks on there, but he reckons the pitch will play well and suggests teams batting first have a chance of piling on runs. Deep Dasgupta adds that teams have to get above the 180-mark, and close to the 200-mark to feel safe, and anything below 180 could spell trouble. Nilashish: "MI's problem lies in1. Overseas Combination 2. Lackluster Boom and Boult3. Form of Tilak, Surya and Hardik4. No Indian Spin optionsAm I missing something?" Parthi: "Hi Abhimanyu, Mi already struggling to put a right path in their game, Hope return of Ro-hit will guide to winning path." 6.40pm Gujarat Titans are a team that function on stability. Mumbai Indians, despite so many similarities to their side from the last time they won the title, have struggled to find stability of their own. Hoping for repeat of the same." 6.30pm It's Match 30 of IPL 2026, and it's Mumbai Indians travelling to Gujarat Titans' home, looking for a reversal in fortunes. They started the season with a win, but have lost four on the trot since to be placed bottom of the table, although they have two games in hand over KKR who are in ninth place and one game in hand over CSK and LSG. commentTextItems.html: That's some way to get your maiden IPL century! Swings a short ball over square leg and it's been an innings of struggle and redemption! He was on 19 off 22, and he finishes unbeaten on 101 off 45! The second timeout break changed everything for him, and he's managed to single-handedly take Mumbai Indians to a very competitive score!

commentPostTextItems.html: Kagiso Rabada: "I'm just glad that all the hard work paid off. We had them under a lot of pressure but good knock from Tilak. [On his pace] The secret is that they are just ramping up the speed guns. I've felt good for a while now. I feel everything is working out for the last three games. Some days you bowl a heap of bad stuff and get wickets and some days you bowl well and get runs. I'm just glad it's going my way a little bit. Bowling with the new ball, you want to get all kinds of dismissals. I think that's the art of bowling, is controlling length and line. You do that for long enough and you'll get rewarded." 9.20pm Well, that was an innings of two halves. Kagiso Rabada was all over Mumbai Indians, and the bottom-placed team were 44 for 3. Naman Dhir and Tilak then helped them stabilise, but Tilak was struggling to get going. But then, after the 14th over, Tilak took off, going 6, 4, 4 against Prasidh and he never looked back. He had the fastest acceleration after 20 balls (where 50 runs or more were scored by a batter after the 20-ball mark) in IPL history, and only the fourth IPL centurion from No. 5 or lower. Whatever the GT bowlers threw at him, he had answers for. And now GT have a tough chase on their hands. Abhijato will be back with you soon for the that.

And that's crashing into middle and leg, so Mumbai Indians end their losing streak with a 99-run win, the biggest this season by runs. Mumbai Indians are off the bottom of the table, thanks to Tilak Varma's stunning come-from-behind century and a commanding bowling display.

commentPostTextItems.html: 11.25pm Right then, Mumbai Indians came to a ground they struggle in while in the midst of a slump, but have pulled off a victory in some style. Tilak Varma of course at the heart of it, after Kagiso Rabada made it look like MI's troubles would continue. GT now are left with questions about how to respond when their top three don't fire. For today, that's all the action from the Motera. On behalf of Abhijato, our own Thilak and everyone else at ESPNcricinfo, it's Abhimanyu signing off. 11.17pm PResentation ceremony time Tilak Varma: "Of course, first 100 will be always special. It was very important for us. We don't have much time from here. Every game is important for us. Last five games i haven't had much time in the middle. So this game I wanted to spend time in the middle. So you saw first 20 balls I was just batting ball by ball. And then later on I knew the ability I have. I was just seeing the situation and what the team needs and I was just stable and keeping my head still and following my basics. I have all the fancy shots. But when the team is under pressure it's just about backing your skills and today it's given me good results. [Partnership with Dhir] It was very important. The way Naman played with positive intent, credit goes to him." Hardik Pandya: "It's always challenging to go away and win but at the same time of time Ahmedabad has been a tough place for Mumbai Indians. We played some good cricket. Feels very special because it was much needed. [On the second timeout] The message I think, I realised that the kind of talent Tilak has, he really doesn't have to worry. So my message to him was just watch the ball and hit the ball. Was about time he came out and delivered. It was much needed for Tilak, the group and Mumbai Indians. [Bumrah wicket] It's quite fascinating. I see a lot of people asking why Jassi isn't bowled up front but he's only bowled 7-8 times the first over. So it's not a Hardik Pandya problem, it's an everybody proble, because Bumrah is so special you want to use him later on. [On youngsters doing well] Really amazing. Ashwani did the same last year. Amazing from the youngsters. Fielding had to click. Special mention to Naman as well. [Is this that game?] Yes." Ashish: "Such a good looking score. 100 for 10. All binary." As we wait for the presentation ceremony, Sampath has some stats for you. Tilak Varma is the first MI batter to outscore opposition in IPL. Lendl Simmons missed out in 2017, when he scored 66 and DD made 66 in reply. Tilak also first player to outscore opposition in the IPL since KL Rahul vs RCB in 2020 - 132* vs 109. Ashwani Kumar: "When we went on the ground I saw length balls would work best so just went for those. I planned with Hardik bhaiiya and bowled as per what the situation demanded. I had been thinking for a while that whenever I get a game, I'll do well. It happened like that last year as well." Shubman Gill: "Honestly, I think we gave away too many runs in the middle overs. On a wicket like that, 160-170 was a par score. Small hiccup but now we have a couple of games on the road so hopefully we'll come back in winning form. I think the wicket was on the slower side. I don't think we hit the right areas. Length balls, some were coming on nicely some weren't. We weren't able to hit that length more consistently. I think batting could have been better because there was dew." 11.05 Well, what a win that is for Mumbai Indians. If they were struggling for answers and struggling for confidence earlier, today solves a lot of their problems. Tilak Varma went through a period of immense struggle but then it brought out the very best of him as he hammered his maiden century. He made 19 off his first 22 balls, and then hit 82 off the next 23. Then, Jasprit Bumrah, Hardik Pandya and Ashwani Kumar removed GT's vaunted top three in the powerplay, and after that, it was easy pickings with the hosts offering little resistance.

commentPreTextItems.html: 7.28pm Rightio, here come the Mumbai Indians fielders followed by the two CSK openers, Ruturaj Gaikwad and Sanju Samson. Jasprit Bumrah will once again bowl the first over. He finally broke the duck in the previous game. Can he find some movement? Bumrah is over the wicket to Samson with a slip in place. Nandagopal: "I like this from CSK. Kartik Sharma lost his place since Sarfaraz started well, now comes back into the XI at the next opportunity. It should do his confidence a world of good, if he can contribute today." 7.20pm Thanks, Abhi. Hello, everyone. Time for El Clasico of the IPL, or has this game lost it's sheen. That's a discussion for another day. For now, time to dig in and enjoy what should be a solid game. VS: "Why no urvil Patel?" Yeah, it's a it bit surprising to me too. ShahA: "After looking at the last game that MI played, they were much more confident and energetic. Looks like they are back and would be a team to beat." 7.10pm So, no Rohit Sharma and no MS Dhoni still. Danish Malewar will likely slot in as MI's Impact Player at the top of the order when they start their chase. Gaikwad said Veer is in for Short, but it's actually Kartik Sharma who's in the team list. Veer is on the impact Player list, but CSK will likely bring on Akeal Hosein or Matt Henry, depending on the captions. Time to say hello to Ashish now. Ashish, what do you make of the lineups? Here are the teams. MI XI: Quinton de Kock (wk), Naman Dhir, Suryakumar Yadav, Tilak Varma, Hardik Pandya (capt), Sherfane Rutherford, Mitchell Santner, Krish Bhagat, Jasprit Bumrah, AM Ghazanfar, Ashwani Kumar Impact Player options: Will Jacks, Raj Bawa, Shardul Thakur, Danish Malewar, Mayank Rawat CSK XI: Ruturaj Gaikwad (capt), Sanju Samson (wk), Sarfaraz Khan, Dewald Brevis, Shivam Dube, Kartik Sharma, Jamie Overton, Anshul Kamboj, Noor Ahmad, Gurjapneet Singh, Mukesh Choudhary Impact Player options: Prashant Veer, Matt Short, Matt Henry, Akeal Hosein, Urvil Patel 7pm It's toss time with Ravi Shastri out in the middle. Tails is the call, heads it is. Mumbai Indians will bowl. Pandya says it looks green, like the one against KKR, but says that one played well. Mumbai Indians are unchanged. Gaikwad says he would have bowled, but it was a 50-50 call as it looks like a good pitch. Veer comes in in place of Short, Gaikwad says. 6.50pm Here's some CSK news while we wait: Akash Madhwal has been signed as Ayush Mhatre's replacement. Vishal with more inputs from the ground: "Looks like CSK will make a change in the bowling attack then - Akeal Hosein, who picked a three-for when he was last here during the recent T20 World Cup, has marked his run up. Let's see which overseas player they leave out." He also adds that Rohit has finally emerged from the dugout. 6.40pm "No signs of Ro-Dho yet," Vishal says from the Wankhede. The two of them were the focal point of Karthik Krishnaswamy's preview, but it also explores who CSK can bring in for Mhatre, how MI can fit in Will Jacks and much more. Dimath K: "We're going to see MI's strongest playing XII today (HAH. This wont get published tho)" -- Well, it just did Dimath. Sanket: "Mi should get Jacks here in place of Rutherfort. firstly Rutherford is batting way to down the oder so more often than not getting an enough balls to make an impact secondly Jack has been in prolific form batting at that lower order position. Also he gives that bowling option even though it's hard to use against csk considering they are stacked with right handed batters and then there is Dube as well." 6.35pm Ricky: "is the BIG guy playing today? we all know who HE is." Could be either one of the two big guys! That's the question everyone is asking, and well, we still don't know! Yuvi: "Whatever the situation, always it lifts me up when these 2 giants meet. Its a different feeling. Cant wait. " Vishal Dikshit is at the ground today, and here he is reporting early: "The biggest day for Wankhede! With the fourth game in Mumbai this IPL comes the big one of MI vs CSK, the most talked about rivalry of the league. It's somehow not as hot and muggy as it usually is in Mumbai in April end as plenty of fans have already taken their seats. No surprises a lot of them in yellow with the number '7' written at the back. Which brings us to the big question - will Dhoni finally play today? He kept wickets in the nets day before, batted in the nets yesterday and hit some big ones beyond the boundary rope. The CSK players and coaches have just started coming down the stairs so no sign of him yet. For MI, no real signs of changes yet as Ashwani Kumar, who got a four-for against GT, recent debutant Krish Bhagat and Bumrah have marked their run ups so far." 6.30pm Hello, hello. It's time for IPL's El Clasico. Ten titles between Mumbai Indians and Chennai Super Kings, evenly spread out between these two teams. A long list of epic clashes. Two teams desperate for momentum. Rarely is it not an entertainer when these two teams clash, and hopefully, it should be the same today. Hello and welcome to ESPNcricinfo's live coverage of today's match. I'm Abhimanyu and I'll be joined soon by Ashish Pant as we become your eyes and ears from the Wankhede.

commentTextItems.html: Finishes it with a boundary! That's his second century of the season, his second for CSK and his fifth in the IPL! Takes on the short ball and nails the pull over square leg, and it lands just short of the boundary. Samson celebrates, and walks off, getting a hug from his India T20I captain Suryakumar Yadav as he does so. What a sublime innings this has been, and it's taken CSK to a fighting score of 207

commentPostTextItems.html: 9.20pm A solo effort from Sanju Samson - the next best score by a CSK batter was 22 - has taken CSK to 207, which will be much more challenging for Mumbai Indians than it could have been had Samson not played the knock he did. He kept going at a strike rate of over 200 but with wickets falling, he slowed down a touch but made sure to stick around and give CSK a strong finish and bring up two centuries in a season for the first time in his IPL career. Bumrah picked up a wicket, while AM Ghazanfar was arguably the pick of the bowlers. He was near impossible to hit, while picking up two wickets. Ashwani Kumar also picked up two wickets, to add to his four he took in the last game. Will the target be enough for CSK, or will MI chase this down? Find out with Ashish in just a bit. Ashwani Kumar: "[On the pitch] Back of length deliveries were sticking, so just bowled according to that. The full balls were coming on nicely to the bat but back of length deliveries were sticking. The target can be chased, given the wicket and the team we have. There's no dew right now but we could get some in the second innings. [Plan to Brevis] The plan was to use a slower bumper as per the wicket and that's what I did."

commentTextItems.html: Edged and taken! Chennai Super Kings have inflicted on Mumbai Indians their biggest defeat by runs in IPL history! Sanju Samson and Akeal Hosein the stars of a famous El Clasico triumph for Chennai Super Kings today. This was a back of length ball angled across and Bumrah tries to jab at it, ends up giving Samson a catch to wrap up a win that he started with the bat

commentPostTextItems.html: 11.45pm Right, then. The derby ends with CSK fans firmly in possession of the bragging rights. We saw some stunning batting from Samson today, and then a brilliant bowling display to deny Mumbai Indians even a sniff. CSK were on top of the chase from the very first over, and it's led to a commanding win. Join us tomorrow for more IPL action. For now, on behalf of Ashish Pant, Thilak Ram and everyone else, it's Abhimanyu signing off. Night! 11.35pm Time for the presentation ceremony. The player of the match is Sanju Samson: "Really feels great to score a century at the Wankhede against MI. Definitely a special moment for me and the team. I am trying to keep things simple. Today the wicket wasn't a normal Wankhede wicket. The ball was holding. So from there it was just about assessing what the team needed to do. We were losing few wickets so I thought it was important for a settled batsman to stay and that's what I tried and that's what happened today. The game tells you what to do. You don't have to come with a preconceived mindset or premeditate that this is how I play and this is what I do. It is my responsibility to understand the game situation and what the team demands and plan around it. If we didn't have a fall of wickets, I'd have gone a bit more earlier, but with the fall of wickets it was important to finish well. It's a very young team but the character and attitude we have shown, even after three losses in the team, is very commanding. We want to build from here. But we know every team is very strong and have intensity, so we just have to enjoy what's going on at the moment." Ruturaj Gaikwad: "[On Mukesh] Pretty tough on him. Hats off to him, coming in that situation it takes a lot mentally. He came back for the team, for the franchise because he knew we needed him. All glory to him. We all wanted to be there for him and chipped away for him. [How does the win feel?] Feels good. I was still 50-50 at the toss. My gut feeling was saying we should bat first because it was a bit green but also a bit dry. We had to assess in the first couple of overs. Me and Sanju said it's not coming on nicely so anywhere around 200 would be good. And then Akeal and Noor did well. Everyone chipped in well. Sanju also played a magnificent knock. He's been in fantastic touch. And our bowling was improving from our earlier games. I feel we are just starting to click. [On the bowling] I think we are headed in a direction where we are trying to cover all bases. Mukesh to get that wicket early set the momentum. And Anshul is always doing well. Jamie, whenever the wicket has pace and bounce, Jamie and Gurjapneet are the ones who can take wickets in the middle. Everyone is settling and getting in their roles and know what to do. [Returning to Chepauk] Got to start from zero, start from assessing again. We enjoy this win but keep it aside and make sure we're ready for the next one." Hardik Pandya: "The powerplay, losing early wickets it's always going to be tricky. We couldn't cope after that. We should have just batted better. They batted on the same pitch. Just that Sanju played an outstanding knock and their batters kept coming and chipping away to a decent total. For us to chase it down we had to have a good powerplay and have the momentum but it didn't work out. [On changing personnel] That will be the chat, going back to the drawing board and seeing what we can do." Akeal Hosein: "The wicket was offering both. Some were swinging and gripping as well. So I wanted to use the conditions. That was definitely the plan, to stay on the stumps. If they hit you off the stumps, then kudos to them. I think one thing that sticks with me is what Dwayne Bravo says. That if you're going to bowl in the powerplay you're going to hit so you have to get that out of your mind. [On Noor Ahmad] Always a pleasure to see Noor doing his thing. Happy to see him successful again tonight." 11.25pm A sensational individual effort with the bat from Sanju Samson was followed up with a brilliant team display with the ball as CSK hammered Mumbai Indians by 103 runs. It's MI's worst defeat in the IPL and also the first time they've slumped to three consecutive defeats at the Wankhede in a single season. Samson was the architect with his unbeaten 101, when everyone around him was reduced to cameos at best. Then Akeal Hosein led the bowling display, finishing with a four-wicket haul, while Noor Ahmad's two wickets in two balls also helped kill off the chase. It was an emotional day for Mukesh Choudhary as well, who picked an early wicket, playing just days after his mother's passing. The win has fired CSK up to fifth, while Mumbai Indians' momentum is halted after just one win.

commentPreTextItems.html: The openers walking out. Bhuvi with the new ball. Let's play! Abhilash: "we have reached that stage of IPL where no more neutral fans exists.. everyone need a result favoring their team.. GO RCB" - Take off your IPL jersey as a fan and there's always another one underneath. Navin Daga: "My last 4 for this year : PBKS, RCB, RR, DC / GT in that order. Hopefully DC's 1 run won't haunt them to tilt it towards GT" - Four from the top or four from the bottom, Navin! 7.25pm Just five minutes away from play. Professor: "It's time for the last year's orange cap holder Sai Sudharshan to put up his hand seriously. He is yet to make a meaningful contribution this year." - GT will twiddle their thumbs and hope he comes good. Ram: "Yup, Tewatia the finisher with a mind boggling SR of close to 100, so difficult to find those gems." - No Iceman slander when I'm at the helm. Next please! Pranav : "Looking forward to Jason Holder vs Tim David, just because of his 3 sixes in an over in IPL 2023!" - Absolute cinema loading. Here's Ashish Pant's cracking interview with David. Dip in before play gets underway. Amit Rana, the umpire, making his IPL debut today by the way. 7.10pm Hello hello! From one Abhi to another, it is then. The inbox looks juicy, so let's dip into it: Ryan: "Why is Bethell in the impact subs? He's a good bowler and fielder..." - They won't need him till the chase. Maybe they just want to hedge their bets and see how the conditions play out before they bring him in. If they named him straightaway, they'd lock up that combination before they sussed out conditions Deepak Gupta: "Can't understand why Tewatia is always in playing XI for GT. He never bowls, not a gun fielder and one dimensional batsmen completely out of form and out of depth. How long can GT continue to back him up!" - I wonder if anyone's ever invested in an uncapped finisher in a franchise league as much as GT have in Tewatia. A very specialised role... Anand: "Happy Birthday Sachin Ramesh Tendulkar!" - Happy birthday! Fun fact: saw my first ever live game, as a kid, on this day in 2013. It was Sachin's birthday and MI were playing KKR at Eden Gardens. The crowd sung him happy birthday. The bigger surprise was when Rohit Sharma stepped out for the toss in place of Ponting... Ishaan: "This season is just getting interesting.. will be interesting to see if teams like MI can come back. My bet for top 4 is RCB, RR, PBKS, MI. Opinions?" - MI in the top four... Hmm, big call, despite their affinity for ridiculous comebacks 7.07pm So, Jacob Bethell has been named in the Impact Player list, so he is almost a lock-in to come in as RCB's Impact Player, while Prasidh Krishna will likely come in for GT when they bowl. Glenn Phillips and Ashok Kumar are the ones who have made way for Suthar and Holder for GT. Time for a change in the commentary box as well. Here comes Abhijato. Let him know what you all think about the teams and the impact of the toss. Here are the teams: RCB: 1 Virat Kohli, 2 Devdutt Padikkal, 3 Rajat Patidar (capt), 4 Tim David, 5 Jitesh Sharma (wk), 6 Romario Shepherd, 7 Krunal Pandya, 8 Bhuvneshwar Kumar, 9 Suyash Sharma, 10 Josh Hazlewood, 11 Rasikh Dar Impact Player options: Jacob Bethell, Jordan Cox, Mangesh Yadav, Vicky Ostwal, Venkatesh Iyer GT: 1 Shubman Gill (capt), 2 B Sai Sudharsan, 3 Jos Buttler (wk), 4 Washington Sundar, 5 Jason Holder, 6 Shahrukh Khan, 7 Rahul Tewatia, 8 Rashid Khan, 9 Kagiso Rabada, 10 Mohammed Siraj 11 Manav Suthar Impact Player options: Prasidh Krishna, Anuj Rawat, Glenn Phillips, Nishant Sindhu, Arshad Khan 7pm Time for the toss. Patidar gives it a spin. Gill calls tails, and heads it is. RCB will bowl first. Phil Salt picked up an injury so Jacob Bethell is in. Patidar says the first innings, the pitch might be a little tacky. Shubman Gill says it looks like an even wicket. Jason Holder and Manav Suthar are in for GT. The pitch is expected to be a good batting track, that won't turn. 6.54pm Jason Holder has just received his cap from Kagiso Rabada. Looks like the West Indies allrounder is set for his first appearance of the season. VS: "Fans' wishes are answered. Holder is playing. Good luck" Johann: "@Paul, no one gets into an IPL team on the strength of their fielding alone. Philips has had opportunity to make an impact with the bat and he has failed. GT needs another bowling option as their back-up for the opening bowlers have not been good enough. Holder ticks both those boxes and is a pretty good fielder himself. GT should not wait until too late before trying something different." 6.45pm The GT middle order has the fewest runs (288) of all teams this season, and the second-lowest average (20.57). It also has just the one half-century between them, the joint-lowest. But that middle order has also faced the second-fewest balls all season, 214, only higher than Punjab Kings (202). Himanshu Agrawal explores how GT's middle order is undercooked and underwhelming. Sai: "Toss could be vital today. Between RCB and GT the team that has won the toss has chosen to bowl and has won every time." Paul: "I have to disagree with the sentiment of 'swapping' GP with Jason Holder, based purely on GP's average batting stats thus far. Swapping the 2 would need careful consideration, given who tops this table." 6.40pm Tim David was instrumental in RCB's title-winning season last year. This year too, he's continued on his merry, destructive ways. Ashish Pant caught up with him and David spoke to him about his T20 mantra, life as a cricketing freelancer and more. That's another must-read for you all right here. 6.35pm Will RCB stick with Romario Shepherd or bring in Jacob Bethell? Are Gujarat Titans going to tinker with their middle order to try and shore up their batting? And what sixy milestone is Virat Kohli close to achieving? Find out all of that in Shashank Kishore's preview, which should be on top of your reading material ahead of today's clash. Himanshu Agrawal is reporting from the ground for us today, and here's what he has to say: "Bengaluru has been unusually dry and humid this summer. But RCB's final game at the Chinnaswamy this season means it's the fans' last chance to catch the national icon Virat Kohli live in action in the city this season. Kohli is up against India's next superstar Shubman Gill tonight, but not a shade of blue is visible in and around the stadium. A thundering roar resonates here while a few hundred phones flash up as the crowd spots Kohli walk out for practice. The stands are more than half full an hour ahead of the toss, and expect nothing less than a full house." 6.30pm Welcome to Match no. 34 in IPL 2026. Defending champions Royal Challengers Bengaluru are set to play their final league stage match at their home ground - the Chinnaswamy - and they take on Gujarat Titans. RCB will look to quickly bounce back from what they would think was a slight blip in their last game, while Gujarat Titans are also coming into this game on the back of a defeat, but a slightly more jarring one. Two powerful bowling attacks. Two batting line-ups where one is more balanced than the other, but both are equally capable of damaging oppositions. Strap in for yet another IPL classic on ESPNcricinfo's live commentary. I am Abhimanyu, and I will be joined today by Abhijato as we bring all the action to you.

commentPostTextItems.html: 9.17pm B Sai Sudharsan scored a fine century, as Gujarat Titans were 121 for no loss after 12 overs. But, from there, they could only get to 205, and it will surely bring up questions on whether they've actually gotten to a par score or are a few short and it will bring up questions again about their top-heavy approach. RCB will feel they did well to pull things back, although they ended up conceding an expensive final over, which was supposed to be bowled by Rasikh Salam but had to be bowled by Krunal due to cramps for Rasikh. Krunal also felt discomfort, and that may affect their chase. Sai Sudharsan seems to indicate it won't be easy getting runs on this pitch. We'll see how the RCB batters go soon enough. Join Abhijato in just a bit for the chase. B Sai Sudharsan: "It was always coming. I was touching the ball well in the last few innings and really grateful to God. Really happy to contribute to the team. I think with the level of communication we understood it was two-paced and sticky and it was a natural instinct to take the game deeper. [On his fist-pump celebration] I have such high standards for myself I want to always put my team in a good position. I've been starting well but not finishing well so it was more than just a century for me. I didn't try to take too much control of the innings and let go. I let it go really well today. I personally feel it is a really good score for the bowlers. Not so easy to play shots as it's not so true."

commentPostTextItems.html: 11.25pm So, Sai Sudharsan's century is pushed to being an afterthought after a swashbuckling chase from RCB that followed some great death bowling to pull Gujarat Titans back to 205 when, as Kohli said, they looked set for 230-plus at one stage. RCB continue to impress this season, with a superb all-round display. We are almost at the halfway stage of the league stage. Stay tuned on ESPNcricinfo for all the action coming you way over the weekend, the season's final double-double header, but that's all from us today. On behalf of Abhijato, Thilak, Sudeep and everyone else at ESPNcricinfo, it's Abhimanyu signing off. Good night! 11.20pm Time for the presentation ceremony. The POTM is... Virat Kohli, who also takes the Orange Cap: "To be honest, we had to assess the wicket early on because A) they have a quality bowling attack and B) chasing 200 in the Chinnaswamy, we were just one partnership away. This is the second time Dev has come and done this. You never see him slogging the ball yet he's playing so freely. His innings was the difference in the first half and then I was trying to stay in the game so he won't feel the pressure. Even in our bowling innings, we did well to pull things back. We were looking at 230-235 at one stage. The feedback was the pitch was not bad at all. Best batting conditions we've had this season. So if we stayed in the game long enough it would get tougher and tougher for bowlers. Dev was going great guns and the idea was to keep the pressure on the bowlers. There was intent, clarity and feedback from the other and and we didn't have any doubts in the partnership and that's what worked for us. The body language comes from a belief in your abilities and we have a tremendous batting lineup. If you look at the talent on display, we have guys who can play good cricket shots, you have the power of Tim David and Shepherd and then you have the smarts of Krunal. So the message is simple - you see a ball to hit, go for it because you have the depth. Firstly, we were quite happy we were able to play five games here and the fans get to see the team again. Special place to play cricket and hopefully we'll be able to come back and play here again later in the season." Rajat Patidar: "It was a tight match but a lot of learnings from this game. The way we started our bowling, the way Bhuvi and Hazlewood bowled was pretty good. After that, the way we came in, Suyash bowled very well. The yorkers bowled by Rasikh and Bhuvi were also very good to see. I think we made the target that if we can stop them around 200, it's a good total for us to chase down. The way the last few overs, according to our plans, the execution was spot on. The way they bowled their yorkers were very good which is why we stopped them around 205. The way Bethell and Vicky bhai [Kohli] have started was great and then the way Devdutt came in and played, quick and fiery was nice to see. But the way we lost wickets in the middle overs was a learning. We'll go back and see what errors we made" Devdutt Padikkal: "Feels great. Been working really hard to get where I am and I'm glad it's coming to good use. I think it's a lot to do with self belief that the management has given me. At the same time there are some technical changes i made in the last few years. You have to commit to those changes. Now I am getting the results. [On the six over cover vs Siraj] It was probably my favourite shot of the day for sure. At the end of the day, it's important I play according to the situation and assess what's going on out there. We were chasing 210 so we needed to make the most of the powerplay and keep the momentum up for the next few overs. I want to help finish games off so hopefully I can do that soon. We've seen what Tim, Romario and Jitesh are capable of down the order so with that kind of firepower, you have the freedom to go out and express yourself." Shubman Gill: "Definitely, I think from 16th to 19th we couldn't get any boundaries and couldn't get as many runs as we would have liked. Those were crucial overs for us. At the end of the powerplay we were in a good position and it was about taking wickets in the middle overs and were not able to after the powerplay got over. [The Kohli dropped chance] When a batsman gets dropped on nought it's always tough on the fielder but it's important how you come back into the game. We had our moments but we were not able to consistently able to hit the length balls. And I think they batted beautifully in the middle overs. [On giving the over to Suthar] When I batted the balls Krunal bowled, it was gripping a little bit so I thought maybe we could try and a few wickets would have brought back my game. [On Sai Sudharsan] he had been disappointed with how he got out in the last few games, but he bounced back. In the next match, hopefully he gives me a little bit more strike in the powerplay (chuckles)." Eric: "Conceding 287 to SRH a couple years back was the best thing to happen to RCB. It forced them to change the way they played and they have been the best team in the IPL since that day!" -- I mean, Punjab Kings have also been right up there since last season, but point taken. Vivaas: "Fitting Krunal finished off the game on a bouncer" 11pm Our preview billed this as a clash of contrasts and so it turned out to be. Gujarat Titans tried to play risk-free, with their openers putting on a 128-run stand in 12.4 overs. The pace they scored at meant their undercooked middle order had to finish the game hard, which they failed to do as RCB's wily bowlers pulled things back. RCB, in contrast, got going in the chase and never stopped. They kept going hard even when wickets were falling, and in the end, they end the day with a very convincing victory that shoots them up to second on the points table. The defending champions looking very much good for the money, like a team that can go ahead and do it all over again. For Gujarat Titans, the same questions that have hung around their heads from the start of the season will continue to haunt them. About their tempo. About their middle order. And if they need to adapt to play a more modern, aggressive brand of cricket.

In the meantime, check this out: Sruthi takes stock with lists of notable performances, players and stats here Abby: "Just came back home in Delhi after a visit to local market and IT IS HOT…respect to players, umps, groundsmen, media and everyone to put themselves out there in such heat…" Yeah, looked scary an hour ago. Clouds are passing by to offer some shadows and relief Sam: "Is Cooper Connolly fit to bowl?" Don't think so. There's been no announcement on it as far as I can tell dipan: "Same 12. Seven games. Zero panic. PBKS have turned team selection into a flex. " PBKS impact options - Nehal Wadhera, Suyansh Shedge, Vishnu Vinod, Harpreet Brar, Yash Thakur Punjab Kings 1 Prabhsimran Singh (wk), 2 Priyansh Arya, 3 Cooper Connolly, 4 Shreyas Iyer (capt), 5 Shashank Singh, 6 Marcus Stoinis, 7 Marco Jansen, 8 Xavier Bartlett, 9 Vijaykumar Vyshak, 10 Arshdeep Singh, 11 Yuzvendra Chahal DC impact options - Vipraj Nigam, Auqib Nabi, Ashutosh Sharma, Dushmantha Chameera, Karun Nair Delhi Capitals 1 KL Rahul (wk), 2 Pathum Nissanka, 3 Sameer Rizvi, 4 Axar Patel (capt), 5 Nitish Rana, 6 Tristan Stubbs, 7 David Miller, 8 Lungi Ngidi, 9 Kuldeep Yadav, 10 T Natarajan, 11 Mukesh Kumar Shreyas Iyer, PBKS captain - Boys have turned up well. It's scorching hot but there are no complaints. That's how we want it to be. We need to keep training hard and get better all the time. We have to keep enjoying the game. I'd have bowled first, had a small discussion with Axar. He said he'll bat. Toss was inconsequential. Same team Axar Patel, DC captain - Dry pitch, it's a day game very hot too. Hope to put up and defend a good total. Looks like the pitch will play slow, bowlers will look to use what's on offer. We have been playing well but aren't winning crucial moments. We've made silly mistakes and need to stop those, in the field and at important moments. Same team 3:01pm Time for the toss. Axar will spin it, tails is the call. It is heads. DC will bat first Daya says that while he's not sure, Pyla Avinash might be getting a cap. We'll find out if he does in a minute or two. Daya Sagar's updates from the ground: For Punjab, Arshdeep Singh, Xavier Bartlett, Marco Jansen, and Vijaykumar Vyshak have marked their bowling run-ups from both ends. From Delhi, Lungi Ngidi and Mukesh Kumar have done the same. Yuzvendra Chahal is practicing his spin bowling on the side pitch. His inclusion in the playing XI is confirmed, but it remains to be seen whether PBKS will also include Harpreet Brar in this day match. Pitch report by Simon Katich - It's a hot day. The square hits are 67 and 59 metres, straight hit is 73 metres. The surface is rock hard, not much grass. So far this IPL, two games have been played. 186 is the average score. But MI scored 168. This could be a little lower scoring because of the heat. It could slow up as the game progresses and offer turn. The outfield is lightning quick. About ten minutes to go for the toss, as we wait do check out Marco Jansen's interaction with Himanshu Agrawal, who'll be on comms soon. Jansen talks about being consistent like Hazlewood, bowling outside the powerplay and making a short career count. Lovely: "The best matchups today would be Arshdeep vs Rahul and Mukesh vs PBKS openers. Mouth-watering clashes" Zoey: "Why did Cooper Connolly go to Australia?" routine back scan 2:40pm Punjab Kings' is the story you want to be part of. The batting is loaded with match-winners from the top to the lower-middle order, the bowling is coming together nicely with five good bowlers and Shashank Singh if needed as a pinch-bowler. They'll hope to improve their catching today after Shashank dropped three the other night, doesn't change the fact that they go in as favourites. Naga: "Delhi's major reason of downfall is their too much chopping and changing of batting order. Miller has been hot and cold whereas Ashutosh not getting enough chances" Veer: "Will Starc play straightaway?" He'll return next week Manish: "It's scorching heat in Delhi, teams winning the toss should choose to bat and protect their bowlers from being dehydrated" Match Preview by Shashank Kishore DC have lots of catching up to do to give PBKS a fight 2:30pm We're nearly halfway into IPL 2026 and don't you miss Test cricket already? Jokes aside, it's been an excellent season for Punjab Kings and they'll on another North Indian team in Delhi Capitals, who haven't had the success that PBKS have had. Their top order has been hit and miss, their impact player selection has been inconsistent. They've had issues with the fifth and sixth bowler at times, they can't afford that if they are to challenge PBKS.

commentPostTextItems.html: KL Rahul: "Obviously happy that we got 260. But the heat.. I've obviously taken a beating. Phenomenal knock from Nitish. Right-hand-left-hand combination worked as well. The wicket was on the slower side. Towards the end, I was pre-meditating. For the first 70-80 runs, I wasn't pre-meditating. My strength is to play proper shots." 5.23pm Rahul crashes 152 out of DC's total of 264. That's more than 57% of his side's score. He nearly beat Brendon McCullum from that opening day 18 years ago. But this is what he achieved: a strike rate of 226 while merrily bashing boundaries in the second half of his innings. That has taken DC to the highest total of the season, but don't forget Rana's contribution. His 91 off 43 balls meant the two batters added a mammoth 220 in 95 deliveries for the second wicket. Some teams don't score that many in the entire 20 overs! Anyway, join Ekanth for the chase, with PBKS still unbeaten this season. But can they climb Mt 265?

commentTextItems.html: Ngidi has misjudged this and hit the back of his head onto the ground. The head bounced as he fell and tumbled backwards, fingers crossed it isn't but could be a concussion. His hands went on the head right away. He's rolled to the side and stayed still for a while, been on the ground for more than a minute. A stretcher comes out to take him off. It'll take some time though. The physio has a long chat while holding his neck, Ngidi able to talk which is good news. Was a full ball at the stumps. Arya made room and slashed. Went right up and Ngidi went back from mid-off. The hands were high and spread apart when the ball came down, got no hand on it. An ambulance now being wheeled in. Doctors, physios, surround Ngidi. A neck brace is slid under his head and goes around his neck as Ponting walks onto the field. A couple of straps across his body as he lies on the stretcher. Visuals cut to the ambulance with closed doors, presumably he's in now.

commentPostTextItems.html: We're done with the halfway mark of the group stages this IPL. It's marked with a record run chase in the history of T20 cricket. From here, though, you can shift to follow Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's six-laden fifty. Until next time, it's goodnight and goodbye from us! KL Rahul is the Player of the Match: "I was very pleased at the end of the first 20 overs. Something that I've been working on for a very long time behind the scenes... for now it was about doing well in the IPL. Just to step back a little back and see where the T20 game has gone. Watching the T20 World Cup and some guys coming in... There was a time when the T20 game was slightly different, and I, as an opener, could take my time. But today's demand is that the first six overs are the most important. I had to sit back and see where I was at. I stuck to being true to my game. In T20 cricket, that's the mindset I'm in right now - that there's no time to say later. There's time in ODI cricket... [but in T20s] there's no time to think you can go next over. I've had to work really hard on my mental set-up." Shreyas Iyer: "I'm running out of words. First of all, it was scorching hot there to come out and field... We were presuming that the wicket would be turning. But there wasn't much turn to offer. The ball was holding a bit. Kudos to KL. In my mind, I was just saying that what get they get from here on, we just need to get one more run. He was improvising and playing beautiful shots. I just said if they can, we can too. We have chased around 220 or 225 with a few overs left. So the mindset was very similar - get as many runs as you can in the powerplay. Right now we just want to go and have fun as much as possible. It was three days of hard work - practising and playing in the heat." Time for the presentations Priyansh Arya: "We just felt that we could score a hundred in the powerplay. The pitch was very good. Initially, we thought they would make 240, which we could chase down... I was having a lot of fun [watching Prabh hitting sixes]. Ricky sir had said that if we play our best game, we could chase this down. Just have some self-belief." Vinny: "KL's score should be the highest T20 individual score on the losing side, right?" --- Yup, beating Chris Gayle's by one run. Axar Patel: "We're making the same mistakes repeatedly. If you don't support the bowlers on such a wicket, I think you deserve to lose. At the same time, our bowling unit also needs to take a look [at them], given their score in the powerplay. If we grab the crucial moments, two or three results would have gone our way." Shashwat: "To think that 264 would have been 50 runs too many at a time in 50-over cricket....CRAZY!!" --- Yup, especially with one man alone scoring that many in the format. Arquam: "Despite all the talk of bat dominating ball, and advantage towards batting, this has been quite a spectacle to watch!" David: "529 runs plundered in 39 overs today, this is crazy!!" Meanwhile, Ravi Shastri says on broadcast that Lungi Ngidi is "stable now" after banging his head on the ground while looking to take a catch. 7.44pm Who would've thunk even 264 wouldn't be enough?! We're in the era of breathless and ruthless T20 batting, and PBKS gave another account of that this evening. To chase 265 down with seven balls left is setting an extremely high benchmark. Prabh and Arya crashed 116 runs in the powerplay - one hundred and sixteen!! - with nine fours and ten sixes. The game was all but decided at the time, you'd think. So the cliche still holds: no score is safe.

commentPreTextItems.html: Pranav : "I don't know which match to watch!" 7.28pm Jaiswal and Sooryavanshi walk out after the SRH team. Cummins gets started with field-setting immediately. He's in action for the first time since the Ashes! Praful Hinge has the new ball in hand. And today it's Jaiswal on strike first up. 7.25pm Thanks, Abhi. We have an absolute humdinger underway in New Delhi, but this match too shapes up to be a fantastic contest. Let's see how Rajasthan Royals' top order does against Praful Hinge (and Pat Cummins, of course) today. 7.05pm So, then, SRH finally chasing. Vidyut: "Cummins won a toss before Kishan" - He lost all seven! Cummins has come in with the toss-winning touch. Let's see if it translates to the match itself... MC: "With a flamboyant batting side like SRH, you'd think conventional wisdom would be to put the added pressure of the chase on them. That they haven't been made to bowl first by more teams despite losing all their tosses is a bit baffling to me." - Let's see how it plays out in hindsight after today's match... And now, say hello to Abhimanyu. Let's see how Sooryavanshi fares against SRH's new-ball bowlers! Send in thoughts about the teams and toss till then. 7pm The captains are out in the middle now. Heads is the calls, tails it is. Cummins wins a toss on comeback. SRH will bowl first. "Wicket looks good," Cummins says. "Feel really fresh, it's been a while. Let's see how it goes, body feels good. [Kishan] is fantastic. Four wins from seven games, he laid down a fearless, stylish approach. The challenge playing away is sensing what a good score is. First game from this venue this season, challenge for both teams. I've come in for Madushanka. Hinge has come in for Harsh Dubey." Parag says: "We were looking to do the same. Past couple of seasons not done well chasing, so happy defending. Feels great, played most of my cricket here. We've had a camp right before season started as well. We've got to be very clinical. We fell short by a couple of overs, here and there. Middle order has to step up. I have to step up, along with a couple of others. Openers have been doing well." Rajasthan Royals: Yashasvi Jaiswal, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Dhruv Jurel (wk), Riyan Parag (c), Shimron Hetmyer, Donovan Ferreira, Ravindra Jadeja, Jofra Archer, Tushar Deshpande, Nandre Burger, Brijesh Sharma Impact Subs bench: Ravi Bishnoi, Lhuan-dre Pretorius, Ravi Singh, Sandeep Sharma, Shubham Dubey Sunrisers Hyderabad: Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan, Heinrich Klaasen, Salil Arora (wk), Aniket Verma, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Pat Cummins (c), Shivang Kumar, Sakib Hussain, Praful Hinge, Eshan Malinga Impact Subs bench: Smaran R, Travis Head, Liam Livingstone, Harsh Dubey, Harshal Patel 6.50pm We are just a few minutes away from toss and team sheets. Krish: "Is it the first reverse fixture of the season? We are at the exactly half way of the league stage. " - So it is! A significant landmark, splitting the IPL season into half with the first reverse fixture of the season. Shadow-Shell: "We went exactly half of this season with only Indian captains" - Well, Cummins isn't a half-bad skipper to slot back into your side... 6.40pm Your first order of business is dipping into Sreshth Shah's preview for the game. Pat Cummins is back, he will take the field as well as the captain's armband from Ishan Kishan today. You can also dip into a study, by yours truly, on what has made Jofra Archer such a potent bowler in the powerplay for RR. He will be up against his kryptonite tonight though - left-handers, three of them, at the top of the SRH batting order. How will he fare against them? kaig: "Punjab playing stick cricket!!!" - So they are, so they are. 131 runs needed off 72 balls now, eight wickets in hand. Surely this is on... 6.30pm Welcome to the second fixture in today's double-header Sunday. I'll be amiss to not mention the carnage that is already preceding this game. Punjab Kings have boshed their way to checks notes 116 for 0 from just six overs, chasing double-checks notes 265 in the sweltering Delhi heat. Go over there and catch up while you can. And once you're done, tuck in for the cricketing feast that awaits us in Jaipur: Sooryavanshi vs Cummins (oh yes, he's back). Travishek vs Archer. No. 3 on the points table vs No. 4. I'm Abhijato, and alongside Abhimanyu, we'll be bringing you all the action as Sunrisers Hyderabad take on Rajasthan Royals.

commentTextItems.html: And now a misadventure ends his innings. He grimaces, he knows he played the wrong shot here. Ball was speared in full, but he turned around in his crease to scoop this over deep fine leg. Could not get under the ball, and it's struck him on the pads. As plumb as it gets. He reviews. Might as well. But he's plumb, and his face reveals it too... And yes, impact in line, wickets hitting. He has to go back.

commentPreTextItems.html: Last ball of a long, thrilling innings.

commentTextItems.html: Cummins has his arms spread and a huge smile on his face, Hinge is smiling too. A plan has come together here. The ball was well outside off, back of a length. Jadeja went for a lofted hoick down to long leg, but Travis Head seems to have been placed there for this exact shot. Umpire checks the catch... and guess what, the ball has burst through his hands! At least that's what the umpire reckons... He's going through a few replays here, and adjudicates it "NOT OUT". Fingers were tucked under the ball, but the delivery burst through his fingers just enough and grazed the turf.

commentPostTextItems.html: 9.35pm Remember the name, except you already too: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. He cracked fours and sixes for fun around the park, and has taken Rajasthan Royals to a mammoth 228 for 6. This will take some chasing. But Sunrisers Hyderabad have the top-order that can give this a good go: just like PBKS earlier in the day. What have Travishek, and Ishan Kishan, got for us today? Let's see on the other side! Abhimanyu will be back to take you through the chase soon. Sooryavanshi speaks now! Puts on the Orange Cap too. "I don't have a plan for a first-ball six. Before the match, we planned to play freely. To back our game. I thought the wicket was playing well, I backed my game. For the team, I wanted to give my 100% and back my game. I thought that about what shots I can play, and try to visualise it. The wicket is playing well. Got help with the new ball, the fast bowlers. It's a good shot. Disciplined ball and looking to execute plans."

commentTextItems.html: What a way to finish off the chase! Too full and on the pads. Salil whips his bat around to flick this over deep square leg. Great wrists on this one. Four wins in a row for SRH, and they are solidifying their spot in the top four...

commentPostTextItems.html: 11.50pm Phew, what a bonkers day of IPL cricket we've had. Two 200-plus totals chased down back-to-back, and with such authority. Catch a breather and catch up on sleep. We'll be back tomorrow with another double-header. For now, from everyone at ESPNcricinfo, bye-bye! And now, for the post-match presentation. And finally, the Player of the Match, Ishan Kishan: "I think as a wicket-keeper, you have to do the same job. Keep it simple. Good wicket to bat on, wanted to restrict them below 230 and we did that. Fun, leading the side of seven games, and then Pat coming back and giving us that extra bowling power. Thinking about batting and wicket-keeping more than leadership. It's just that you have to keep on watching ball, you have to play your game. I think it was pretty quick [first Jofra ball], happy to get six off it. Fortune favours the brave. I think we were pretty calm, most important thing is have a good powerplay. I was just communicating with Abhishek, well aware of what run rate was. We had a great partnership in the middle, which helped our team. [Where does calmness come from?] The skillset is always there. Good headspace is there. I was just thinking, let's watch the ball. I'll get more gaps. You always get big gaps. You keep the run-rate moving. Just bat and enjoy. [Is this the best you're batting?] No, the best is yet to come." Well, that ending was quite the statement, and why not, for Kishan the batter! SRH captain, Pat Cummins, has the mic. And a huge smile on his face. "Really happy. Never quite sure how it'll come out first game. I pick it up better than ten years ago. [On bowlers in 2026] I guess you just work on your batting... Even if you have one or two bad overs, you can bounce back and make an impact, like Praful did. We've got a good dugout, with bowlers and young guys. They were quite calm. Could have got away from us. Really good win." Abhishek Sharma has the Orange Cap now. Ringa-ringa-roses at the top of the run-scoring leaderboard! "Good to be on the winning side. I had my chances, lucky day for me. I wouldn't say they were 15 short, but they could have got 15-20 runs more. I mean bowler like Jofra, if they're bowling to you... I just wanted to create room just to trouble them with line and length a bit. What me and Ishan wanted to do, especially with the new ball. I feel once you chase that kind of score, the way the batters are performing... Bowling side coming after powerplay... You can feel the confidence in the team. We always knew Pat would come and lead the side. Of course, Patty came and gave that extra experience in the side. How he bowls in those crucial overs give you confidence." Parag, the RR skipper, speaks to the broadcasters: "Dropped a few too many catches. Quality players like Abhishek, can't drop quality batters. Could have been better on the field. We've got to be clinical. Fielding plays a major part in that. We've got a day's break. Mentally refresh and come back the next day. We left 10-15 [runs] on the table. To be honest, they bowled well in the 18th and 20th. Executed their yorkers. Would've liked another 15 runs. [On Bishnoi's late introduction] There were two lefties, I thought me and Don had better chances to get wicket. Wicket was not spin-friendly, I just had to manage four overs.. Didn't really go to plan. Different venues, different games, different ways to approach it. Don't know how Chandigarh will go." 11.27pm Sooryavanshi's century has gone from the starring note of the night to a footnote in SRH's victory. A rather spotty bowling line-up past Archer and Berger disrupted their ability to defend this. Archer's two-for was a great spell, but around him fielders kept dropping vital chances and putting in slot balls. Ishan Kishan's 74 off 31 put SRH in the driver's seat, and NKR stuck around to bolster's the SRH middle-order's credentials. His knock took them right to the finish line, and that's another two points in the bag for his team.

commentPreTextItems.html: 3:29pm Samson and Gaikwad are out in the middle. Siraj has the ball. Sole slip. Ring field. JK: "Why is Prasidh not playing?" Gill didn't mention reasons, in fact he didn't mention who was left out. Just said Arshad is in nimmit jain : "why no sarfaraz ???" CSK are keeping their options open, Sarfaraz likely to come in, Prashant Veer can come in if they need a batter later in the innings. GT might bring in Tewatia CSK impact options - Sarfaraz Khan, Mukesh Choudhary, Prashant Veer, Ramakrishna Ghosh, Matt Short Chennai Super Kings 1 Sanju Samson (wk), 2 Ruturaj Gaikwad (capt), 3 Urvil Patel, 4 Dewald Brevis, 5 Shivam Dube, 6 Kartik Sharma, 7 Jamie Overton, 8 Akeal Hosein, 9 Noor Ahmad, 10 Anshul Kamboj, 11 Gurjapneet Singh GT impact options - Glenn Phillips, Anuj Rawat, Kulwant Khejroliya, Nishant Sindhu, Rahul Tewatia Gujarat Titans 1 Shubman Gill (capt), 2 Sai Sudharsan, 3 Jos Buttler (wk), 4 Shahrukh Khan, 5 Washington Sundar, 6 Jason Holder, 7 Rashid Khan, 8 Arshad Khan, 9 Kagiso Rabada, 10 Mohammed Siraj, 11 Manav Suthar Ruturaj Gaikwad: I feel wicket's on the drier side. It'll remain the same more often than not. Wouldn't mind defending. Confidence is high after a big win last game. This game starts from zero. Just one or two areas where we need to click. I've been getting starts but not able to convert, it's very rare. As long as I'm getting starts and someone's there to go over the line, we're okay. When I feel it's my day, I want to cash in. Urvil come in and we'll play around with the impact player. Shubman Gill: Hopefully the heat won't be too tough on the bowlers. We're doing a lot of things right, we're leaking too many runs in the middle overs. Need to hit our lengths. (On powerplay batting) If the wicket is nice, you've to get 70-80 in the powerplay, we have to assess things based on conditions. Arshad is back. 3pm Toss time. Ruturaj will spin the coin, heads is the call. It is heads, GT will bowl From Deiva, who's hopefully in the cool comforts of the media box: Hello, it's a scorching day in Chennai. Warning for "excessive heat" has been issued to various areas in the city this weekend. The Chennai boys are used to this weather, though. Sai Sudharsan is doing some running drills - the guy loves sprinting even in this heat. Sai Kishore is wheeling away on one of the practice pitches along with fellow left-arm fingerspinner Manav Suthar. Gurjapneet Singh is warming up with the CSK boys, but can't spot MS Dhoni yet. This game is set to be played on pitch no.6 - a mix of red and black soils. Gaikwad had reportedly made a quick trip home to Pune after the match against MI in Wankhede, but had trained with CSK on Saturday and looks set to go today Pitch report by Katey Martin: It's hot but it has been hotter in the past. What are the dimensions like, we are on pitch six - 63m and the other side is 70m. Straight is 79m which is quite a big hit. The first thing about this surface is the mixed soil, a mix of black and red - black traditionally stays low and turns more, red just aids a bit of hardness. On this surface, it's been about spin. Noor Ahmad and Akeal Hosein will be a handful. The in-between lengths will be crucial here. It will be a real assistance to spinners as historically it is. You want to get a 190 or more. Batting first you can defend if you score that number. RajNV: "Pitch Reporter are having what qualification to predict the Pitch nature? Just curious." They're generally done by former players, Varun: "Genuine query: Why has R Sai Kishore not played a single match till now? Injured?" Think it's just team combinations. They gave Suthar a go in the last game. Sai Kishore might come on today, let's see Abhilash: "Close to thousand runs were scored just yesterday. I'm predicting it would be 160-170 run matches today" Aditya: "Why is everyone criticising Shivam Dube's form? One low score in the last game, but a strike rate of 142 averaging 32 this season!!" He's scored 20 or more three times this season, two of which were 20 and 21. There are three not outs that bulk up the average Ranjith: "While we understand why Dhoni is not ready to play but it hurts as a Dhoni Fan - if it don't happen in this season it never will." 2:45pm After a day of batting dominance, bowlers might have some respite at the Chepauk where spinners might find some assistance. Pace-off might be an option for the seamers, batters would likely have to go down the ground for runs rather than behind the wicket. Powerplays could make or break the game. Let's see if any of those things play out. Match Preview by Hemant Brar CSK host stuttering GT in Chennai heat Tej: "Chennai heat will go even higher month of May.. it wouldn't be ideal to play evening to avoid heatstroke?" Just three more games in Chennai this season, one of which is a noon game. This game should've been in Ahmedabad but was moved due to elections Daman: "CSK have found a genuine match-winner in Akeal. while Shivam Dube's form is a big concern for them. CSK's playoff prospects lies a lot on Dube's form" arjun: ""Has Dhoni travelled with the team?"" Not sue, he isn't expected to play 2:30pm It's raining heat in Chennai. Drops of sunshine have flooded the city and baked the ground. People aren't in yet, if many of them are taking ice baths it'll be no surprise. The two teams will need some coolers too, especially the one that'll bowl first. CSK are coming in on the back of two wins in the last three games. Samson is among the runs now, their spinners are on a roll too. For GT, their successful template might need a relook. Might not happen mid-season, adjustments though might be forced. Will that happen first or will they pull things back.

commentPreTextItems.html: Can CSK reach 160?

commentTextItems.html: No, they don't but finish on 158, which looked unlikely after the ten-over mark. Tossed up outside off, he hammers this to the right of long-off for four

commentPostTextItems.html: Here's Sampath: 1) Most dot balls faced by a batter in an IPL innings: 31 - Shikhar Dhawan vs SRH, 2023 (99* off 66) 30 - Dwayne Bravo vs KXIP, 2009 (70* off 59) 30 - Ruturaj Gaikwad vs GT, 2026 (74* off 60) 14 of 31 dots by Dhawan in 2023 were while batting with the No. 11 in the last five overs of the innings. 2) Highest % of team's total scored after the end of 12th over in an IPL innings: (150+ totals) 71.07 - MI vs KXIP, 2015 (113 out of 159) 68.29 - MI vs RR, 2015 (112 out of 164) 67.72 - CSK vs GT, 2026 (107 out of 158) Top two instances came in back to back games for MI. Shivam Dube: [Final score] The first ten overs, we did not have a good start but then we have reached 158, which is an amazing score. I think 158 is one of the best scores here. It is not easy for the fast bowlers or spinners. The ball is not coming evenly. Holder and Arshad bowled well. The bounce is not even, it is coming fast as well as slow. [Chat with Gaikwad] We wanted to bat till the 15th or 16th over, bat deep. 5.22pm What a whirlwind finish for CSK, who have smashed 107 runs in the last eight overs to reach 158 for 7. They were going nowhere, lost three wickets in the powerplay and Gaikwad was struggling. He was on 20 off 37 balls at one stage before picking up pace. His 49-ball fifty was still the slowest of his IPL career as CSK reached 100 only in the 16th over. Overton and Kartik injected some momentum into the innings while Gaikwad remained unbeaten. CSK have managed a score on the board. But the question is will it be enough?

commentTextItems.html: That's that! GT back to winning ways after two defeats; CSK lose at home. Buttler hits the winning runs. Fullish on the stumps, he jumps down the track and smacks this straight down the ground for a big six. GT win by eight wickets with 20 balls to spare.

commentPostTextItems.html: Righto, with that Gujarat Titans move to fifth on the points table and CSK have dropped down to sixth. If you missed any of the action, Alagappan's report has you covered. We're not done yet, though. The LSG-KKR clash is in full flow with the LSG bowlers starting well. So hop onto the other tab to follow Shashwat on comms there. Till, then this is me Ashish Pant, signing off on behalf of Ekanth, Sudeep and Thilak. Ciao! Kagiso Rabada is the player of the match: I actually didn't feel I started pretty well. That's how cricket goes. I am glad to play a part to take the team acroos the line. We needed the two points. [Is it clicking?] 100% yeah, it is and it's just about maintaining that and staying ahead of the game. So yeah, simply to answer that, it's clicking. How do you stay ahead of the game?] I guess it's just not taking anything for granted. Sticking with your process and always looking to improve. The day that you stop looking to improve is the day that you retire. [Combination with Mohamed Siraj and the other seamers] Yeah, a lot of fast bowlers, that's been a clear tactic of Gujarat over the years, playing at Ahmedabad. So it's nice to see the fast bowlers union coming together and yeah, it's been working thus far. I think we've been taking a lot of wickets, but at the same time, we need to find ways to contain too. So it's been a really, really lovely journey I guess that we've had so far. GT captain, Shubman Gill: [On the win] Very happy. To get a win like that in this part of India, I am very happy. Apart from the last four or five overs, it was a complete performance. [Toss] I was a little confused whether to bowl or bat but we bowled well in the powerplay. If I have to be critical, finishing an innings has been a problem. [On Rashid bowling one over] There was confusion in the middle, when Dube came in, I thought should we bowl Washy, but the game was in our hand. He [Suthar] bowled a decent last over, gave 12 or 13. Pretty good effort from us. [On Sai Sudharsan] He is batting brilliantly. It [form] was always with him. All about spending the time in the crease Presentation time B Sai Sudharsan: Feels very grateful. Very happy, not a lot of words at the moment, I was overwhelmed. [On his innings] Just getting the confidence from the last innings, keeping this innings as fresh as possible. I just wanted to take the confidence from the last innings to this innings. [Pitch in second innings] I felt it slightly got better but first six overs, it was tough. Shubi [Shubman Gill] played an extraordinary cameo. [Playing late] When I am hitting the ball well, then I play late. [Plans tonight] Will go to my favourite tea shop and spend some time there with bun maska and chai CSK captain, Ruturaj Gaikwad: [First innings where CSK lost] Sometimes I hate to assess, it this way but it was challenging in the first innings. It was holding for the medium pacers and the bounce was up and down. We lost too many wickets but it was difficult to play some shots. [Pitch] Not expected. It is hard to assess how it plays. This game we didn't have any idea. By the time, we wanted to adapt it was too late. At the first timeout, when Flem came out I told him, I am trying to attack but it was tough. There was more bounce, or less bounce, and I told him I am trying to change. It just did not come good. It was just an off day and even on the field we were lethargic. [His innings] I got off to a really good start, and then I thought to keep up the momentum. But after the wickets fell, I though to build a partnership. I then just wanted to take my time and rotate the strike. Any other pitch, any other day, I would have rotated the strike. Once I got hit, I just thought let's keep going. [Team tactics] We were batting well, so once we cross the powerplay, we thought let's get a bowler in, Mukesh was supposed to come in. But we lost wickets and had to bring Sarfaraz in. 7.10pm Chennai boy Sai Sudharsan has continued his stellar run to down CSK at home, giving GT an important win. A target of 159 was going to be tricky on a two-paced Chennai surface but local boy BSS and Shubman Gill for GT off to a quick start. Even when Gill fell, BSS did not lose focus. He struck 87 off 46 balls, his innings laced with seven sixes and four fours. Buttler also played his part as GT got over the line comfortably.
