Shami has the new ball. Can he get it to move? Slip in place. Let's play! Pitch Report: There is a slight bias in terms of the square boundaries - 64m to one side, 69m to the other. 73m hit straight down the ground. There is a jigsaw look to the pitch with the cracks, and it could be two-paced, says Simon Katich. Low bounce could also be a theme tonight. Lucknow has been the lowest-scoring venue so far in the IPL this season. will: "why does fin Allen not play for KKR?? you can't tell me Tim Seifert has done anything to deserve a place over the guy who scored 100 off 30 balls not long ago" -- Well, Allen did get his chance and it did not quite come off. So, KKR have pivoted. Krish: "KKR going batting heavy till number 9, that means Anukul and Ramandeep needs to bowl 4 overs between them." -- Maybe not because they have Green in the mix too, and they will most probably bring in Varun, unless something goes drastically wrong with the bat. 7:07pm The big news from the toss is that Pathirana is still not a part of the KKR side. That, though, means Seifert gets another game, and another chance to set the tone at the top of the order. LSG have stuck with Pooran, meanwhile, and have added an overseas left-arm spinner in Linde, who also strengthens their lower middle order. It will also be interesting to see how the LSG pacers fare in the first innings, especially with the form they have been in. Lucknow Super Giants bowling-first XI: Mitchell Marsh, Aiden Markram, Rishabh Pant (capt & wk), Ayush Badoni, Nicholas Pooran, Mukul Choudhary, George Linde, Digvesh Rathi, Mohammed Shami, Prince Yadav, Mohsin Khan LSG bench: Himmat Singh, Akshat Raghuvanshi, Abdul Samad, Avesh Khan, M Siddharth Kolkata Knight Riders batting-first XI: Ajinkya Rahane (capt), Tim Seifert (wk), Angkrish Raghuvanshi, Cameron Green, Rovman Powell, Rinku Singh, Sunil Narine, Anukul Roy, Ramandeep Singh, Kartik Tyagi, Vaibhav Arora KKR bench: Manish Pandey, Finn Allen, Tejasvi Singh, Navdeep Saini, Varun Chakravarthy 7pm Time for the toss. Pant and Rahane out in the middle. Pant gives the coin a spin. Rahane calls heads, but tails it is. LSG will field first. Pant says they want to put the opposition in first and see how things pan out. Linde comes in for Siddharth, says Pant. Adds that they are working towards finding a way and reckons they are pretty close to doing so. Rahane says he would have batted first anyway. Says he wants to give freedom to the batting unit, which is why he would have batted first. Winning crucial moments is important and Rahane says they are going in with the same team. Says the week off has been good, and has helped them reflect. Says it is always about improvement and that they have had a good couple of practice sessions. 6:50pm A return to nailing his yorkers, paired with learning variations like slower bouncers, has helped Prince Yadav become one of the leading wicket-takers in the IPL this year. Read all about it here in S Sudarshanan's piece. Mustafa Moudi: "KKR vs LSG have produced many thrillers but LSG have ended up winning all of them. But their Win Margins - 1 Run, 2 Runs and 4 Runs, shows how interesting these match were. And of course the reverse fixture between the 2. Glad that this rivalry is getting another game this season !!" 6:35pm Bowling has been a concern for KKR throughout the season. Their bowling stocks, though, could be reinforced tonight with Matheesha Pathirana, a big-money buy at the auction, primed to return. Ashish Pant sets the scene in his match preview. 6:30pm The motto of the IPL, when translated to English, says this is where talent meets opportunity. Where countless unheralded individuals enter, itching to capture the imagination and write themselves into folklore. When the Lucknow Super Giants and the Kolkata Knight Riders last met, Mukul Choudhary's talent met the opportunity of a game crying out to be seized. And mayhem ensued. LSG won a match they had no business winning; KKR lost from a position considered perfect for winning. But LSG have not won since. KKR have also won only once. Meaning the pair of them are currently marooned near the foot of the table. Maybe even wondering where and how their next win will come about. And so, from a bit of Mukul magic and MukulMania at the Eden Gardens, we now waltz into Lucknow. The home of the Super Giants, but where they still await the happy homecoming they would have envisioned, and where the Knight Riders hope to find a sprinkling of the sparkle that breathes new life into IPL campaigns, and would reiterate their pedigree and status as possible contenders still. Neither will definitively get eliminated tonight. We are not there just yet. But another unfavourable result tonight, and the route back will get arduous and perhaps, untenable. Lots to look forward to, so hop on to ESPNcricinfo's live coverage!

commentTextItems.html: a huge mix-up, but Raghuvanshi survives! Back of a length on middle and off. Raghuvanshi punches it to mid on and sets off, only to be sent back from half-way. He sprawls across the turf and cops a throw from Shami for his troubles. LSG did indulge in a hint of an appeal but the batter did not change direction to get in line with the throw. Well, that is what it seemed like in real-time but the third umpire has now been called into action. Oh wow. Raghuvanshi's turning radius was more than what might be deemed normal. He did look at the ball too, and the third umpire reckons he changed direction. Raghuvanshi has to go, and he is not at all happy. The key question here was how big his turning radius was. It was a little more than what would be deemed normal, and he ended up outside the cut strip while diving. The third umpire seems to agree with that assessment. KKR three down now!

commentPostTextItems.html: 9:20pm Wow. What a finish. 26 came off the final over and that has propelled KKR to 155, which seemed a distant dream when they lost Ramandeep. Rinku was front and centre of this resurrection act, registering his highest-ever T20 score, and that has given KKR a fighting chance, even though the rest of the batting unit did not cover itself in glory. LSG will be disappointed with how the final phase of their bowling innings went. Prior to that, they had done everything right, with Mohsin running through the KKR line-up. Prince and Shami (at the start especially) did their bits too, although neither could get on the board in wicket-taking terms. This does not look a very daunting total, but this is not an easy pitch to get started on, meaning LSG will have to bat well to get there. Join us in a bit for the resumption. Mohsin Khan: I was just thinking about how to make the team win, and winning is very important for us tonight. I am fine, and I have worked a lot (on my fitness) in the off-season. Body feels good and everything feels nice. (On his plans) We read the wicket and tried to execute the plans we had made. Felt the slower one (or change of pace) could be useful. I am working on my body and want to stay fit and healthy, and want to keep playing matches. (On the score) We gave away some runs in the last few overs. But we will win today. shareef : "Rinku smoking sixes in the last over. hey it's a classic. I've seen this before. "

commentTextItems.html: and we are going into a Super Over! Goodness gracious me! Mohammed Shami, what are you made of?! All those years. All that experience. All that pedigree. And all of it has now unfurled itself when LSG needed it most. Shami, a match-winner for every team with the ball, now pops up with heroics with the bat. In the slot outside off and Shami slams it over long off. Shami storms off, somehow still livid about something. Does he think he should have finished this game off altogether? commentPostTextItems.html: 11:34pm Right. The LSG batters make their way out. Markram and Pooran to take guard for LSG. Narine to bowl, which is not at all a surprise. Narine has famously bowled a Super Over to Pooran, albeit in the CPL. What do we have in store tonight? 11:29pm What a game. What drama. And it is still not done yet. We are going into over-time. KKR crestfallen. LSG over the moon having pulled a tie out of the fire. It should probably not have gotten this deep, given the batting LSG had. But they just could not get out of second gear throughout. Credit to KKR for it. They stuck to their guns, they held their lengths, they tried their best but in the end, they just could not find the nerve to close out the game. They will have a chance to set things right, though. LSG will too. But until this Super Over is done, we will not know who will end the night happier, and who will end this evening having experienced the elation of winning a match that they, at some point, would have felt had slipped.

commentPreTextItems.html: 7:28pm The players make their way out to huge cheers. A few DC flags flying in the stands, but there is a considerable chunk of RCB support too, perhaps even outnumbering the DC folks. Parakh, on debut, will open alongside Rahul, fresh off a 152*. Bhuvneshwar to take the new ball. Parakh on strike, slip in place, play! Thisath: "Sad to see Pathum being left out. He's a world-class player, but it's not going well for him " -- His class is undeniable but it has not worked out as well as he or DC would have imagined. Adarsh: "It is surprising that DC's batting pretty much ends at no 7. They could have included Ashutosh in the batting first-XI and used Chameera as the impact sub." -- They have, like CSK, kept that option open. In case they need some batting muscle late, Ashutosh can come in. The make-up of their starting eleven means they will still have five proper bowling options. Arun Kamboj: "It's sad to see Ashutosh not getting a chance. He was brilliant for DC last year" -- Well, DC's lower middle order is stacked. 7:10pm Lots of changes from DC. One of them was forced, with Ngidi unavailable. But they have opted for more overseas fast-bowling firepower, sacrificing Nissanka in the process, although it must be added that Nissanka did not quite live up to expectations. Not many surprises in the RCB side. Bethell will likely come in as their Impact Player. Delhi Capitals batting-first XI: Sahil Parakh, KL Rahul (wk), Nitish Rana, Sameer Rizvi, Tristan Stubbs, David Miller, Axar Patel (capt), Dushmantha Chameera, Kuldeep Yadav, T Natarajan, Kyle Jamieson DC bench: Auqib Nabi, Ashutosh Sharma, Vipraj Nigam, T Vijay, Abishek Porel Royal Challengers Bengaluru bowling-first XI: Virat Kohli, Devdutt Padikkal, Rajat Patidar (capt), Jitesh Sharma (wk), Tim David, Romario Shepherd, Krunal Pandya, Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Josh Hazlewood, Suyash Sharma, Rasikh Dar RCB bench: Jacob Bethell, Jordan Cox, Mangesh Yadav, Vicky Ostwal, Venkatesh Iyer 7pm Time for the toss. Axar and Patidar out there in the middle. Axar, by virtue of being the home captain, will give the coin a spin. Patidar calls heads, and heads it is. RCB will field first. Says it is a pretty obvious decision, with this being a high-scoring ground, and he hopes to put DC under pressure while chasing. Adds they have played good cricket in the first half, and that they want to continue it in the second half. Same team, says Patidar. Axar says he would have fielded first too. You can only give confidence, says Axar, when asked about the message after the previous game. He reiterates that things could have been different had they taken their catches, while also stressing continuing momentum as key. Three changes, says Axar. Jamieson and Chameera come in, alongside opening batter Parakh. Mukesh is one of the players missing out, and he says they have given him some chances and it has not worked out, adding that a break might be best for all parties at this stage. Here is a snippet from Daya, who is our eyes and ears in Delhi: Good evening once again from Delhi. This is the second match here in three days, and looking at the pitch, we can expect another high-scoring game. On this same pitch number 5, the DC vs GT match was played, where both teams scored more than 200 runs. Right now, the whole of Delhi is under Kohli mania, and outside the stadium, only Virat jerseys can be seen everywhere. Kohli came to his home ground, did a little warm-up, addressed the team huddle, and then walked back to the pavilion. For DC, Mitchell Starc has given Kyle Jamieson his franchise debut cap, while Starc himself is currently unavailable for selection. Lungi Ngidi, who got injured in the last match against PBKS, is also not on the field. Meanwhile, young Maharashtra batter Sahil Parakh is also making his debut. It will be interesting to see whose place he takes in the playing XI. Sanket: "Can Delhi play both Chameera and Jamieson here, in the last game DC's bowling was really poor and your best bowler is not available against this formidable RCB's batting unit so you want to have that quality and depth. But that means you cant play Nissanka, Shaw or even someone like Porel can be very good option to start with." -- Early signa are that Nissanka might not be playing, purely based on the cap Parakh has received. That might open the door for two overseas pacers to feature. Ngidi has not recovered yet, so it is a bit of a wait and watch to see who DC go in with. Naveen: "Is there any news on Phil Salt's injury? Is he fit to play today? " -- Think this game might come too early for him. JUST IN: Kyle Jamieson has received his DC cap from Mitchell Starc. Sahil Parakh is also set to make his DC debut tonight. Pitch Report: 63m square boundaries either side, so no bias at all. The pitch is a batter's paradise, says Eoin Morgan. Batters cash in on length balls, so bowlers might have to be careful about that. This strip is a little drier, and Morgan says it will be interesting to see if the ball spins and bites for the spinners. 6:35pm KL Rahul has been in stunning form, and arrives on the back of a record-breaking 152*, albeit in a losing cause. He also has a knack of turning up against RCB. What can he come up with tonight? All that and much more in Abhimanyu Bose's preview. VS: "Hoping for a 200 vs 200 match today. As a neutral i want DC to win. It will make the table interesting" 6:30pm Sport gives second chances. To individuals. To teams. To right a wrong. To replace more sombre memories with cheerful ones. That is, in fact, the very essence of sport - of wanting to get back up each day, knowing there will always be an opportunity for the taking. A week ago, David Miller got it. In another last-over chasing scenario. Against the defending champions. Away from home. And he put behind what may have been gnawing at him from earlier in the tournament. Now, the Royal Challengers Bengaluru will have their second chance. To get back at the Delhi Capitals. To get back at one of only two teams that have defeated them all season. Even as the Capitals, after the events over the weekend, chase a second chance themselves. And so, here we are. Back in Delhi. Where a mountain of runs was put up a mere 48 hours ago, and where that peak was scaled in unprecedented and breath-taking fashion. On the one side, the Capitals, still smarting from Saturday but maybe drawing inspiration from the reverse fixture; on the other, RCB, aware of the need to cast aside events of the past, and reinforce the belief that this is their title to win, yet again. Plenty to tuck into, so sit back, relax and enjoy ESPNcricinfo's live coverage!

commentTextItems.html: zing bails go flying, and DC have been rolled over for 75! Hazlewood has four, and he fittingly lands the final blow. Searing yorker on middle and leg. Porel looks to jam it out into the off side but is too late on it. Ball sneaks past his blade and crashes into the furniture. Third lowest-score in the IPL for the Delhi-based franchise, and RCB have run rampant across an hour and a half in the capital!

commentPostTextItems.html: 9:07pm An absolute rout. No other way to put it. This game, of course, is not done yet, but it will now require something incredibly special from DC. RCB, though, did produce something special. Bhuvneshwar and Hazlewood produced an opening salvo that would not have been out of place in a Test match. They got the ball to hoop around, and they caused all sorts of problems. The DC batters were like deer caught in the headlights. They had no plans to counter the movement and crumbled like a pack of cards. The only solace they can probably take is that they did not get bundled out for the lowest-ever IPL score, which seemed a real possibility when they were reduced to 8-6. Join us in a bit for what should be a routine chase. Bhuvneshwar Kumar: It is swinging this year - don't know why. When ball swings and you get wickets up front, it makes it easier at the back-end. It was a good batting wicket, especially the way the ball was coming on. It was one of the good days when they were nicking (or getting bowled). Fortunate to get those early wickets. (On if he was asking the captain for a fourth successive over) I was not saying that because I was kind of tired. Did not want to push myself (smiles). Virs: "How poetic would it be if DC defended the lowest total ever in IPL after being on the wrong end of the highest successful chase 2 days ago.." -- Poetic, yes. But at this stage, highly optimistic and wishful.

commentPostTextItems.html: 10:20pm A very early finish tonight, on the heels of a marathon game yesterday. Sums up T20 cricket. Sums up how unpredictable the IPL can be. What will we have in store tomorrow as the table-topping Punjab Kings take on the Rajasthan Royals? Well, join us then to find out. Until tomorrow, from all of us here at ESPNcricinfo, it is goodbye! Josh Hazlewood, Player of the Match: Probably turning up here after 500-plus runs in the last game, was not sure what was going to happen. Was just following his (Bhuvneshwar) lead. There was a bit there in the first six overs - enough there to work with, and it was skidding on quickly from a short of a length. Once the ball got soft, it got more even. (On the Rana dismissal) In general, you wanted the batter to hit it down the wicket and in the V. The short ball was nice as well, just about the accuracy. When that ball was nice and hard, it was tough to bat. Would have been nice to bowl four and get off the field (laughs). Our spinners got into the game, dotted it up nicely. We have picked up from where we left off last season. We summed up conditions quickly and adapted our games (on the road in 2025). Feel like we are hitting our straps again at the right time. Rajat Patidar, RCB captain: Even I am surprised (at how the game went). All credit to the bowlers - Hazlewood and Bhuvi, the way they bowled in the powerplay. The good thing was we got early wickets and it kept us in the driving seat. (On bowling out both bowlers early) We had planned that if we get early wickets, they would bowl 3-3 each. Suyash got a lot of spin - the way he bowled stump to stump, it was pleasing to see. Very important to follow your routine. Still long way to go. We are taking it one game at a time. The positive was different players coming up and doing it for the team. You should have a good bowling attack (on flat pitches in T20 cricket) because only bowlers can win you championships. Axar Patel, DC captain: I still cannot understand what happened. That is why they say you have to be on your toes at all times in cricket. Ifs and buts will be there - like if we had taken that catch or taken that run (against GT). That will keep happening. But each day, you have to be on your toes and keep doing what you have been doing well. You cannot take it easy for even one day. Rather than thinking about what has happened, think about what is to come. Even if you stay negative or positive, you still have to play. Tonight was a bad day. We have to be positive and do what we had been doing (earlier). (On the early movement on offer) I was not surprised. They (Bhuvneshwar and Hazlewood) are world-class bowlers. 1-2 overs, if our openers and number three had batted, it could have been a different game. Devdutt Padikkal: It was great to see the way we bowled in the first six overs. Those guys (Bhuvneshwar and Hazlewood) are so good. The pressure on the batting side is immense, and it showed. I am expecting a catch every ball - when those two are bowling, every ball is an opportunity. (On his improvement as a slip fielder) It has a lot to do with time out there. When I started slip fielding, was not very good at it. As you do it more often, you get better at it. (On the chase) When you have a total like that, important you try to finish it off as quickly as possible. 9:57pm Well, that happened rather quickly. Bethell landed a few early blows. Padikkal then took over, with Kohli also helping himself to a couple of pristine maximums. RCB were never really hard-pressed in this chase and most of their work was done long away - inside their bowling powerplay. An NRR bruising and morale bruising loss for the Capitals. They have now been chastened in two vastly different circumstances in their two most previous games, and they will now have to find a way to pick themselves up after it.

commentPreTextItems.html: 7:28pm The players make their way out. This could be an event-a-ball powerplay. Arya and Prabhsimran to open. Archer, of course, will take the new ball. Can he get the ball to move early and create chaos? Prabhsimran on strike. Slip in place. Expect fireworks one way or the other. Play! Prashant: "Who'll be RR's batting sub in the second innings - Hetmyer?" -- Likely to be Vidarbha batter Shubham Dubey. VS: "How is the pitch today? Another high scoring one?" -- After yesterday, who knows...For what it is worth, this pitch was used for the GT-PBKS game, which was not particularly high-scoring. Ishan Jain: "These two franchises have given us very close matches - Tewatia's redemption, Kartik Tyagi's defence, etc. Given the lineups, this is going to be a tough game. I have a feeling RR will stop PBKS' unbeaten run." Mr. K: "@Shashwat I don't know why, but maybe Wadhera might perform today. seems like he loves playing versus RR, scoring 49, 62, and 70 in his 3 innings versus tem." Jatin Panchal: "What is reason of Bishnoi not in playing 11? He was wkt taking bowler and not included in bowling 11?" -- Not entirely sure. He was expensive against KKR. Maybe RR want to use that element of surprise against a right-hander heavy batting unit. Pitch Report: Slightly skewed square boundaries - 70m to one side, 64m to the other. There was a bit of rain around, and it is a very good surface, says Danny Morrison, and he does not expect a team to be 8-6 like last night, even though there could be some help early for the pacers. The ball might skid on otherwise, and Deep Dasgupta concludes by saying it should be a good batting surface. 7:10pm So, PBKS have finally been forced into a change. Prior to tonight, they had only used 12 players but Shedge, an all-rounder who plays his domestic cricket for Mumbai, and Lockie Ferguson will become the 13th and 14th players they use this season. RR have also made a couple of changes, with Shanaka's all-round ability trumping Hetmyer's X-Factor in the middle order. Yash Punja, who made his IPL debut against KKR earlier this month, replaces Bishnoi. Vishnu : "Watch out for Suryansh Shedge. This boy will do well. It's a wildest prediction. " -- He is a hard-hitting middle order batter and perfectly fits the brand of cricket PBKS usually play. samirdave: "PBKS might have had the upper hand this season, but writing RR off in this clash would be a serious misread. Their losses have hinged more on sloppy fielding than a lack of firepower--because man-to-man, few sides can match an opening punch like Suryavanshi-Jaiswal or the raw threat of Archer and Burger with the new ball. This isn't a game PBKS can cruise through; it's a real test, and a perfect chance for RR to remind everyone of their bite" Amandeep: "What do u mean by forced change? Also why Shashank is sitting out?" -- Forced change is what Shreyas said at the toss. No further info apart from that from him. Abhilash: "Summarizing both the batting line-ups, it's the immovable object vs the unstoppable force.." -- Well, both can make a case to be the unstoppable force. Rajasthan Royals bowling-first XI: Yashasvi Jaiswal, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Dhruv Jurel (wk), Riyan Parag (capt), Donovan Ferreira, Dasun Shanaka, Ravindra Jadeja, Jofra Archer, Brijesh Sharma, Nandre Burger, Yash Punja RR bench:Ravi Bishnoi, Ravi Singh, Tushar Deshpande, Shubham Dubey, Shimron Hetmyer Punjab Kings batting-first XI: Priyansh Arya, Prabhsimran Singh (wk), Cooper Connolly, Shreyas Iyer (capt), Nehal Wadhera, Marcus Stoinis, Suryansh Shedge, Marco Jansen, Lockie Ferguson, Arshdeep Singh, Yuzvendra Chahal PBKS bench: Vishnu Vinod, Vijaykumar Vyshak, Xavier Bartlett, Harpreet Brar, Musheer Khan 7pm Time for the toss. Shreyas and Parag out in the middle. Parag calls tails, and he calls correctly. RR will bowl first. Parag says it looks like a good wicket, and that there were a few showers, which has led to this decision. Hetmyer goes out, as does Bishnoi. Shanaka comes in, along with Yash, says Parag. Shreyas says he would have bowled first too, saying that this pitch had been covered for a couple of days. Any time you bat or bowl, it is a great challenge and he notes that they are proactive. Suryansh comes in, and that is a forced change, with Shashank sitting out. Ferguson replaces Bartlett. 6:40pm PBKS are unbeaten so far, and have only failed to win when rain denied them at the Eden Gardens in early April. Can RR dent their charge in the first meeting between this pair this season? Sreshth Shah sets the scene in his match preview. 6:30pm Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Yashasvi Jaiswal. The irresistible force. If Jaiswal does not get you, Sooryavanshi does. If neither does, Jofra Archer and Ravindra Jadeja do. And if none of them do, Nandre Burger does. The Rajasthan Royals may not have been entirely spotless so far. But on their day, which has been more often than not this season, they have been irrepressible. Tonight, though, they run into a juggernaut. A well-oiled machine seemingly devoid of any chinks or weaknesses. A side that is an irresistible force themselves. And an immovable object. Seven teams have tried and have failed to trip up the Punjab Kings. Sides have put up more than 200 and have lost. Sides have scored 260 and still lost. And throughout most of it, PBKS seem to have barely broken into a sweat, casting themselves as the team to beat, irrespective of whether they are on the road, or at home. Which brings us to New Chandigarh. For possibly the last time this campaign. For a contest between two genuine playoff contenders, and two certain title aspirants. To test out how strong and infallible this PBKS aura of invincibility is, and remains. Even as the Royals try to create an air of impregnability around themselves, and inscribe the first blot on an otherwise unblemished Punjab Kings record. A cracker awaits, so hop on to ESPNcricinfo's live coverage!

commentTextItems.html: four to finish the innings, and Stoinis has ransacked his way to 62 off 22! Low full toss outside off. Stoinis shuffles across and smears it through square leg. Perfect finish to what turned into another bruising PBKS innings, and they have made it past 220!

commentPostTextItems.html: 9:07pm Wow. What a finishing act. And PBKS will be thrilled that Stoinis has finally come to the party. When he arrived, PBKS were stuttering but by the end, they were motoring along, thanks to an unbeaten 62 off 22 balls. Arya was similarly brisk at the top, until he was outdone by Archer. Prabhsimran and Shreyas found it a little tougher and that was when RR threatened to turn the screw, only to run into a Stoinis storm. From an RR POV, Archer was sensational with the new ball and it was strange that he was not given his third over in the powerplay. Brijesh was also tidy in his first two overs, with Punja and Jadeja applying the squeeze through the middle. This will not be an easy chase, but RR have a firecracker opening pair to eat into this target significantly. Join us in a few minutes for the chase. Marcus Stoinis: (On his innings) Enjoyed that - it has been a different season, watching the boys smack it all around the park. Nice to get a hit tonight. They bowled really well. If you can make an impact in a couple of overs, it can change things. Funny we are talking about 200-210 not being enough - that is a compliment I think (for our team). They (the top order batters) did say it (the pitch) was a little bit slower. Not a lot of spin bowled on this ground. It was a little bit slower and they (RR spinners) executed really well. I think it is a good score. Start well, and then see how we go. Manish Kumar: "What is the duration of an innings break in IPL?" -- Somewhere between 10-15 minutes.

title: Jansen to Ferreira, SIX

commentTextItems.html: Ferreira with a fitting finish, and the streak is over! A tremendous knock under pressure, and the Punjab Kings have been subjected to their first loss of the season! Full toss on the stumps and that sums up how PBKS' night has gone. A little too easy for Ferrreira and he accepts that gift with glee, clubbing it over mid on and sealing the deal. A fist bump or two from the South African. RR's middle order, under fire for most of this tournament, has come to the party, and they decided to turn up against the table-toppers!

commentPostTextItems.html: 11:22pm And that will be all from us. We will be back at it tomorrow with more IPL action. Until then, from all of us here at ESPNcricinfo, it is goodbye! Donovan Ferreira, Player of the Match: It was a good innings - keeping my mind nice and clear, like when I was a kid playing with a toy truck. We need to keep showing intent and not be predictable. So, let's be calculative and play our shots. Important to take it ball by ball. Kept reminding myself it was only 11s and 12s. Luckily for me, Shubham took the pressure off me. It is a long tournament. We keep reminding ourselves that different guys need to put their hands up. Really pleased I am hitting the ball well. Important for us to win the match for the team. Riyan Parag, RR captain: As a team, what we have discussed, we achieved in this game. We could have restricted them to a lower score but the batters picked up the slack. Feel we could have bowled a few overs better here and there, and batted better. You are never going to get 40 overs (of perfect cricket) but our preparation has to be to play 40 overs of good cricket. (On the middle order standing up tonight) Concerns were from everyone else. It was their concerns, not our concerns. When middle order does not fire, the top three has to pick it up. When they fail to fire (or play at a slower rate), we have to pick it up. All the worries were from the outside, not from us. Plan was to keep wickets in hand and not fall behind the run-rate, they (Jaiswal and Sooryavanshi) made our jobs easier for us. After the powerplay, we got behind a little bit but picked it up again. (On Dubey) Him and Don - the way they played, they took it away from Punjab. Felt they would bowl a few more slower balls but the way they batted, it is commendable. Shreyas Iyer, PBKS captain: (Where it went wrong) 224 was a brilliant score - kudos to the batters. It was an exceptional performance on this pitch, which was tacky and slow. We fell short in our execution (with the ball). They had a tremendous partnership in the middle - Ferreira and Dubey scoring those crucial runs in the end. This is the format where a lot of players have changed their game and they go from ball one. At the end of the day, I feel it is about execution. Tonight just was not our day. It is important that we stick to the things we have been doing and have been following throughout. The body was also a bit fatigued but that cannot be the reason here. We have a couple of days to go back to the drawing board and come back (stronger). This is our first loss, it definitely teaches you a lot. We have played games where we have chased and defended 200-plus. One of those days where it did not go our way. Want to be positive and optimistic. (On their spinners) I felt it was difficult to score off the spinners. It was holding and offering a bit of turn. Brar, coming into his first game, showing that sort of personality, hats off to him. Yashasvi Jaiswal: (On batting with Sooryavanshi) He is playing amazing, always happy seeing from the other end. (On how it feels becoming the older partner) I don't think so I am older - I am still very young (laughs). Don't know what to say about it. We knew it is a high-scoring ground. So we had to go whenever we feel like. If it was in my range, wanted to hit it. Everyone trusts each other. Everyone is not going to perform on the same day. We have a very good team, so we are practicing hard, and we are enjoying a lot. We are just excited for all the games. 10:56pm Some run-chase this. And it was, unsurprisingly, set up by RR's openers. Sooryavanshi blazed away at the start, with Jaiswal joining in on the fun soon after. There was a brief wobble post it but Parag and Dubey played the requisite cameos, with Ferreira dominating the back half and ensuring that there were no hiccups. PBKS will be disappointed with their bowling effort. They bowled too many boundary balls and were made to pay. Their spinners held their own, and that might give them confidence and belief. But this is a night they will want to put behind quickly, and bounce back from.

title: Cummins to Jacks, 1 run

commentPreTextItems.html: 7:29pm We are almost in readiness. Cummins to take the new ball. Jacks and Rickelton to open. Jacks will take strike, and this could be a crucial powerplay in the game's context. The countdown timer runs down, slip in place, let's play! Pitch Report: There is a bias, in terms of the square boundaries - 61m to one side, 67m to the other. 72m hit straight down the ground. There is a nice covering of grass near the good length area when batters will be batting at the North End, and it gets a little barer at the other end. Taking pace off could be the key, and Ian Bishop reckons a fascinating contest might be in store. SRHFan: "You meant title has been elusive for Cummins & co, right? Because SRH do have a title - Achieved through diametrically opposite approach to the current bang-bang approach." -- Of course. For this particular bunch. SRH's title ascent in 2016 was and is the stuff of legend, capped off by Ben Cutting's incredible cameo in the final, which RCB fans might not want to look back at too fondly. Adil: "Surprising Mumbai playing only 7 batsmen in a bat first XI. Would have expected to play one more batter and have Ashwani or Gafanzar as impact sub. Hardik and Jacks can definitely complete 4 overs as the fifth bowler. " -- The balance does seem a little off. Rozezkhan: "What happened to Quinton De Kock? He was the match winner in a previous match." -- Hardik, at the toss, said he had picked up a wrist injury. Prasanna Kumar : "Robin Minz is the man whoz gonna change the fortunes for the MIs. 6 wins out of 7 is very much on the cards !! " Praveen: "Where should Jacks bat? Middle order or Open the innings?" -- Going by the team sheets, he might be opening tonight. He did open for the Oval Invincibles in the final of the most recent edition of the Hundred, and managed 72 off 41. Arjun_M: "RR's Shubham Dubey and SRH's Harsh Dubey are not related, but both represent Vidarbha in interstate events. Both also bat left-handed like Shivam Dube. Shivam and Shubham have shown their big-hitting ability, it's time Harsh shows his too." -- Harsh's primary suit is his left-arm spin, though. That said, he has improved as a white-ball batter in recent times and a captaincy stint for Vidarbha has only helped him develop further. 7:08pm Plenty to dissect from the toss. MI have made a whole host of changes, which is not a surprise given how their season has gone. Jacks is slotted to open alongside Rickelton, meaning this could be their fourth different opening combination this campaign. They seem a little light in the batting department, though, with Boult carded as high as eight. SRH, meanwhile, have opted for the finger-spin of Dubey over the wrist-spin of Shivang, which might have something to do with the possibility of dew. Aniket is likely to come in as SRH's Impact Player when they bat, although they also have the option of calling upon left-handed middle-order batter Smaran, who plays his domestic cricket for Karnataka and has been a prolific run-getter across formats. Mumbai Indians batting-first XI: Will Jacks, Ryan Rickelton (wk), Naman Dhir, Suryakumar Yadav, Tilak Varma, Hardik Pandya (capt), Robin Minz, Trent Boult, Ashwani Kumar, Jasprit Bumrah, AM Ghazanfar MI bench: Mayank Rawat, Raghu Sharma, Shardul Thakur, Krish Bhagat, Raj Bawa Sunrisers Hyderabad bowling-first XI: Travis Head, Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan (wk), Henrich Klaasen, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Salil Arora, Pat Cummins (capt), Harsh Dubey, Eshan Malinga, Praful Hinge, Sakib Hussain SRH bench: R Smaran, Aniket Verma, Liam Livingstone, Shivang Kumar, Harshal Patel 7pm It is toss time at the Wankhede Stadium. Hardik out in the middle alongside Cummins. Hardik will give the coin a spin. Cummins calls heads, but tails it is. MI will bat first. Looks like a good, breezy, slightly cold evening than usual, says Hardik and he does not expect dew to play a big role. Important for all of them to reset, he adds, and mentions they had a couple of boys' evening to refresh. de Kock misses out with a wrist injury. A couple of changes is all he says, before adding that Rickelton and Minz are playing. Rohit might take a couple more games to return, he concludes. Cummins says they would have bowled first anyway, and reckons the pitch could be a little tacky early. Adds it is pretty high-scoring normally, so about executing properly and about going in with a clear mind. Harsh Dubey comes in for Shivang, says Cummins. Sruthi chimes in with another snippet from the venue: MI are in urgent need of a reset, and quickly. News from the stadium is that Will Jacks has been seen marking his run-up. Could he be the spark that MI or at least their fans have been waiting for? He could play a role against SRH's lefties here…Speaking about SRH's lefties, heard that a sizeable section of the crowd has turned up to watch Abhishek Sharma. Will MI dampen their enthusiasm? There's a happy MI huddle going on atm here. Oh, and for those asking about Rohit, there's no sign of him out on the ground just yet. I'll keep an eye out. Amit: "In terms of batting LSG and MI possess some of the best T20 batter currently, its just the case of too many batters out of form at same time." -- Interesting take. A case can also be made that MI lack a batter who can tee off from ball one and is in the Abhishek/Sooryavanshi/Arya/Patidar mould. Vippsy: "Hardik Pandya played crucial knocks for MI in the pre GT era. Handling one of the most renowned franchise, batting, bowling is asking for too much from him. He was not handed India captaincy for the very same reason. I think he is too burdened for captaincy today" 6:45pm Hardik Pandya makes significant contributions in crucial situations for India, but he hasn't had the same impact for Mumbai Indians this season, which makes you ask the question - why is Hardik of MI so different from Hardik of India? Dimath K: "Tough start, but I've seen MI recover from worse. Still believing in a comeback." VS: "Is Rohit fit to play? MI needs his services badly. For SRH Head needs some runs" -- No clarity yet, and looks like we will only know about Rohit's availability at the toss. 6:35pm Ishan Kishan will be returning to his former home ground, and that should be intriguing to watch, as would the possible inclusion of Will Jacks, who picked up the POTM award against SRH last season. Will he play, though? Sruthi Ravindranath, who has settled in at the ground, says that he has marked his run-up. All that and much more in Vishal Dikshit's preview. Sai Krishna: "Nervous as an SRH fan. We never do well at the Wankhede. " 6:30pm Five IPL titles. Six IPL finals. Multiple playoff appearances. A fast bowler who is a cheat code. A pace-bowling all-rounder the envy of most teams. World Cup and IPL winning captains. And yet, the Mumbai Indians languish. Just a rung off the bottom. Looking anything but the champion team they are, and the franchise that has, on umpteen occasions, sprung to life after a sluggish beginning. Then there are the Sunrisers Hyderabad. Perhaps lopsided, in terms of team balance, but still finding a way. Their full-time captain is back, their team is winning, their batting is firing, and their bowling attack is doing just enough. But for this effervescent bunch that has made jaws drop in the IPL and has made countless people wonder about the possibilities of this format, a title remains elusive, and their dream, unrealised. And so, to the city of dreams. Where SRH have had nightmarish previous experiences and will not be able to immediately fulfil what this current complement of cricketers would have dreamt of, but where they can land a few significant punches - to reinforce their credentials, and to perhaps suck further wind out of Mumbai's sails. Even as MI, more successful than anyone else in the comp but now up against a ticking playoff clock, hope for an encore of some of their most famous hits, and for one of those trademark comeback tales. This has all the makings of a classic, so hop on to ESPNcricinfo's live coverage!

commentPostTextItems.html: 9:30pm Stunning. Just stunning. Rickelton carries his bat, and ends up scoring 123 out of 243 for MI. He set the powerplay up, he kept going through the middle and despite being bogged down by the heat, he found the energy to find the fence right at the end. Jacks was similarly enterprising at the top, with Hardik also finding his range. Suryakumar and Dhir, though, struggled, and that phase through the middle perhaps cost MI a score in excess of 250. SRH will be happy with how they closed out the innings. Prior to that, exerting control was an issue, unless Malinga was bowling. He was the pick of the bunch, with Cummins not shabby either. And even though this is a stiff chase, SRH, with their firepower, will feel they can give it a proper rattle. Join us in a bit for the chase. Jacks: Buzzing to be here after having some time off. Brilliant pitch and what we spoke about was playing with freedom. Loved batting with Ryan - amazing innings. Ryan got a late call-up after Quinny was not quite well. Last few times I have been here, it has been a batting paradise. We know we have our work cut out (even though we have 243). They bowled a lot of slower ball bouncers, and that was probably the hardest ball to hit. It is a big score but we have seen so many high scores chased down. We are in a good position but we have to bowl well. (On if he will take the new ball) We will see.

commentTextItems.html: a disdainful short-arm-jab, and SRH canter past MI to register the highest-ever run-chase in the IPL at this venue! Five on the trot for SRH, and MI have, once again, been blitzed out of the water at home! Back of a length and this sits up just outside off. Salil gets those fast hands through the ball and pummels it flat over deep mid wicket. Plenty of hugs and handshakes and smiles in the SRH camp. They were staring down at a mountain of runs, but have still managed to scale it with room to spare!

commentPostTextItems.html: 11:59pm That will be all from us. Another amazing and record-breaking night in the IPL. We will be back with more tomorrow, but until then, from all of us here at ESPNcricinfo, it is goodbye! Heinrich Klaasen, Player of the Match: (On if counter-attacking was the plan after the quick wickets) No, not really. Big gap at cow corner so had to take a risk early. Wicket was good. They had a quality bowling attack, so had to take a chance and see if we could make light work of it. (On the inside-out shot) The left shoulder gave me some issues, so I am not as strong over cow corner. Slinger is feeding me a lot of balls, so it is going nicely. (On if he is feeling invincible) Not at all. Humble. New day tomorrow. It is always fun, you can feel them (Abhishek and Head) putting the bowlers under pressure. If they are going (at a brisk rate), it makes your job easier. (On Arora) I told him that he does not have to worry. He asked me if he could hit it (when 11 were needed off 12) and I said yes - finish the game. Incredible to see him do it on the big stage, and we see it every day in the nets. Happy to see how his career is going. Pat Cummins, SRH captain: Tough to start with, but knowing our line-up and the pitch, few things had to go right but thought it was chaseable. (On the openers) When the pitch is good, they have so many different shots. Glad I am not bowling to them. (On the youngsters) They are super aggressive. They have a fearless attitude. Now, even 12 an over, you can chase as a batting unit, so you have to reset your expectations as a bowling unit. (On if he has any sympathy for the bowlers) A lot. How long do we have? (smiles) Really good bowlers, Eshan in our team, have a huge impact. Everything is going well at the moment, so keep hanging in there. Hardik Pandya, MI captain: (On how challenging it was) I don't think dew played much of a role, just that they played some good shots, we bowled bad balls. I enjoyed and had fun on the ground today. 244 - I will back my bowlers to stop it. But we could not execute. Enjoyed bowling barring the last three balls but enjoyed myself. Been that kind of a season. You get chances, you grab them. If you don't, it hurts you. This season, we don't have much options. I won't put my bowlers under the bus. As an overall unit, we have not been able to do what MI stands for. We have passionate owners and support staff, hopefully we will figure out something. (On the crowd support) We have not given them much opportunity to back us - but they have been fantastic and loyal. Sometimes it hurts when the opposition comes and they start chanting their name. But we probably need to give them more (to cheer and shout about). Abhishek Sharma: (Feeling as Orange Cap holder) If you see the total every team is scoring, you have to step up and do it for your team. I always try to get something out of Head, but he is quiet (and does his talking with the bat). Philosophy we have been using is to just see the ball and hit it. we always just congratulate each other on fifties and hundreds, and nothing else. We watch the ball and react. (On Malinga and Cummins) Big credit to the bowlers - the way they have stepped up. That is the reason we are winning games. It is a tough job. We are asking a lot of them but the way Malinga, Pat and others are keeping it simple…the way Pat is talking to the bowlers, it is effective. 11:35pm Wow. An exhilarating run-chase, punctuated by an emphatic exclamation mark at the end. Salil and Klaasen with the finishing act, but this was a coherent chasing effort throughout. Abhishek and Head set the stage with another whirlwind powerplay. There was a brief passage, especially once Abhishek and Head were dismissed, where MI would have felt they could apply the squeeze. But they ran into Klaasen, who began his innings with some risk-free strokes before clicking into over-drive and zinging past the five-time champions. Lots to ponder for MI. They bowled on both sides of the wicket, and kept dishing out boundary balls. Their decision to bring in Shardul as their Impact Player and then not use him at all was also baffling, as was their ploy to not begin their innings with Jacks, despite the obvious off-spin match-up against Abhishek and Head. Their season now hangs in the balance, and they will need to find a way to get it back on track soon.

Right now, both are teams in transition pretending they're still dynasties--and that's the real problem" VS: "CSK miss Dhoni the finisher. Is he fit to play today?" Unlikely, as the preview says, and Deiva can't spot him at the ground. Rohit Sharma also unlikely for MI btw Match preview by Deiva Muthu CSK vs MI: IPL's iconic rivals fast approaching must-win territory 6:30pm Hard fact first - a five-time champion team is facing a five-time champion team. Context, though, has been unsympathetic towards that fact and has left Chennai Super Kings and Mumbai Indians languishing. CSK had a horrid start and found bits of promise and success in their first and second thirds of the group stage. MI's trajectory started on a higher note before fizzling in a hope-sucking way. Both teams aren't out of the competition yet, but have very little margin now.

commentPostTextItems.html: Jamie Overton: Two-pacey, some balls went through nicely, others stayed low. Wanted to keep the stumps in play. We've found a rhythm of how our bowling needs to go. Mukesh, AK have been skilful, Noor is one of the best in the world in the middle overs. Pace on worked for me, stuck to hitting a length till it worked. If I got hit off that, I'd change it, that was the thinking. Will have to play good cricket shots, target is just 160. Have to be smart and hopefully we'll get over the line. Regan: "Only 3 sixes in the 14 overs after powerplay. " Yep, and pp had seven sixes Kannan: "CSK's powerplay will decide the winner" Sivaraman : "Irrespective of runs /wicket, I am happy with csk bowlers... Only one wide or no ball bowled in whole innings.. very discipline from all bowlers.." Just the one wide and even that came in the last over 9:24pm That was a poor back-ten from MI. CSK's pacers were clinical, spreading out their lines, bowling hard lengths and yorkers. They didn't have to vary their pace all that much. Overton hurried batters, Kamboj changed things up nicely. Noor took key wickets and might be the pick of th bowlers. Ricketon was sixy at the start for MI. SKY started well but couldn't carry on. Dhir top-scored with a fifty but did get stuck in the later alongside Hardik, whose timing deserted him bigtime.

commentTextItems.html: Late reverse to finish, amazing reverse to finish. Kartik was deep in the crease, likely awaiting the yorker. Got a fullish length ball that angled away sharply. So he stood diagonally in front of the wideline and saucered the bat across his body to lift it over short third. Gun celebrations from Kartik

commentPostTextItems.html: Single-game super Saturday is done. El Clasico has been wiped out by CSK. Two games coming up tomorrow. See you for that, bye for now. Ruturaj Gaikwad, POTM and CSK captain We started well, then they got momentum. We pulled it back after powerplay and were chasing 20-30 runs less. It was about getting a good start and then one of the batters had to go deep. (Kamboj) He keeps it simple. He understands how the pitch plays, he thinks like a batter. Noor needed momentum and wickets like this, he comes into play. He's made adjustments and is doing well. We thought about how to get the balance right, get the batter at No. 8 and the extra bowler if needed. Veer does that role well, both youngsters (Kartik) are doing well, so gave them a chance (and no Akeal). Feels good to bat till the end. I was always feeling well, confident. But in T20s you can hit good shots straight to fielders. But my wife, team-mates and management made sure I was feeling well. I wanted to make sure to take the team to the end if I got a start. Confidence booster for Kartik. (Urvil) He's a six-hitter but doesn't slog wildly. Picks and chooses his bowlers and deliveries. Coming in at No. 4, he gives balance. Plays well to pacers and spinners. Once he gets going, he'll give a lot more in the coming years. (Approach for next game) Have to keep it simple. Mistakes will happen, but we've to give everything for the jersey and the fans. Kartik Sharma I was thinking we have to chase this and finish it. Glad to have done it. Ruturaj said play the game you know, not anything else. Pitch was slow, was holding for the spinners. All shots felt nice. (About his celebration) Had decided to do it if we won. No questions on his batting for Hardik Hardik Pandya (Not his day?) Not the season, I feel. They played better; bowled, fielded and batted better. At one point, we were looking at 180-190. We couldn't get momentum post-10 overs, not the finish as well. Not easy to play shots early in the innings. It was about playing calculated innings, which they did. Batters couldn't get under the batter, they bowled better. We would've had to throw fireballs to get them out. We went with our bowling options, they played smart cricket and were better. Edwin: "CSK definitely lacking power hitter - the way Krish over went only for 4 runs??? The game should have been done in 2 balls but needed 8 balls. CSK should look at this. " Navin Daga: "In a 150 chase, if you cannot let Bumrah bowl 4 overs, then you have some horrible planning and match awareness" 11:14pm Another feeble performance from MI. They lost it in the first innings. Positives pile on for CSK's batting. They could've finished it earlier but solid fifties from Kartik and Ruturaj. Ruturaj actually got off to a quick start but stablised later on. Urvil played some fantastic shots too. Bumrah pretty much had Samson twice in one over but nothing afterwords. Ghazanfar bowled a few wicket-taking balls but was picked for boundaries too. Raghu showed control on debut but like Boult, Bhagat and Hardik, didn't take wickets.

commentPreTextItems.html: 3.29pm Alright then, we are ready to go. Sunil Narine is going to open the bowling for KKR! Over the wicket to Abhishek Afzal: "I selected NKR as man of the match in the game.. guess what he is not playing". Ouch! Arnav: "Crazy to think that the last time Manish Pandey played in any professional capacity was against SRH in May of 2025... Almost an entire year. What has he even been up to?" V. Kalyani : "TraviSHAKES the opponent!" Ronish: "Both Manish Pandey and Smaran playing their first game this season.Contrasting stories Pandey was left out from the Karnataka team with the rise of youngsters like Smaran" V. Kalyani : "Who's the wicketkeeper for KKR?" -- Angkrish Raghuvanshi is set to keep for KKR. 3.20pm Thanks Himanshu, and hello everyone. Will we see another Travishek special today? Can KKR keep Klaasen quiet? We have an exciting first innings lined up. Dylon: "Why NKR not playing today? Any news?" -- He's out with illness. We're running a live prediction game called SIX SENSE for this match. Let's see how much of an expert you are. Who do you think will win the match? Who'll be the Player of the Match? Click the link and submit your predictions. 3.15pm We're 15 minutes away from the action, and here comes Abhimanyu, who'll be with you for the first 10 overs. Let him know which side you're supporting. AdnanKapri: "Not sure why thinktank not allowing Allen and Seifert to open together for KKR." --- Rahane's strength remains to open, and even if he were to drop down, playing both Allen and Seifert would leave KKR to choose one from Powell and Green. Kolkata Knight Riders: 1 Ajinkya Rahane (capt), 2 Angkrish Raghuvanshi, 3 Cameron Green, 4 Rovman Powell, 5 Manish Pandey, 6 Rinku Singh, 7 Sunil Narine, 8 Anukul Roy, 9 Kartik Tyagi, 10 Varun Chakravarthy, 11 Vaibhav Arora. Impact bench: Allen, Ramandeep, Tejasvi, Saini and Seifert. Sunrisers Hyderabad: 1 Travis Head, 2 Abhishek Sharma, 3 Ishan Kishan (wk), 4 Heinrich Klaasen, 5 Salil Arora, 6 Aniket Verma, 7 R Smaran, 8 Pat Cummins (capt), 9 Harshal Patel, 10 Eshan Malinga, 11 Shivang Kumar. Impact bench: Dubey, Hinge, Livingstone, Sakib and Zeeshan. 3pm Time for the toss. SRH opt to bat first. Pat Cummins says the "pitch looks really good". He doesn't spot too much moisture in it. Cummins feels the youngsters have been "fantastic", and announces the changes: Smaran and Harshal in for Reddy and Dubey. Ajinkya Rahane wanted to bat first too. He says the long break has helped his side. Two changes for KKR as well: Allen and Pandey play for Seifert and Ramandeep. Satya: "Only Seifert and Allen opening can combat this SRH team" VS: "I expect Pathirana to play today. I will bolster their bowling, with Narine and Varun doing well" 2.50pm There's ten minutes to the toss. Would you like to see any change in the two teams today? Remember, while SRH are entering this contest with five successive wins, KKR have won two in a row. 2.40pm It's KKR's misfiring batters up against explosive SRH, as Sruthi Ravindranath's preview reminds us. Both teams had similar starts to the season; while SRH have staged a resurgence, KKR have fallen behind. Krishna Sumanth: "My fiancee is from Kolkata and I am from Hyderabad. Whom should I be supporting today?" --- Just hope that there's a washout cricket which wins. Pranav: "Is this pitch expected to be a belter?" --- Is it going to rain during the monsoon?! Tish: "I want this to be a high-scoring match today!!" --- A matter of time before the 300 comments make their way if SRH bat first. 2.30pm It's a Sunday, and that could only mean a chilled morning with late (or no) breakfast, binge watching from the couch... and an IPL double-header, in case you forgot. We're into match No. 45 - how did nearly 60% of the tournament finish already?! - and no matter the heat and the overflow of runs, the eyeballs are all set for one more take of Travishek. It's SRH vs KKR in Hyderabad this afternoon, with the hosts on a five-match winning run and the visitors desperate to rise up from No. 8 before it gets too late.

commentTextItems.html: stunner from Powell!! This is perhaps the catch of the season. He was at deep midwicket and ran forward, but seemed to have overrun. Realising that, he threw himself nearly behind him with his right hand stretched out like a mit. The ball managed to stick in it even as Powell tumbled and banged his head down on the ground. Even his glasses broke in the process, but the third umpire checks replays multiple times to confirm if it was a clean catch as Powell's hand touched the turf while he fell. He's finally satisfied - Powell already has a new pair of glasses on in the meanwhile - and Klaasen walks back. Klaasen had pulled this bouncer from wide of off, and ended up mistiming it

title: Kartik Tyagi to Patel, OUT

commentTextItems.html: gone!! SRH are bowled out for 165. Nobody ever said 300 was easy, if I have to borrow a line from The Scientist!! Slower delivery from Tyagi, who bowled it short and outside off. But he still got good carry despite the lack of pace. The ball finished around middle, and Harshal went for the pull. He ended up getting a top edge, and Arora took the skied ball by moving to his left

commentPostTextItems.html: Mounika: "This is going to be interesting. SRH definitely has the bowling attack to defend this score. Here's hoping for a thriller!" --- Harshal Patel's slower balls and cutters could be key. Abhishek Sharma takes the Orange Cap from Rovman Powell, before the latter speaks: "We know they are very good with their top three and four batters. Our spinners are our strength. It's good to see Chakravarthy back in the wickets. Those things [the catch] happen when you have good hands! I was about five to ten meters off the boundary... so I came up a little bit and ensured I gave himself enough time to take the catch. I'm aware of everything that's going on, man! Our bowlers didn't start the competition the way they wanted to... so we have to take those catches. I think it's a below-par total. It's a good wicket. When the ball gets old, it's a little bit harder. But it's still a good wicket." 5.12pm SRH lose 8 for 60 in the last ten overs. That's the most un-SRH thing you could ever think of after seeing them fly their way to 105 in nine overs, not least when you expect them to tickle the 300 mark even in sleep. The KKR spinners found turn, and the slow nature of the pitch helped their cause too. Narine and Varun combined for figures of 8-0-67-5, and SRH slipped, stopped and fumbled. They need to defend just 166 to win six in a row. But can they? Join Abhi for the chase.

commentPostTextItems.html: That's it from the first match of the double-header Sunday. KKR's third win in a row keeps those above them on the points table on their toes. But they're still eighth, and have a long way to go before they threaten their competitors for a place in the playoffs. For now, though, you can switch over to GT vs PBKS. Until next time, it's goodnight! Varun Chakravarthy is the Player of the Match, and he's still hobbling: "It's just the impact pain. Still I'm not able to put my foot fully down. He hit it very fast, and I had to stop it as he hit it very straight; otherwise it would've been a four. I've been saying this every year. When the IPL starts, the first four matches are going to be flat wickets. Because Head was extending his hands very well, I didn't want him to do that. The guys are coming together. Nice to see the batting group finish it this way. We can make a serious dent in the IPL." Ajinkya Rahane: "It was a good wicket to bat on. I thought 190-200 would have been difficult to chase. Credit to our bowlers. They kept on taking wickets. The bowling unit has been doing really well. Credit goes to our bowling coaches. It's all about planning and executing. As long as you're clear in your head, that's important. Going into the break, the victory was very important. We lost those five matches, but the atmosphere was calm. We kept it really cool. Really happy for Varun. The way he came back was amazing. Works really hard. Great attitude. He has been bowling in the tough situations. I'm sure he'll continue his performance." Time for the presentations Shameer: "So Finn Allen is MoM?" --- I would go for Varun. Angkrish Raghuvanshi: "I'm just happy we won. When I was walking back, I saw my coach shaking his head with the way I got out. It just got very easy after Finn and Ajinkya gave us the start. Not worry about the previous game too much. Just go and try to enjoy the game. When I was a kid, I used to dream of this. It's just me living the dream. So many stars to learn from. I was trying to hit straight back over his [the bowler's] head. Maybe if I went inside out, I would connect. In a long tournament, that [a dip in form] happens." Pat Cummins: "Not our best day. We got off to a pretty good start. From where we were, we should have found a way to get 200 or 180. You've just got to adapt. Our first eight or ten overs were excellent. I think 180 or something like that [was par]. It did dry up. We dragged it right to the end. There's only little moments that can make the difference." 7.02pm The win should have come much earlier, but KKR eventually get there in more than 18 overs. That's three wins in a row for them, and they break SRH's streak of five victories in a row. KKR had blazed away to 71 in the powerplay, and you thought they would hunt 166 down with at least five overs remaining. But that was not to be. Raghuvanshi and Rahane batted patiently on a slow pitch where the ball gripped, and took their side to a smooth win.

So, a contest with decent stakes then. There were reports of rain in parts of the city over the course of the day but the weather at the Feroz Shah Kotla is fair and should remain so. commentPostTextItems.html: Rajkumar Lingav: "Hats off to CSK management for backing Kartik Sharma with an extended run. Earlier, he often threw away his wicket after a couple of sixes, but this innings showed real maturity and composure. It's a big step forward, well played, Kartik!" ranjana: "You missed the 100 run partnership bro" I did indeed, 114 off 66 balls to win the chase for CSK. Another chase done and dusted too easily in the end this season. Axar Patel reckons DC were 10-15 runs short, and that the wicket got a little better to bat on later in the game, especially for the batters who were set. He says it wasn't easy for new batters to get set, but with set batters they were able to take the game away. I'm still surprised that he chose to bat first today. VS: "It is always advisable to bowl first. For the chasing team they know the score and can pace their innings accordingly " Mukund: "Rutu losing the toss is good after all." I'll have the presentation for you shortly, with Samson waiting to collect his POTM award. Edwin: "Karthik Sharma was on 17 runs off 21 balls. He ended up scoring 24 runs off last 10 balls helped the NRR boost for CSK" Ramesh: "Chennai did not even use their impact player." Ruturaj Gaikwad: We were always positive, we were always closer than we were last year, we had covered all bases, Sanju coming in ... we just needed a couple of wins, after the third game we got that and it started coming together. Obviously Sanju is the backbone now ... the bowling wins you tournaments, we have Akeal, Overton ... Kamboj is also there, smart bowler, he had an off day today but he's been impressive. (Kartik Sharma) His skillset was already there, he just needed a couple of games to start with, he didnt get the time in previous games, now he got the time, he's not a wild slogger, he can rotate strike and hit the pockets, good to get his confidence going. Sanju Samson: They are calling me Chetta but I like Sanju more ... (laughs) I have been working a bit on my initial movement and it has been coming off. I've been doing it for the last few years and it's tactical as well depending on the bowlers and how you want to approach them ... to be very honest I am always like this (calm) but you are seeing me more in the middle now so you feel I am calm, even outside I am calm. Looking at what we were chasing, how the wicket was behaving, even if we were 35 for no loss in the powerplay, we could capitalise in the middle overs. I had to be a bit too selfish to get a hundred so I thought lets win the game ... finishing not out, winning the game gives you more satisfaction. Srini: "CricInfo's Top 5 MVP for the day are either CSK or Ex-CSK players (Sanju, Hosein, Rizvi, Noor and Ngidi). YellowForLife uh? " Thank you for following the game with us and for all your emails. We'll be back tomorrow for SRH vs PBKS. Big game that. Good night.

Also, the playoffs week will be hosted at three venues. Have you tried today's WORD PLAY game? The answer is a legend of the game. Try and guess it in fewer than six attempts. 7pm Tails says Shreyas, and tails it is. PBKS bowl. "Two losses, amazing learnings. But still being on top of the table gives us amazing motivation," he says. "Surface looks beautiful. Haven't seen a single blade of grass." Shashank Singh and Lockie Ferguson come in. "I can't read pitches, they seem to all be high-scoring here," Cummins says. Nitish Reddy is back for Aniket Verma The XIs for you: SRH: Abhishek, Head, Kishan, Klaasen, Smaran, Salil, Nitish, Cummins, Shivang, Malinga, Sakib Impact: Aniket, Hinge, Livingstone, Harshal, Dubey PBKS: Prabhsimran, Connolly, Shreyas, Shashank, Shedge, Stoinis, Jansen, Lockie, Vyshak, Arshdeep, Chahal Impact: Arya, Brar, Bartlett, Musheer, Vinod VS: "It is Travishek vs Prabharya show today. Whoever win the battle have a chance to beat the other team. Looking forward to see a cracking contest." Arjun reckons: "With Suryansh Shedge latching on the opportunity given last match, PBKS have finally got a replacement of Wadhera, should Shashank comes back. Now their only worry is Bartlett vs Ferguson. Guess they will go with the latter" Arsh: "Last year after getting hammered by SRH at this venue, PBKS started their serious ascent to the playoffs, as a PBKS fan I don't mind another defeat today." - Really? It'd be their third straight loss. Could seriously dent momentum. VR8: "While Smaran got dismissed to a needless shot in the other match, I would like SRH to give him another chance!" -- The IPL world can be ruthless. With Nitish Reddy having recovered from an illness and ready to go, it's likely Smaran will make way. Have you played the SIX SENSE GAME yet? Make your predictions for the SRH-PBKS game and see how many you get correct. 6.30pm Hello everyone. A blockbuster awaits in Uppal as table toppers Punjab Kings take on third-placed Sunrisers Hyderabad. If PBKS win, then we'll have no change to the points table for a fifth straight day. If SRH win, they will go top of the table. I'm Shashank Kishore. For company, I've got Himanshu Agrawal joining us in a little while. Stay locked. Brace for another exciting, but long evening - as is the norm.

title: Vyshak to Klaasen, OUT

commentPreTextItems.html: Ohh, Vyshak stops into his run-up... and sees one of the floodlights go off. So we have to wait for the final ball of the innings. But it's a short wait, and we're ready. A six to finish? That'll take them past 240.

commentTextItems.html: Jansen takes it at long-off!! SRH can't touch 240. Vyshak bowled a slower delivery, and on a hittable length outside off. But all Klaasen could do was balloon it up miles in the air. Jansen moves forward and takes it low to restrict SRH to 235

commentPostTextItems.html: RaviP: "Someone commented Klassen needs to be there at crease for 19.6, and here he is getting out on the same ball." Heinrich Klaasen puts on the Orange Cap: "Once again a fantastic start from Travishek. They make it look so easy. We lost wickets at crucial stages again. It started stopping a little bit. There's not a lot of bounce. It's a fantastic wicket to bat on. The bowling unit just need to do what they've been doing." 9.08pm Are SRH 15 short? Remember, PBKS have even successfully hunted down 265 this season - a record T20 chase. We're in a day when even 235 feels like being restricted. There's a cagey feeling there; why couldn't we get to 250? Once again, Abhishek and Head flayed their way as long as they lasted. PBKS dropped three catches and missed a stumping chance. What would have been had some if not all of them been taken? Maybe a small total of 200? But PBKS will believe they can hunt this down. Join Shashank for the chase.

commentPostTextItems.html: With today's win, SRH displace PBKS at the top of the points table. But a lot of movement would've taken place by the time they're next in action - on May 12. For now, though, they've taken a step towards playoffs while leaving PBKS wondering what would've been. But thanks for joining us tonight as we wrap this up. Goodnight and goodbye! Pat Cummins is the Player of the Match: "Punjab are a really good side. I thought the batters to get off to what we did was sensational. No matter what the score is, bowling second against that side was clinical. We're pretty good at playing it at our pace. It's just trying to max out. We're no good during the day [at home]! It gripped a little bit, which suits our bowlers. We've seen it before; we can adjust. I fell really good. Came into this fresh. Not much has worked for any team in the powerplay, really. We've got lots of options. Good result [for Connolly]. Good to see the Aussies do well. Hope so [it's our season]." Time for the presentations Chavan: "So PBKS dethroned after remaining there for almost 49 matches" Daniel Vettori: "When you lose the toss, you go against what you want. Got lucky with the catches. You saw how difficult Sakib was in the end. I think there's enough in the wicket. We understand what we need to do. We've got some tricky surfaces coming up in Ahmedabad and Chennai. Cummins and Ishan have been brilliant this season. The main thing he brings is calmness." Shreyas Iyer: "It was a bit too much because we dropped catches at the start. The wicket kept getting slower. They played comprehensive cricket, and showed us how to win the match. I feel we got a fairytale start in the tournament, and everyone was in a great space... If we are going to continue with the same form, that's not going to help us. Connolly is phenomenal. His mindset is top notch. He has got a knack of scoring big runs in pressure situations. The way Chahal bowled, he was fearless. I asked him to be attacking - especially when new batters were in. Unfortunately, we weren't able to take catches." 11.08pm So PBKS save a bit of face in the end. But what do they do about the dropped catches? They put plenty of them down to help propel SRH to 235, and eventually fell 33 runs short despite Connolly's maiden T20 century. PBKS have now lost three in a row, and nine in a row in Hyderabad. The next highest after Connolly's 107* was 28. For SRH, it was the usual show from Abhishek, Head and Klaasen that set it up.

commentPreTextItems.html: Nearly game time. Mitch Marsh and young Arshin Kulkarni to open the batting for LSG. Bhuvneshwar Kumar with the new ball for RCB. Toss, 7pm Rishabh Pant flips the coin, huge roar from the crowd ... because RCB have won the toss and decided to bowl first. Rajat Patidar says it's a black soil pitch on which the scores have been low, so they want to restrict LSG and chase. Same team for RCB. Three changes for LSG! Arshin Kulkarni for Josh Inglis, who is injured. Inglis had copped a blow on the hand while fielding in his first game in Mumbai. Mohsin is also out with a niggle, Mayank Yadav might come in for him. And Shahbaz Ahmed replaces M Siddharth. Pant reckons this pitch is better than previous ones in Lucknow, and says it's a 180-190 pitch. LSG batting-first XI: 1 Mitch Marsh, 2 Arshin Kulkarni, 3 Nicholas Pooran, 4 Aiden Markram, 5 Rishabh Pant (capt & wk), 6 Akshat Raghuwanshi, 7 Himmat Singh, 8 Shahbaz Ahmed, 9 Digvesh Rathi, 10 Mohammed Shami, 11 Prince Yadav LSG's Impact player options: Mayank Yadav, Mukul Chowdhary, Abdul Samad, M Siddharth, Avesh Khan. RCB bowling-first XI 1 Virat Kohli, 2 Jacon Bethell, 3 Devdutt Padikkal, 4 Rajat Patidar (capt), 5 Jitesh Sharma (wk), 6 Romario Shepherd, 7 Krunal Pandya, 8 Bhuvneshwar Kumar, 9 Josh Hazlewood, 10 Suyash Sharma, 11 Rasikh Dar RCB's Impact Player options: Tim David, Jordan Cox, Mangesh Yadav, Vicky Otswal, Venkatesh Iyer. Tim : "As a Saffa I am a bit perplexed why LSG haven't shown any faith in Breetzke? Especially with Marsh not firing." Manish: "who is Arshin? is this a debut for him (reminded me of Arshavin, I am a happy Arsenal fan, with fingers crossed)" He played a couple of games for LSG last season, he was part of the previous India U-19 World Cup team. Sanket: "With PBKS recent loses means that top spot is up for grabs. And we all know that how important is to finish in top 2 for winning the title. After a short break RCB must be looking to take advantage of that PBKS slip up. But these games are not easy ones, considering how the Ekana surface has played this season. RCB might need another spinner here they should start Bethell, he can be handy option against LSG right handed batters. " Arjun_M: "Let's just hope Mayank Yadav gets to play all the remaining matches. He can't be much worse than Avesh Khan right now, or even a very out-of-form Shami." word is that he might be playing today. Chuvi : "Unable to understand as to why LSG were unable to play with freedom given the talent " Adarsh: "Lucknow has been a seamers' paradise so far. Eagerly awaiting Bhuvi and Hazlewood's bowling here." SamirD.: "If there's one ground RCB's "see ball-hit ball" batters won't enjoy, it's Lucknow. Ekana isn't a runway -- it exposes technique, patience and game awareness. Flat-track merchants struggle here, proper batters survive.That said, with LSG's trademark "Luck-now" energy this season, expect another dramatic one-over finish instead of domination. " 6.40 pm Have you played the SIX SENSE game today yet? Make your predictions for LSG vs RCB and see how many you get right in the end. LSG are on a six-match losing streak; RCB also lost their previous game to GT, and are in action after a week's break. VS: "When will Salt be back? Hope Bethell makes his chances count." No definite word on Salt's return yet. I miss watching him in the field. Sowmya : "On current form unable to see LSG challenging RCB leave alone winning. " Arjun: "Lucknow have nothing to lose here, considering their chances to qualify are almost non existent. I hope they come out and play some inspiring cricket." 6.30 pm Good evening folks, and welcome to match #50 of IPL 2026, between RCB and LSG in Lucknow. It's No. 3 vs No. 10, so there's a clear favourite, but as Sidharth Monga says in his preview, it could also be one of those banana-peel fixtures. Last night, we had a new No. 1. Punjab Kings had led the points table for a month, and then they nose-dived, losing one, two, three in a row and gave up the top spot to Sunrisers Hyderabad. SRH's stay at the top could be short-lived if RCB win tonight, they will go to No. 1 on net run rate and with a game in hand. There was some rain in Lucknow in the lead-up to the game but it looks fine at the moment. Word is that the majority of the fan support might be ... for RCB. Hussey: "I came across a lot of pre match reviews that this match is going to be a low scoring game due to nature of the today's pitch to be used. What's your take on it? Is it black or mixed soil pitch? Used before right?" Tonight's pitch is the one on which LSG and KKR played that Super Over game, after a tie on 155 in normal time. The highest total at this venue in four games is only 165, and that's saying something in this high-scoring season. Sanket: "From last couple of season RCB is one of those teams who follows that modern style of playing aggressively from ball 1 , no matter what conditions you get. But this Lucknow ground is not really suited to that kind of batting style so far this season. so someone like Kohli can play that anchor kind of role here especially if they bat first. LSG's batting has been really poor (apart from the last game), so you can take this approach, you dont always need to play that aggressive brand."
