commentPostTextItems.html: 8.51 pm Okay, the RCB players are getting ready just beyond the boundary. Kohli's having a very animated chat with Romario. Anu Joseph: "In reply to Vaneez: If Hazlewood could Hazlewood the way Hazlewood should Hazlewood, then Hazlewould." Applauds! MT34: "Now Hazlewood is definitely going to end the game with a 3-fer!" Only 47 minutes lost so far so no overs will be reduced. We can lose another 13 minutes before losing overs, I think. dev: "Left field opinion on the shepherd discussion, why not play iyer instead of shepherd that opens up a slot for duffy instead of salam as your third pace option. Would be something to see duffy and Hazelwood together in rcb colors with bhuvi swinging it up top. " 8.45 pm Work is being done to get the ground ready for the restart. Super soppers, cloths being dragged around the outfield. shouldn't be too long now. Vaneez: "As a RCB fan, I feel this season Hazlewood hasn't Hazlewooded the way Hazlewood used to Hazlewood." Well played! Him: "@cricfan I agree but having an extra batsman allow the batters to go all in if duffy replces shpered than batting don't look as explosive as it looks now" Nabin Basnet: "I know its not gonna get published. But still replying to cricfan. Every team looks short on bowling options when a batter gets in the zone.And Shepherd isn't picked just as a backup bowler, his finishing ability adds balance to the XI. If top order fails, that's not really on him alone. RCB probably prefer overall depth over an extra specialist." Oh ye of little faith. Sachinfan: "aah the memory of an IPL fan, didnt Hazlewood hazlewood at Delhi?" lakesidey: "Vaneez that sounds like it should be How much wood would a Hazelwood hazel if a Hazelwood would hazel wood? Same energy!" 8.38 pm Covers coming off! Super-soppers on. YD: "While the criticism towards Kulkarni is valid, if overs get reduced, not having retired him out as of yet would probably be better after DLS adjustment." We're not yet at the over-reduction stage, but it's getting closer. Cricfan : "Hoping for George to have come back from tea break to publish my comment - This is the problem I have with RCB playing XI. There is no 6th bowling option (due respect to Shepherd) if one opposition batter is in the zone. Can't count on shepherd the batter when top order finds it tricky. Similarly, can't count on his bowling when others take a hit. Better to have Duffy or left hand variety of mangesh yadav." Tea? I'm a coffee person but I haven't gone anywhere. 8.30 pm The square is still covered, the fans have moved from the lower seats under the shelter of the upper stands. But the rain seems to have eased up at the moment. MT34: "@Ben: Don't really think it's a 200 pitch, it's just that its been outrageous batting from Marsh. Have a feeling that even other batters will struggle." If you haven't played today's WORDPLAY game yet, give it a go and try and get it in six attempts. Or if you're a quiz person, See if you can get these questions right? Kabeer: "@Deepak Gupta Looking at my wet hair n wet seat, I am sure the game is happening in Lucknow.Though rain is gone now n hope the game resumes soon" 8.22 pm The players are going off for rain, covers being brought on. Surely LSG will not send Kulkarni back out once the rain stops? Manikanta : "How heavy is the rain,RCB fan here and seeing this, I would prefer settling for a washout." It's not massive at the moment, but hard to tell what the overhead conditions are like in the night. Deepak Gupta: "Living 3 km away from Stadium. No rain at my place and children playing cricket in my society. Is this match really happening in Lucknow?" Been getting a few such comments, hopefully this shower will blow over quickly. Shriram: "Outrageous that 70 of 76 runs Marsh has scored have come in boundaries" Nalin : "This reminds me of all the negative comments to a certain player called Tewatia" Well if Kulkarni has a similar turnaround, a legend will be born.

commentPostTextItems.html: 9.55 pm Play should restart shortly, and I'm hearing that no overs lost yet! We're in for a late finish tonight, folks. Will confirm soon. Ishwar: "The concept of Orange cap needs tweaking. The number of runs alone doesn't cut it anymore. A new composite metric that incorporates strike rate, game situation and number of runs should be used to award that cap. Same for purple cap too, a bunch of tai lender wickets, wickets in a one sided affair or 4/60 in a high scoring game shouldn't be valued the same as 1/20 in a high scoring game. A bit more nuance is needed to award merit than merely looking at number of runs or wickets." 9.46 pm The cover protecting the square has been taken off. Rohan: "Kohli is not even in the top 5 in the race for the orange cap but still most of the people think that he is going to win the orange cap. Aura of VK." Shadow-Shell: "@Swaroop I guess Sanju is immune to that trend" Sahan: "Rain is unfortunate for Marsh and Pooran - their rhythm will get broken" Shaurya: "Such an epic season...a 15 year old boy in contention to win the orange cap amongst such seasoned veterans of the game!!" AdiCan: "@Rohan: That is not aura. That is people not looking at things objectively and letting bias rule their mind. " And to counter that, Ruthwik : "Can someone tell Rohan that Kohli only played 9 matches. It's not aura it's common sense" 9.35 pm Scratch that, the drizzle is back and so are the covers. Akshith Rao: "when do we start losing overs?" We're probably in that territory already. Swaroop : "Don't forget this was the same ground which RCB chased close to 230 successfully and with 8 balls to spare! Interestingly Pant had then scored a century and still ended up on the losing side. Batters scoring 100's and ending up on the losing side has been a trend of this IPL!" Still drizzling and the covers firmly in place at 9.42 pm. DM: "The players have to get back on pretty soon or we will miss the second timeout." LOL. 9.30 pm Covers coming off. Ground staff getting a HIIT workout in. AdiCan: "This is advantage RCB. DLS is not made for the quick fire scoring of T20 era. Any target RCB will get is probably lower than the actual targe than LSG would've set" 9.23 pm More rain, I'm afraid, and off the players go and on come the covers. Sujatha : "101/139 is insanity! What a knock" Ashish: "@Harish Bubna - considering the fact that it is drizzling, LSG are in a good position as they have lost just 1 wicket. In case their innings gets terminated or RCB's innings gets terminated then the taregt would be bigger for RCB. SHortened chase is not always easy. The RRR pressure would be extreme for RCB if LSG dont lose too many wickets and keep scoring at this pace. DLS would take into account how LSG would have approached when they knew they had lesser number of overs to bat." I expect the game will now start getting shortened and overs will be lost. vaibhavR: "6/10 centuries ended up in losses before this match, hoping to see one more added to that list (sorry Bison and lsg fans)" paramdev: "How many comments for 175 ? just trying to Jinx as an RCB fan" If Marsh bats though and gets enough strike, it may be on. Humaid Salman : "Don't understand the captaincy here. Why do you bowl Shepherd in a rain-curtailed match. Be shrewd and bowl out your main bowlers."

commentTextItems.html: just the single to long off, LSG have a win at long last, a win after eight losses at home, a win after six losses this season, they are still at No. 10 in the points table but there will be some relief in their camp tonight

commentPostTextItems.html: RCB miss their chance to go top of the table. RCB captain Rajat Patidar: I think we were sure of how we wanted to go about the target, we did well, just one or two shots behind. Really good pitch, batting track, was coming nicely on to the bat, just 2-3 shots away. Difficult to analyse just after the game, I need time to analyse it. We have four games more, we're taking it one step at a time. Alex: "Rather unusual to choose a leg spinner for the final over. It worked but Pant would have been toasted and roasted if it didn't." Indeed, both Rathi and Shahbaz wanted it, I think and well done to him. Prince Yadav says he got over his misfield pretty quickly and was focussed on the next ball. He says he had a chat with Virat after their previous game and Kohli had told him to stick to his lengths, and he did just that today. Says LSG can't do much about the matches that have gone past, but will try and finish the season well. Harshit Goyal: "Wow, their first win since April 9 for LSG! " Kaleem : "At 9/2 many teams would lose heavily. The margin was single digit, that shows the depth of this RCB team" I'll have the presentation for you shortly. Srini: "Finally, a match that could have truly gone either way till the last 3 balls." I know! It's been a while. Hari B: "Marsh played excellent knock! But Pant's cameo really changed the momentum at the halfway stage!!" LSG captain Rishabh Pant: It was a good game for us, for sure. We have been trying a lot of things, it means a lot for us. We have been trying to put together a perfect game where batting and bowling comes together, we have had some bad luck, but really happy to get a win here. (Decision between Rathi and Shahbaz) It was a tough one, but you have to trust your bowler, Rathi was the right match-up for Shepherd and he got the job done. Our strength this season has been bowling, Prince, Shami bhai, Rathi, Sid ... there have been good things for out bowling unit. Mitch Marsh is the POTM: It has been a tough season, nice to get on the right side, really good for morale, disappointing season until today ... A few of the Indian boys said before the game the pitch looked better so I tried to maximise the powerplay. I just tried to get as many as I could in the powerplay, get a good start and have an impact on the game, it's an area we haven't got right so far. I think we batted well last two games, 10-15 short in Mumbai ... we were courageous in the way we bowled tonight. Bangalore bat deep, really proud of the young guys in our attack. Phew. Match. No 50 done and dusted and it was a good one. That's all we've got for you tonight, and thank you for all your emails, do join us for DC vs KKR tomorrow. Cheers!

commentPreTextItems.html: 7.30pm Spin to start the game! The keeper is standing up to Anukul Roy's left-arm spin, Nissanka on strike, no slip. Let's get this show started! 7.27pm KKR get into a huddle while Rahul and Nissanka wait beyond the boundary to walk in any time now. Out come the umpires, Rohan Pandit and Nitin Menon, followed by the players to a bit of an applause. nav: "This team selection by DC makes no sense. It seems like they've preferred Vipraj over Kuldeep - which is a massive call. Nissanka over Miller is already a bad decision, and now Mukesh over Natarajan and Vipraj over Kuldeep are just making it worse." Kuldeep will probably come in as Impact Sub tonight. So Nigam has come in for a fast bowler 7.20pm Howdy people? No changes for KKR, who are on a winning streak and DC make a couple of tweaks and have been put in to bat. For this particular strip, this is the first evening game of this IPL. DC also have a poor home record in this edition. Let's see how things unfold today... Have you played our prediction game SIX SENSE yet? Try it. Who do you think will win? Who'll be the Player of the Match? Click the link and submit your predictions. Shrikant : "Why Sunil Narine is not opening these days?" Might be because Rahane has to open. Vishal's padded up to open here RaviP: "If Miller had taken that one single, he would have been playing every single game of DC so far." Given Axar said Natarajan's out, and they don't collapse, Kuldeep will be DC's impact player. Allen likely to come in for KKR DC impact options - Kuldeep Yadav, Karun Nair, Abhishek Porel, T Natarajan, David Miller DC 1 KL Rahul (wk), 2 Pathum Nissanka, 3 Sameer Rizvi, 4 Tristan Stubbs, 5 Nitish Rana, 6 Axar Patel (capt), 7 Ashutosh Sharma, 8 Lungi Ngidi, 9 Mitchell Starc, 10 Vipraj Nigam, 11 Mukesh Kumar KKR impact options - Finn Allen, Ramandeep Singh, Tejasvi Singh, Navdeep Saini, Tim Seifert KKR 1 Ajinkya Rahane (capt), 2 Angkrish Raghuvanshi (wk), 3 Cameron Green, 4 Rovman Powell, 5 Manish Pandey, 6 Rinku Singh, 7 Sunil Narine, 8 Anukul Roy, 9 Kartik Tyagi, 10 Vaibhav Arora, 11 Varun Chakravarthy Axar Patel, DC captain Makes no difference whether we bat or bowl. You've to be ready either way. Two changes - Mukesh in for Nattu, VIpraj in for Nair. From what I've played here, there's no spin but it's slow, ball holds in the pitch. Spinners get help, pacers go slower. So, we thought of using three spinners and pacers. Small boundary on one side makes no difference. Can't make too many technical changes. Bad balls will get hit no matter what. You've to focus on bowling good balls. Ajinkya Rahane, KKR captain Stats tell you to bowl first. Last three games have been different - 260s and 160s. Better to see the wicket. No changes. Difficult to read the wicket. Important to assess conditions early. Gaps between games worked out well. The mood was important, we got a win to start. Now it's about starting fresh. 7pm Rahane and Axar are out for the toss with Harsha Bhogle. Axar tosses the coin, heads is the call. It is heads. KKR bowl Ramandeep Singh: "I hope Shaw gets a game today, could spring in a big surprise" Pitch report This was the pitch where DC made 264 vs PBKS. Katey Martin says the pitch is hard to predict. It's pitch 6 and there was more grass in the PBKS game. It looks barren today, pitch looks glued on top but there are cracks in between and it's dry. It'll be slow, support spin bowlers and change ups. If no one knows what's happening, it's better to chase. 6:50pm KKR's trajectory is excellent. Narine and Chakravarthy's threat levels increasing has played no small part in that. Their bowlers have restricted oppositions to 165 or under in their last three games. If they do that tonight, it's half the battle won. If not, Rahane and Raghuvanshi might have to bat quicker while Allen will have to do well too. Virat: "KKR is the team to watch out rising from the bottom of the table to all the way to qualification.. All their players have shown good form over the last couple of matches, and they are set to go all the way!!" Smit: "DC is lacking captaincy here, they should drop axar and let rahul lead." Even if that is the case, think it's too late to change things up at this stage Mustafa Moudi : "Fun Fact for Sujeet: Since 2011, all KKR Captains are former DC Players, except Eoin Morgan - Gautam Gambhir, Dinesh Karthik, Shreyas Iyer and Ajinkya Rahane!!" 'It is frustrating' - Miller waits for his turn 6:40pm It certainly has been a challenging season for DC, both players and fans as the comment below shows. Their issues are like whack-a-mole, one's smashed and the other pops up. Still Nissanka making room for Miller does seem like a reasonable call given the middle order is what's underperforming more. Doesn't help that Axar has had near-zero impact with the bat. Kuldeep needs to find turn and hit his lengths consistently, that would make a big difference too. sujeet: "Delhi fan since 2010, this year is a wash. No strong identity, patchy wins, disgusting losses (265 defence fail, 75 all out from 8-6, Miller/Kuldeep v GT). Only hope comes from Starc and Kuldeep usually doing well against their former team" VS: "I really hope that Miller plays today. DC can sacrifice Nissanka for Porrel." MC: "I was mindlessly looking through all the games featured on the Cricinfo home screen and came across the China-Hong Kong women's game. Apparently it ended with a hat trick of run outs. Fascinating stuff" Preview by Vishal Dikshit Does DC's middle-order have an answer for KKR's spin twins? 6:30pm Home sweet home. Hasn't exactly been that for Delhi Capitals, it's what they'll need to change tonight to stay in reach of that 16-point mark. KKR will want to build on the hat-trick of wins, their middle order needs to get among the runs and the top order needs to pick up pace. Their spinners are on top of their game, so they could decide the game tonight.

Doubt it'll be one-sided cos a massive powerplay's needed Prawin: "Today is Lungi's day:)" Sunil Narine It comes with hard work and bowling in the nets. Strong bowling group with spinners containing in the middle. If you allow spinners to bowl to you, it's tough. We have to get a good start and use that momentum. When plans work in the middle, you get self-belief. We had a plan and respected the game to executed. You believe in a small total but you have to win the powerplay, rotate strike in the middle overs and chase it down at the death. Meanwhile in some rare good news for Indian football, the U-17 Indian women's team have become the first Indian side in history to qualify for the Women's Asian Cup quarterfinal with an excellent 4-0 win over Lebanon. Here's how they made history. 9:11pm There was mystery surrounding the pitch. Katey Martin said as much in the pitch report, so did the captains at the toss. Turns out it was okay for the batters at the start before it became a dream strip for slower bowlers and pacers who used variations. Nissanka gave DC a good start but lost partners in a cluster. Tyagi and Green did the early damage before the spinners barged in. DC were 85 for 3 in 10 but the wind was taken out by Narine and Anukul especially with Varun for company. Wickets were regular and DC didn't seem to want to use the sub on a batter. So an out-of-sorts Axar and Ashutosh started super slow. Ashutosh's late burst took DC past 140 but the batting issues remain. Shoutout to Tyagi who was excellent at the death.

commentPreTextItems.html: Only three KKR batters have scored a century so far

commentTextItems.html: Make it four, with a six! Allen pick-up pulls it off a back of length over midwicket. Hugs his partner, lid comes off. KL congratulates him

commentPostTextItems.html: It was a win delivered by the batting, designed by the bowling though. The second-half of the first innings was oldy-worldy. It's left DC all but out, KKR are on the rise. Great timing too for the east Indian franchise. Two west Indian franchises play each other tomorrow. Join us for that, thanks for coming in tonight. Bye. Finn Allen, POTM I've been working on having more strings in my bow. Had to be more responsible after a couple of early wickets. I tried to knuckle down early, was challenging early on, Axar bowled early. Strategy was to get in a good position and bat deep. That's my model, stay in when it's tough, give myself a chance. I've got a few starts, frustrating not to carry on, nice to have some personal success. When the situation comes, you forget about your batting and focus on the situation. I knew if I stayed out for a long time, 40 balls, doesn't happen too often [I'd score enough]. Sometimes, being left out changes your perspective. Allows time for mental refresh. I was putting on too much pressure on myself. Ajinkya Rahane, KKR captain Happy for Allen, he was struggling and worked hard. Want to praise our bowlers, they've done well so consistently, spinners and death bowlers. We've been working hard on the fielding, it's helping us. Credit to the fielding coach. Leaving Narine alone is the way to go, lucky to have him and Varun in the side. He's learning and sharing his experience all the time, he's always in the nets and is willing to bowl at any time. We've been playing well in the first five games, crucial moments are important. Credit to our bowling coaches, they've been worked hard with the bowlers. Happy with Anukul, who's had a fantastic domestic season and Tyagi who's confident. Varun's okay, he's happy as long as he's bowling. Cameron Green Was special, not often you get to stay at the non-strikers. All Finn said was 'see you next over', I played second fiddle. Did the math 29 runs off, knew I'd be the most hated player in Kolkata if I didn't help him get the ton. Winning has been satisfying, bowlers have been great, spin exceptional. Can't look far ahead, gotta win every game from here. DC are not mathematically out of the playoffs race although you wouldn't know it from Axar's post-match interview Axar Patel, DC captain We were short on runs. Spinners made a lot of mistakes, gave away too many step-hits. We lost five wickets in 2-3 overs with bat, lost momentum there. [Partnership with Ashutosh] We knew if we make a mistake, it'll be difficult for the incoming batters. We had to take one-two overs to consolidate after a cluster of wickets. [Moving forward] We'll go and figure out where we've made mistakes. There's next year too, we'll have to think of plans and preparation for next year, and accordingly, think of which players who are currently on the bench should be given chances. Elsewhere, the AIFF are up to their usual shenanigans in Indian football, with a chaotic ISL schedule leaving some coaches branding it a 'disaster' amidst allegations of unfairness. Just another day in the Indian Super League. Sudipta: "The table can be split into 4 parts now: PK, SRH: Toppers, RCB, RR, GT: Challengers, CSK, KKR: Dark Horses, DC, MI, LSG: Backbenchers" VS: "One sided match, but Allen's century made it worth watching." V. Kalyani : "KKR gave away only 2 extras....wait.....DC conceded none....Moral win?" 10:32pm That was easy, should have been anything but on that pitch. There was turn for the spinners. DC may have felt they had a chance to pull things back post-powerplay. But Green and Allen consolidated before Allen blew the roof out of the stadium. Not sure how conditions got conducive for six-hitting. Maybe they didn't, maybe it was just Allen having a day out. DC had a small target to work with. commentPreTextItems.html: 7:27pm The umpires make their way out. RR, in their changed pink outfits, are in a huddle near the edge of the rope. Lots of smiles. Jaiswal's first team talk in the huddle as skipper. Gill and Sudharsan to open. Archer to take the new ball. He has a handy record against the GT skipper. Sudharsan on strike for now, though. Slip in place - let's play! Pitch Report: Pitch no.6 is being used today, and it is the first time this strip is being used this season. Slightly skewed square boundaries - 63m to one side, 68m to the other. Simon Katich says he sees plenty of runs on this track. In night games, chasing has been the way to go, which explains Jaiswal's decision at the toss. There is a small bare patch at one end and that might make it two-paced, but the pitch, in general, is rock-hard. Dinesh: "Hope Washi gets to bowl for RR's lefty lineup." Akash jain: "RR last 05 games performance..LWLWL means today W" -- Ah. Only if cricket (or any sport for that matter) was that simple and formulaic. Yoshin: "Should RR consider giving Shanaka an over or two to try and get a wicket or two after the power play?" -- Shanaka's presence does provide them an extra option but it remains to be seen how much of his bowling RR use. Might be dependent on how well their opening bowlers fare. 7:10pm Right. A lot to dissect from the toss. First things first, RR have a new skipper, with Parag ruled out due to a hamstring injury. They have also shuffled their team balance, opting for the batting security Hetmyer provides over the new-ball threat Burger offers. GT, meanwhile, expect this pitch to be more conducive to pacers, and have subsequently included Prasidh, with Suthar missing out. Praveen: "If a starts with 4 foreign players in 11, why do they keep another one as impact sub ?" -- If they need a sub fielder, it has to come from the five named as substitutes, hence. Rohit: "Shashwat, it's funny how you say "how close the points table has been this season". Just a few week ago there was an article on "4 way dominance and a lopsided points table", goes onto show that it took just a week for the IPL to humble us all." RR bowling-first XI: Yashasvi Jaiswal (capt), 3 Dhruv Jurel (wk), Shimron Hetmyer, Donovan Ferreira, Ravindra Jadeja, Shubham Dubey, Dasun Shanaka, Jofra Archer, Brijesh Sharma, Tushar Deshpande, Yash Punja RR bench: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Adam Milne, Ravi Singh, Ravi Bishnoi, Sushant Mishra GT batting-first XI: Shubman Gill (capt), Sai Sudharsan, Jos Buttler (wk), Nishant Sindhu, Washington Sundar, Jason Holder, Rahul Tewatia, Rashid Khan, Arshad Khan, Kagiso Rabada, Mohammed Siraj GT bench: Prasidh Krishna, Glenn Phillips, Anuj Rawat, R Sai Kishore, Kumar Kushagra 7pm It is toss time in Jaipur, and the first big news of the evening is that Jaiswal is captaining the Royals. Gill standing alongside him. Gill calls tails, but heads it is. RR will field first. Jaiswal says the wicket is good and they want to chase. Parag has pulled his hamstring, he adds, and hopes that he is back soon. Hetmyer comes in, as does Punja. Really excited, he says, and adds that he is looking forward to a good game. Gill says he would have bowled first too. One change, says Gill, with Prasidh replacing Suthar. Mentions that it is important to look at your strengths as a bowling and batting group. Notes most of the games they have played have been close, and that it is about putting in that little bit extra. Says they will see how the first couple of overs go, and then try to figure out a par score and get 10-15 more. Have you played SIX SENSE, our prediction game, yet? Give it a go. Who do you think will win the match today? Who'll be the Player of the Match? Click the link and submit your predictions. Pradeep: "Does MI and LSG still have a chance?" -- Yes, they do have a chance, even if those hopes are, at this point, slim. No team has been mathematically eliminated yet, although if both of them lose tomorrow, that might be a real possibility. Adarsh: "GT, CSK and KKR have started gaining momentum recently. RR, RCB and PBKS need to be careful not to slip up." -- GT could go level on points with the table-toppers tonight if they win too, which shows how tight this points table is this season. VS: "Will RR drop Burger today? He's been poor recently. Who will replace him Maphaka, Milne, shanaka…..?" -- That is one of the selection headaches RR have. There are signs that Parag may not play tonight, which would be a big bit of news. 6:35pm Both teams have been on contrasting recent runs, but are still -deadlocked, with both having won six games apiece. What might be in store tonight then? Ashish Pant sets the scene in his match preview. 6:30pm The last time the Gujarat Titans and the Rajasthan Royals met, they produced a thriller. Tushar Deshpande held his nerve and the Titans were subjected to two defeats in their opening two games for the first time ever. A lot has happened since. And GT have begun doing GT things again. Their top order is standing up. Their middle order is doing just enough. Their pace battery has found its spark. And they are putting wins together to mount a playoff dash. The Royals, strangely enough, have also reverted to old and possibly unnerving habits. After blitzing their way to four successive wins at the start, they have stumbled. And while they have not quite gone off the rails, they may have spiralled enough to make their fans wonder if this is another one of those false dawns. But tonight, they will have a chance to tweak that narrative. To show that this season could be different and that it could indeed be a throwback to those winning times. Just as the Titans hope to prolong a theme that has now become very much their own. Hello and welcome to ESPNcricinfo's coverage. This is Match 52 - an opportunity for both the Royals and the Titans to secure a place (for the time being at least) alongside the table-topping Sunrisers Hyderabad, but also a contest that may make one of these teams' playoff run-in much more tedious than what would be deemed ideal. This should be fun, so hop on!

commentPostTextItems.html: 9:16pm A power-packed GT innings, spearheaded by their star openers. Sudharsan and Gill teed off in the powerplay, helping GT register their joint-highest powerplay score. Gill then continued and offset a slightly sluggish period post the powerplay. Sundar and Tewatia played their hands too, and GT have now gotten up to a score they will feel they can defend. RR, strangely, will be happy they are only chasing 230. Their bowling was all over the shop at the start, with only their spinners exerting any sort of control. Jadeja and Punja, unsurprisingly, were their best bowlers. RR will not baulk at this chase but if they do get there, it will be their highest-ever in the IPL. Join us in a bit for the second half. Sai Sudharsan: To start with, the wicket was really good, but once the ball got rough, it became a little slow and started to turn a bit. Always great challenge playing against Jofra, but we had it in our mind that if an over started well for us, we would go after it. If we use a lot of slower ones, cutters and try to spin the ball, it is not easy to hit (on this pitch). We were going after the bowlers and there was no hesitation. I lost my wicket at the right time for the RR team - we could have had a bigger partnership. (Gill's influence) We share a very good partnership and relationship. I look up to him for a lot of things.

commentPostTextItems.html: 11:32pm That will be all from us for tonight. We will be back tomorrow with a double-header and would love your company for those games too. Until then, from all of us here at ESPNcricinfo, it is goodbye! Rashid Khan, Player of the Match: Quite happy. It was something unusual for me (last two seasons). This season, more about enjoying myself and hitting the right areas consistently. Happy with that (so far). When I had that surgery, I took only two months to get back. That time, I made a huge mistake (of coming back soon). Last year, when IPL was over, I had 2-3 months off and tried to work on my fitness. The rhythm I bowl through the crease - it was something I was missing. Had a good Hundred competition and then kept on. The moment I bowled the first ball, I knew there was something for me. Pace was something I was trying to mix up. If I leave the stumps, it gets easy for the batters to take a single or hit a boundary. Wanted to hit a length but also the line. I made that move in my mind - that if I pitch it in the right area, there will be help. The moment it left my hand, I knew. (On working with the Indian spinners) It is so good. We have been together for a long time. Important to have those players around you. When I come here, I have those good conversations (on how to bowl at different venues in India), and I share my international experiences. Modern cricket demands more variations. Sai Kishore is working hard on his variations and working hard on a wrong'un - looking forward to seeing it (in matches). Shubman Gill, GT captain: Boys were having that conversation that we had not had the perfect game. We got 10-15 extra, it was not easy to hit sixes or boundaries (against the spinners). Always knew if we got a couple of wickets in the powerplay, we would have a good game. (On Siraj and Rabada bowling three each in the powerplay) We believe it is important to hold fort up front. If we take wickets, it gives the bowlers more chance to attack through the middle. You have to keep taking wickets - there is no other way. (On how he is feeling with his team's current form) Very happy. Next game is at home and hopefully we will have another good match. (On his injury) I twisted my ankle a bit but after half an hour, it settled down. Yashasvi Jaiswal, RR captain: We were just thinking to bowl good areas, they batted well. We were just thinking of how to cut down boundaries, so it was pretty good from them. (On Archer's performance tonight) It is cricket. There are some days when you cannot bowl how you want. He has been doing well for us, and I think he will be coming back strongly. We are going to look at what we can do better and learn from this game. Kagiso Rabada, Purple Cap holder: Everyone is just determined, I am determined myself. Everyone is just given a role - try to perform to the best of your ability. (Duel with Sooryavanshi and what is his plan) What has worked for 11 years will continue to work. About hedging your bets and hoping it works. Lot of hard work done behind the scenes. Lot of nuances but apart from that, it is same-old, same-old. Body feels good. This is where the fatigue starts to set in, so just trying to stay on top of it and be as fresh as possible. Hopefully I can just continue what I have been doing. (On his slower balls and if he is putting in some extra work) Not really. I have not bowled too many this season, but when they are needed, I will bowl them. 11:05pm Another commanding win for GT, and they now look like a team in perfect sync. Their batters srt up this game and their pacers, after the onslaught by Sooryavanshi, recovered to dent the Royals. There were a couple of cameos from the home side but nothing lasted long enough to really threaten the Titans or the mountain of runs they put up. Lots to ponder for RR. Their early season success now seems a distant memory and with their next game not until May 17, they might find themselves well out of the top four by the next time they play, and with serious must-win complications.

title: Starc to Arya, SIX

commentPreTextItems.html: 7:28pm The players make their way out. Arya and Prabhsimran to open the batting. DC emerge from their huddle and they will be aware of the mayhem this pair can cause. Starc to take the new ball. This could be a cracking opening passage of play. Slip in place for Arya, let's play! Adarsh: "If there was a time to remove Nissanka, it was earlier in the season. Not after he scored a 50 which was the only fluent innings in a low-scoring innings. " -- That perhaps sums up how their season has gone. Kirat: "Playing against a side who have accepted elimination is more dangerous than playing against a team who's eyeing playoffs. So many new faces in DC tonight, could be a big surprise waiting tonight. May be a youngster having a dream match today " Sumodh : "The HPCA Stadium is one of the few venues where the ball actually swings. The "Baramulla Express" is coming off a legendary Ranji season (60 wickets) and is known for swinging it both ways." Pitch Report: Dimensions first. There is a slight bias - 63m to 65m, in terms of the square boundaries. 72m hit straight down the ground. Nick Knight says he wants to put his pads on, looking at the pitch. Nice, even covering of grass and there could be a little bit in it for the new-ball bowlers, but apart from that, he expects a good batting track. 209 is the average score in the last five games, and Danny Morrison concludes, saying he cannot wait for this to get underway. Ravi: "Kings need to get back to doing what they were doing best earlier in the season batting first, bat with freedom and really pile the runs on in the powerplay " -- Well, for most of their unbeaten run, they only chased... Ryan: "Dwarshuis is the kind of player that can get 3/25 or 0/56...PBKS will be hoping for the former, but Lockie Ferguson is a gun and will be waiting in the wings..." -- Based on what Shreyas said, it seems a forced change. He mentioned at the toss that Lockie had a 'niggle'. 7:10pm Well, plenty to unpack from the toss, mostly because of the truckload of changes DC have made. Porel might open, but they have another left-handed option in Parakh. Might have to wait and see if Rahul is shunted down the order to accommodate the two youngsters. Miller adds muscle to the middle order and there is another gig for Nabi, who had a stellar red-ball domestic season but is yet to set the IPL stage alight. Interesting change from PBKS too. As things stand, their starting eleven only has left-arm frontline pacers. Thakur, who plays for Vidarbha in domestic cricket, could change that but if they opt for a spinner, it is likely to be Brar, who is also left-handed. Punjab Kings batting-first XI: Priyansh Arya, Prabhsimran Singh (wk), Cooper Connolly, Shreyas Iyer (capt), Marcus Stoinis, Suryans Shedge, Shashank Singh, Marco Jansen, Ben Dwarshuis, Arshdeep Singh, Yuzvendra Chahal PBKS bench: Harpreet Brar, Yash Thakur, Xavier Bartlett, Vishnu Vinod, Pravin Dubey Delhi Capitals bowling-first XI: Abishek Porel, KL Rahul (wk), Sahil Parakh, Tristan Stubbs, David Miller, Axar Patel (capt), Madhav Tiwari, Mukesh Kumar, Auqib Nabi, Lungi Ngidi, Mitchell Starc DC bench: Ashutosh Sharma, Sameer Rizvi, Tripurana Vijay, Pathum Nissanka, Vipraj Nigam 7pm It is time for the toss. Axar and Shreyas out in the middle. Shreyas will give the coin a twirl. Axar calls tails, and tails it is. DC will bowl first. Axar says him winning the toss is something that is going right for them, and he says it with a smile. Mentions they have been losing crucial moments and have not been playing bad cricket per se. Says the thinking has been to play their own brand of cricket and take the result as it comes. Notes that you should enjoy the tough times, just as you enjoy the good times. Adds that it is a fresh wicket and that they are a little unsure of how it will play. Five changes, says Axar - Porel and Parakh are playing, as are Miller, Nabi and Madhav Tiwari. Shreyas says he has no idea about how the pitches are playing until you play on them. He says you do not have to think much about the points table and focus instead on the small details, and backing your instincts. He says that (backing your instincts) is what they are falling short of in the previous few matches. In the IPL, there will be ups and downs, and it is all about getting the best performance. Dwarshuis comes in for Lockie, who has a slight niggle, and that is the only change, says Shreyas. JUST IN! Ben Dwarshuis has been handed his PBKS cap, which means he is likely to debut tonight. Will be interesting to see who misses out, though. Have you played our prediction game SIX SENSE yet? Give it a go. Click the link and submit your predictions. VS: "As CSK fan I'll be rooting for DC today. Hope Miller finds a place in the DC line up." -- Finding a spot for Miller will mean either one of Nissanka or the overseas pacers getting dropped. Might be unlikely. 6:47pm Suryansh Shedge has had to bide his time, but help from Ricky Ponting, Shreyas Iyer and Jatin Paranjape has helped him "stay in the present" and be ready for all situations. Read all about it in this piece by Himanshu Agrawal. Ravi: "One of the problems of PBKS this year has been Jansen's form. He had a dream season last time. With Dharamsala pitch set to assist the bounce and pace, hope he finds his rhythm" -- Arshdeep not finding his range consistently has only magnified that, given how important both have been to PBKS' fortunes previously. Varun: "From bossing the league in the first half, PBKS are now into the must-win territory." -- Not must-win territory yet. If they win all their remaining games, they go up to 21, which will all but confirm a top-two spot. But they will like a win after three successive losses. Sunil Kumar: "I would suggest, Delhi play Prithvi Shaw today as opener along with Pathum Nissanka, KL can come one down and drop Nitish Rana. I believe Prithvi will be eager to prove his point with a flourish." -- With DC somehow still alive in the comp, there is a chance they stick to an opening combination that has largely worked well for them. Vivek: "With Qualifier-1 set to be played in Dharamsala, PBKS must secure the top-2 spot to have an advantage to go straight to the finals." -- Well, the Eliminator is in New Chandigarh, which will have been their home ground for longer this season... 6:35pm DC have won just one of their last five games, with PBKS also losing each of their previous three fixtures. All that and much more in Hemant Brar's preview. 6:30pm Let's do this again then, shall we? The last time the Delhi Capitals met the Punjab Kings, carnage ensued. 529 runs were scored. DC made 264 of those. But PBKS, to the disbelief of the home crowd and those watching, scored 265. And did so with room to spare. DC, it could be argued, have not recovered since. They have won only one game and their campaign has fizzled out. Funnily though, PBKS have also found it tough. The air of invincibility has evaporated and while it may not be panic stations yet, one more defeat and they might start to wonder if this is another one of those what-if seasons. And so, from that record-breaking afternoon in the capital, to the foothills of the Himalayas we go. Into the serene and colder confines of Dharamsala, where the Delhi Capitals now cling on by the barest of qualification threads, and where the Punjab Kings hope for the swashbuckling trajectory that defined most of their early-season fortunes. A PBKS win will catapult them to the top, with qualification within grasp, and with DC most certainly consigned to elimination. But a DC win, and the Capitals will remain afloat (for now), even though it may lead to some introspection on the other side - over how a campaign that began in such spotless fashion has gone pear-shaped so quickly. Lots to look forward to, so hop on to ESPNcricinfo's live coverage!

commentPostTextItems.html: 9:25pm A strange innings, set up by Arya, who teed off in the powerplay yet again and put Starc and Ngidi, in particular, to the sword. Nabi, though, was brilliant and he made use of the help on offer, and that spell helped DC pull things back, with PBKS huffing and puffing through the middle. Shreyas had to bat through, and with Connolly along for company (with Shedge producing a cameo at the end), PBKS have gotten to a score they will be confident of defending. DC will be happy with how they fought back, having conceded more than 50 in three overs. Their death-bowling display was not shabby either. And they will largely be happy with how their Indian pacers fared. The overseas quicks travelled, though, and that means DC now have to do what no team has ever done in the IPL at this venue - chase more than 200. Can they do it and stay alive? Join us in a bit for the second half. Madhav Tiwari: I am really glad about the opportunity. Was just looking to make use of the conditions. There is a bit of help for the fast bowlers - was trying to hit the right areas. (When he knew he would play and bowl four overs) There was a bit of chat between me and Axar bhai. For now, he told me that I would bowl four overs. (What the right areas were) There was a bit of help, so I was going for length balls. Not easy for batters to hit off a length. (What Axar said after the powerplay) He was pretty chill and asked me the fielding I wanted. We were not looking at the scoreboard, just wanted to execute. (On if there is dew) It is quite wet and the ball is skidding through.

title: Yash Thakur to Auqib Nabi, SIX

commentPreTextItems.html: Free hit to tuck into for Nabi, with just one more needed

commentTextItems.html: a stirring blow over the bowler's head, and the Capitals are alive! Eight teams remain in contention for four spots, with the Punjab Kings, once table-toppers, now consigned to their fourth successive defeat! Full toss outside off and Nabi cannot believe his luck. He sits deep in his crease and smokes it over long off. Excellent, excellent cameo by Nabi, and a brilliant run-chase overall by the Capitals, and while their road to the playoffs is still tough, they remain afloat, and still in with something resembling a shout!

commentPostTextItems.html: 11:55pm That will be all from us. We hope you enjoyed our coverage and we will be back with more tomorrow. Until then, from all of us here at ESPNcricinfo, it is goodbye! El Fuego: "When do we enter the permutations and combinations territory?. Almost time, isn't it?. " -- Right about now! Madhav Tiwari, Player of the Match: I would like to thank the management for giving this opportunity. Lucky enough to be on the winning side. (On how hard it was when he was not playing) The mindset is that if the things are not in your hands, you try to be better in each practice session. I worked on my bowling a lot and my range hitting with my batting coach. It was fun and happy I was able to contribute for the team. (On if he is a batting or bowling all-rounder) I would like to say I am a 100 percent bowler and a 100 percent batter. The wicket was helping the length balls, and was sticking to that, mixing it with wide balls and short balls in between. I was prepared (to bowl four overs). Conditions were supporting fast bowlers. As Axar said, he would have probably bowled if I conceded runs in my first over (smiles). Lucky to get to bowl four overs for the team. Our batting coach told me that I have the power, and asked me to not do anything fancy - to just hold my shape. Axar Patel, DC captain: The pressure moments, we have been losing. Have been saying our team is good and that we have been playing good cricket too, but we are here (because of losing those crucial moments). Very happy with how the team played, and hopefully we can do the same in the next two games. In the bowling, first 3-4 overs, they had 60 runs but to finish with only 72 in the powerplay, that was a winning moment. Then, Mukesh and Madhav bowling in the middle, and after that, my partnership with Miller, with the youngsters then finishing off the game. (On not bowling) The way the wicket was, when Nabi was bowling in the fourth over, it was swinging and seaming. In the first few overs, we did not bowl in the right areas. After the powerplay as well, it was moving around, so I thought there was no need to bowl spin since I had five pacers. (On his batting) Today, it clicked. Earlier as well, I used to come out with same intent. I got a chance today. Luck changed a little, and I was trusting my process, and the runs came. The cricket we are playing and the players we have, the future is strong. The runs Sahil also made, I had said before as well, he could be a good player in the future. A captain is very happy when he has youngsters like this, and as you said, the Delhi Capitals can do anything. Shreyas Iyer, PBKS captain: (Where it went wrong) Don't have to beat around the bush, but fielding and bowling again. (On if the score was enough) Absolutely. Feel it was 30 runs more on this wicket, given how the ball was seaming and the variable bounce. (On not bowling Chahal) It was a thought but the way it was seaming, if we had executed our lines and lengths, we may have gotten wickets. But we did not. I always say that hard length or short of hard length is the best ball. Not easy to hit (for someone coming in). We fell short of planning. David Miller: (Partnership with Axar) We were (behind). Axar has been working very hard. Tonight, it came off. That is why he has been playing for so long - dug in deep and came out with good energy. We complement each other well, so it is good. (On the finisher's role) It is a difficult thing, but just trying to stay calm. Always a long journey to get to the end, so about staying in the present. Can only control the next ball, so keep reminding myself. Just trying to clear the mind and think clearly. (On if there was extra incentive playing against Punjab) There is always incentive. It is the nature of league cricket - you go from one team to another. Nice to get the job done and the boys did really well at the back end. There was something in the wicket - every now and then, stayed a bit low. About playing good cricket shots, get into good positions. The lengths we bowled, we stuck it out really well, knowing that is a tactic they would bowl. 11:27pm Phew. What a game. And what a run-chase. DC had everything going against them. No team had ever chased these many to win a game here. DC then lost their leading run-scorer of the season (Rahul) early. But somehow, they found a way. Axar led the resistance with his first fifty of the season. Miller joined in on the fun soon, with Ashutosh, Tiwari and Nabi all playing pivotal cameos towards the end. PBKS will be disappointed with how their defence panned out. They dropped two catches, indulged in several misfields and erred with their lines and lengths too often. And they were made to pay by the Capitals, who have now consigned the Kings to four successive defeats, and have introduced even more jeopardy for the team that was being looked at as pace-setters earlier in the campaign.

title: Cummins to Sai Sudharsan, no run

commentPreTextItems.html: 7:27pm The umpires make their way out, followed soon by the players. Gill and Sudharsan to open. Looks like the SRH skipper is taking the new-ball responsibility upon himself. GT got off to flier against RR. Can they replicate it tonight? Sudharsan on strike, slip in place, let's find out! Akhil: "Hinge has bowled really good overs after his first overs. Though the numbers suggest otherwise. " -- His figures, in isolation, may not have been great against CSK but in that game, he did hold his own at the death. Sumodh: "SRH is rewarding the hot hand. Hinge's ability to dismantle top orders in the first few overs has earned him the spot over Harshal's veteran experience. What if it backfires and Hinge is taken to the cleaners?" -- Only one way to find out... Pitch Report: The square boundaries are skewed - 70m to one side, 64m to the other. 74m hit straight down the ground. We are on pitch number five, which is the surface on which MI trounced GT earlier in the season. There is a nice covering of grass, which could bring the pacers into play, reckons Sunil Gavaskar. There could be some help with the new ball, but it might also help the batters, with the ball coming on. Gavaskar expects plenty of runs, and he thinks finger-spinners might struggle here. This is a pitch good enough to have a 190-plus score, Gavaskar concludes. 7:10pm Both teams largely unchanged, which is along expected lines. SRH have brought in the extra pacer, though, with Hinge in place of Dubey. One Vidarbha player out, another in. GT have kept their options open. Based on the conditions, one of Sai Kishore or Prasidh could come in. As for SRH, Head will likely be their Impact Player. Gujarat Titans batting-first XI: Shubman Gill (capt), B Sai Sudharsan, Jos Buttler (wk), Washington Sundar, Jason Holder, Nishant Sindhu, Rahul Tewatia, Rashid Khan, Arshad Khan, Kagiso Rabada, Mohammed Siraj GT bench: Prasidh Krishna, Sai Kishore, Anuj Rawat, Kumar Kushagra, Glenn Phillips Sunrisers Hyderabad bowling-first XI: Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan (wk), Heinrich Klaasen, Nitish Kumar Reddy, R Smaran, Salil Arora, Pat Cummins (capt), Shivang Kumar, Praful Hinge, Eshan Malinga, Sakib Hussain SRH bench: Travis Head, Liam Livingstone, Aniket Verma, Harshal Patel, Harsh Dubey 7pm It is time for the toss. Gill and Cummins out in the middle. Cummins calls heads, and heads it is. SRH will field first. Cummins says they have not played here before this season and that is why they want to see what the conditions are like. Says they have earned the right to give themselves a few chances to get to the playoffs. No changes, says Cummins. Gill says he is not looking at the stats much, when asked about batting first. All about being consistent with your thought process, adds Gill, and that it is important to bring your A-Game to the table. Same teams, says Gill as well. Have you played SIX SENSE yet? Let's see how good your prediction-making skills are. Click the link and submit your answers. 6:53pm It is that time of the year again, folks, when calculators are brought out and permutations and combinations for qualification are worked out. S Rajesh has crunched the numbers, and here are all the potential scenarios. Riyaz: "@Shashwat - is it win toss bat first put runs on board and chase successfully match or the other way round?" -- On this particular strip, the team batting first has enjoyed better fortunes lately. MC: "Today is the anniversary of perhaps the most entertaining IPL final of all time. Here's hoping we can see another thriller tonight from these two teams!" 6:45pm SRH, like GT, arrive in a rich vein of form. But they have failed to get past the Titans at this venue since the beginning of the 2023 IPL season. Can they turn that record around tonight? All that and much more in Deivarayan Muthu's match preview. Suren: "Burning the midnight oil in Australia for my team in Orange, hope SRH continue their dominant run. " -- Might not be easy against a GT side that is firing on all cylinders too. Sai Krishna: "SRH will break its Ahmedabad curse tonight. Go SRH!" Mannat: "As a CSK supporter, very difficult to figure out whom to root for today...maybe rain? But then again I want to watch good cricket too. Is there a way for both teams to lose the game :p" 6:30pm The landscape in the IPL keeps changing. Every second. Every minute. Every day. And every game. Someone seems to always have a chance to go top. Or get into the top four. Or cling on to survival for a few more moments, like the Delhi Capitals did yesterday. And right in the thick of this merry-go-round are the Gujarat Titans and the Sunrisers Hyderabad. Perhaps written off at the start of the season - either for being too old-school or for being too gung-ho - but now within touching distance of a spot in the playoffs, and within touching distance of where they will feel they should always be. A win tonight will take either of these teams top and while a loss will not derail their playoff charge completely, it might just throw a little spoke in their wheel. That too at a time when every single encounter feels consequential. Hello and welcome everyone to ESPNcricinfo's live coverage. This is Match 56, and we are back in Ahmedabad. The Gujarat Titans, arguably the most in-form team in the competition and with aspirations of contesting the game that matters at this very venue in three weeks' time; the Sunrisers Hyderabad, victorious in six of their previous seven games themselves, and with a batting engine that is now purring and threatening to rattle past the rest of the pack. Plenty to tuck into, so tag along!

commentPostTextItems.html: 9:20pm A scratchy team innings, but that was down to the slightly sluggish conditions too. Buttler and Gill departed in the powerplay, with Hinge accounting for both of them. Sudharsan held things together - first in the company of Sindhu, and then alongside his state teammate Sundar. Sundar almost batted through and his fifty has ensured GT have something to play with, and perhaps a score they might even be confident of defending. SRH may have wanted to keep GT down to under 160, but might not mind 168 as such. Hinge was brilliant throughout phases, as was Cummins. It was, thus, a little puzzling that Hinge did not bowl out. SRH have the firepower to get these runs, but they will be aware of the conditions and the incision GT's bowlers have. Join us in a bit for the chase. Sai Sudharsan, Orange Cap holder: At the start, surface was a bit soft, there was moisture and it was seaming around, so it was my turn to take it deep (and get a decent total on the board). Probably 10 (more) runs would have been a cushion, but our bowlers will hopefully do the job. 175-180 would be a great score, but this is also a very good score. (On if this total is par) Yes, it is par (smiles). Hitting good lengths and trying to swing and seam the ball will give us the best opportunity. Wicket is still a little soft and it suits our bowlers' abilities.

commentTextItems.html: stumped by an absolute mile, and GT have won by an absolute landslide too! commentPostTextItems.html: 11:18pm And that is a wrap for tonight. We hope you enjoyed our coverage and we will be back with more IPL action tomorrow. Until then, from Harshith, Thilak and myself (Shashwat), it is goodbye. Take care, folks! Kagiso Rabada, Player of the Match: (On the dropped catch of Kishan) Did not react fast enough and did not judge (the pace of the ball). Luckily, we got the wicket (off the next over). Season in, season out, all you try to do is do the best you can. I have been backed and it has been clear what my role has been: leave everything out for the team. Rhythm is everything. About bowling as much as I can but also preserving myself to be match ready. Need to find a way to somehow click. (Chat in the bowling group before an innings) Just about finding out the kind of pitch we are playing on and bowling accordingly. We each have our own natural attributes, and it is about seeing how much you can extract, without looking too far ahead. If your strength is not working out, then you can look at something else. (On the pitch and if bowling a Test match length was the way to go) 100 percent. They showed how to bowl on it and we tried to follow suit. Wicket got a little more sticky and patience and simplicity worked. Shubman Gill, GT captain: Teams batting first…worked out for us nicely. We bowled very well. We knew if we bowled well, we would always be in the game. We spoke about if we get anywhere near 160-170, it will not be easy for them with our bowling attack. The way Sai and Washy batted, getting us close to 170, and then the way we bowled in the powerplay, kudos to both of our bowlers. It is all about being consistent and being ruthless. We are not a team who play a particular style and brand, and assess the conditions (and play according to it). (On Holder adding balance) he is such an experienced campaigner. He has been relentless for us, bowling four on the trot and he is doing a terrific job for us. Pat Cummins, SRH captain: (What they could have done differently) Thought they (GT pacers) bowled really well. Pretty happy when we walked off. Tricky wicket, they bowled well. Try to look for ways to get through that spell maybe. Looked like a tough wicket when you hit that back of a length. Maybe we could have held our lengths a little longer. But that is as good a T20 bowling (performance) as you can see from them. Our batting has been fantastic, so not reading too much into that. Guys have gone really well. This happens in T20 cricket. We (now) go to venues we know well, so we take confidence from that. We won five or six (out of our last 7-8) and that gives a bit of breathing room (in the playoff race), so going back to what got us those wins and putting this behind quickly. Washington Sundar: (On his innings) Definitely happy. Just focussing on reading the situation. Wicket was different from previous games - wanted to understand what shots to play, and having a set batter (at the end) helps. (On the six off Malinga in the 19th) I was trying to get that shot right, they were nailing the yorkers, happy to get it (well). The plan was to not think much. Thoughts do come in now and then. I was more focused on understanding the wicket and the situation - it demanded one of us to play till the end, and happy with the way I finished. Until the 17-18th over, did not want to go all-out, but in the last couple of overs, tried to get as many boundaries as I could. (On facing Siraj and Rabada in the nets) I don't think I should give away too much (laughs). Have to be disciplined and watch the ball very closely (and hope that they make an error). (On defending this score) Speaks a lot about our team setup - the kind of people who are part of it, they give a lot of importance to playing good cricket. Playing according to the conditions is important, even in this format. 10:55pm A proper thrashing. No two ways about it. At the half-way stage, the jury was out on whether GT had a par total on the board. As it turned out, they had far too many for SRH. Siraj and Rabada were irresistible in the powerplay, and blew the top order away. Klaasen threatened a resistance but once Holder sent him packing, it was a long, long road back for the visitors. Rabada and Holder finished with three apiece, with Siraj also getting himself on the board. Prasidh, on his return to the side, bagged two with Rashid landing the final knockout blow. GT have boosed their NRR too and in the process, they have also severely dented SRH's to make this crazy season even more interesting.

Shreyash: "Which bowling side is gonna benefit more from the rain-kissed pitch?" -- Bhuvneshwar and Hazlewood might not mind these conditions... Sudipta: "The rain has come to collect its due. It gifted KKR a point when they were losing everything. Now it has come to take it back when they are winning everything" -- Ha! For what it is worth, though, think we will get some kind of game today. The rain has stopped, and it seems like there isn't any more coming our way. 6:58pm Looks like the rain has stopped. On-field umpires Nitin Menon and Rohan Pandit have made their way out and are engaged in conversation with the fourth umpire Kaushik Gandhi. Umbrellas not a part of that conversation. But there is water on the covers, and that might need some mopping up. One of the covers, which was occupying the square, is also being peeled off. And we have an inspection time too. Shashank says an inspection is scheduled for 8:15pm local time. VS: "When the whole ground is covered why do you need more than an hour for inspection?" -- A lot of water has gotten accumulated on the covers and that needs to be scraped off before the covers are fully removed to disallow water from seeping into the ground. msa: "we might be having a delayed start but surely a full 20 over game is very much on the cards" -- We usually have an hour and a bit of buffer time, so there is still a chance we might get a full 40-over game. Kaleem: "How good is the drainage system at the Raipur stadium for play to begin after rain stops" -- Well, we are about to find out. On a serious note, having the whole ground covered should also help. Siddharth: "@Shashwat - I sure hope that this will not be a damp squib. But moving on to the tactics, winning the toss and bowling first would now be the obvious choice, no? And do you think these weather conditions would have caused the teams to alter their team XII?" -- Yes and yes. If this game is a very shortened game, like a 6-7 over game, teams might not want more than five bowling options. Or, conversely, they might want to have more specialist bowlers because the batting unit, in such a short duration game, might not be as stretched as usual. Srividya : "If at all game on tonight, toss will surely decide the result! Not discrete mathematics!" -- The toss, in such situations, does favour the team bowling first but in another similarly curtailed game (RR-MI), RR actually lost the toss, batted first and still won comfortably. Shahed: "@Shashwat - while losing one point will be a disadvantage to both teams, the loss of that one point for KKR will be severely denting their playoff hopes if not ambushing them - right?" -- Let's put it this way - a point will be much more helpful to RCB than it will be to KKR. The maximum KKR will then be able to get to is 16, and a few other teams can get there, which will then make them more dependent on other results. 6:50pm Just ten minutes to go for the scheduled toss time. Covers still firmly in place, and streaks of lightning are visible on a rather frequent basis too. And it is no surprise that the toss has been officially delayed. 6:40pm The entire ground has been covered, for what it is worth, but it is still raining quite heavily at the venue at the moment. 6:32pm Before getting into the excitement of the game, though, we have some damp news. It is not raining currently but a thunderstorm earlier has meant that some water has accumulated on the covers. Shashank Kishore, who is at the venue, also tells me there is lightning and thunder around, which might make the prospect of an on-time toss tough. We sill await official confirmation, though. The entire square has been covered, despite there being no rain currently, and that seems like a pre-emptive measure. Scratch that, because Shashank chimes in, saying it has begun to rain heavily now. 6:30pm A team with a winning streak, including big victories in their two most recent games. A side stuttering and stumbling, and barely breaking their winless run over the weekend. A month ago, had someone said this would be the backdrop to this fixture, chances for disagreement would have been sparse. The Kolkata Knight Riders seemed in freefall; the Royal Challengers Bengaluru seemed to be going from strength to strength. But the topsy-turvy nature of the IPL means that those roles have now been reversed. And it is KKR who arrive with a four-game winning streak intact, with the defending champions huffing and puffing to get back among the points on Sunday. That, of course, has not completely changed the complexion of the table. But it has added another layer of intrigue to this contest. And for KKR, perhaps given them hope that a playoff spot could actually come to fruition, and that their impressive recent run could, in fact, achieve all-timer status in days to come. Hello and welcome everyone to ESPNcricinfo's live coverage. This is Match 57 and we are back in Raipur - raucous on Sunday, and expected to be just as rousing tonight. RCB, with a place at the top of the table in their sights, looking to hit their earlier stride; KKR itching to stretch out their legs (and campaign) further, and sprint before the playoff bus passes them by. Plenty to look forward to, so sit back, relax and enjoy!

commentPostTextItems.html: 10:22pm A coherent batting effort, with almost all of the batters playing a part. Allen teed off early, even if he could not prolong it for a chunk of the powerplay. Rahane also got a few away at the top but it was not until Green and Raghuvanshi got together that KKR mustered sustained momentum. Raghuvanshi held things together at one end, while also ticking along at a healthy rate. Green partnered him initially, with Rinku helping in applying the finishing touches. If this will be enough is another matter, especially with this looking like a better strip than Sunday. RCB did not have a standout bowler but none of them went off the rails dramatically, meaning they are now confronted with a score they will be confident of chasing down. Join us in a bit for the second half.

commentPostTextItems.html: 12:53am And that will be all from us. Hope you enjoyed our coverage as much as we loved bringing it to you, and we hope to have your company tomorrow too. Until then, from all of us here at ESPNcricinfo, it is goodbye! Virat Kohli, Player of the Match: The celebration was not a big one because we know the importance of the points. It is a conscious effort to contribute more to the team. The fact I did not score runs, it eats me up because I have been playing well. It bothers you because that has been the goal - to be the best version. Century or no century, the more important thing is to finish the game. (On if he was feeling pressure) There is a reason people say pressure is a privilege - it keeps you humble. Good pressure always helps you improve your game. A couple of games that do not go your way, you feel a bit of nervousness and that helps you. It takes a lot of effort, but it helps your game go up. Those failures are so important because that puts you in a place to get back (to where you have been and do what has gotten you there). (What pleased him most) Just my positions at the crease, not doing anything extravagant and backing my game. Picking length, hitting the gaps I can hit. Happy I was able to back my game. (On breaking so many records) I just love batting, even after all this. That is my core feeling. What an honour to be competing at this level and against the very best still. Just give my heart and soul out there because it is going to finish one day. Want to make the most of it, and look forward to pressure situations, where I am feeling a bit of heat and then I challenge myself to just go for it. Sport teaches you a lot as a person. You build your character (when you perform under pressure). Even after all these years, it is the love for the game. I just love hitting the ball in the middle of the bat. That joy is still there and it is all God's grace, and I am thankful and grateful. Rajat Patidar, RCB captain: (On his injury) I am okay, it was a proper headshot (laughs). (On topping the table) It feels great. You play well in the tournament and everyone came in the different stage and doing their job for the team. We are taking it one game and one step at a time. (On how he felt after the first innings) Very satisfied. After ten overs, the way we controlled their innings….to restrict them (for 192 after their start) is a good sign for us. Last game, we played on the same track and there was variable bounce, and so we played four seamers. (On Kohli) I don't have words, but he is used to doing great things. We have played good cricket. Two more league games, one game at a time. We are traveling to Dharamsala - good track to bat, and we will try to win. (On Salt's possible return) I don't know but he will come soon. Ajinkya Rahane, KKR captain: We thought 190 was a competitive total. The batters who batted thought it was a competitive total. Good effort by the batters. Our fielding was really good (in last few games). Defending a total, that catch of Kohli, you want to hang on - that I felt was the difference. First six overs, we knew it was going to be easy (to bat on). Last five games, in the middle overs, we took wickets. But credit goes to Kohli, and that partnership between him and Padikkal was the game. While chasing a total, Virat is a dangerous player. He is a dangerous player anyway. Padikkal has also been batting well. Guys are working hard but you can drop catches - that is okay. (On Tyagi) He has been really good for us, working really hard. What I like about him is his clear mindset. Padikkal: It was an important game for us, want to make sure we keep pressure on the other sides. It has been going good. Important that I keep this momentum going. As long as I am doing that, I am happy. (On Kohli's knock) It is incredible to bat alongside him. He does this so often. If you wake him up at any time of the day, he is going to come in and do this. Just watching and learning. (On if Kohli was nervous after two ducks) I don't think so (smiles). Don't think he needs to get nervous. He got his 14000th run today, so that does not require any nervousness. You want to finish in the top two spots and hopefully that momentum will carry us into the playoffs. 12:21am A brilliant run-chase, spearheaded, unsurprisingly, by Kohli. He set the tempo early and ensured it never dropped. He attacked pace, he took down spin whenever he got the chance and he batted through, ensuring there would be no hiccups. Padikkal supported him throughout and that partnership knocked the stuffing out of KKR. KKR did get a few wickets towards the end but by then, RCB had effectively killed off the run-chase. This result means RCB are now nicely-placed at the top and even eyeing a top two finish. KKR's hopes are hanging by a thread, meanwhile, and they will now need to win all their remaining games, while also hoping for several other results going their way.

commentPreTextItems.html: 7:28pm The umpires make their way out, followed soon by the players. Arya and Prabhsimran to open, and PBKS will hope for their uncapped opening pair to tee off up front. Looks like Chahar will be taking the new ball. Arya on strike, around the wicket, slip in place, let's play! Have you played SIX SENSE yet? Simple questions. You need to guess them right. Click the link and submit your predictions. Amit: "Why MI dropped Ghazanfar today ? Is he not fit ? He was only bright spot in MI bowling unit this season." -- The answer is two-fold. With SKY absent, they felt the need for an overseas batter in Rutherford. That meant they could not play Ghazanfar. They may also be unsure of how much of a role spin will play today, and hence did not want to use an overseas spot on a spinner. Hari Krishna: "Hi @Shashwat is it the first time bumrah is captaining the IPL side??" -- Yes, it is. He joked at the toss too, saying he never expected to be a Test captain before an IPL captain. V. Kalyani : "CSK fans are rooting for an MI win today. Strange no?" -- Well, you had Spurs fans possibly rooting for an Arsenal win last Sunday, so... Madhav: "It rained a lot in Dharamshala yesterday. And there is a decent breeze too today. The dew shouldn't be as heavy as the other day tonight. Shouldn't be." -- Let's find out soon. Saket: "so last game they didn't bowl a single over of Chahal and now they bring Brar in?" -- Well, he is not technically in yet. But Shreyas and the pitch report does suggest this pitch could be a little drier than the other evening, which might bring spinners into play. Ram: "Wait what wrong did Stoinis do? He has atleast been way better than Jansen, very harsh to drop Stoinis here." -- It does seem a little harsh but for this game, PBKS are maybe valuing Jansen's bowling over Stoinis' batting. Time for the South African to repay that faith. 7:08pm Right. A fair few changes then. MI have brought in Rutherford and Shardul for now, with Rohit likely to be their Impact Player later in the game. Raghu gets another game and will be their primary spinner, although it remains to be seen how much of a role spin plays. PBKS, on the other hand, have included Omarzai and Bartlett, with Stoinis and Dwarshuis missing out. Brar has been listed on the bench, and though Shreyas said he was playing tonight, that could still change if conditions are more suited to fast bowling. In that case, Vyshak could be a possible Impact Player. Mumbai Indians bowling-first XI: Ryan Rickelton (wk), Naman Dhir, Sherfane Rutherford, Tilak Varma, Will Jacks, Raj Bawa, Corbin Bosch, Deepak Chahar, Shardul Thakur, Jasprit Bumrah, Raghu Sharma MI bench: Rohit Sharma, Mayank Rawat, Robin Minz, Krish Bhagat, Trent Boult Punjab Kings batting-first XI: Prabhsimran Singh (wk), Priyansh Arya, Shreyas Iyer (capt), Cooper Connolly, Shashank Singh, Suryansh Shedge, Azmatullah Omarzai, Marco Jansen, Xavier Bartlett, Arshdeep Singh, Yuzvendra Chahal PBKS bench: Vijaykumar Vyshak, Harpreet Brar, Mitchell Owen, Vishnu Vinod, Pravin Dubey 7pm It is time for the toss, and Bumrah is out in the middle alongside Shreyas. Bumrah will call and he calls tails. And tails it is. MI will field first. Bumrah says with the cold weather, the wicket might settle down only later, with the ball coming on better in the second innings. Jokes he did not expect to be a Test captain before becoming an IPL captain. New challenge and new responsibility, and he hopes to have fun. Says they want to take as many positives as they can and create an impact, and ruffle a few teams. Two changes, he says, with SKY and Ghazanfar missing. Shreyas says he would have bowled first too. Pitch looks dry, he adds, and mentions the pitch got better later in the game the other day. He reckons something around 200-210 could be par. Going forward, we have to be proactive, he says. Brar comes in, Bartlett comes in and Omarzai comes in. Pitch Report: There is a shorter side tonight (63m as opposed to 68m on the other side). Danny Morrison says the pitch looks very similar to the other evening. A bit of live grass, and Morrison reckons you might need to get more than 200. There are a few dark patches, which could lend to the strip being two-paced. Be careful if you are a batter, says Deep Dasgupta, because there could be something in it for the bowlers. 6:55pm Looks like PBKS might be making a change (at least) based on their final team huddle before the toss. Omarzai could be coming in to play his first game of the season tonight. Could that be at the expense of an overseas quick, or will it be a more like-for-like swap with one of Jansen or Stoinis? Toss in five. Sanket: "Punjab is still one of the best side in this campgain but their bowling needs to improve. You can't always outscore the opponents, and in the bowling apart from Chahal who didn't bowl single over in the last game everyone is leaking runs. They played Bartlett, Fergusson and even Dwarshius in the last game but nothing has changed. And add the catch efficiency in that, they need to fix these issues now otherwise another promising start would end in nothing." gayathri: "Why is SKY not playing today? Is he injured? Dropped? " -- He had flown back to Mumbai for personal reasons after the RCB game. Jugilee: "Goes to show how important every win is. PBKS' wins have enabled them to absorb losses. Time to start winning again" 4R-ALR: "Who would potentially come in for SKY today?" -- They could bring in either Minz or Malewar. Minz, though, might be better-suited to a middle order role. Jacks and Tilak can, of course, deputize at four with SKY absent. 6:42pm Both sides have lost far more often than they have won in recent games, but PBKS' seven-game unbeaten run to start the season means they are still very much in contention for a playoff spot. All that and much more in Abhimanyu Bose's match preview. 6:35pm Some potentially big news trickling in. Jasprit Bumrah is likely to lead the Mumbai Indians today. VS: "Punjab should play X. Bartlett today. He may be the X factor they need to stop their losing streak." -- Well, he was a regular fixture at the start but has since been side-lined owing to a lack of form. Nagraj Todur : "Hows weather in Dharmshala today? Hope no rains around and disturb this thrilling encounter!!" -- There are a few clouds overhead but they do not look menacing. Seems to be clearing up too, and fingers crossed we get a game without any interruptions. 6:30pm What goes up must come down, they say. It happens in all walks of life. And it also happens in sport. Teams could be gliding over the highest of clouds, unaware that their plunge back to earth is round the corner. Conversely, teams that have had nothing going for them, end up feeling that the only trajectory possible, having hit rock-bottom, is upwards. The Punjab Kings this season, somehow, are both. Irresistibly good in their first seven games. But unable to buy a win since. And in real danger of seeing their once high-flying campaign crash and burn. Especially if these fortunes continue. The Mumbai Indians fall firmly into the latter category. But unlike the Kings, they may now hold others' destiny (as opposed to their own) in their hands, and as uncharacteristic as it may sound, that, with more than a week of the league stage remaining, might just be MI's greatest motivation tonight. Hello and welcome everyone to ESPNcricinfo's live coverage. This is Match 58, and we are back among the mountains, where the Punjab Kings now have a much steeper climb into promised land having seen their campaign plateau, and where the Mumbai Indians scheme to spoil Punjab's party and restore some personal pride in the process. Plenty to gorge on, so tag along!
