commentPostTextItems.html: 9:17pm Another strange innings in the IPL. Arya and Prabhsimran enjoyed themselves at the crease and helped the Kings get up to 107-1. But after that, they lost six wickets for 40 runs, meaning that even 180 seemed a distant possibility. Omarzai then played a vital hand, with Vinod, brought in as Impact Player, finishing things off nicely alongside Bartlett. MI will feel they let PBKS off the hook, having induced a massive slow-down through the middle overs. Almost everyone travelled at the death barring Shardul, who was comfortably their best bowler throughout. This will not be an easy chase, especially with Hardik and SKY not in play, but MI will hope their experienced stars can come to the fore. Join us in a bit for the chase. Shardul: After the powerplay, we were trying to hit a length, because there was something in the pitch. (On team talk before play) Just trying to cheer. Not had the season we would have wanted to. But the huddle is something where we like to create energy and get the fun going, because that reflects on the field. (What changed after his first over) He (Prabhsimran) tried some fancy shots and was able to get rid of it. But you see the length was working beautifully later on, did not change much (after my first over). Outfield was fine. Not much dew right now but we are hoping there is dew later. yazoo: "How come 19.6 has been deemed to be insignificant? Didn't the batters run a single and get a leg-bye, so since the LBW was overturned shouldn't it count for a run?" -- Once the decision is given, ball is deemed dead, and no runs get added, even if the decision eventually gets overturned. It is a rule that needs working definitely, but it is what it is at the moment.

commentTextItems.html: Tilak finishes it off in style! A stunning hit to cap off a truly stunning innings, and the Punjab Kings lose for the fifth time in a row! Banged in short outside leg. Tilak spots the length early and he swivels to clatter this flat over the long leg fence. He wheels away in celebration soon after and then leaps into the air in delight. He has pulled this game out of the fire, and he has inflicted further misery on the Punjab Kings, who have now lost five on the spin, and are now in real danger of missing the playoffs!

commentPostTextItems.html: 11:44pm That will be that for tonight. Tilak the star as MI ice another 200-plus run-chase, and leave PBKS in must-win territory. One of the beneficiaries of this result aka CSK, will be in action tomorrow against LSG. Do join us for that game too but until then, from all of us here at ESPNcricinfo, it is goodbye! Tilak Varma, Player of the Match: I always say I love finishing games. Playing World Cups, playing international games, it helps, you get experience and confidence. We did not expect a wicket like this - it was slow and low. We saw how Punjab struggled in first 15 overs. We thought to take the game deep, and I was believing in myself, was holding my shape and backing myself (and my game). (On the 16th over bowled by Chahal) When we had second time-out, I was talking to coach that just one big over, we will finish off the game, and to believe in me. Was just waiting for that one big over. Glad I could finish the game. (Chats with Jacks) His innings really helped. I just said to hold the shape and to wait for the slower ones. That is the only ball we were struggling to hit sixes. He held shape, got sixes and they were under pressure. Jasprit Bumrah, MI captain: One from one - good game of cricket. Both teams played some good cricket. We really pulled back well after a good start (for Punjab). Bowling in the end has become more difficult now (smiles). The wicket in this game looked a little drier. Previous game had a bit more pace, and ball was holding up and keeping low (when we were bowling). We were pretty clear in what we wanted to do (at the toss). Holding your length was the key. If you bowl too short or too full, at the altitude, the ball flies. Credit to the bowlers - they executed and held their nerve as well. (Turning point) Tilak's knock and Shardul's bowling. The way Tilak held his nerve, he kept his shape, kept his belief and Jacksy as well (for his contribution at the end). Really happy everyone contributed. (Experience as skipper) I have captained a Test match, a T20I and now only thing left is an ODI (laughs). But jokes apart, really enjoyed my time. Shreyas Iyer, PBKS captain: Tough pill to swallow. Don't want to pinpoint a situation. It was a great game of cricket. He (Tilak) played an amazing knock, and manoeuvred the field nicely - so credit to him. (On Omarzai) At a point, we were looking at 170-180, and he simply changed the momentum towards us. Getting to 200 was a commendable performance. (On their next game) Definitely excited about the next opportunity. An afternoon game and we need to win two out of two - can't wait to play (those matches). Will Jacks: These games, still so much to play for, and good to get the win. (Chat with Tilak) Kind of focussing on what they were trying to do. One big boundary, so we knew they were trying to defend that. Not sure about pace-off but when we were bowling, cross-seam and back of a length, some were skidding through. Enjoy these games, something in it for the bowlers. Difficult to bowl (because there are so many options). Every day is different. You cannot chase it - you do as you are told. 11:21pm Wow. What a game. And what a run-chase. MI, at one point, seemed out of it, especially when Rohit fell, and when Rutherford was struggling. But with the chips down, Tilak stood up. Yet again. A 33-ball 75, which included several jaw-dropping shots took MI past the finish line, and take nothing away from Jacks either, who popped up with 25 off 10, which included a six in the final over. PBKS will feel they have missed another opportunity. They had tightened the screws through the middle but their decision to hold an over of Chahal back did not pay off. MI ransacked 20 off the 16th, with 22 also coming off the 18th, and those two overs ultimately ended up costing the Kings.

commentPreTextItems.html: 7:28pm The umpires make their way out. Debut game for Tony Ematty in the IPL and he is accompanied by the experienced Ulhas Gandhe. Samson and Gaikwad to open. Shami to take the new ball, and this opening burst could have a huge bearing on how this contest goes. Samson on strike, slip in place - let's play! 7:26pm A minute's silence will be observed before the start of play today. Playing XIs of both the teams and the Match Officials will be wearing black armbands as a mark of respect for the victims who lost their lives in the storms in Uttar Pradesh. Karthik Siram : "Has pitch number 4 been used previously this season?" -- Yes, it has been. LSG have been bowled out for 141 and 119 in those games. RR did defend 159 on this track too. Arjun: "Will love to see how Pant, Markram and Pooran play Noor. Also how Josh Inglis attacks him. " Arul: "I feel Akeal should be in the Playing XI, not Spencer... they should've trusted his batting abilities!" -- Seems like CSK definitely want a hit-the-deck bowler through the middle to replace Overton, and they are keeping the option open to even bringing in Akeal, if this pitch takes more turn than expected. 7:09pm Well, plenty to unpack from the toss. Gaikwad said they had brought in Gurjapneet but he is on the bench for now. They still have the option of bringing in Akeal, if the pitch is helpful to spinners. If there is a collapse, Sarfaraz or Short could come in. LSG, meanwhile, will likely bring in Inglis when they bat. A pretty straightforward change that. But they have Mayank in the eleven, and it will be interesting to see how he fares. CSK batting-first XI: Ruturaj Gaikwad (capt), Sanju Samson (wk), Urvil Patel, Kartik Sharma, Dewald Brevis, Shivam Dube, Prashant Veer, Anshul Kamboj, Spencer Johnson, Noor Ahmad, Mukesh Choudhary CSK bench: Gurjapneet Singh, Akeal Hosein, Sarfaraz Khan, Matthew Short, Matt Henry LSG bowling-first XI: Mitchell Marsh, Nicholas Pooran, Rishabh Pant (capt & wk), Aiden Markram, Mukul Choudhary, Abdul Samad, Shahbaz Ahmed, Mohammed Shami, Mayank Yadav, Akash Singh, Prince Yadav LSG bench: Josh Inglis, M Siddharth, Digvesh Rathi, Himmat Singh, Ayush Badoni 7pm It is time for the toss. Gaikwad and Pant out in the middle. All smiles at the moment. Gaikwad calls tails, but heads it is. LSG will field first. Wicket is looking a little tacky maybe, says Pant, and he mentions they did not want to bat first on it. As a team, they have a lot to achieve, adding that they run on trust. Akash Singh is playing today, he says, and adds they are trying out a few things for next season. No running away from the way we have played, Pant quips, and he says they are frustrated as a team because they know they have it in them to make things happen. Two more changes - Samad and Mukul also come in, but he does not mention for who. Big cheer as Gaikwad comes up to chat to Pommie Mbangwa. Privilege to wear this yellow jersey and represent this franchise, he says. Adds that this is a kind of venue where you have to bat and bowl well, and notes scores have been defended here too. Says there is a bit of moisture in the surface. 170-180 could be a good total, Gaikwad reckons. Says it is tough with all the injuries going around, but also quips this acts as opportunities for those coming in, citing the examples of Mukesh and Urvil. We want to take it one game at a time, he says. Couple of changes, Gaikwad says, with Gurjapneet coming in for Akeal, and Johnson making his CSK debut. Have you played SIX SENSE yet? Simple questions. You have to guess the answers. Click the link and submit your predictions. Babu: "Standard question. Dhoni?" -- Don't think he has travelled to Lucknow. Pitch Report: We are on pitch number four, which means the square boundaries are a little skewed - 57m to one side, 63m to the other end. 77m hit straight down the ground. This has been a low-scoring pitch and Sunil Gavaskar expects it to be similar. There is no grass covering but there are patches, perhaps created due to the bowler's footmarks, and if the ball pitches there, variable bounce could be a factor. Gavaskar says it is a dry track in general and reckons the teams will have to bat extraordinarily to get close to 200. Neeraj Pandey, who has settled in nicely at the venue, has some possible LSG team news: Akash Singh, Shami and Prince Yadav have marked their run ups for LSG. Spencer Johnson, Akeal Hosein, Kamboj, Gurjapneet from CSK have done the same. Adarsh: "After the first half of the tournament, if anyone had said CSK will make it to the playoffs, and RR and PBKS won't, they would have been laughed out of the room. Yet it seems a realistic possibility now." -- That said, CSK will not want to get complacent, and will want to take it one game at a time. They have a much better chance now but nothing has been secured just yet. VS: "Who will replace Overton today? Johnson or Forrester or may be gurjapneet. Go csk, play off spot in sight." -- Forrester may not have arrived just yet or may not be ready to play today. They could bring in Johnson if he is fully fit, and play with five specialist bowlers (Akeal, Noor, Kamboj, Johnson and Mukesh/Gurjapneet). 6:35pm CSK have been hit hard by injuries throughout the season, and they will now have to finish their campaign without Jamie Overton, who was arguably their MVP alongside Samson. What changes might they be forced into making and can they cope against an LSG side that has nothing to lose? Abhimanyu Bose sets the scene in his match preview. Jugilee : "Too many injuries for CSK (right from the word go )one feels and that is precisely why they are highly unlikely to make it to the POs. " -- Well, they are still hanging in there and if they win tonight, they will move into the top four for the first time this season. 6:30pm Chennai Super Kings versus Lucknow Super Giants. Take two, and...action! Just last Sunday, two wicket-keeper batters indulged in a breath-taking display of stroke-play. Josh Inglis teed off under the afternoon Chennai sun before Urvil Patel ripped LSG to shreds later in the evening. In the end, CSK did just enough and remained hopeful of a playoff berth, with LSG, by the time the day finished, finding themselves out of contention. Neither team has played since. But the feeling around CSK's campaign may just have changed. And with the Punjab Kings dropping points (again), and the Sunrisers Hyderabad losing heavily, CSK might now actually believe that this season, which began with them rummaging for answers (and personnel) from pillar to post, could culminate with them returning to their natural habitat: the playoffs. And so, from that bright and muggy afternoon on the southeastern coast, where two teams produced a memorable opening salvo apiece, we now arrive further up north in Lucknow, where the closing and finishing act of the league stage cries out to be seized. For CSK, the brief - of winning all their remaining games - is simple and straightforward, although potentially tricky and tedious; for LSG, their objectives revolve around intangibles but having seen their campaign fizzle out, they might love nothing more than to throw a spanner in another's works. A cracker awaits, so sit back, relax and enjoy ESPNcricinfo's live coverage!

commentTextItems.html: half-tracker, and tonked into next week! Dube finishes with a flourish, and CSK end up with 187! Sits up outside off and Dube picks it really early. He gets into position and smokes it over deep mid wicket. Clean strike to end the innings, and CSK will be chuffed with this score now!

commentPostTextItems.html: 9:25pm Brilliant finish to the innings. Dube remains unbeaten on 32 off 16, with Veer also mustering 13 off 10. But the bulk of the heavy lifting had been done by Kartik before it, who dazzled on his way to 71 off 42, despite beginning sluggishly. The rest chipped in, without going into overdrive fully, and CSK now have a total they will be confident of defending. LSG did things well in patches. Akash's spell was the standout, with him removing Samson, Gaikwad and Urvil. Mayank also bowled at pace, but LSG's death-bowling left a bit to be desired. This is not the easiest of tracks to bat on, and LSG, with their firepower, will need to be at their best to chase this down. Join us in a bit for the second half. Akash Singh: I was very happy, but when you don't play in the IPL, you have to push yourself. I stuck to my task of working hard (when not playing) and today it worked for me. We knew how they dominated in the previous games, and I was focussing on bowling to their weaknesses with my strength. (Plan to CSK openers) Whenever I play in the IPL, I want to take big wickets. You come to the IPL not to play but to dominate. You need to have that mindset, irrespective of whether you play or not. IPL is becoming a batters' league and if you cannot dominate, you cannot move forward. Batter does not matter for me. But I like getting big batters out and that is my mindset. (On his celebratory chit) This gives me motivation - nothing else. And what can give me motivation to make me perform better, I will try to do it.

commentPostTextItems.html: 11:39pm And that will be that for tonight. We hope you enjoyed our coverage and we will be back with more IPL action tomorrow. Until then, from all of us here at ESPNcricinfo, it is goodbye! Mitchell Marsh, Player of the Match: Nice to get a win, few and far in between for us this season. We have stuck together as a team and nice to get a reward tonight. (On his form) We have great people within this group, some great kids. (On opening with Inglis) Feels like he takes the pressure off me. Have grown up together playing for Western Australia, we know each other well and it was a good partnership tonight. (Back-end of the powerplay) The first 2-3 overs can be hard work and at the start of the tournament, we were two or three down and were not able to get through. It is a good wicket once you get going. Sort of reminds me of Perth Stadium a little bit (chuckles). (On his dismissal) Cricket is a funny game, isn't it? (On fielding a lot more this season) Had a bit of bad luck in the summer (smiles). Inglis has hurt his finger a few days ago, so he has rightfully taken over the mantle (of being the Impact Player) and I enjoy being out there with the boys - it is always good fun. Rishabh Pant, LSG captain: (How these wins feel) It feels good. Getting a win definitely feels good. The things we talk about, of having a lot to play for, regardless of how the season ends, we take a lot of pride (in playing like this). (On Akash) He has been working hard. Sometimes, it is harder to give everyone a game. He is one guy who sticks to the plan more often and it definitely paid off. Really good to see. (On the opening partnership) That was the first thought - to get two overseas to open, with Nicky batting three. Four fast bowlers, it has been working for us. The team we have, I am going to say it again, is so amazing. The only thing that can harm us is having too many thought-process. I was ready to bat (tonight). But the idea came in on why not to try players who have not played much. Still wanted to be out there but sometimes, you have to respect some things. Ruturaj Gaikwad, CSK captain: There was a bit of something for the fast bowlers. Found it difficult to hit it off a hard length. We were looking at 160-170, and got 180. Nothing much better we could have done from a batting point of view. They (LSG) batted well and played some extraordinary shots. We were looking (to bowl the short ball) but Inglis played differently in the last game, and Marsh plays the short ball well, so we were trying to hit a hard length. We missed on execution but they played extraordinary shots. Looking back, once the opening batters fell, coming batters found it tough. Felt there was still something in it (when you hit a hard length). (On how much does this hurt) Sometimes the opposition can play good cricket than you, and you have to accept it. From a batting point of view, Kartik getting that 70-odd was impressive. Going into last couple of games, really confident that we are starting to click (in the batting). Bowling had an off-day today. (On their next two matches) First challenge is getting to Chennai and make sure we improve on the areas we need to improve, and then adapt and assess the conditions. (On their playoff hopes) It is simple, nothing complicated. Nothing to worry about, just ensure we have a good day and hope that we turn things around. Josh Inglis: We keep playing every game trying to win, not playing for what we want to play for, but good to put in a performance tonight. (On his partnership with Marsh) Felt like I was batting with a stump tonight. The way Mitch started, it really helped. Tried to be mature about it and get off strike. He got us off to a flier. Kamboj did not get the figures he wanted tonight, but he was a little skiddier than the others (and easier to play on this pitch). (On if the pitch got better in the second half) Not the man to ask because it felt hard all the time (smiles). Could not miss the middle of the bat the other day, felt a little rusty (tonight). Felt a bit like a Perth wicket tonight. I have been run-out before (with Marsh hitting it back at the stumps), have learned my lesson and have been staying in my crease or maybe even a couple of yards behind. 11:13pm Some run-chase, eh? At the half-way stage, it felt CSK had lots of runs to play with, especially on a track where run-scoring was not as easy as some other pitches this IPL. Marsh, though, smirked at that narrative and plundered his way to a 38-ball 90, which saw him tear CSK apart. Inglis did his bit too, even if he was not as belligerent as the other evening, with Pooran also indulging in some range hitting towards the end. CSK looked bereft of ideas once Marsh teed off and as the game came to a close, they looked shell-shocked too. They would have felt they had the resources to make a fist of this game but as it turned out, they fell well, well short. Here is Deep Gadhia with a stat: Worst economy in an IPL innings (min 2 overs): Anshul Kamboj v LSG, tonight - 23.6 Washington Sundar v DC, 2024 - 23.0 Ali Murtaza v RCB, 2013 - 22.5

commentary_clean: four sixes to finish the game, and four daggers to CSK hearts! CSK's playoff charge has been dented, and LSG have run rampant in front of their fans! Misses the yorker again on the shorter side. In the slot on middle and leg, and Pooran slams it over long on. Kamboj concedes 63 in 2.4 overs, and CSK do not know what has hit them tonight. LSG have been full value for their win, and they have blown CSK out of the water tonight!

commentPreTextItems.html: 7.27pm Eoin Morgan rings the bell and the umpires walk out, followed by the KKR openers and Gujarat Titans. Finn Allen and Ajinkya Rahane out in the middle for KKR. Mohammed Siraj has the new ball in hand. Rahane on strike first up. One slip in place Ashu: "Bring on Rashid in PP ,he is a road block for Finn All(e) in. " -- I'm sure they'll want to see Siraj and Rabada deal with him before that move is needed. But yes, if Allen gets through the first four or five overs, we may see Rashid in the powerplay. Vedansh : "Is there a scenario where both PBKS and DC quality and one of them goes to top 2 too?" -- You'll find your answers here. SS: "A loss does not "eliminate" KKR, yes chances will be very remote but if PBKS, RR and CSK lose all their remaining games we can still qualify with 13 points :)" -- Never, ever let anyone take away your optimism. 7.15pm Thanks Himanshu, and hello everyone. A lot of scrutiny will be on KKR's batting and how they cope with GT's new-ball burst. I really want to see how Finn Allen goes today, in what should be one of the tougher challenges for him. Kiran: "Wait ..... we could be seeing Pathirana today!" -- Indeed we could. KKR have only fielded three overseas players, so the Sri Lankan could be coming on as an impact sub. 7.10pm What do you feel about the teams? Will KKR keep their campaign alive? Remember, a loss will eliminate them. Here's Abhimanyu offering some discussion and plenty of action. Gujarat Titans: 1 Shubman Gill (capt), 2 B Sai Sudharsan, 3 Jos Buttler (wk), 4 Jason Holder, 5 Washington Sundar, 6 Nishant Sindhu, 7 Rashid Khan, 8 Arshad Khan, 9 Kagiso Rabada, 10 R Sai Kishore, 11 Mohammed Siraj. Impact options: Tewatia, Phillips, Rawat, Prasidh and Kushagra. Kolkata Knight Riders: 1 Finn Allen, 2 Ajinkya Rahane (capt), 3 Cameron Green, 4 Angkrish Raghuvanshi, 5 Manish Pandey, 6 Rinku Singh, 7 Sunil Narine, 8 Anukul Roy, 9 Varun Chakravarthy, 10 Saurabh Dubey, 11 Kartik Tyagi. Impact options: Arora, Ramandeep, Tejasvi, Powell and Pathirana. 7pm Time for the toss, before which Ravi Shastri throws his lungs out. GT opt to bowl. Shubman Gill says the wickets looks sticky, and hopes it "gets better in the second innings". He credits his bowlers for their form, and says "momentum is with us" after five successive wins. Gill says GT are unchanged. Ajinkya Rahane, meanwhile, is taking one game at a time as KKR seek three victories. He says he would have bowled first as well, and spots some moisture on the pitch. Varun is back for KKR. Akash: "Just Varun back for KKR" Ashu: "Umran should get an opportunity." --- Ummmm, not for a must-win game, you'd think? 6.50pm We're ten minutes away from the toss. What changes, if any, would you like to see in the sides for tonight? Have you played our prediction game SIX SENSE yet? Six simple questions, you have to predict the outcomes. Click the link and submit your predictions. Ved: "First things first :) How is the weather forecast for the evening?" --- It's dry for the moment, although it rained considerably in the lead-up. 6.40pm Remember, GT will become the first team to qualify for the playoffs with a win, while KKR's chances will take a further hit with a loss. All that and more in our preview for tonight's game. Meanwhile, KKR batter Rachin Ravindra, who spent the entire season on the bench, leaves the squad to prepare for England Tests. 6.30pm Who in Kolkata is still discussing about the Bengal election results? No surprises if most are, even 12 days after the verdict. Who remembers about the cricket in Kolkata, though? KKR had last played there nearly a month back, on April 19, and so much has happened since - a change in government in the state, and KKR running the risk of not making the playoffs. Sorry for kicking up a storm with the mention of politics! Anyway, it's time for action at Eden Gardens in what's going to be the first of three successive home games for KKR. This is Himanshu saying hello, with Abhimanyu set to join me soon.

commentPostTextItems.html: Finn Allen: "Sometimes you get little bit lucky. I just tried to continue for as long as I could. It's a beautiful ground to bat on. At the start it was quite challenging with the new ball. Raghuvanshi is a proper player. He's a quality player. I just wanted to be clear with what I was doing. I definitely back our boys to defend." 9.14pm Yet another incredibly high score batting first this season. KKR thumped 22 sixes in comparison to just 12 fours. Finn Allen hit ten of those sixes despite facing just 35 balls. He ended up scoring 93 runs, and set the tone for what was to follow. GT dropped four catches - one of them was a sitter of Allen by Siraj - and Raghuvanshi (82*) and Green (52*) have taken KKR to a mammoth 247 in a must-win game. Will we see yet another incredibly high score chased down? Join Abhi soon for the chase.

commentTextItems.html: edged behind. Raghuvanshi takes a low catch. Tewatia got across the stumps and went pulling at this rising short ball around middle. He swung too hard, and eventually fell to Green. KKR win by 29 runs, and keep their slim playoffs hopes alive

commentPostTextItems.html: That's a wrap from this run fest at Eden Gardens, where 247 played 218. Here's Karthik Krishnaswamy's report, in case you missed any of the action. And here's the points table, where GT are second and KKR seventh as the tail end of the group stage nears. Until tomorrow's double header, it's goodnight and goodbye from us here! Take care. Sunil Narine is the Player of the Match. He bagged 2 for 29 in a high-scoring game. He says: "It comes from hard work. The guys have been preparing well. It's all about planning what is in front of you. Every game brings a different challenge. If you overthink, it gets tougher than what it normally is. It's a blessing [to have played 200 games for KKR]." Ajinkya Rahane: "Really happy with two points. The way we started with the bat [despite] losing the toss. Amazing to see Finn Allen's knock. Preparation always has been fantastic. The talk was always to take it one game at a time. Today the batters backed their strengths. Overall it was a fantastic effort from the bowling unit. It's all about trusting their ability. Whenever you do well in domestic cricket, you carry that confidence. Dubey has been bowling well in the Vidarbha league. Credit goes to these guys. It's all about belief and confidence. Narine makes my job really easy. Varun showed the courage to play this game. He has a sore foot." Time for the presentations Yogesh: "Narine and drop catches were the difference" Sandy: "We are into the 60th game of the IPL and still no Q mark besides any team yet." Angkrish Raghuvanshi: "Finn Allen was amazing. It was so easy for me. I just had to give strike to him. I'm not used to wicketkeeping duties, and it's taking everything out of me. It was a great surface. I hope we can play on these surfaces every game. They have to kick me out of nets - I hit a lot of balls! Ever since I was a kid, my coach Abhishek Nayar has got me to hitting 1000 balls a day." Shubman Gill: "Looking at the wicket, I thought 200-210 was par score. We dropped too many catches, and it wasn't easy for the bowlers. The pitch was good. The ones were stopping and sticking. I feel we did well to get where we did. No concerns, but our fielding could have been much better. Dropping three sitters, I don't think we deserved to win this one. Best to have a game like this now rather than in the qualifiers. Rest and recover for a couple of days. Travel back to Ahmedabad, and see how the wicket behaves." 11.30pm While four dropped catches certainly played its role in making it tougher for GT, don't miss the difference in sixes: KKR's 22 vs GT's 12. Both Gill and Buttler, despite scoring 85 and 57, respectively, struggled to gain any momentum for most of their innings. And by the time Gill got a few away, it had become a mountain too high for GT to climb. GT lost only four wickets in scoring 218, but fell well short. KKR get two big points, and keep themselves alive after being led by Allen's 93 off 35 balls.

commentPreTextItems.html: Kohli and Bethell out in the middle. Arshdeep Singh with the new ball. What a start we potentially have on hand. 3.20pm Hello then! All quite make or break for Punjab Kings. Their bowling hasn't quite showed up this season, and they'll start off here with the ball in hand. Let's see what they've got for us today... Dharamsala is such a beautiful stadium. Most picturesque in the country? Manu: "In this hot summer, if there's any place in India to play a cricket match during afternoons, then it would definitely be in Dharamshala " vS: "Spectacular Dharamshala, all in its glory in the beautiful sunshine" Ashutosh Kumar: "RCB is almost in playoff even if they lose their remaining matches with lower margin and others wins their matches with low margin, and this is only in case of RCB, isn't it??? I think, their one win place them in top 2 playoff team." A win seals their spot in the top four, not necessarily in the top two. But if they pick up two more points here, they're most likely to stay in the top two, yes Right then, it's time to say hello to Abhijato, who will take you through the first ten overs. Have you played SIX SENSE yet? Six simple questions, you just have to get your predictions right. Click the link and submit your predictions. Sai Mehta: "RCB's nemesis Harpreet Brar returns!" Jashan : "Correction: Ferguson and RCB's Kryptonite comes in" Here are the teams: PBKS: 1 Priyansh Arya, 2 Prabhsimran Singh (wk), 3 Cooper Connolly, 4 Shreyas Iyer (capt), 5 Shashank Singh, 6 Suryansh Shedge, 7 Azmatullah Omarzai, 8 Harpreet Brar, 9 Lockie Ferguson, 10 Arshdeep Singh, 11 Yuzvendra Chahal Impact options: Marcus Stoinis, Xavier Bartlett, Vishnu Vinod, Musheer Khan, Praveen Dubey RCB: 1 Jacob Bethell, 2 Virat Kohli, 3 Devdutt Padikkal, 4 Venkatesh Iyer, 5 Tim David, 6 Jitesh Sharma (capt, wk), 7 Romario Shepherd, 8 Krunal Pandya, 9 Bhuvneshwar Kumar, 10 Suyash Sharma, 11 Josh Hazlewood Impact options: Rasikh Salam, Jordan Cox, Abhinandan Singh, Swapnil Singh, Kanishk Chouhan 3pm Alrighty, it's toss time. Jitesh Sharma out in the middle with Shreyas Iyer. Tails is the call, heads it is. Punjab Kings will bowl. "I'm not going by the stats. We have clearly seen how the game pans out immediately. More you have belief in your ability and skills it doesn't matter if you bat or bowl first. It's all about the execution. I feel we've been bowling fantastic, but not executed in pressure moments. Brar comes in and Lockie comes in," Iyer says. Jitesh Sharma says RCB wanted to bowl as well but the wicket looks good. "Rajat is doing fantastic now and hopefully we'll see him in Hyderabad," he says. "Every game is important. This win can change a lot of things for a lot of teams and hopefully for us as well." Suyash Sharma and Romario Shepherd come in for Rajat Patidar and Jacob Duffy. Jashan: "Just checked the RCB squad, and unless they wanna change the combination, we could get a U-19 debutant today! Excited to see Vihaan or Kanishk" -- Let's see if RCB go down that route. Sam: "Very glad to see coverage on the Arshdeep situations, colorism is racism!" 2.50pm Just stepping away from the cricket momentarily, Arshdeep Singh's recent comments to Mumbai Indians' Tilak Varma, calling hin 'andhera' on social media has come under the scanner, and rightly so. Mumbai Indians, on their behalf, reacted with a social media post of their own, but Sidharth Monga explains why this should not be treated as banter or a laughing matter, but rather taken more seriously. 2.45pmVS: "Is Salt fit to play? Only a week to go before play offs Salt will like to have a hit." -- Unfortunately, he is still not available. In fact, for more team news, stats and everything else you need to know in the build-up to this game, have a look at Vishal Dikshit's preview. Huzefa: "Who needs to win to keep the table more open?" -- Interesting question. On the face of it, a PBKS win will make sure there still isn't a team to secure qualification. But a win for RCB will make it more realistic for teams outside the top four currently to sneak in. 2.40pm Bhuvneshwar Kumar has been sensational for RCB this season, with the India fast bowler in possession of the Purple Cap at the moment, and now he has come in for some fine praise from his strike partner Josh Hazlewood. Hazlewood, part of Australia's iconic pace troika, has likened bowling with Bhuvi to bowling with Pat Cummins and Mitchell Starc. Virat: "Feel bad for Patidar missing out today. commentTextItems.html: David picks the fielder and RCB finish on 222. But wait, Tim David has reviewed this for height! It's a full toss that David tries to flick away over square leg. One hand comes off the bat and the ball doesn't carry beyond the fielder. The check confirms it was a fair delivery and RCB do finish on 222

commentPostTextItems.html: Devdutt Padikkal: "[The total] I think it's a pretty good total but like any other game we have to bowl well and restrict them under that. I think you expect [slower surfaces] in day games. It plays a little slow with the new ball not coming on as nicely but it's important we make use of that and make sure our bowlers know that as well. [On his partnership with Kohli] When I go in the powerplay I know it's important that I stitch a partnership, push the momentum and take it forward for the team. I have to put the team in a good position at the halfway point and I'm very happy I was able to do that today." 5.15pm Excellent knocks from Virat Kohli, Devdutt Padikkal and Venkatesh Iyer have powered RCB to a total they should feel happy with. Venky Iyer in particular, started slow but once he got going, he really gave RCB the acceleration they needed. He's not played a lot this season, so it's an important knock for him. He stays unbeaten on 73 off 40. David came in and helped finish the innings in style. And now PBKS' batters face a steep task against a strong RCB attack to avoid a sixth consecutive defeat. Abhijato will be with you for the start of the chase.

commentTextItems.html: Slower ball outside off, miscued to long-off and RCB become the first team to reach the playoffs in IPL 2026. A stellar batting display followed up by a stellar bowling show after losing the toss, and it's scenes of joy for the defending champions. PBKS, the losing finalists last year, slide to their sixth consecutive defeat, and are staring now at the very real probability of missing out on making the playoffs

commentPostTextItems.html:
7.45pm Right, then, RCB have secured a playoffs spot with a game to go. Punjab Kings, meanwhile, have to go win in Lucknow and also pray that other results fall their way. The business end of the IPL is well and truly here, with just nine league games remaining. That's all from here, although there's more IPL action in store for you with Rajasthan Royals taking on Delhi Capitals. On behalf of Abhijato, Ranjith and Chandan, this is Abhimanyu signing off. 7.35pm Time for the presentation ceremony. The player of the match is Venkatesh Iyer: "Technically, it's my second game. Today is the first time I got to properly bat. That was the pleasing thing and getting two points of course. [Being in RCB] They welcomed me very well. Obviously it's a very professional setup. Credit to Mo (Bobat), Andy (Flower) and DK (Dinesh Karthik). The brand of cricket that RCB plays is something that excites me a lot. Obviously I played for KKR so there is an emotional bond but I really feel at home here. I'll be lying if I said I wasn't frustrated because I wanted to play. But I do understand that this is a champion team and to tinker with the combination isn't always right. But I always made an impression on the coaching staff that I want to play and will make an impact and am happy for the opportunity. It was scratchy at the start but I was lucky to be batting with Virat Kohli. The mindset shift that he's able to communicate with you. All the legends of the game, one good thing is they know how to communicate. I played after a long time and needed a few balls to get into the groove. Once I understood the wicket and had the freedom to go after the bowling, it was good for me. Jitesh Sharma: "I think we were in control, with the batting and bowling. [On the total] We were not under pressure. We were in control. We knew what to do and batters gave good feedback on what's working on the wicket. We planned for each batsman and executed those plans. [On Bhuvi and Hazlewood] We are priveleged to have them at RCB and I have experienced guys who help me as a captain. Our motto is simple: one game at a time. We just want to do well in every match."
Bhuvneshwar Kumar: "[On practicing the yorker] I think it's not about doing it before the match but what i do throughout the year is what makes the difference. When you bowl to world-class opponents and get it right, it gives you confidence. [On bowling with Hazlewood] It makes a big difference, the experience and skill he has. I think we are complementing each other. But credit to Rasikh as well, he is going under the radar but he's doing well. [On qualifying] Feels great. First aim is to qualify for the playoffs. If you can get top two then it's great. You can see it means a lot to us, we've been working very hard for the last two months." Shreyas Iyer: "Obviously they got off to a great start and them taking on the bowlers right after the powerplay. Getting to 222 is a commendable performance. I think the match was lost in the powerplay. We were three down in the powerplay and a majority of our run scorers were out early. Really disappointed but commendable performances with Shashank and Stoinis and a few others. We were up there with the 10-runs an over mark but amazing bowling by Hazlewood and Bhuvi. I am always positive irrespective of the results. I always approach with a strong attitude and I am not someone who doesn't dwell too much on the past. This is over, this is the past and I always look towards the light at the end of the tunnel." Karthik: "Thanks RCB, from a CSK fan" 7.21pm RCB, like they have done on so many occasions this season, bring out an all-round A-Game and register a comprehensive victory in Dharamsala. Handshakes and high-fives all around for them, while the mood is more grim in the Punjab Kings camp. With Rajat Patidar out with concussion, Virat Kohli, Devdutt Padikkal and Venkatesh Iyer played sumptuous innings before Bhuvneshwar Kumar set up the win with another excellent new-ball display. Marcus Stoinis and Shashank Singh threatened a comeback, but with Bhuvneshwar and Josh Hazlewood showing off their death-overs expertise as well, it ended up in a comfortable win for the reigning champions.

title: Archer to Marsh, 1 leg bye

commentPreTextItems.html: Inglis and Marsh head out to the middle now. What have they got for us today? They face Archer first up: a bit expensive in the powerplay recently, but still incredible to watch when he's at his peak this season. Meanwhile, Arjun has been counting the syllables: "Mitchinglis might not sound as good as JaiSoorya/TraviShek/PrabhArya but every should have 3 syallables and MitchInglis is the only fitting the syllable count" - The academic analysis has spoken. Mitchinglis it is (for now)... 7.20pm Who is Sushant Mishra, playing for Rajasthan Royals today? Ashish Pant and Rajan Raj profiled him earlier this year. You can read all about it here. Nithin: "Don't understand having Parag on bench if he has hamstring injury. Anyway they dont want to risk it for sub fielding nor they use him for bowling" - Yeah, curious to have him on the list at all. But mostly an academic impact bench, besides fielding subs. Sooryavanshi a shoo-in for the chase. Have you given our game SIX SENSE a go yet? Your predictions are all we want. Click the link and submit your answers. 7pm Captains out in the middle now. Jaiswal to give the coin a flip. Heads is the call, and tails it is: so RR are going to bowl first. "I feel like it's a good wicket and there will be dew later on," he says. "[Parag] He had some hamstring injury, he'll be fine soon. Three changes. Wonderful day, we'll enjoy the cricket. Jaddu bhai is recovering, he has some niggles but he will be fine soon, I hope." Sandeep Sharma, Sushant Mishra and Lhuan-dre Pretorious come in. Rishabh speaks now: "Really happy to bat first or bowl first, doesn't matter. We have a lot to play for, as a team. At the same time, we want to put our best foot forward. Aiden is not here. Shami is not playing, Mohsin is playing. Markram not here, Badoni comes in." Lucknow Super Giants batting-first XI: Mitchell Marsh, Josh Inglis, Nicholas Pooran, Ayush Badoni, Rishabh Pant (wk, c), Abdul Samad, Shahbaz Ahmad, Mohsin Khan, Mayank Yadav, Akash Singh, Prince Yadav LSG Impact Bench: Mukul Choudhary, Manimaran Siddharth, Digvesh Rathi, Himmat Singh, Arshin Kulkarni Rajasthan Royals bowling-first XI: Yashasvi Jaiswal (c), Lhuan-dre Pretorius, Dhruv Jurel (wk), Donovan Ferreira, Shubham Dubey, Dasun Shanaka, Jofra Archer, Sandeep Sharma, Sushant Mishra, Birjesh Sharma, Yash Raj Punja RR Impact Bench: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Yudhvir Singh Charak, Aman Perala, Ravi Bishnoi, Riyan Parag 6.55pm A couple of big updates, now. One for this match and one for the India team. Nagraj Gollapudi has let us know: Yashasvi Jaiswal will captain RR. It is understood Riyan Parag has been advised to rest his left hamstring which he hurt while batting in RR's previous match. As for India's Test against Afghanistan, which begins soon after the IPL, Gurnoor Brar and Manav Suthar have been called up to the Test squad. Jasprit Bumrah and Ravindra Jadeja have been rested. You can read up about the full squad for this Test, and the three-match ODI series squad, here. Prashant: "Why is RR not picking Ravi Bishnoi for so many matches now? He had shown reasonably good performance overall before he stopped getting picked." - His form took a bit of a nosedive in the middle of the season, and I think RR have just lost confidence in him. It's quite the U-turn after he was the Purple Cap leader, for a brief while. It looked like he had sorted out his line-and-length issues. But the pitches he bowled on, tbf, were quite brutal through that stretch of bad form... Pranav: "mitchinglis? don't you mean 'inch' or better yet, 'itch'?" - I've always been a fan of minimalism but this is making me reconsider. 6.45pm While we wait for the toss and team sheets, read Shashank's preview here. Ravindra Jadeja is unlikely to feature for RR today, still dealing with a niggle. It might be another blow for RR, who head into this game as a virtual must-win, if they are to keep their fate in their own hands. If you want to read more about all the permutations and combinations for the teams vying for that last playoff spot, go and study up on Sampath's IPL scenarios piece here. VS: "Its Jaisoorya vs Mitchinglis show today. As a CSK fan hope Mitchinglis trump the other" - Mitchinglis... This really is the season of portmanteaus isn't it... 6.30pm Five teams are in contention for the final playoff spot this IPL. Out of those teams, Rajasthan Royals are the only one with their fate still in their own hands. Win both their games and they finish in the top four. Simple as that. Except it isn't: they are up against Mumbai Indians and Lucknow Super Giants. Those two teams might be lurking at the bottom of the points table, but they have found a new vein of form. LSG, who take on RR today, have won two of their last three games. Their overseas batters - especially Mitchell Marsh and Josh Inglis - are in top form. And with RR's bowling attack in a bit of a rough batch, we might be in for a humdinger. I'm Abhijato, and alongside Vishal Dikshit, we'll be bringing you all the action from Jaipur.

commentPostTextItems.html: 9.24pm At one point it looked like LSG would get 250-odd after the smashing century opening stand but they've been kept to 220 in the scorching heat in Jaipur. They were 149 for 1 after 12, and Yash Raj Punja's stifling bowling slowed them down even though most other bowlers leaked runs. Sushant Mishra from Jharkhand was on IPL debut on a really flat pitch and leaked 46. LSG could have scored a lot more but Archer almost single-handedly tightened the noose with a fiery last over for just five runs with searing pace, bouncers and yorkers. His 1 for 39 doesn't do justice to his bowling, quite a few runs off edges. Abhijato is itching to start the chase, just like Jaiswal waiting near the rope. Shrihari S : "Bowling an economical last over is one , Bowling it Vs a set batter like Mitch Marsh is another level. Jofra may have given RR the much needed momentum for their chase " AK: "With what LSG left on the table, I could have my dinner." Laal maas or Lucknowi kebabs? VS: "May be the old ball was difficult to hit. Expected more than 220" Pranav: "Just noticed that there is no real heavily reputed international bowler in this LSG lineup, so there's a chance Sooryavanshi will fall cheaply! I wish for an LSG victory here to keep things interesting in the rest of the league stage." Jay: "CSK can still mathematically qualify. Go Shami, Go prince, go akash!!!" No Shami today though. But yes, five teams for one spot! Marsh: They bowled well in the end, to be honest felt like torture out there. Maybe a few more boundaries would have been nice but they bowled well. We've seen the game change over the last five years. We've (he and Inglis) played a lot of cricket together, he takes a lot of pressure off me and hoping that partnership will help us get over the line. It's a really good wicket, good balls can go for four or six, but execution is key. It's probably due (on his run out)

commentPostTextItems.html: 11.50pm That's the end of RR's losing streak of three games and the playoffs race continues. Five teams still in the race for one spot although Delhi Capitals look effectively out with that negative NRR. If you missed another day of how the 15-year-old is spending his summer vacations, you will be able to read the match report soon enough. Until next time, it's good bye and good luck from Vishal Dikshit and Abhijato. Ciao! Here's the presentation: Sooryavanshi is the Player of the Match, for the third time: I was sitting while bowling and the wicket looked good, I didn't want to rush and take me time. I knew that was going to help the other batter too. I always knew I could hit anytime and didn't want to rush at all. I don't read papers and all, I just think this is the start and if I have a long career then a lot of things will be said. I just want to focus on my game. (on his fifty celebrations) Even I don't know what that was, even the last game's celebration didn't mean anything. I just keep trying new things (laughs). We just want to focus on the last game and enjoy it, and we want to win. Yashasvi Jaiswal: Everyone put the hard yards and worked rally well. The way Jofra and Brijesh bowled, we knew it was a good pitch. The way they bowed after the powerplay. the way Vaibhav batted absolutely killed the game. And the support staff as well behind the scenes. Brijesh and Sandy had some niggles so I had to manage them. But Brijesh came back, so I had to take those decisions. I really enjoyed it and the way they showed character, because we knew it was going to be a big score on this pitch. It was unbelievable. I wanted to play good cricketing shots and get the momentum. Vaibhav and I said one of us should play till the end and he killed the game. (on the last game) I just want to play with a smile and enjoy the game. 11.35pm Lap of honor for the Rajasthan Royals players as it's their last home game while Mr Goenka, the LSG owner, has a chat with Sooryavanshi. Rishabh Pant: In the middle overs, the way Archer bowled the last over was really good. Here we could have scored five or 10 more runs but we couldn't in the last over. You always want to back your bowlers but it's hard. On a wicket like this it's hard, and too many suggestions also doesn't work. Experience is something you'll always miss, it takes years to get that. It always keeps you out for sure in pressure situation. Definitely the left-handers (to not bowl Shahbaz earlier), so we bowled Rathi and we didn't want to expose Shahbaz. I'm proud of the team regardless. It doesn't take away the fact that we're a f***ing good team. Abby: "Rishabh Pant..you were on live cam national tv, my friend!" Arun: "DC is out, I guess due to poor NRR" Yash Raj Punja: I just feel like with the way we started, I wasn't trying anything fancy and put the pressure back o the batting team and stay composed. This season, I try to keep it simple and talk to the coaches to execute. There was pressure in the previous game as well but it's all about learning from experience and taking a second longer to bowl, which worked for me today. The death bowlers did quite well as well. I'm just trying to take it one match at a time, lot of things to learn before coming back next season. It's an amazing environment and makes it easier to express ourselves. 11.25pm Rajasthan Royals overtake Punjab Kings on the table as celebrations, high-fives and fist-bumps take over the home dugout. That's Punjab Kings slipping out of the top four first time this IPL! What a downfall for them, although they can still go through. PBKS and RR have one game each to go and have positive NRRs, while CSK, DC and KKR are all in the negative among the teams still in contention. But let's not forget what a night it was for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who absolutely demolished this 221 chase despite starting much slower than usual. Jaiswal, the captain today, did the early damage and then Sooryavanshi took over with his sixes all around.

commentPreTextItems.html: 7.28pm Alright then, Gill and SaiSu stride out. So do CSK. Sai Sudharsan will take strike first up. Mukesh Choudhary has the new ball in hand. Vinod Kannan: "An ardent CSK fan and its appalling to see they keep dropping Akeal." Nick: "GT's batting first already includes 4 seamers and 4 spin options! Crazy!" MW: "What happened to Overton? Such a good start to the season and then he disappeared. Injured?" -- Yeah, he suffered a thigh injury. 7.16pm Thanks, Ekanth. And hello everyone. And I have been welcomed by this very strong comment first up. Praveen: "@Niyam, Injury didn't screwup. It's the captain and management. Starting from Auction and the team selection. Who would drop a most economical and striking bowler every other match ??? CSK leadership is on another level " Stadium's filling in nicely, should be a good game. Abhimanyu will be here for the start Ishwar: "It's terrific to see 6 bowling options while GT's batting first...and later prasiddh will join party...well sundar doesn't get to bowl that much though." VS: "CSK truely miss the all rounder Overton. Without him it is such a long tail." Yeah, even with Kartik at 7, but yeah, it seems thin GT impact options - Prasidh Krishna, Anuj Rawat, Glenn Phillips, Kulwant Khejroliya, Kumar Kushagra Gujarat Titans: 1 Shubman Gill (capt), 2 B Sai Sudharsan, 3 Jos Buttler (wk), 4 Nishant Sindhu, 5 Washington Sundar, 6 Jason Holder, 7 Rashid Khan, 8 Rahul Tewatia, 9 Kagiso Rabada, 10 Arshad Khan, 11 Mohammed Siraj CSK impact options - Kartik Sharma, Macneil Noronha, Sarfaraz Khan, Kuldip Yadav, Aman Khan Chennai Super Kings: 1 Ruturaj Gaikwad (capt), 2 Sanju Samson (wk), 3 Urvil Patel, 4 Dewald Brevis, 5 Shivam Dube, 6 Matt Short, 7 Anshul Kamboj, 8 Noor Ahmad, 9 Spencer Johnson, 10 Mukesh Choudhary, 11 Gurjapneet Singh Shubman Gill, GT captain: We'd have bowled. Doesn't make a difference as there's not much dew. One change - Prasidh returns for Sai Kishore. It's all about keeping the intensity up. Our fielding hasn't been on par in the last couple of seasons. Our bowling has been right up there, batting has been good too. All three departments need to come together. Just because we have a Q, doesn't mean the job is done. Hope for three more good games. Ruturaj Gaikwad, CSK captain: There's pace and bounce in the pitch, we want to exploit it early on. Couple of changes due to conditions: Akeal out, Gurjapneet in; Short in, Prashant out. Last game, we gave a good fight, it's all about turning up and getting that W. 6:59pm Ashish Nehra has last-minute words with Shubman Gill as he walks out for the toss. He meets a smiling Ruturaj Gaikwad. Gill spins the coin, tails is the call. It is tails. Big cheers. CSK bowl Pitch report: 62 metres and 70 metres square boundaries from the North End. 72 metres down the ground, 55 and 60 metres fine. Aaron Finch says it's a red-soil pitch with a beautiful covering grass, which is rolled into the surface. It'll be great for batting. It'll hold enough pace and batters will be able to use that pace. Doesn't look like there'll be turn for the spinners. Discrepancies in square boundaries will play a part. Win the toss and bat second is his call. Niyam: "It rly sucks how injury screwed up CSK these past two years. Very out of character results for us." 6:50pm GT's template stays the same, the top-order still does the heavy-lifting. The bowlers are all-rounded and can break down oppositions. They might have had doubts early in the season but the team has come up trumps. Jos Buttler finding form has been big after his poor showing in the T20 World Cup. Rashid Khan, too, has made a big comeback. Can they continue their form tonight and take GT towards that top-two finish? Arquam: "Prediction Time: Rabada and Kamboj will take 3 wickets apiece, while Samson and Sudharsan getting out for ducks. Gill will score 10 and Buttler 75" 6:40pm CSK's batters have taken turns to stand up in different games, consistency from individuals has been lacking. Losing Ayush Mhatre didn't help their cause either. The focus will return to Ruturaj Gaikwad and his strike rate. If he and Samson get going, GT will be put under serious pressure. Bowling-wise, Spencer Johnson may not be Jamie Overton, he will come in with experience at this stadium as he has played for Titans. They have the pieces, can they come together this evening? Rajesh: "It's the first time CSK not going playoffs 3 times in a row! " VS: "Win or lose CSK forever. Hope they come back stronger next season." Shashank Kishore's match preview No Dhoni for CSK as they fight for survival 6:30pm It all boils down to this for Chennai Super Kings, a win and they stay in with a chance of making it to the playoffs; lose, and they're gone. That's quite an unfavourable bargain but there's only one spot that five teams are competing for. Hosts Gujarat Titans, on the other hand, have qualified for the playoffs and they have a strong chance to make Qualifier 1. You'd much rather be in GT's camp, if the season goes in CSK's favour though it'll be quite a tale.

commentTextItems.html: Given caught behind. Seam-up from around the wicket. Slot ball with a sharp angle away. Sundar looked to slap it over extra, got a feather to the keeper

commentPostTextItems.html: CSK will need to keep an eye on NRR, so this will be a heck of a chase if they get what they want. But will they have Samson for it? Find out after the fireworks show at the ground, with Abhimanyu. Neon: "If CSK chase this, it will be their record chase... seeing that they chased 180 against LSG after like 7-8 years, this looks hard imo" Yep, their highest is 208 Sai Sudharsan is back with the orange cap: Shubby was unbelievable, Buttler started great too. If I were at my best, we could've scored 10-15 more. We don't see our score and play accordingly. I wasn't firing, we were slightly behind in the powerplay. But I'm not looking at my score or Shubby's score, that's why we bat deeper and stitch partnerships. Really happy with five fifties in a row but lot of work to do. 9:27pm Pretty much the perfect innings for GT - the phase-wise splits read 62, 111 and 56 runs, showing they started well and never lost pace or control. Gill was the cruiser at the start while Sudharsan was scratchy. As time passed, Gill kept going and Sudharsan got some of his rhythm back. When Gill fell, CSK could've made inroads. Buttler ensured that didn't happen. Bowling-wise, CSK were hit off their lengths early on. Noor didn't get much purchase. Later on, the pacers went wide and full, which brought about mixed returns. Gurjapneet, who had two three-run overs, was the pick of the bowlers. Johnson closed out well. The over-rate penalty in the last two overs pinched them. sandip: "Unless there is a Samson cameo, target is little too much for CSK!"

title: Rabada to Johnson, OUT

commentTextItems.html: Appeal for caught behind, not given. GT review. Johnson removes his gloves and helmet, looks like this is out. Hard length on middle and off, Johnson showed all three stumps and looked to defend straight... and Hawk-Eye shows he got a thin feather. GT, with a net run rate 0.699, have all but confirmed their spot in the top-two. CSK's campaign is done!

commentPostTextItems.html: The joint-youngest IPL side continues to take massive strides in its initial years. Five-time champions have not had a good 2026. They'll have to return next year, who knows how that'll be. We'll have full clarity on the top-two sides this year, tomorrow, as SRH take on RCB. Join us for that. See you for now. 89-run win is GT's biggest win in terms of runs in the IPL. Three of their biggest wins by runs have come in the last four games Mohammed Siraj, POTM: Ball's coming out nicely. Was out of the XIs during the WC, the rhythm for the game was missing. Then I watched videos and it's coming out nicely now. During practice, I use the new ball to work on my rhythm and line and length, and then go for yorkers. Red-soil pitch, I'm happy to be driven through covers. That's what came off with Samson. While bowling in the powerplay, my priority is to build pressure. With that, even Rabada can get wickets. That's how you bowl in partnerships. Shubman Gill, GT captain: Important win. Happy to go in with the momentum we have. Even the first two games we played were close. We knew we were competitive, needed 5% which we got in the Delhi game. Our bowlers hit lengths consistently, odd ball will go over the rope but it's about backing your lengths. Happy with my batting, every time you're out you think you could've done better. Catching was much better, hope we continue. [Dube shush celebration] When you're playing a high-emotion game, it comes out. Neck's okay. Have to keep up with the good things. Need to maintain intent and impact in the playoffs. After 12 games, we were No. 1 last season, same this time. We lost last two last season. There was some deja vu but I don't think we've done much different this season. We've been consistently No. 1 or 2. Very grateful for fans who turn up and support us. Sides like RCB and CSK will have an edge, nothing will change in that matter. Nilesh : "Can someone please explain how is GT's spot is sealed in top two with a chance of SRH also getting to 18 points? Thanks " One of RCB or SRH's NRR will be lower than GT's after tomorrow Vivek: "So the top-two race is in a delicious situation now: Looks like SRH might find it easier to get past RCB than GT, since it's a zero-sum game between RCB and SRH as far as NRR is concerned. If SRH wins by some 80 runs, they might get past both RCB and GT, while RCB's NRR would dip below GT's. Waiting for S Rajesh's piece on this :)" Scenarios for SRH tomorrow: They need to win by 88 runs if they score 220, by 87 if they score 200. if they're chasing 150, SRH need to win in around 11.1 to 11.3 overs, informs S Rajesh Kagiso Rabada I realise now (that I'll be on a hat-trick next game). Our top-three were phenomenal, scored the bulk of the runs and put up a good total. Put up a total we could defend. It's about doing your best every game no matter how you feel. As long as you rock up and not afraid of being competitive, that's all I try and do. I've bowled in all three phases. For me, it's whatever the coach and team require of me. We've got a while now. Feet up, I guess, get stuck in your hotel room, watch some series and hit the ground running. [Is the wait time better or worse?] All the waiting is too much [smiles] Ruturaj Gaikwad, CSK captain: We wanted to chase whatever the total is asap. When you're chasing 230, it's not easy against that bowling attack. Thought why don't we give it a shot and express ourselves, credit to them. Wicket was spongy to start, they started well. Our bowling wasn't good in the powerplay. Hard to stop their openers. We had our chance to restrict them under 200, failed to do it. Tough season, after a hat-trick of losses first up. We found momentum, we found the right spots and combinations, but then were hit by injuries. Ghosh and Overton going out unsettled us, we were a batter or bowler short in the last three games. Not many people buy the fact that we are a young team in transition , with a lot of inexperienced players. More than 8-10 players have played less than 20 games, they've gotten exposure, we've found out what areas we're lacking. We still got six away wins, proud of the unit. We missed out on chasing 80 in 10 in Hyderabad and couldn't restrict them in Chennai. Not able to do that. Still proud. Moving on from Rahane, Rayudu, etc the experience we had is tough... Karthik, Urvil and Brevis, who missed out initially, are there. Karthik has potential, has areas to improve. Urvil's playing a full season for the first time, that comes with expectations. [Dhoni] You and I'll get to know it next year. It's a hard miss for us. He can come in those late overs and change the game just by staying in the crease. Never know about next season but really happy with the guys we have. Edwin: "It the season for second timer. So definitely it is going to be RR in the fourth spot. All top 4 will be chasing their 4 title. If PBKS make it playoffs then, they will chase their first title. If KKR make it to Playoffs, they will chase their 4th title. My prediction is- the 4th team making the playoffs will go on win the title. RR/KKR/PBKS" Deep: "Start your season with 3 losses and end it with 3 losses... Tough luck for CSK.. " 11:01pm Hard to imagine how that could've gone better for GT... or worse for CSK. It was always going to be a tall chase, but Siraj taking three quickly ensured it was insurmountable. There was no shortage of intent from CSK, but the top-order fell cheaply. By the time the middle-order threw in their hail mary, the asking rate and the mass of runs needed was too much. Dube's fireworks gave them a slimmer of hope but that hope was short lived thanks to Rashid and Co.

commentPreTextItems.html: Bhuvneshwar Kumar has the new ball in hand, which has been a lethal weapon for him through the years and this year as well. One slip in place 7.26pm RCB team in a huddle before the teams head out. Amit Rana and J Manadagopal, the two umpires, walk out to the middle as well. And cheers go out as Travishek walk out! Kalyan B: "it's either 300 or 80 all out, that I can gurantee" -- Bold prediction No. 1 for the day. Joseph : "I don't understand why, SRH cannot push GT to 3rd place, if they win by a big margin and over take them on the net run rate. " -- Because in any scenario, one of SRH or RCB will slip down below them! Nilesh: "Anupam man.. WHY??!!! Why did you have to do it before the match??" Anupam: "Fun Fact: This fixture is yet to witness either team doing a "double" over the other. SRH are due a win today to keep that streak going on." VS: "Looks like the pitch is suitable for Travishek fireworks. Buckle in guys. " So, Tim David is not starting for RCB and will likely come on as RCB's Impact Sub. Anyway, Michael Clarke in his pitch report said he "feels sorry for the bowlers tonight as it's an absolute belter". No grass on the pitch and it looks consistent and even. He reckons it'll have great bounce and carry for batters to hit through the line. For the bowlers, he says the only thing that could work is change of pace and varying their angles. "Runs, runs and more runs," he concluded. Here are the teams: SRH XI: 1 Abhishek Sharma, 2 Travis Head, 3 Ishan Kishan (wk), 4 Heinrich Klaasen, 5 Salil Arora, 6 R Smaran, 7 Nitish Kumar Reddy, 8 Pat Cummins (capt), 9 Shivang Kumar, 10 Eshan Malinga, 11 Sakib Hussain Impact options: Aniket Verma, Praful Hinge, Liam Livingstone, Harsh Dubey, Harshal Patel RCB XI: 1 Venkatesh Iyer, 2 Virat Kohli, 3 Devdutt Padikkal, 4 Rajat Patidar (capt), 5 Jitesh Sharma (wk), 6 Romario Shepherd, 7 Krunal Pandya, 8 Bhuvneshwar Kumar, 9 Rasikh Salam, 10 Suyash Sharma, 11 Josh Hazlewood Impact options: Tim David, Kanishk Chouhan, Swapnil Singh, Abhinandan Singh, Jordan Cox 7pm It's toss time! Cummins give the coin a toss. Patidar calls heads, tails it is. SRH will bat. "I think it's a long shot finishing top two but we just want to give it a crack. Want the boys to enjoy tonight," Cummins says. SRH unchanged. Patidar is greeted with loud cheers as well. "Wherever we go it feels like a home game," he says. Patidar says Bethell picked up a finger injury and the skipper is replacing him in RCB's only change. Navanee : "Is it mathematically possible that GT can be pushed to 3rd?" -- Nope, Gujarat Titans are confirmed for Qualifier 1. umar: "Travishek vs Hazleshwar today!! Hope the former defeats the latter, go srh!" 6.45pm I know I said Ashish would join us in a bit, but he already has some pre-game reading for you. Match context, players to watch out for, team news... he has it all covered in his preview. 6.40pm Alright, I know what all of you are wondering. Can SRH make it in the top two? Is RCB's top-two spot under threat? Well, all your questions about all permutations and combinations are answered here. A bit of good news early on for RCB fans: Phil Salt is back with the RCB squad. He has travelled with the team but Matt Roller reckons it'll be unlikely that he will play today, given he landed in India last night. He has been out of action for a while with a finger injury. 6.30pm Hello and welcome, everyone. It's Match No. 67 of IPL 2026 and it's Sunrisers Hyderabad taking on Royal Challengers Bengaluru, in a rematch of the season opener which RCB won. These are two of the most exciting sides in the league, and while both teams have historically been known more for their batting, their bowling attacks have stood out as well this year, leading to both teams making it to the playoffs. RCB will of course look to sign off the league stage with a win, and finish as table-toppers, while SRH will look for a miraculous thrashing, that could help them make it for Qualifier 1. So, get ready for a blockbuster clash. I am Abhimanyu, and I'll be your eyes and ears along with Ashish Pant, who will join you soon.

commentPostTextItems.html: Heinrich Klaasen: Wasn't easy initially. Was under the pressure initially. The wicket was a bit slow and it was tough finding my timing. I think I might have gone for too many shots. But it got easier later. [Wicket getting slower?] I would hope so. I can't see that wicket getting any better and it might slow down. It was a game that we could try a little if we needed to. It is a nice game to play and you never know what can happen. 9.22pm RCB need to score at least 166 to cement a top-two spot. They need 178 to finish top of the points table. This is a belter of a surface and RCB will be confident of not just getting to 166 but the 256-target. If SRH restrict RCB to below 166, they will seal a top two spot and RCB will drop down to No. 3 on the points table. A top batting performance once again from SRH. Ishan Kishan top scored with 79 while Klaasen and Abhishek also got fifties to take SRH to 256. Can RCB chase this down? Join us in a bit to find out.

commentTextItems.html: Length ball on leg stump, he works this to deep square leg. RCB go down by 55 runs, but they won't mind. They have sealed a top spot, while SRH remain at No. 3

commentPostTextItems.html: RCB lose by 55 runs, but they have secured what they set out for at the start of the game - a top spot. They will play GT in Qualifier 1 in Dharamsala while SRH will head to New Chandigarh to play the eliminator. Thanks for tuning in this evening, if you missed any of the action, Sreshth Shah's report has you covered. Until tomorrow, this is me Ashish Pant, signing off on behalf of Abhimanyu, Ranjith and Thilak. Night! Ishan Kishan is the Player of the Match: [On his innings] Just happy about it, taking one match at a time, not making it complicated for myself, just keeping it simple like I spoke earlier before the tournament. It's just about watching the ball and playing your game. [On scoring runs against RCB] I don't know to be very honest. Like I said, I just take one match at a time, but I don't know why but I do feel confident when I'm playing against them and I think end of the day, fortune favors the brave and I just try to do my thing and it works in my way. [On being mature with his shots] I mean more than maturity, it's about shot selection. So, you know when to play which shot, who to target. So I'm just trying to you know, take one ball at a time, know the situation, understand the pitch and just play your shots. You need to feel confident in the middle and if you're feeling that way just make sure you play those good shots. [On the top two spot] We had that in mind. We wanted to finish in the top two because it does give an opportunity for the team to reach the finals easily. But at the same time, Pat coming in, helping us with everything getting one of the best bowlers in our side, leadership qualities there. So it's very good to have him and the way he's leading the side I can't ask for more also as a team. [On the team atmosphere] It's about enjoying in the middle because end of the day pressure is always there. But if you're enjoying you might get in a zone where you just play your best game. I need to give that credit to support stuff and Pat Cummins because he has always been that person who has always motivated players in the middle. Pat Cummins: [On the win] Yeah, it's pretty impressive to get the score that we did. I thought the boys batted fantastically and some good performances. So everyone's hitting their straps. [On a chance at making the top two] I knew a lot of things had to go our way. Yeah we got close, I think they were trying to make sure they got up to that score. So we threw a few different things at him, but it's still a big win. [On the bowlers] They've been fantastic. I've actually learned a lot of from those guys as well. Eshan Malinga has been the form bowler and he's mixing up different things. And of course, you know, Sakib there as well. So a captain's dream. [Eliminator] Yeah, I think it's still five six days away. So yeah, we'll rest up for a couple days head up there and yeah, the guys know the ground pretty well, so get out there. We'll know who we're playing in the next day or two Presentation time A stat nugget from Sampath: No team before RCB had lost by 50 or more runs despite having six or more wickets in hand in a men's franchise T20 league game. Ddn: "I don't think that this would dent RCB's confidence. After DDP got out, it was quite evident that they were playing for 166 then, which they did. In their mind, they did well." Prasanna : "RCB should have sent Jitesh ahead of David so that he gets some practice ahead of playoffs. " Abhi: "incredible achievement by srh to even qualify for the playoffs with that inexperienced bowling lineup. hats off to the coaching staff and cummins" Nitin : "One can say, RCB did not show intent but still effortlessly made 200. Scary...." Sakib Hussain: [Gameplan] The plan was to bowl according to the wicket. Varun bhaiya asked me to bowl to my strengths. Virat Kohli's was a dream wicket for me. [On Malinga] The plan was to bowl slower balls as the ball was gripping and sticking onto the surface. I just want to improve. I just want to give my 100% Rajat Patidar, the RCB captain: [Target too steep?] The top five [SRH] batters played very well and they dominated. [Pitch slowed down] Not really, the slower bouncer was gripping. They executed the bouncers and yorkers very well. [Job done?] Top priority was to be on the top but the target was a lot. 255 was a big target. Hyderabad is a good wicket but once you start bowling the slow bouncers it becomes tough. 11.29pm RCB end with a loss, but will they care? Don't think so. They have sealed a top-two spot, and finished the league stage at the top of the points table. RCB started the 256 chase in style with Venkatesh Iyer going for it. Once he and Virat Kohli fell, Patidar was intent on the magic 166 number. He scored a sedate fifty and had Krunal Pandya for company, who was 41 not out. The duo ensured RCB first cemented the top-two spot, and then the top position even if they managed just 200 for 4 in their 20 overs, going down by 55 runs. A sweet loss for RCB, who will play Gujarat Titans in Qualifier 1 on May 26 in Dharamsala. SRH will play the eliminator on May 27. Krishna: "Say what you will about this situation, but there is a certain downside to playing out a game like this for RCB. If this dents their confidence, and it will to some degree, the margins could prove damaging in the qualifier. "

commentPreTextItems.html: Josh Inglis and Arshin Kulkarni are LSG's openers. Arshdeep Singh with the new ball for PBKS. PBKS must win to have a chance of making the playoffs. LSG have nothing to lose. Game time ... Toss, 7pm Pant tosses the coin, Shreyas calls tails and wins. PBKS are going to bowl and have brought in Marco Jansen and Vijaykumar Vyshak. "Super excited," says Shreyas. "Do or die for us." He's got his game face on. Arjun Tendulkar is making his debut for LSG, and Arshin Kulkarni also comes into the team. "We want to say sorry to our fans," says Pant, "we want to come back strong." Only two overseas players in the LSG team - a lot of them have gone home. LSG bat-first XI: Inglis, Kulkarni, Pooran, Badoni, Pant, Samad, Mukul Choudhary, Tendulkar, Shami, Prince, Mohsin. LSG's sub options: Shahbaz, Rathi, M Siddarth, Himmat, Akash PBKS bowl-first XI: Arya, Prabhsimran, Connolly, Shreyas, Shedge, Shashank, Omarzai, Jansen, Vyshak, Arshdeep, Chahal PBKS sub options: Harpreet, Stoinis, Bartlett, Vinod, Pravin Dubey Phani: "No better chance for PB than today - Facing a bottom ranked team and further depleted with Marsh missing. So much inexperience in the ranks as well - Arshin, Arjun, Mukul, etc" Naveen Batchu: "Nice to See Arjun playing today, hopefully his gets some wickets with his Yorkers." Karthik Siram : "Cooper Connolly has been a surprise package. Tipped more as a bowler, but he has delivered with the bat. He's Australia's next Steve Smith. I'm telling it here. Mark my words!" Deepak: "Nostalgic to see the name 'Tendulkar' on the LSG list even thought its not the Master Blaster " 6.30 pm Good evening folks, and welcome to match #68 of IPL 2026: The Last Chance for the Kings. How on earth has it come to this, Shreyas Iyer and his squad might be pondering ahead of tonight's fixture against Lucknow Super Giants in Lucknow. PBKS had a glorious first half of the season, winning six of their first seven games with one washout, and then an inglorious second half, suffering six consecutive defeats to drop from first to fifth. If they lose tonight, their season is over. If they win, then they must wait and hope that tomorrow's results go their way. The silver lining for PBKS is that their must-win game is against the bottom-placed team, LSG, who don't have their best batter for this match. Mitch Marsh has gone home. Hasibul Hassain: "I don't think punjab is winning this…KKR deserves the playoffs spot after what they have done in the second phase off the tournament." Sai Krishna: "Marsh a big miss and that's a huge boost to Punjab." Siddhart: "What's the most consecutive defeats record for a team in a single edition of a franchise tournament?" Pune Warriors lost nine in a row in 2013, and KKR lost nine in a row in 2009. Virat: "Great teams will give their best when they are under tremendous pressure irrespective of situations... Chance for PBKS to take motivation.." Daya is in Lucknow for the game and here are his observations: "Since LSG are already out of the tournament, the crowd is quite small. For PBKS in this important match, Arshdeep Singh, Vijay Kumar Vyshak, Marco Jansen, and Azmatullah Omarzai have been marked their run-ups. For LSG, Mohammed Shami and Arshin Kulkarni have done so. Kulkarni is likely to replace Mitchell Marsh in the LSG XI. VS: "With the start they had, pbks deserve to be in the playoffs. All the best"

commentTextItems.html: Prabhsimran is interested in the stumping/caught behind after he whips off the bails ... Badoni tried to cut a quick one from Chahal outside off but was beaten, that really zipped through outside off with good bounce ... no edge, but  what do we have here? Has Badoni lifted his back foot off the ground? He has! And Prabhsimran has broken the stumps at that very millisecond. What a soft end to a fiery innings, he simply lifted his foot off the ground for no apparent reason and Prabhsimran was ready to pounce on the error.
