commentTextItems.html: maiden IPL century for Shreyas Iyer, and what a time to get it. Winning runs to keep PBKS alive in the race for the final playoff spot. He gets to his hundred by smashing a length ball over the wide long on boundary and raises his arms in delight and relief. After six consecutive defeats, PBKS have finally won a match, and now their fate rests on the result between RR and MI tomorrow afternoon.

commentPostTextItems.html:
So PBKS are up to fourth on the points table. If RR beat MI tomorrow afternoon, it is all over for PBKS. But if MI beat RR, then KKR have an outside chance to overtake PBKS on NRR if they beat DC by 77 runs if they score 200. Or if KKR are chasing, they would need to chase 180 in around 12-12.4 overs. But if that doesn't happen, and if RR have lost, then PBKS are through.

Priyankar: "No one in the commentary cared to write at 17.6 that DC's campaign has formally ended....A DC fan"

Rishabh Pant: It's a tough one, we have to bite the bullet, keep our head high, has been a lot of learning ... tough season for us for sure. I think we scored enough, it's harder in the second innings because the batting gets easier, that's why everyone wants to field first. As a team we want to look at the positives, Josh Inglis, Mitch Marsh, Prince had a terrific season, Mohsin coming back from injury ... Shami bhai. Definitely a lot of positives. It's been a long season, we promise to come back stronger next year.

Ricky Ponting: We did it the hard way. We were sloppy in the field again, gave them 20 more runs than they should have got. Pretty clinical chase, the captain has done that often before. It's his first IPL century and we'll celebrate that tonight. He's a brilliant guy, very mature player, mature leader, keeps his emotions in check, the respect he has is second to none, delighted to work with him, delighted with the season he has had ... Prabh is a terrific player, only in the last couple of years has he realised how good he can be at the top of the order. Mature innings tonight in a good run chase. We have a nice team room, we'll get the boys together and watch it (MIvs RR) ..."

I'll have the presentation for you shortly.

Shreyas Iyer is the Player of the Match, having scored his maiden IPL century in a crucial chase: Ecstatic, first hundred of the season, we won eventually after six consecutive losses. Support MI tomorrow. Elated by the bowling performance after going for 16 off the first over, Azmat bowled brilliant ... it's all about momentum in this situation, Yuzi got a crucial wicket of Pant, he showed his character after leaking runs in the previous game ... I know if I give myself time in the middle and time the ball, rather than getting on top of the ball ... I know I need to stay out there for as long as possible. Prabh was temperamentally active and the communication we had was great ... surreal feeling, finishing a game and scoring a century, I was in a great mind space, felt super from within. Partnership was crucial, creates momentum in the game, seriously elated. We just kept it simple, rather than having meeting and putting pressure on the boys. Free flow of mind is required in. crucial games, don't want to make them overthink, told Ricky we don't need to do a team meeting.

And so the race for the IPL 2026 playoffs will only be decided on the final day of the league stage. RCB, GT and SRH are through, the final spot is currently held by PBKS. And that may or may not change depending on Sunday's results. Do join us tomorrow for what will hopefully be a thrilling end to the league stage. Cheers.

commentPreTextItems.html: 7.27pm Aaron Finch rings the bell at the Eden Gardens to signal the start of the final league game of IPL 2026. Out walk the two on-field umpires followed by the KKR fielders. Credit to the KKR fans who have turned out in droves to support their side. The two DC openers, Abhishek Porel and KL Rahul are also out in the middle. KKR are opening the bowling with Anukul Roy, who is around the wicket to Porel. So, left-armer to left-hander first up. Less go! 7.25pm Thanks, Himanshu. How's everyone doing? The KKR fans and players alike will have as much an eye on this game as the MI-RR game where Jofra Archer is keeping RR in the contest. He's just picked up his third wicket, sending back Hardik Pandya. Suryakumar Yadav, however, is the key man for RR to get. Follow the game as MI-RR clash goes down to the wire. As things stand, MI need 56 off 24 balls. 7.15pm We're just 15 minutes away from the action at Eden. Let Ashish know whom you're supporting, and what you think of the sides today. Now that we know KKR will be chasing, here's what they need to do assuming MI beat RR: If DC score 180, KKR will have to chase it down in anywhere between 12 and 12.4 overs, depending on their final winning score. If DC score 200, KKR will have to win in 12.1 to 12.4 overs. Delhi Capitals: 1 Abishek Porel, 2 KL Rahul (wk), 3 Sahil Parakh, 4 Tristan Stubbs, 5 David Miller, 6 Axar Patel (capt), 7 Ashutosh Sharma, 8 Madhav Tiwari, 9 Auqib Nabi, 10 Mitchell Starc, 11 Lungi Ngidi. Impact options: Vijay, Rizvi, Nigam, Rana and Kuldeep. Kolkata Knight Riders: 1 Ajinkya Rahane (capt), 2 Tejasvi Dahiya (wk), 3 Cameron Green, 4 Rovman Powell, 5 Manish Pandey, 6 Rinku Singh, 7 Sunil Narine, 8 Anukul Roy, 9 Varun Chakravarthy, 10 Saurabh Dubey, 11 Kartik Tyagi. Impact options: Allen, Ranjan, Arora, Ramandeep and Tripathi. 7pm Time for the toss. KKR opt to bowl. Ajinkya Rahane says "the wicket looks really good", even as his side banks on MI vs RR. He wants his side to finish with a win irrespective of what happens in Mumbai. KKR are unchanged. Axar Patel would have bowled first too. He wants to test his team while batting first. Remember, DC are eliminated already. Kuldeep and Nabi are back for DC. 6.50pm What do KKR need to do to make it to the playoffs? There's more to it than just MI beating RR. Find out in S Rajesh's scenarios piece. Meanwhile, here's our man Sreshth Shah's report from Eden: "The emcee at Eden is giving periodic score updates from Wankhede." Atulya: "As a season one KKR fan, I'd love to see SKY take it home for his former franchise" 6.30pm KKR fans, how many of your minds are in Mumbai? In some not-so-good news for you, MI, who need to beat RR for KKR to stay alive in the playoffs race, are struggling. But sport is all about belief even in the toughest of times. So hang tight and hope, for who knows if a miracle is on the way? This is Himanshu saying hello ahead of KKR vs DC at Eden Gardens, with Ashish Pant set to join me soon.

commentPostTextItems.html: Here we are nearly two months after the league stage of IPL 2026 began. The four playoffs teams are finalised - they are RCB, GT, SRH and RR - but we don't leave the round-robin fixtures without a good game. It was a bit to and fro, but DC eventually beat KKR rather comfortably. We won't see both these teams in action until another year. But remember, this season's playoffs are just two days away. Until then, it's goodbye and good night! Kuldeep Yadav is the Player of the Match: "I wasn't happy before this match because the way we wanted as a team, we didn't finish. I didn't have a great season. I was expecting more from myself. After the last game, I went back home and worked with my coach. I played one game over there. There are small things which you forget very quickly. I thought I was bowling a bit more open-chested. Sometimes you're not using your full body. That's where T20 batters are strong. It was a lovely game for me coming back from the last game. I was very clear with my plan. I saw the wicket in the first innings; it was a bit slow... The wicket of Rinku was the perfect example. It was a good ball to get him out. It happens [drop catch off the hat-trick ball]! The way I bowled, I'm pleased. When I spoke to my coach, he was very straightforward. He said you need to spin the ball; try to deceive the batter. When you spin the ball, there's chance of getting the batter out." Axar Patel: "The way we played the last three matches, I'm very proud. We saw the effort right till the last match. First we need to accept our mistakes. It's a matter of one match. We played well most of the time. It was important to catch that momentum. It's a high-pressure tournament. At the end of the day, if you're in a good frame of mind, then you can take the wrong decision. It's important to stay calm. I give myself time if I feel frustrated. I feel SRH look the strongest. When their top three makes runs, they look so good." Time for the presentations Lungi Ngidi: "Tonight was good. We've had an up-and-down season. It makes it easier to look back and see where we went wrong. Just to minimise the small errors next time. It took me years [to work on the slower ball]. It has taken years to build the confidence to bowl it. When you play in certain conditions and do well, it builds your confidence. That T20 World Cup for me showed I can do it in these conditions. We definitely weren't a bottom-of-the-table team. Definitely happy to end on this note. Starc is making us step our game up! He's an absolute athlete. Seeing him do that puts a big smile on my face." Kris: "Top 5 and bottom 5 in table are divided nicely by positive and negative NRR." Ajinkya Rahane: "I was batting really well. I tried my chances. Just want to say the kind of season we had, really proud of each and everyone. The situation we were in, from there keeping the league alive... I'm proud of each and every individual. They put that effort going out there. We didn't qualify, which is disappointing. At the moment, guys have their commitments. We'll then probably connect over the call and have discussions. For me, just couple of days off. I'm going to play my local league in Mumbai." 11.25pm KKR lose 7 for 35 in just more than five overs. They fold for 163 in pursuit of 204 despite at one stage looking strong to end the season with a win. The collapse began when comeback man Kuldeep got a set Rahane for 60. As harsh as it gets, though, Porel dropped Dahiya on the hat-trick ball to deny the wristspinner three in a row. But Kuldeep still finished with 3 for 29, and set DC's win up.

commentPreTextItems.html: 7.28pm More red than blue in the Ahmedabad stands, but that is not surprising, is it? The red carpet is laid out as defending champions RCB walk out. GT follow them, with Gill leading the way. We will have the national anthem first. Aight, here come the two GT openers, Shubman Gill and B Sai Sudharsan. How much will Sai Suds be thinking about the two hit-wickets? Just an FYI: We have two hours of back-up time tonight and need a minimum of 10-overs-a-side game. Jacob Duffy has the new ball, and not Bhuvneshwar Kumar. That's interesting. He is over the wicket with a slip in place to Sai Sudharsan. LET'S GO! Kaushal: "This IPL has witnessed batting records be shattered but has been a little short of nail-biting thrillers compared to the last few seasons. Hope we have a last ball finish here!!" On that note, with five minutes to go to the start, here's Ashish Alien: "Thank god, the final is not at Chinnaswamy. Its raining cats and dogs here, would've wasted a lot of time. But still I heard lots of cheers from my damp neighbourhood when RCB won the toss. " Alfred: "@Atul same for purple cap" Atul: "Today if Gill or Sai fall before overtaking Vaibhav in the orange cap race, then RCB will win. Basically, orange cap and cup for the titans or neither " Yep, Ashish and I were discussing just that earlier. I think GT will be happy as of now because their stronger suit will be on show in the second half. VinayMudunuru: "Buttler will have one of the biggest nights of his career!!" Sam: "No Phil Salt but might be better that way…" Yeah, guess he hasn't fully recovered. RCB have played without him for a while now, so it shouldn't be too big an issue Jashan: "So it's Romario over Suyash..." Vikram: "Conventional wisdom would have said Bat first. But if RCB restrict GT under 200, then Kohli will gobble this chase and stay till the end. GT needs to be aggressive, this is the same pitch where India scored 250 in the finals. This match will be tasty affair." Prasidh should be GT's sub going by what was said at the toss GT sub options Prasidh Krishna, Glenn Phillips, Anuj Rawat, Kumar Kushagra, Sai Kishore Gujarat Titans: 1 Shubman Gill (capt), 2 B Sai Sudharsan, 3 Jos Buttler (wk), 4 Jason Holder, 5 Washington Sundar, 6 Rahul Tewatia, 7 Rashid Khan, 8 Nishant Sindhu, 9 Kagiso Rabada, 10 Arshad Khan, 11 Mohammed Siraj Venky Iyer will likely come in as the sub for RCB RCB sub options - Venkatesh Iyer, Kanishk Chohan, Swapnil Singh, Abhinandan Singh, Jordan Cox Royal Challengers Bengaluru: 1 Virat Kohli, 2 Devdutt Padikkal, 3 Rajat Patidar (capt), 4 Krunal Pandya, 5 Tim David, 6 Jitesh Sharma (wk), 7 Romario Shepherd, 8 Bhuvneshwar Kumar, 9 Josh Hazlewood, 10 Jacob Duffy, 11 Rasikh Salam Shubman Gill, GT captain We'd have batted. Hope to put runs and them under pressure. Typical wicket, third match on it. Might be movement for 2-3 overs for pacers. We're feeling fresh and ready. One of the biggest stadiums, always a privilege to play here. Arshad comes back in place of Sai (Kishore) Rajat Patidar, RCB captain Good wicket, won't change in the 40 overs. Will try to get them out early. Lot of memories from last year, but it's 2026 now. Have to do our best to win. Important to stay in the present. Love to play here because of the crowd. Same team 7pm Ravi Shastri out for the toss. Javagal Srinath hands over the coin to Patidar, who'll spin the coin. Heads is the call, it's tails. RCB bowl Huge cheers Pitch Pitch No. 6, equidistant, both square boundaries 66 metres. Aaron Finch says it's a mix-soil pitch, good for batting. It's very even and flat. Doesn't mean it's a belter. Might be slightly slow, might not spin with the soil composition. Ian Bishop says there'll be a high percentage of balls on a good length from pacers, and then the preference of hit-the-deck bowlers to go good or short of good length. Win the toss and chase, says Finch, will get better and better. Karthik Siram : "Any signs of a new debutant today? I feel Gurnoor Brar could be a great surprise pick for the final. An element of surprise can be a powerful weapon." Highly doubt it Krishna Sumanth: "who is going to be the 'Ben Cutting' of Gujarat tonight?" Eric: "Whether Kohli makes it through the powerplay or not is going to be key. When he does everybody gets their ideal entry point and when he gets out early we've seen RCB get into trouble especially with Jitesh and Shepherd out of form" Nikhil Parupall: "Good Evening from Singapore!! 9:30PM and i am ready to celebrate with 2time winner .." 6:50pm Under 10 minutes to go for the toss. Attendance is healthy, the roads outside the ground have been packed for a while. Gill is suited up for the toss, he run down the stairs. Sunshine's still there but floodlights are also taking effect. Nehra has a small chat with GIll. Captain inspects the good length of the pitch. Celine : "Greetings from Helsinki! Being a RCB fan, I'm nervous cos the game is with home advantage to GT. Go RCB, ee sala cup namdeh!" Arul: "GT didn't have much prep time, I think Rcb today.." Virat: "GT team has mainly 5 players (2 batters, 2 bowlers and 1 all rounder) and if RCB will have strategies to handle these 5 players then they will easily win the match. " With Rashid, Prasidh and Holder, they don't really have a weak link in their bowling, do they? Also, Buttler's still great with bat With 45 minutes to go, coach Andy Flower is on one knee, in the middle of RCB's huddle, giving a pep talk. Players and staff forming two concentric circles around him, it's a long talk. Kohli follows with choppy, pointy gestures into the palm while speaking. A bit of applause and the huddle breaks Hus Silverado : "All 3 matches in the playoffs have been won by the team losing the toss..So don't be surprised if it happens today as well !!!" Now this for me is more of a hot take Gummalla: "Unpopular opinion: GT are being underestimated. RCB may be favorites on paper, but finals are won by handling pressure, not hype. GT for me." GT at home are favourites, no? 6:40pm Thanks, Ashish. Hey all. I'm afraid toss-winner might be the match-winner tonight. If the team losing the toss wins, it'll be quite the achievement. The point is there's no running away from the destroyer of free will that is T20 dynamics. There's also the other cliche - bowling wins teams tournaments. While GT has arguably the strongest attack in the comp, RCB have a couple of the best new-ball bowlers but can their middle-overs bowling stand up too? shishank dahiya: "Any rain around ?" Not at the ground, no From Shashank, our rep at the ground: RCB leaning towards a similar combination from Q1. Duffy & Hazlewood marking run-ups. I am off for a coffee. Meanwhile, please welcome RCB fan Ekanth into the comms seat for the first time today. Who's winning this, Ekanth? 6.30pm Here is a potentially controversial statement. Virat Kohli's IPL of 2026 has been as good as if not better than his IPL of 2016. Scoring 973 runs at a strike rate of 152.03 is an extraordinary feat, but his 600 runs at 164.38 this year are more indicative of a proper team plan from RCB and Kohli slotting in in that plan perfectly. Here's a banger of an article from Sidharth Monga on why Kohli's 2026 could be better than Kohli's 2016. Dhruv: "Jason Holder has changed the fortunes of GT in second half, I expect him to play the decisive role tonight." Shadow-Shell: "5 seasons, 4 playoffs qualification, 3rd final, playing for theird 2nd trophy. Is GT the new CSK? Especially with the recent decline of CSK" 6.20pm When Rajat Patidar leads RCB out for their second straight IPL final in Ahmedabad on Sunday, he will have the chance to join an elite list of captains who have won back-to-back IPL titles. But his route towards this peak has been remarkably different. When MS Dhoni completed the double for Chennai Super Kings in 2010-11, he had already established himself as a bona fide great. By the time Rohit Sharma led Mumbai Indians to consecutive titles in 2019-20, he was already a multiple-time IPL-winning captain. Patidar, in comparison, last played for India in early 2024, and was dropped after poor returns in three Tests. He hasn't come close to national selection since. Yet, the sheer weight of his runs at IPL 2026 - 486 runs at a strike rate of 196.76 - has brought him back into conversations for a T20I spot. Here's Shashank Kishore on the quiet captain. Shaurya: "It's so crazy to me that Bhuvi denied RCB the trophy 10 years ago when i was a little kid...now i my early 20s again but this time he has joined forces with VK and just hoping they don't break my heart again..!!" 6.10pm The RCB and GT buses are making their way to the ground. The stands are filling in nice and early. GT face the unenviable task of playing a third game, at a third venue, in six days on Sunday. Their captain Shubman Gill isn't too perturbed by it, though he conceded that their well-rested opponents may have an edge heading into the final. Usually, IPL knockouts are held in only two venues, but this year's scheduling has given the winner of Qualifier 1 a bigger advantage. 6pm Rajat Patidar isn't thinking of the final as possibly being legacy-defining. Neither is he stressed about T20I selection or India captaincy. He simply wants to enjoy the occasion RCB have worked doubly hard for. "I've never thought about what other captains have done before or whether I want to compete with someone," he said. "As an individual, my journey has had its ups and downs, but I've never focused on that [captaincy, legacy]." 5.50pm A decade ago, Bhuvneshwar Kumar and SRH denied Virat Kohli's RCB the title. Ten years later, Virat Kohli is at the centre of RCB's hopes again. He is already an IPL champion once and will have Bhuvneshwar with him as they align to achieve the common goal - the IPL trophy. Here's Shashank Kishore on the contrasting journeys of Kohli and Bhuvneshwar but how they are getting together to help RCB achieve a second IPL title. Vas: "Will Salt be fit to play? Romario or Duffy? Lots to ponder for RCB." 5.40pm For the last eight straight IPLs, the team winning Qualifier 1 has gone on to become champion. Does that come true again? RCB had beaten GT quite comfortably in Qualifier 1. But, they lost to GT in Ahmedabad in the league stage, bowled out for 155. They've won only three of their seven away or neutral games in IPL 2026. But, all of that can be tossed to the wayside if any of their match-winners come off. GT's campaign has been built on the hard work of Kagiso Rabada and Mohammed Siraj; in particular the unstinting way they attack oppositions in the powerplay. Both quicks have been encouraged to go pace-on. Both quicks have been remarkable at assessing the vulnerabilities of specific batters. Both quicks have the potential to break the game early. Here's Alagappan Muthu's preview for the final. 5.30pm IPL S19. The Final. After 64 days, 70 league matches, and three playoffs, we have two teams fighting for the crowning glory. Royal Challengers Bengaluru and Gujarat Titans. RCB, adored by millions, envied by millions. One of IPL's nearly there teams finally broke the duck in the 18th season. They are back in the 19th, bigger and better and hungrier than ever before. Then there's GT, one of the IPL's newest teams. Unlike their opponents, they wasted no time in getting their hands on the silverware. They won it in their debut season in 2022 and then nearly defended it in 2023. The captaincy has changed hands since then, but with a well-rounded team who are at home, they are worthy title contenders. So, where does the IPL trophy go? Does it remain in Ahmedabad or does it travel to Bengaluru for the second straight season? I am Ashish Pant, nice and early because why not. There's lots to build up, lots to look forward and lots to dissect. Sit back and relax, one of these two teams is going to double their IPL championship count.

commentPostTextItems.html: 9:35pm Show done, Ashish will be here for the chase soon. Manikanta: "Is there any dew on the pitch ?" No signs yet Anav: "Captain standing next to Hardik Pandya in the photoshoot has gone on to win the IPL in the past few seasons so accordingly...Shubman Gill and GT should win...but you never know" Yeah, Hazlewood hasn't lost a tournament final and Krunal an IPL final. So, one of that will chase Nihar Noronha : "What are the chances of a super over happening in the final?" Cheuk: "Maybe having a second spinner with Suyash instead of Duffy would have worked better on today's pitch." Went at 9.5 and nearly got a wicket. Not too bad. Think he shouldn't have bowled the first over though Neelesh: "This score reminds me of 2016 T20WC final. Hoping for nail biting finish like that match" same total! Okay folks, there's a live show. Might take a while. So, send in your comments please Shiv: "@Eknath is this a good score on this two-paced pitch?" Feels 20 short. Early wickets could change that Phani: "It's official! Kohli can't score 176 runs! Vaibhav for Orange Cap!" never in danger 9:18pm GT finish with 155, the same score they restricted RCB to in the league game here this season. The first half was owned by RCB after Haxzlewood and Bhuvi got Gill and Sudharsan cheaply. GT promoting Sindhu to No. 3 didn't work. Buttler never got going after looking to restrict damage. GT got 63 in the first ten and 92 in the back ten thanks to Washington. He was nearly out early but got a reprieve with a grounded catch from Cox. There were small contributions from Arshad and the lower order. Krunal was excellent as the lone spinner. Rasikh had arguably his best game of the season. The pitch has been two-paced, slightly slow. The bowlers used the pitch brilliantly

commentPostTextItems.html: What a time to be an RCB fan, could things have together any better for them?! Ten years ago, they would've felt the world was against them. That sentiment continued for nearly a decade. Chris Gayle left, AB de Villiers left. Virat Kohli stayed and they reworked their strategy, it was a gradual shift earlier in the decade. It took full flight after the mega auction last year, now they have two trophies to show for. This could be a dynasty forming. Even if not, it's been special. On that note, it's time to say goodbye one last time. I'm Ekanth, signing off on behalf of Ashish Pant, our scorers Chandan Duorah and M Venkat Raghav, and everyone from the Cricinfo team who've covered the comp. Thanks again for joining us. See you again soon. Rajat Patidar collects the IPL trophy, the team-mates run in onto the dais. Captain holds it aloft, everyone's screaming their hearts out. Trophy handed to Kohli as confetti rains along with the cheers. Turns taken with the trophy-lifting. Dinesh Karthik and Coach Andy Flower join in. They pose and everyone walks across to the Champions tag. Fingers signal a V for the two-time champions. Rajat Patidar, RCB captain It feels superb. There were a lot of memories from last year but we had to stay in the present. Don't have words to express but feeling good. Plan was clear, it was easier to chase. Wanted to get their top-three. Our bowlers throughout the tournament have been superb. Bhuvi, Hazlewood, Rasikh, Krunal, Sheppie, all have been superb. Never dreamt I'd win for RCB, it's all written. Last year, there was a lot of pressure. This year, we were confident. All were in a good frame of mind as compared to last year. Was good to see fans coming, everywhere you go it was like home. Pre-tournament prep was very good for me. The way I look at my batting, I try to work on where I can improve, against pacers especially. Got a lot of ideas and help from DK and Kohli bhail.
